feed.title: OCaml Ecosystem (All Weeklies)
feed.subtitle: Comprehensive weekly summaries across all OCaml ecosystem activity

entry.title: Week 37, 2026: opam shipped 2.6.0-rc1 as x509 1.2.0 cascaded breaking TLS-stack releases, while oxcaml advanced DWARF-5 debug info and LTO prototyping.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Tools ocaml/opam published the 2.6.0-rc1 release candidate after fixing a performance regression that read .tar.gz repositories twice per package install, saving roughly 500ms per install (ocaml/opam#7131) by Kate; the same candidate was mirrored as 8 packages on opam-repository (ocaml/opam-repository#30686).
  • OCaml Ecosystem x509 1.2.0 shipped breaking changes to Distinguished_name equality/matching and RFC 9525 hostname validation by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#30712), cascading same-day releases of tls 2.1.3 (ocaml/opam-repository#30725), dns 10.2.6 (ocaml/opam-repository#30726), letsencrypt 2.1.1 (ocaml/opam-repository#30727), albatross 2.8.1 (ocaml/opam-repository#30728), and ca-certs-nss 3.129 (ocaml/opam-repository#30713).
  • OxCaml DWARF-5 debug output became selectable via a -gdwarf-version flag by Mark Shinwell (oxcaml/oxcaml#6923), with follow-ups for DWARF-5 line-table file registration (oxcaml/oxcaml#7021) and base-address/offset range lists (oxcaml/oxcaml#6926); all-void records are now permitted (oxcaml/oxcaml#7070) by Will Sturgeon, and Bigarray accessors now only require @ read access instead of @ shared (oxcaml/oxcaml#5768).
  • OCaml Core Runtime_events gained new major-heap allocation counters and a Gc.ramp_up span (ocaml/ocaml#15001) plus lost-event reporting to replace spurious "corrupt stream" failures (ocaml/ocaml#15016, closing ocaml/ocaml#14151), both by Tim McGilchrist; Lambda IR no longer trusts GADT equations from refutable/partial-match arguments, fixing a native-code segfault (ocaml/ocaml#15035) by Florian Angeletti; Set.union/inter/diff gained better complexity on physically-shared sets (ocaml/ocaml#15009) by Nicolás Ojeda Bär.
  • Multicore ocaml-multicore/eio added Eio.Process.environment/getenv_opt (ocaml-multicore/eio#923), a new Eio_unix.File module for wrapping arbitrary Unix file descriptors (ocaml-multicore/eio#937) by Thomas Leonard, and Windows rename support handling FAT/NTFS overwrite semantics (ocaml-multicore/eio#934) by Anil Madhavapeddy.
  • OCaml Tools odoc compressed .odoc/.odocl files for a roughly 4-5x size reduction and memoized doc-comment parsing to cut driver CPU by ~13% (ocaml/odoc#1486, ocaml/odoc#1480) by Jon Ludlam; ocaml-lsp added constructor-application and whole-call completion snippets plus .mli go-to-implementation (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2212, ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2074) by Rudi Grinberg.
  • OCaml Ecosystem tyxml 5.0.0 reworked its API to follow the current WHATWG HTML living standard and SVG 2 (ocaml/opam-repository#30641) by Vincent Balat; new packages included json-pointer (RFC 6901/6902/8620 support for jsont) by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml/opam-repository#30656), secret (zeroized out-of-heap secret memory) and kube (typed Kubernetes client) by Ville Vesilehto (ocaml/opam-repository#30672, ocaml/opam-repository#30662), and Robur-coop's MirageOS networking stack additions mnet, utcp, mhttp, and bstr by Calascibetta Romain (ocaml/opam-repository#30674, ocaml/opam-repository#30675).

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    x509 1.2.0's breaking release cascaded through opam-repository's TLS stack while ocaml.org fixed a doc-page OOM incident.

    New Features

  • x509 1.2.0 ships breaking changes to Distinguished_name equality/matching, RFC 9525 hostname validation, and PKCS signing fixes by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#30712), with cross-package bound adjustments landing first to prepare revdeps (ocaml/opam-repository#30714)
  • Downstream TLS-stack releases adapting to x509 1.2.0 followed the same day: tls 2.1.3 (ocaml/opam-repository#30725), dns 10.2.6 (ocaml/opam-repository#30726), letsencrypt 2.1.1 (ocaml/opam-repository#30727), albatross 2.8.1 (ocaml/opam-repository#30728), and ca-certs-nss 3.129 with updated NSS trust anchors (ocaml/opam-repository#30713), all by Hannes Mehnert, partially funded by Tarides
  • opam 2.6.0~rc1 release candidate published opam-client, opam-core, opam-format, opam-installer, opam-repository, opam-solver, opam-state, and opam-devel (8 packages) by Kate (ocaml/opam-repository#30686)
  • tyxml 5.0.0 reworks the library to follow the current WHATWG HTML living standard and SVG 2, with breaking changes to hidden/contenteditable attributes and URL-typed attributes plus many new HTML5/SVG2 elements, by Vincent Balat (ocaml/opam-repository#30641)
  • New aho-corasick package implements multi-pattern string matching over byte strings with overlapping search, leftmost-longest selection, and chunked streaming, by Ville Vesilehto (ocaml/opam-repository#30724)
  • New json-pointer package adds RFC 6901 JSON Pointer, RFC 6902 JSON Patch, and RFC 8620 JMAP wildcard support for jsont codecs, by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml/opam-repository#30656)
  • New secret package provides zeroized secret memory outside the OCaml heap with constant-time equality, optional page hardening, and new Windows support, by Ville Vesilehto (ocaml/opam-repository#30672)
  • New kube package brings a typed Kubernetes API client and controller runtime built on native OCaml threads, by Ville Vesilehto (ocaml/opam-repository#30662)
  • New rpmfile package parses RPM package files (version 3.0, partial 4.0 support), by Михаил (ocaml/opam-repository#30709)
  • Robur-coop's MirageOS networking stack expanded with mnet (TCP for Miou & Solo5, 7 packages, ocaml/opam-repository#30674), utcp (RFC 793 TCP implementation, ocaml/opam-repository#30675), mhttp (HTTP for unikernels, ocaml/opam-repository#30667), and bstr (bigstring library, ocaml/opam-repository#30665), all by Calascibetta Romain
  • bytesrw 0.4.1 shipped an extensive round of bug fixes across its TLS, zlib, xxhash, and PSA-crypto bindings, largely reported by Anil Madhavapeddy, released by Daniel Bünzli (ocaml/opam-repository#30716)
  • tiny_httpd 0.22 masks the authorization header by default in responses and forbids duplicate sensitive headers, by Simon Cruanes (ocaml/opam-repository#30690)
  • logs-async 1.5 adds native systemd journal logging support to the Async reporter, by Vincent Bernardoff (ocaml/opam-repository#30702)
  • ocaml-version 4.1.4 adds recognition of the OCaml 5.5.1 compiler release, by Mark Elvers (ocaml/opam-repository#30706)
  • ppx_deriving 6.2.0 adds a pp deriver/extension for show, polymorphic-variant printer support, and clearer @value conflict errors, by Simmo Saan (ocaml/opam-repository#30722)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/opam-repository shipped the breaking x509 1.2.0 release, cascading same-day updates through tls, dns, letsencrypt, albatross, and ca-certs-nss (ocaml/opam-repository#30712), alongside opam 2.6.0~rc1 (ocaml/opam-repository#30686) and a major tyxml 5.0.0 rework (ocaml/opam-repository#30641)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org focused on reliability: a doc-page rendering OOM incident was root-caused and a bounded-fetch fix opened (ocaml/ocaml.org#3765, ocaml/ocaml.org#3767), alongside routine Planet feed and documentation-link maintenance
  • opam-repository merged roughly a dozen new package submissions and releases while continuing an OCaml 5 C-stub compatibility sweep (ocaml/opam-repository#30663, ocaml/opam-repository#30661), with repeated re-submission cycles for atproto and hegel-ocaml before merging
  • Maintainers on both repositories pushed back on process concerns this week: opam-repository maintainers flagged high-frequency release cadences consuming shared CI capacity (ocaml/opam-repository#30664, ocaml/opam-repository#30697), while ocaml.org maintainers traced a production incident to an unbounded external data fetch (ocaml/ocaml.org#3765)

    • Activity

  • Newly opened opam-repository PRs awaiting merge include scheduling openai-gym for archival due to unmaintained upstream and OCaml 4.11 build failures by Dmitrii Kosarev (ocaml/opam-repository#30719), archiving the lwt alpha/beta packages pending a companion archive-repo PR by Raphaël Proust (ocaml/opam-repository#30711), a Frama-C/Frama-Clang 0.0.20 update targeting Clang 21/22 compatibility that surfaced conf-libclang gaps across distributions by Allan Blanchard (ocaml/opam-repository#30680), and an fsevents 0.4.0 macOS binding release still blocked on test failures diagnosed by Marcello Seri and Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac (ocaml/opam-repository#30479)
  • An obs-loki-eio 0.1.0 submission by Logan B. Nielsen remains blocked because its obs-eio 0.1.1 dependency has never been released (ocaml/opam-repository#30597)
  • Repeated atproto re-submissions (0.1.0 through 1.0.2) by David Engelmann worked through packaging feedback from Anil Madhavapeddy and Marcello Seri on offline-safe testing and redundant metadata before merging (ocaml/opam-repository#30695, ocaml/opam-repository#30698, ocaml/opam-repository#30703, ocaml/opam-repository#30707)
  • The hegel-ocaml property-based testing packages saw four successive re-releases (0.17.3 through 0.18.2) by Ethan Chou, with Calascibetta Romain flagging the tight release cadence's CI resource cost before the final version merged (ocaml/opam-repository#30673, ocaml/opam-repository#30685, ocaml/opam-repository#30696, ocaml/opam-repository#30697)
  • The binaryen/libbinaryen bindings saw four releases (binaryen 0.39.0/0.40.0, libbinaryen 131.0.0/132.0.0) by Oscar Spencer, prompting Anil Madhavapeddy to ask about the release rate and Mark Elvers to propose halving build time by linking the shared library from the static archive instead of rebuilding both (ocaml/opam-repository#30650, ocaml/opam-repository#30658, ocaml/opam-repository#30664, ocaml/opam-repository#30691)
  • CI-compatibility maintenance continued with Dmitrii Kosarev fixing OCaml 4.11/5.4 bound issues across named-pipe, ppx_interact, mlmpfr, sundialsml, and tplib (ocaml/opam-repository#30721, ocaml/opam-repository#30717, ocaml/opam-repository#30718, ocaml/opam-repository#30608, ocaml/opam-repository#30484), and Jan Midtgaard correcting v-prefixed version bound tripwires in ocaml-ai-sdk and oxbow (ocaml/opam-repository#30687, ocaml/opam-repository#30688, ocaml/opam-repository#30225) plus OCaml 5 upper bounds for odbc and misuja after their C stubs called unprefixed alloc_custom/alloc_tuple runtime functions (ocaml/opam-repository#30663, ocaml/opam-repository#30661)
  • Broken package source URLs for metapp were reported and fixed by redirecting to the opam-sources-archive (ocaml/opam-repository#30669, ocaml/opam-repository#30700, ocaml/opam-repository#30704)
  • On ocaml.org, the doc-backend fetch bounding fix remains open, submitted by Cuihtlauac Alvarado: it caps http_get responses at a configurable size ceiling, prefers a search_index_digest from status.json over downloading the full odoc index, and switches Sidebar_cache to Hashtbl.replace to stop duplicate entries accumulating (ocaml/ocaml.org#3767, fixing ocaml/ocaml.org#3765)
  • An automated platform-releases scrape PR from the scrape_platform_releases.yml workflow has been open since June and remains unmerged, carrying 852 additions across 19 files (ocaml/ocaml.org#3693)
  • The Metaprogramming page's PPX documentation link was updated by Khalid to point at the "latest"-tagged version instead of a four-year-old pinned release, merged this week (ocaml/ocaml.org#3769)
  • The dead lthms blog feed (soap.coffee, no longer resolving in DNS) was disabled rather than removed by Cuihtlauac Alvarado, preserving the 21 already-archived posts while stopping daily scrape failures, tracked in ocaml/ocaml.org#3753 (ocaml/ocaml.org#3763)
  • Two automated OCaml Planet scrapes merged, pulling in new posts from cwn, ocsigen, jonludlam, anil, and tunbury, while logging recurring scrape failures for 0branch, patricoferris, mirage, and several dead YouTube playlist/channel IDs (ocaml/ocaml.org#3762, ocaml/ocaml.org#3766)

    • Notable Discussions

  • Kate opened a compiler support timeline proposal through 2030 on opam-repository, sequencing lower-bound raises to OCaml 4.13, 4.14, and eventually 5.2 alongside distro end-of-life dates (ocaml/opam-repository#30671)
  • Dmitrii Kosarev proposed archiving opam-repository packages whose upstream GitHub repos are marked archived, identifying candidates such as opam-lock, cconv, ocaml-bigstring, and ocaml-sodium (ocaml/opam-repository#30550), with Raphaël Proust suggesting a discuss.ocaml.org notice for batch archivals
  • Raphaël Proust proposed an opam-packages-option-static-linking convention package for expressing static-linking preferences across dependency trees, closing the issue pending further discussion on the compiler side (ocaml/opam-repository#29975)
  • Community pushback on high-frequency release cadences for the binaryen/libbinaryen and hegel-ocaml packages, raised by Anil Madhavapeddy and Calascibetta Romain on opam-repository, highlighted the shared CI resource cost of near-daily republishing (ocaml/opam-repository#30664, ocaml/opam-repository#30697)
  • On ocaml.org, Cuihtlauac Alvarado documented a root-cause investigation into intermittent Varnish 503 errors, tracing them to web-server replicas being OOM-killed because rendering any documentation page downloaded the entire odoc search index (371 MB for the awso package) into memory just to compute a cache-busting digest (ocaml/ocaml.org#3765)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Continued OCaml 5 compatibility sweep on opam-repository across older C-stub packages that call unprefixed runtime allocation functions (alloc_custom, alloc_tuple) instead of the required caml_-prefixed equivalents (ocaml/opam-repository#30663, ocaml/opam-repository#30661)
  • The v-prefixed version scheme tripwire (affecting packages depending on re2, core, and similarly-versioned libraries) continues to require repeated manual bound fixes on opam-repository, prompting calls to fix it upstream (ocaml/opam-repository#30687, ocaml/opam-repository#30688, ocaml/opam-repository#30225)
  • Robur-coop's MirageOS unikernel networking stack (mnet, utcp, mhttp, bstr) saw coordinated releases on opam-repository in the same week, reflecting active development toward a pure-OCaml TCP/IP and HTTP stack (ocaml/opam-repository#30674, ocaml/opam-repository#30675, ocaml/opam-repository#30667, ocaml/opam-repository#30665)
  • Maintainers across the group are increasingly pushing back on unsustainable automation: opam-repository maintainers on rapid-fire package re-releases that consume shared CI capacity (ocaml/opam-repository#30664, ocaml/opam-repository#30697), and ocaml.org's incident response on unbounded automated fetches of generated content (ocaml/ocaml.org#3767)
  • On ocaml.org, dead-feed cleanup in the OCaml Planet aggregator continues as a recurring maintenance pattern, disabling rather than removing feeds so archived posts keep rendering (ocaml/ocaml.org#3763, tracked in ocaml/ocaml.org#3753), and automated scrape workflows continue to make up the majority of ocaml.org PR volume, with the platform-releases scrape (ocaml/ocaml.org#3693) sitting unmerged for an extended period

    • OCaml Tools

    opam shipped 2.6.0~rc1, odoc cut .odoc/.odocl size via compression, and a cross-repo odoc/dune doc-linking bug surfaced.

    New Features

  • odoc compressed .odoc/.odocl files for a roughly 4-5x size reduction, memoized doc-comment parsing to cut odoc_driver CPU by ~13% and peak RSS by up to 16%, merged word-run comment storage, removed an internal id-wrapping optimisation (~30% disk reduction), and shared shape-reducer caching, all by Jon Ludlam (ocaml/odoc#1486, ocaml/odoc#1480, ocaml/odoc#1488, ocaml/odoc#1479, ocaml/odoc#1487)
  • odoc now renders items included via include functor for OxCaml code, by Marek Kubica (ocaml/odoc#1452)
  • ocaml-lsp added constructor-application and whole-call completion snippets with independent argument placeholders, interactive destruct-generated branch bodies, and .mli go-to-implementation support, all by Rudi Grinberg (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2212, ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2199, ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2204, ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2074)
  • ocaml-lsp semantic highlighting now classifies function parameters, labelled/optional argument modifiers, and built-in vs. user-defined types, by Rudi Grinberg (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1857, ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1858)
  • opam fixed a 2.6 performance regression that read .tar.gz repositories twice per package install, saving roughly 500ms per install, and shipped opam 2.6.0~rc1, by Kate (ocaml/opam#7131)
  • dune made generated files and shared-cache metadata always read-only (a breaking change), and let dynamic-run actions issue multiple sequential/parallel invocations with explicit dependency batching, by Rudi Grinberg (ocaml/dune#16388, ocaml/dune#16403, ocaml/dune#16394)
  • merlin fixed cursor detection for expressions wrapped in a type constraint (e.g. (x : int)) and added a show-location test helper, by Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac (ocaml/merlin#2120)
  • jsofocaml gained build support for Introcaml (an OCaml fork instrumenting values for runtime introspection), a wasmofocaml --setenv flag, and a single-linear-memory Wasm runtime for Safari compatibility, by Frédéric Bour, @hhugo, and Jérôme Vouillon (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2409, ocsigen/jsofocaml#2415, ocsigen/jsofocaml#2405)
  • jsofocaml fixed a Safari 17 JavaScriptCore parsing bug where a line break after static in a generated class body broke Int64.of_string, reported and fixed by first-time contributor habakan (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2421)

    • Overview

  • opam completed the 2.6.0~rc1 release cycle, fixed an install-time tar.gz double-read performance regression, and opened 2.7.0 development (ocaml/opam#7131, ocaml/opam#7064)
  • odoc merged 13 PRs focused on shrinking .odoc/.odocl files and cutting odoc_driver CPU/memory usage, plus several cross-referencing and rendering bug fixes (ocaml/odoc#1486, ocaml/odoc#1482)
  • dune advanced the action-plugin dynamic-run RPC migration and shipped breaking read-only file/cache and RPC API changes, while a large package-dependency-closure PR stack was closed and restarted (ocaml/dune#16256, ocaml/dune#16362)
  • ocaml-lsp merged 18 PRs adding interactive snippet-based completions and code actions plus .mli go-to-implementation, almost entirely authored by Rudi Grinberg (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2074)
  • merlin merged a cursor-detection fix for type-constrained expressions while a larger rewrite of the "enclosing" (selection range) request stayed open for review (ocaml/merlin#2120, ocaml/merlin#2121)
  • jsofocaml merged Introcaml runtime-introspection build support, a Safari 17 static-field bug fix, and several Wasm/bigarray correctness fixes (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2409, ocsigen/jsofocaml#2421)
  • No summarized activity was recorded this week for ocaml/ocamlfind, ocaml/opam-file-format, or ocaml-dune/spawn

    • Activity

  • dune's action-plugin RPC migration (ocaml/dune#16256) was hardened with fixes for sandbox population, in-flight request draining, cwd-relative path resolution, and shared-cache exclusion, largely by Rudi Grinberg (ocaml/dune#16340-ocaml/dune#16405); a roughly two-dozen-PR stack on package-dependency closure tracking from Ali Caglayan was closed unmerged and restarted as ocaml/dune#16362
  • opam's 2.6.0~rc1 release required a re-do after an ordering mistake was caught mid-process (ocaml/opam#7129, ocaml/opam#7134); nine new PRs opened include Haiku OS support and a opam switch show fix, and two competing long-running drafts continue reworking incremental repository loading (ocaml/opam#6871, ocaml/opam#6924)
  • odoc opened a "Several driver fixes" PR still not ready for review, and two issues on odoc_driver usability, including automatically building docs for dependencies declared in odoc-config.sexp (ocaml/odoc#1461, ocaml/odoc#1491)
  • ocaml-lsp ran an extensive test-first workflow around the Inline into uses code action, landing reproduction tests before the fix itself, by Rudi Grinberg (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2208-ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2214); a URI-normalization PR and an odoc-cross-reference documentLink PR (disclosed as largely LLM-drafted) remain open (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2023, ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2139)
  • merlin's rewrite of the "enclosing" (LSP selection-range) implementation by Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac and PixieDust remained open for review with an outstanding FIXME on begin...end locations (ocaml/merlin#2121); Brian Ward continued iterating on custom-operator location fixes (ocaml/merlin#1917)
  • jsofocaml opened five unmerged PRs including a full JavaScript-introspection prototype building on Introcaml, base64-encoded binary constants to shrink a 30MB toplevel bundle to 26MB, and a Split_toplevel Wasm pass for oversized toplevel functions (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2430, ocsigen/jsofocaml#2432, ocsigen/jsofocaml#2423)

    • Notable Discussions

  • odoc cross-package documentation linking was debugged collaboratively across dune and odoc, with Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac pointing at odoc-config.sexp as the underlying mechanism (ocaml/dune#16363, ocaml/odoc#1492)
  • Rudi Grinberg rejected a proposal to have dune pkg ignore upper version bounds on the dune dependency, calling incorrect upper bounds a general opam-ecosystem problem (ocaml/dune#14637)
  • Hannes Mehnert proposed integrating opam-audit vulnerability warnings into opam; Kate pushed back on a second advisory-repository format and suggested a security-advisories URL field with severity-based filtering instead (ocaml/opam#7113)
  • Daniel Bünzli asked odoc not to run Sherlodoc's tyxml-version-sensitive tests in public CIs such as opam-repository, since failures there disrupt unrelated contributors (ocaml/odoc#1490)
  • On merlin's enclosing rewrite, Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac flagged that the typedtree cannot distinguish begin...end from parenthesized sequences except by location, tracked as a FIXME test (ocaml/merlin#2121)
  • On jsofocaml's Introcaml introspection prototype, Frédéric Bour raised performance, code-size, and DevTools-integration concerns before merge, and @hhugo documented two upstream Introcaml limitations found while testing (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2430)
  • opale disclosed that a sizeable (1000+ line) ocaml-lsp feature PR for odoc cross-reference links was largely LLM-drafted under their direction and review (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2139)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Test-first regression workflows are now standard across the group: dune's action-plugin RPC series (ocaml/dune#16340/ocaml/dune#16342) and ocaml-lsp's Inline into uses fix (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2208-ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2214) both landed failing-test PRs ahead of their fixes
  • Performance and footprint reduction is a shared theme: odoc cut .odoc/.odocl size and odocdriver CPU/memory (ocaml/odoc#1480, ocaml/odoc#1486), opam fixed a tar.gz double-read install regression (ocaml/opam#7131), and jsofocaml worked on shrinking Wasm bundle size and splitting oversized toplevel functions (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2432, ocsigen/jsof_ocaml#2423)
  • LSP-facing location and completion precision continued to improve in both merlin (enclosing rewrite, cursor detection) and ocaml-lsp (snippet-based completions, semantic highlighting), reflecting shared investment in editor tooling (ocaml/merlin#2121, ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2212)
  • OxCaml/OCaml-fork compatibility work spans multiple repos: odoc's include functor rendering for OxCaml (ocaml/odoc#1452) and jsofocaml's new Introcaml build support (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2409)
  • Release engineering and portability dominated opam's week (Haiku, 32-bit architecture, arm64 BSD, autoconf 2.72), while jsofocaml continued targeted Safari/JavaScriptCore compatibility fixes (ocaml/opam#7138, ocsigen/jsofocaml#2421)
  • Large speculative PR stacks are being abandoned and restarted narrower rather than merged piecemeal, as seen in dune's package-closure work (ocaml/dune#16362)

    • OxCaml

    oxcaml/oxcaml drove all recorded group activity: DWARF-5 debug support, void-record typing, and heavy LTO/Merlin-diagnostics prototyping.

    New Features

  • Bigarray Genarray/Array0/Array1/Array2 get, unsafe_get, and blit now require only @ read access instead of @ shared, letting read-only callers avoid a full shared lock (oxcaml/oxcaml#5768)
  • DWARF-5 debug output is now selectable via a -gdwarf-version flag, landed by Mark Shinwell (oxcaml/oxcaml#6923), with follow-ups registering the source file as DWARF-5 line-table file 0 on macOS (oxcaml/oxcaml#7021) and using base-address/offset pairs in DWARF-5 location and range lists (oxcaml/oxcaml#6926)
  • All-void records (fields entirely void-layout) are now permitted, by Will Sturgeon (oxcaml/oxcaml#7070)
  • Non-scanned unboxed layouts (bits8/16/32/64, float32, float64, untagged_immediate, vec128/256/512, void, word) now cross externality inherently rather than requiring a syntactic mod external_ annotation, by Ryan Tjoa (oxcaml/oxcaml#6973)
  • Legacy OCaml-runtime-4 support markers were removed by Nick Barnes (oxcaml/oxcaml#6707): Config.runtime5 and the deprecated Gc.eventlog_pause/Gc.eventlog_resume are gone, and Unix.file_descr's kind annotation was simplified to plain immediate
  • Fixed an allocation-pointer bug on stack overflow (oxcaml/oxcaml#7020) and corrected C stack alignment on stack overflow (oxcaml/oxcaml#7088), both by Nick Barnes
  • Fixed [@unboxable] crashing on local parameters when the enclosing function is not local-returning, by Nathanaëlle Courant (oxcaml/oxcaml#6592)
  • CFG dead-code elimination no longer deletes atomic loads whose result is discarded, preserving side effects, by Xavier Clerc (oxcaml/oxcaml#7101)
  • Switches sharing the same destination with many arguments are now merged, reducing generated code size, by Basile Clément (oxcaml/oxcaml#6784)
  • No new-feature activity was recorded this week in oxcaml/opam-repository, oxcaml/merlin, oxcaml/jsofocaml, or janestreet/opam-repository

    • Overview

  • All recorded activity in the group this week came from oxcaml/oxcaml; oxcaml/opam-repository, oxcaml/merlin, oxcaml/jsofocaml, and janestreet/opam-repository had no summarized activity for week 37
  • oxcaml/oxcaml activity centered on completing the runtime-5-only cleanup (oxcaml/oxcaml#6707), enabling DWARF-5 debug output (oxcaml/oxcaml#6923), and continued link-time-optimization (LTO) and Merlin structured-diagnostics prototyping
  • Robin Ricard merged a large series of PRs vendoring external tools (jsofocaml, sedlex, ppxlib/ppxlib_jane, ocaml-compiler-libs) directly into oxcaml/oxcaml as in-repo subtrees, reducing reliance on separately tracked opam pins
  • Type-system and mode-polymorphism work continued from Gavin Gray, Jakub Bachurski, and @ainageorges, alongside garbage-collector and runtime internals work from Nick Barnes

    • Activity

  • LTO prototyping continued heavily, with Simon Spies opening a consolidated LTO-prototype PR (oxcaml/oxcaml#7156) plus batched rebuilds (oxcaml/oxcaml#7128), keeping data symbols global (oxcaml/oxcaml#7130), and disabling -Oclassic during LTO (oxcaml/oxcaml#7131), while Miriam Vellacott opened PRs to make the Reaper assume a closed world under LTO (oxcaml/oxcaml#7144) and store less data in .cmr/.ltosol/.reaped.cmx files (oxcaml/oxcaml#7177)
  • Mode-polymorphism and typed-diagnostics work opened several new PRs from Gavin Gray, including modality printing relative to explicit defaults (oxcaml/oxcaml#7170) and allowing skipping of intermediate return modes in moregen (oxcaml/oxcaml#7168), alongside @ainageorges opening functor mode variables in .cmi files (oxcaml/oxcaml#7157)
  • CFG backend optimization work continued from Xavier Clerc, opening store-to-load forwarding for CFG CSE (oxcaml/oxcaml#7123) and merging of adjacent Ioffset_loc instructions on amd64 (oxcaml/oxcaml#7132)
  • Jkind/sort-variable refactoring opened by Jakub Bachurski, overhauling sort-variable levels (oxcaml/oxcaml#7179) and adding moregen_occur for sort variables (oxcaml/oxcaml#7178), following the merge of "Untangle equating sorts" (oxcaml/oxcaml#6886)
  • Joe Kerrigan opened support for layout-polymorphic records and variants (oxcaml/oxcaml#7152), and Zack Eisbach opened support for mixed tuples (oxcaml/oxcaml#7135)
  • Nick Barnes continued garbage-collector and runtime infrastructure work: measuring the speed of marking, sweeping, and compaction (oxcaml/oxcaml#7161), removing the old compaction algorithm (oxcaml/oxcaml#7160), and fixing the GC idle phase so Gc.major_slice() always advances the GC (oxcaml/oxcaml#7158)
  • The Reaper dead-code/unboxing pipeline saw ongoing refinement from Nathanaëlle Courant, including a flag to prevent lambda-lifting (oxcaml/oxcaml#7080) and re-landing running the reaper with -Oclassic (oxcaml/oxcaml#7075)
  • Several of Gavin Gray's structured-diagnostics PRs were closed unmerged and superseded, including the original structured diagnostic model (oxcaml/oxcaml#6808) and its natural-language generation (oxcaml/oxcaml#6816), with work continuing under producing structured mode diagnostics (oxcaml/oxcaml#6817)
  • Merlin gained a module-type-impls query from Gavin Gray to support the Interface Strengthener (oxcaml/oxcaml#6811), and kind-template module coercions were opened by Jakub Bachurski for layout-polymorphic module item subsumption (oxcaml/oxcaml#6792)

    • Notable Discussions

  • On the Merlin module-type-impls query (oxcaml/oxcaml#6811), Liam Stevenson questioned surprising signature-substitution behavior and pushed for a variable-argument loop instead of repeated manual $MERLIN single module-type-impls invocations in tests, while also flagging what looked like an AI-generated prompt that had leaked into a commit message
  • Reviewers on kind-template module coercions (oxcaml/oxcaml#6792), including Zesen Qian, discussed whether unrelated reformatting diffs should be avoided to keep git blame usable, and whether kindtemplate_coercion's invariant that tc_args/tc_params are never the identity permutation should be encoded in the type
  • Rudi Grinberg reported that Persistent_env checks an imported interface's CRC vector twice on a checked cold lookup, with a proposed patch caching a per-import "already checked" flag to avoid the redundant traversal (oxcaml/oxcaml#7114)

    • Emerging Trends

  • A clear push toward vendoring external dependencies (jsofocaml, sedlex, ppxlib, ppxlib_jane, ocaml-compiler-libs) directly into oxcaml/oxcaml as in-repo subtrees rather than relying on opam pins, led by Robin Ricard across a dozen-plus PRs (oxcaml/oxcaml#6968-oxcaml/oxcaml#7074)
  • Continued iterative churn on the link-time-optimization prototype, with several PRs opened and closed/superseded within the same week (e.g. oxcaml/oxcaml#7141 superseded by oxcaml/oxcaml#7142; oxcaml/oxcaml#7149 and oxcaml/oxcaml#7146 closed) as the design settles
  • The Merlin structured-diagnostics stack from Gavin Gray is being repeatedly restructured, with earlier PRs closed in favor of reorganized follow-ups (oxcaml/oxcaml#6808, oxcaml/oxcaml#6816 closed; oxcaml/oxcaml#6817, oxcaml/oxcaml#6896, oxcaml/oxcaml#6900 open)
  • Ongoing removal of legacy compatibility shims now that the runtime-5-only transition is complete, seen in the removal of Config.runtime5 and deprecated Gc eventlog functions (oxcaml/oxcaml#6707)
  • Development activity within the group remained concentrated in the single oxcaml/oxcaml repository, with the four other group repositories showing no recorded changes this week

    • OCaml Core

    ocaml/ocaml advanced runtime_events tooling, GADT-soundness and Windows fixes, and governance changes; ocaml/RFCs recorded no activity.

    New Features

  • Weak.get_copy no longer copies continuations, since doing so was unsafe (ocaml/ocaml#14988) by Jeremy Yallop; Gabriel Scherer followed up with a PR to deprecate Weak.get_copy outright (ocaml/ocaml#15064).
  • The expansiveness check now accounts for effect cases, closing a soundness gap around match ... with effect ... (ocaml/ocaml#14986) by Jeremy Yallop.
  • Lambda IR no longer trusts GADT equations introduced by refutable/partial-match arguments, fixing a native-code segfault (ocaml/ocaml#15035, closing ocaml/ocaml#14898) by Florian Angeletti.
  • Runtime_events gained new counters EV_C_MAJOR_DIRECT_ALLOCATED_WORDS, EV_C_MAJOR_SUSPENDED_ALLOCATED_WORDS, EV_C_MAJOR_RESUMED_ALLOCATED_WORDS, plus an EV_EXPLICIT_GC_RAMP_UP span for Gc.ramp_up (ocaml/ocaml#15001) by Tim McGilchrist.
  • Runtime_events consumers that fall behind the producer now see lost-event reporting instead of spurious "corrupt stream" failures (ocaml/ocaml#15016, closing ocaml/ocaml#14151) by Tim McGilchrist.
  • Set.union, Set.inter and Set.diff gained better complexity on physically-shared sets, avoiding unnecessary traversal/allocation (ocaml/ocaml#15009) by Nicolás Ojeda Bär.
  • Unix.realpath now normalizes Win32 UNC paths correctly (ocaml/ocaml#15056, closing ocaml/ocaml#15044) by Nicolás Ojeda Bär.
  • Parser precedence for the with module type constraint was fixed (ocaml/ocaml#14978) by 314eter.
  • The power backend now emits fsqrt directly instead of calling into C, matching the earlier riscv change (ocaml/ocaml#15006) by Zane Hambly.
  • libunix build fixes for Cygwin/mingw covering gethostname/IPv6 guards, blocking-section handling around realpath/lockf, and root registration (ocaml/ocaml#14740, ocaml/ocaml#14921) by Antonin Décimo.
  • No new features were recorded in ocaml/RFCs this week.

    • Overview

  • ocaml/ocaml was the only active repository this week, with 11 new PRs opened and several merged across runtime_events, GADT soundness, Windows/Win32 robustness, and non-x86 backend parity.
  • ocaml/RFCs recorded no commits, issues, or PRs in this window.
  • Governance moved forward in ocaml/ocaml: Stefan Muenzel was added as a maintainer (ocaml/ocaml#15057) and five long-inactive maintainers were proposed for retirement (ocaml/ocaml#15063).
  • Contributor-facing documentation was tightened, including guidance to consider writing an RFC before large changes (ocaml/ocaml#15055) and a simplified local-build workflow (ocaml/ocaml#15041).

    • Activity

  • Eleven PRs were opened and remain open in ocaml/ocaml, covering codegen (dead-code elimination of discarded atomic loads, ocaml/ocaml#15045 by Xavier Clerc), tooling (ocamllex cleanup on a fatal missing-case warning, ocaml/ocaml#15048 by cui fliter; a new EV_PROCESS_CREATE lifecycle event and CI curl-retry/opam-validation hardening, ocaml/ocaml#15049 and ocaml/ocaml#15050 by Tim McGilchrist), typing (an escaped-Equality_trace fix, ocaml/ocaml#15052 by Samuel Vivien; a [@@deprecated_unlabelled] attribute proposal, ocaml/ocaml#15054 by Nicolás Ojeda Bär), scheduling (always advancing the work counter in idle slices, ocaml/ocaml#15062 by Nick Barnes), governance (ocaml/ocaml#15063, ocaml/ocaml#15064), CI (disabling the beyond-2038 check on 32-bit CI, ocaml/ocaml#15065 by Olivier Nicole), and testing (skipping the AFL fuzz test without --with-afl, ocaml/ocaml#15066 by @akashchamp, addressing ocaml/ocaml#15046).
  • David Allsopp opened parsetree support for wildcards/holes in expressions and module expressions (ocaml/ocaml#15051), which merged just after this reporting window closed.
  • Runtime_events work continued from Tim McGilchrist beyond the merged counters and corrupt-stream fix, with open documentation improvements (ocaml/ocaml#15039) and lost-word truncation handling (ocaml/ocaml#15010).
  • Three OSEC security-advisory reference PRs were merged by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/ocaml#15059, ocaml/ocaml#15060, ocaml/ocaml#15061).
  • Backend/codegen work continued with an open PR to drop redundant memory-model fences around atomic RMWs on AArch64 (ocaml/ocaml#14936 by Sebastian Pop) and a proposal to emit clz/ctz primitives on amd64/arm64 (ocaml/ocaml#15018 by Zane Hambly).
  • Larger in-flight proposals remain open: Raphaël Proust's link-time-linking design (ocaml/ocaml#14895), Damien Doligez's new GC-pacing logic (ocaml/ocaml#14796), Vincent Laviron's support for unlimited non-constant constructors (ocaml/ocaml#14507), Florian Angeletti's structured compiler diagnostics (ocaml/ocaml#13766), and Jeannalyse's new Hashtbl implementation (ocaml/ocaml#14956) and Atomic.compare_and_exchange addition (ocaml/ocaml#14912).
  • Two long-dormant PRs were closed: an RFC to add a single file to the load path (ocaml/ocaml#9056 by Nicolás Ojeda Bär) and Lambda.shallow_fold_left (ocaml/ocaml#8784 by Vladimir Keleshev).
  • No activity was recorded in ocaml/RFCs this week.

    • Notable Discussions

  • David Allsopp proposed at the maintainer meeting merging flexdll into the compiler repository rather than keeping it as a submodule (ocaml/ocaml#15058); Gabriel Scherer noted the general usability pain of git submodules.
  • Issue ocaml/ocaml#15043 (a runtime_events ring-buffer hang) prompted a discussion about AI-tool transparency after Sadiq Jaffer explained the report had been filed autonomously by a Claude instance; Gabriel Scherer asked for transparency about tool-produced issue text going forward, and Tim McGilchrist landed the confirmed fix (ocaml/ocaml#15016).
  • Governance changes were discussed and merged: Stefan Muenzel was added as a maintainer (ocaml/ocaml#15057), while Gabriel Scherer opened a companion PR to retire five long-inactive maintainers (ocaml/ocaml#15063).
  • The Windows stop-the-world barrier report from Daniel Larraz (ocaml/ocaml#15042) drew a root-cause discussion from Antonin Décimo, pointing to Sleep's millisecond resolution in caml_plat_spin_back_off and proposing a high-resolution waitable timer.
  • Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac and Florian Angeletti worked through a discrepancy between interface- and implementation-context typing of a functor argument alias (ocaml/ocaml#15047).

    • Emerging Trends

  • Runtime_events remains the most active area, with counters, corrupt-stream handling, lifecycle events, and documentation touched by Tim McGilchrist (ocaml/ocaml#15001, ocaml/ocaml#15016, ocaml/ocaml#15039, ocaml/ocaml#15049, ocaml/ocaml#15010) and a ring-buffer hang report (ocaml/ocaml#15043).
  • Windows/Win32 robustness recurs across the stop-the-world barrier latency report (ocaml/ocaml#15042), the Unix.realpath UNC-path fix (ocaml/ocaml#15056), and Cygwin/mingw libunix build fixes (ocaml/ocaml#14740, ocaml/ocaml#14921).
  • GADT/type-soundness edge cases keep surfacing, from the Lambda-IR value-kind segfault fix (ocaml/ocaml#15035, closing ocaml/ocaml#14898) to open reports on module-type subtyping with present/absent aliases (ocaml/ocaml#13976).
  • Non-x86 backend parity continued with power emitting fsqrt directly (ocaml/ocaml#15006), AArch64 atomic-fence pruning (ocaml/ocaml#14936), and a clz/ctz primitives proposal (ocaml/ocaml#15018).
  • Project governance saw concrete action, with a new maintainer added and inactive ones proposed for retirement in the same cycle (ocaml/ocaml#15057, ocaml/ocaml#15063), while ocaml/RFCs itself stayed inactive despite ocaml/ocaml's documentation now pointing larger proposals there (ocaml/ocaml#15055).

    • Multicore

    Activity this week was confined to ocaml-multicore/eio: Windows rename/NT-path fixes merged and an eio_linux spawn bug was traced to an upstream io_uring kernel issue.

    New Features

  • ocaml-multicore/eio: Added Eio.Process.environment and Eio.Process.getenv_opt for reading process environment variables, with Env.get_opt changed to return None rather than raising Invalid_argument for invalid names, by Patrick Ferris with review from Thomas Leonard and Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#923)
  • New Eio_unix.File module adding import_rw and import_ro to wrap arbitrary Unix file descriptors as Eio files, closing a gap where Eio_unix.Net.import_socket_stream was the only option and didn't support operations like pread, by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#937)
  • Windows backend gained rename support, handling Win32's differing overwrite semantics for files versus directories (FAT volumes cannot replace a directory), by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#934)
  • Windows NT path handling and stat/symlink fixes: corrected an uninitialized-handle check in the openat/unlinkat stubs that misreported failures, fixed nofollow dropping directory/non-directory constraints so stat kinds worked again, fixed ELOOP symlink recovery resolving against the process directory instead of the sandbox root, fixed unmapped Unix errors escaping open_in, stopped stat from creating a missing file, and made stat ~follow:false actually avoid following the link, resolving ocaml-multicore/eio#931, by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#932)
  • Fixed a gcc calloc-transposed-args warning in fork_action.c by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#933)

    • Overview

  • Of the nine repositories in the multicore group, only ocaml-multicore/eio recorded activity for week 37 (2026-09-07 to 2026-09-13); ocaml-multicore/domainslib, ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring, ocaml-multicore/meio, ocaml-multicore/saturn, ocaml-multicore/eio-trace, ocaml-multicore/picos, ocaml-multicore/kcas and ocaml-multicore/ocaml-iomux had no recorded changes
  • eio's week centered on merging environment-variable access (ocaml-multicore/eio#923), a new Eio_unix.File module (ocaml-multicore/eio#937), Windows rename support (ocaml-multicore/eio#934), and Windows NT path/stat fixes (ocaml-multicore/eio#932)
  • A large Windows process-spawning PR opened for review (ocaml-multicore/eio#936), while anonymous pipes on Windows remained a draft in progress (ocaml-multicore/eio#929)
  • An intermittent eio_linux spawn failure (ocaml-multicore/eio#935) was diagnosed as an upstream io_uring kernel bug rather than an eio defect, requiring no code change

    • Activity

  • Anil Madhavapeddy opened Windows process spawning support (ocaml-multicore/eio#936), layered on the still-open pipes fix (ocaml-multicore/eio#929); Thomas Leonard gave detailed review feedback on the child-wait/cancellation logic, suggesting a simplified Fiber.fork_daemon pattern modeled on eio_posix's existing approach
  • Anonymous pipes on Windows (ocaml-multicore/eio#929) remains a draft, with Anil Madhavapeddy investigating whether cancellation requires a move to IOCP after finding that Unix.write on a full pipe raises EPIPE and large writes deadlock
  • Issue ocaml-multicore/eio#935, an intermittent eio_linux spawn failure with Unix.EUNKNOWNERR 26 (ETXTBSY), was closed after Thomas Leonard and Anil Madhavapeddy traced it to an upstream io_uring kernel bug, reproduced it directly against liburing, and got confirmation from the maintainer that a fix is planned for kernel 7.4
  • Issue ocaml-multicore/eio#931, Windows paths being passed unqualified to NtCreateFile, was closed via the fixes in ocaml-multicore/eio#932, verified against the ocaml-forester test suite in collaboration with Kento Okura
  • Issue ocaml-multicore/eio#925, a request for hard-link support (Eio.Path.link) using linkat to avoid TOCTOU races when extracting untrusted OCI tar archives, remains open, with Anil Madhavapeddy noting it is queued behind the Windows symlink work

    • Notable Discussions

  • Investigation into ocaml-multicore/eio#935 combined bpftrace kernel tracing and a minimal C reproduction against liburing to show that a file descriptor closed before execve was nonetheless still considered open by the kernel on ZFS (but not ext4); Jens Axboe confirmed it as a known io_uring kernel bug with a fix planned for 7.4, so no change was needed in eio itself
  • Design discussion on ocaml-multicore/eio#923 between Patrick Ferris and Thomas Leonard over whether environment access should live on Eio.Process.mgr or a separate Vars capability, settled by benchmarking get_all/get_opt versus a direct accessor and by the observation that anyone spawning processes already has environment access
  • Review of ocaml-multicore/eio#936 surfaced a discussion on correct cancellation semantics for waiting on a Windows child process, with Thomas Leonard proposing a Fiber.fork_daemon-based pattern that signals the process on switch cancellation while still awaiting its exit

    • Emerging Trends

  • Windows backend completeness remained the dominant focus in eio — process spawning (ocaml-multicore/eio#936), anonymous pipes (ocaml-multicore/eio#929), rename (ocaml-multicore/eio#934), and NT path/stat handling (ocaml-multicore/eio#932, ocaml-multicore/eio#931) — driven by regression testing against the real-world ocaml-forester project with Kento Okura
  • Recurring attention to capability-safety in filesystem APIs, seen both in the Windows symlink/stat fixes in ocaml-multicore/eio#932 and in the hard-link request in ocaml-multicore/eio#925, which asks for linkat-based semantics to avoid TOCTOU races when extracting untrusted archives
  • The other eight repositories in the group (domainslib, ocaml-uring, meio, saturn, eio-trace, picos, kcas, ocaml-iomux) had no recorded activity this week
entry.summary: opam shipped 2.6.0-rc1 as x509 1.2.0 cascaded breaking TLS-stack releases, while oxcaml advanced DWARF-5 debug info and LTO prototyping.

entry.title: Week 36, 2026: OCaml 5.5.1 and opam 2.6.0~beta2 shipped alongside Dune's RPC-based dynamic actions, new oxcaml atomic pointers/DWARF-5, and eio's typed Process.Env.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Core ocaml/ocaml published OCaml 5.5.1, fixing a Marshal.data_size integer-overflow security bug (ocaml/ocaml#15030) by Xavier Leroy, a bytecode-loading overflow, a module-dependent-functions type-system bug, and restoring macOS switch-cloning support.
  • OCaml Core Native rounding instructions for Float.round/trunc/ceil/floor now emit directly on arm64 and power instead of calling into C, by Zane Hambly (ocaml/ocaml#15017), alongside a POWER assembler fix for large stack-frame offsets by Tim McGilchrist (ocaml/ocaml#15021).
  • OCaml Core Two Win32 Unix.select correctness bugs and a Windows thread-starvation bug that could hold the runtime lock forever were fixed by Nicolás Ojeda Bär (ocaml/ocaml#15025, ocaml/ocaml#15029, backported in ocaml/ocaml#15034).
  • OCaml Core The Haiku/BeOS native-code backend was activated on trunk by Anarchos (ocaml/ocaml#14773).
  • OCaml Ecosystem ocaml/opam-repository published OCaml 5.5.1 as ocaml/ocaml-compiler/ocaml-base-compiler/ocaml-system packages by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/opam-repository#30637) and opam 2.6.0~beta2 as 8 packages by Kate (ocaml/opam-repository#30603).
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/opam released opam 2.6.0~beta2 by Kate (ocaml/opam#7115), fixing a pinning performance regression that recursively scanned entire project trees and improving opam update performance by roughly 8% (ocaml/opam#7101, fixes ocaml/opam#7098).
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/dune moved dynamic actions (used by ppxs and dune ocaml top) onto RPC instead of an ad hoc sandbox protocol, by Rudi Grinberg (ocaml/dune#16256), a breaking change for dynamic-action plugin code, plus five follow-up deadlock/dependency fixes; qualified module references are now supported under (include_subdirs qualified) by Antonio Nuno Monteiro (ocaml/dune#15633).
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/ocaml-lsp merged 48 PRs including interactive construct completions with tab stops by Rudi Grinberg (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2198) and a fix for off-by-one diagnostic line numbers (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2163, fixes ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2145).
  • OxCaml oxcaml/oxcaml added new atomic pointer primitives (%unsafe_atomic_load_ptr and friends) by Joe Kerrigan (oxcaml/oxcaml#6747) and a -gdwarf-version <4|5> flag for DWARF-5 output cutting debug-info size roughly 26%, by Mark Shinwell (oxcaml/oxcaml#6923).
  • OxCaml Two production bugs were fixed by Nick Barnes: an allocation-pointer corruption on stack overflow, and a C-stack-alignment crash under TCMalloc (oxcaml/oxcaml#7020, oxcaml/oxcaml#7088).
  • Multicore ocaml-multicore/eio merged a typed Eio.Process.Env module replacing raw string array environments on Process.spawn/run/parse_out, with Windows case-insensitive name handling, by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#930).
  • OCaml Ecosystem New opam packages json-pointer and tdmrep by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml/opam-repository#30656, ocaml/opam-repository#30616) and kube, a Kubernetes client, by Ville Vesilehto (ocaml/opam-repository#30662); tyxml 5.0.0 shipped breaking API changes by Vincent Balat (ocaml/opam-repository#30641).

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    OCaml 5.5.1 and opam 2.6.0~beta2 published to opam-repository while ocaml.org curated Planet feeds and announced opam 2.5.2.

    New Features

  • OCaml 5.5.1 published to ocaml/opam-repository as ocaml, ocaml-compiler, ocaml-base-compiler, ocaml-system, ocaml-src and ocaml-variants by Florian Angeletti, fixing the macOS switch-cloning failure from ocaml/opam-repository#29496 (ocaml/opam-repository#30637)
  • opam 2.6.0~beta2 published as 8 packages by Kate (ocaml/opam-repository#30603), while ocaml.org separately carried the stable opam 2.5.2 release announcement by the same author (ocaml/ocaml.org#3712)
  • CI on ocaml/opam-repository now honours x-ci-accept-failures on Windows (msys2-mingw/cygwin-mingw), by Samuel Hym (ocaml/opam-repository#28856)
  • tyxml 5.0.0 shipped with breaking API changes (typed Xml.uri attributes, SVG 2 documents, enumerated hidden/contenteditable) by Vincent Balat (ocaml/opam-repository#30641)
  • New packages json-pointer and tdmrep by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml/opam-repository#30656, ocaml/opam-repository#30616), kube (Kubernetes client/controller runtime) by Ville Vesilehto (ocaml/opam-repository#30662), caps by Yoann Padioleau (ocaml/opam-repository#30627), amlc-lsp by Christopher (ocaml/opam-repository#30622), typegist alongside jsont 0.4.0 by Daniel Bünzli (ocaml/opam-repository#30614), the pidgio family by Xavier Van de Woestyne (ocaml/opam-repository#30638), and obs-prometheus-eio by Logan B. Nielsen (ocaml/opam-repository#30596)
  • ocaml.org's OCaml Planet aggregator gained a new source, gilwath.com, filtered to caml-tagged posts only, by Cuihtlauac Alvarado (ocaml/ocaml.org#3760)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/opam-repository published official OCaml 5.5.1 (ocaml/opam-repository#30637) and opam 2.6.0~beta2 (ocaml/opam-repository#30603), alongside a breaking tyxml 5.0.0 release (ocaml/opam-repository#30641) and roughly a dozen new package submissions
  • Maintainers on ocaml/opam-repository increased scrutiny of automated/LLM-driven release patterns, closing or questioning several fast-iterating submissions (ocaml/opam-repository#30623, ocaml/opam-repository#30634, ocaml/opam-repository#30643)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org focused on OCaml Planet feed curation — adding gilwath and disabling two dead feeds (dinosaure, lthms) — plus an opam 2.5.2 release announcement, jobs-page cleanup, and a CI flakiness investigation (ocaml/ocaml.org#3760, ocaml/ocaml.org#3763, ocaml/ocaml.org#3712, ocaml/ocaml.org#3764, ocaml/ocaml.org#3759)
  • Both repositories saw active involvement from Anil Madhavapeddy (new packages and account-authenticity scrutiny on ocaml/opam-repository; Planet-aggregated blog posts on ocaml/ocaml.org) and Cuihtlauac Alvarado (the topup/river packages on ocaml/opam-repository; Planet curation and CI triage on ocaml/ocaml.org)

    • Activity

  • On ocaml/opam-repository, Calascibetta Romain pushed a broad ecosystem update across h1, miou, hurl, httpcats, the 7-package mnet stack, mhttp, vif and bstr (ocaml/opam-repository#30612–#30642), while Oscar Spencer released 8 rapid binaryen/libbinaryen version bumps (ocaml/opam-repository#30650 and others)
  • Several package releases needed 2-3 opened-and-closed iterations before merging, including matcha (ocaml/opam-repository#30607, ocaml/opam-repository#30617, ocaml/opam-repository#30623), topup (ocaml/opam-repository#30562, ocaml/opam-repository#30600, ocaml/opam-repository#30602) and hegel (ocaml/opam-repository#30644–#30646)
  • An automated vscoqbot PR for VSRocq 2.5.0 was closed pending human review, and Enrico Tassi then opened and merged a corrected version (ocaml/opam-repository#30643, ocaml/opam-repository#30653)
  • On ocaml/ocaml.org, Cuihtlauac Alvarado closed an opt-in feed-repair PR that would have pinned an unreleased river branch, favoring the simpler disable approach tracked in ocaml/ocaml.org#3753 (ocaml/ocaml.org#3756)
  • Cuihtlauac Alvarado opened a CI flakiness issue on hilite.markdown missing at build time, traced to an unreleased git pin on hilite (ocaml/ocaml.org#3759), later investigated further by Sahil Nayak
  • Daniel Lamping removed two dead XenServer job listings from the jobs page after their links started 404ing (ocaml/ocaml.org#3764)

    • Notable Discussions

  • On ocaml/opam-repository, repeated fast-iterating releases from Andreas Eldh's matcha package prompted Calascibetta Romain, Anil Madhavapeddy and Raphaël Proust to question whether a human was driving the account, citing the repository's contributor-accounts policy (ocaml/opam-repository#30617, ocaml/opam-repository#30623)
  • Anil Madhavapeddy raised similar authenticity concerns about shoopeur-eng's realdentalcosts submission, noting the submitting organisation was days old and spraying packages across repositories; the submitter withdrew (ocaml/opam-repository#30634)
  • Dmitrii Kosarev opened a discussion on whether packages with archived upstream repositories should themselves be archived in opam-repository (ocaml/opam-repository#30550)

    • OCaml Tools

    Dune moved dynamic actions onto RPC, opam shipped 2.6.0~beta2, ocaml-lsp merged 48 PRs, and odoc pursued OxCaml memory/disk work.

    New Features

  • ocaml/dune: dynamic actions (used by ppxs and dune ocaml top) now run dynamic-run requests over RPC instead of an ad hoc sandbox protocol, by Rudi Grinberg (ocaml/dune#16256), with follow-up fixes for deadlocks and missing dependencies (ocaml/dune#16340, ocaml/dune#16341, ocaml/dune#16342, ocaml/dune#16343, ocaml/dune#16344); this moves read_directory_with_glob from Dune_action_plugin.V1 to Dune_rpc_lwt.V1.Action_plugin, a breaking change for dynamic-action plugin code.
  • ocaml/dune: qualified module references are now supported in fields such as per_module under (include_subdirs qualified), by Antonio Nuno Monteiro (ocaml/dune#15633, fixes ocaml/dune#15578), plus a fix for nested qualified module groups (ocaml/dune#16322) and a clearer error hint for invalid dotted references (ocaml/dune#16152).
  • ocaml/dune: (env (env-vars ...)) in a dune-workspace (context ...) stanza now correctly takes precedence over the root env stanza, by Puneeth Chaganti (ocaml/dune#16290); a crash on non-boolean opam command filters was also fixed by art-w (ocaml/dune#16313).
  • ocaml/opam: opam 2.6.0~beta2 released by Kate (ocaml/opam#7115), bundling a fix for a pinning performance regression that recursively scanned entire project trees (including _build and .git), also improving opam update performance by roughly 8% (ocaml/opam#7101, fixes ocaml/opam#7098).
  • ocaml/opam: dependency lockfile upgraded (base64, spdx_licenses 3.28.0, menhir, patch, checkseum) and release builds bumped to OCaml 4.14.4 (ocaml/opam#7116); install scripts updated with SHA512 checksums for the 2.6.0~beta2 binaries (ocaml/opam#7119); conflicts field documentation corrected by Ryan Gibb (ocaml/opam#7082).
  • ocaml/ocaml-lsp: generated construct completions (match/function skeletons) are now interactive with tab stops for clients with snippet support, by Rudi Grinberg (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2198).
  • ocaml/ocaml-lsp: diagnostic locations derived from Merlin's formatted error messages are now converted to zero-based LSP line numbers, fixing relatedInformation ranges that pointed one line below the actual declaration (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2163, fixes ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2145); find references now honors the client's includeDeclaration flag (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2164); selection range and destruct-line case analysis gained several correctness fixes (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2061, ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2170, ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2194).
  • ocaml/odoc: a fix for OCaml 5.5 compatibility, correcting rendering of optional arguments wrapped in a TPoly constructor, was opened and merged by Jon Ludlam (ocaml/odoc#1489); payload compression on .odoc/.odocl files was proposed for a reported 4-5x size reduction (ocaml/odoc#1486).

    • OxCaml

    Atomic pointers, DWARF-5 debug info, and dependency vendoring landed in oxcaml/oxcaml, while opam-repository relaxed dune/eio/mdx guards.

    New Features

  • New atomic pointer primitives (%unsafe_atomic_load_ptr, %unsafe_atomic_set_ptr, %unsafe_atomic_exchange_ptr, %unsafe_atomic_cas_ptr, %unsafe_atomic_fetch_add_ptr) implemented by Joe Kerrigan in oxcaml/oxcaml#6747, with follow-ups avoiding an extra shift+tag on idx_atomic field access (oxcaml/oxcaml#6802) and relaxing the idx_atomic kind constraint (oxcaml/oxcaml#6831)
  • New -gdwarf-version <4|5> compiler flag for DWARF-5 output, added by Mark Shinwell in oxcaml/oxcaml#6923; cuts .debug_loc/.debug_ranges payload by roughly 26% on the compiler itself, building on compact DWARF forms for small constants and high PC offsets (oxcaml/oxcaml#6922)
  • [@@or_null] types now support GADTs, including a missing partial-match-warning fix, from Jules Jacobs and Nathanaëlle Courant (oxcaml/oxcaml#6981)
  • Constructors whose arguments are all-void can now be represented as statically-allocated block atoms without the [@immediate_all_void_constructor] attribute, by Ryan Tjoa (oxcaml/oxcaml#6880)
  • Fixed an allocation-pointer bug on stack overflow that could corrupt recently-allocated values, and a related C stack alignment bug that could crash in TCMalloc, both by Nick Barnes after production sightings (oxcaml/oxcaml#7020, oxcaml/oxcaml#7088)
  • ppxlib, sedlex, js_of_ocaml and ocaml-compiler-libs began being vendored directly into oxcaml/oxcaml as git subtrees and compiled in-tree rather than pulled from opam, by Robin Ricard (oxcaml/oxcaml#7011-oxcaml/oxcaml#7074 series)
  • In oxcaml/opam-repository, version guards on 24 oxcaml-* packages (dune, eio, mdx dependents) were narrowed so compatibility patches no longer apply once upstream dune >= 3.24.2, eio >= 1.4, or mdx >= 2.6.0 is installed, by Anil Madhavapeddy (oxcaml/opam-repository#59)
  • A wasm_of_ocaml runtime link failure under dune 3.24 (where %{deps} now expands paths with a leading ./) was fixed in runtime/wasm/args.ml, backported from ocsigen/jsofocaml#2371 and applied across wasm_of_ocaml-compiler 6.0.1+ox1, 6.0.1+ox2, and 6.3.2+ox, by Anil Madhavapeddy (oxcaml/opam-repository#59)

    • OCaml Core

    ocaml/ocaml shipped OCaml 5.5.1 with a Marshal overflow fix and merged Windows correctness and arm64/power codegen work; ocaml/RFCs had no activity.

    New Features

  • POWER assembler fix for stack frames whose offsets exceed a 16-bit signed immediate in loads, stores, addi, and li, by Tim McGilchrist (ocaml/ocaml#15021)
  • Native rounding instructions for Float.round, Float.trunc, ceil, and floor now emitted directly on arm64 and power instead of calling into C, by Zane Hambly (ocaml/ocaml#15017)
  • Two bugs fixed in the Win32 implementation of Unix.select that could return incorrect results or fail when the same file descriptor appeared more than once across the input lists, by Nicolás Ojeda Bär (ocaml/ocaml#15025)
  • Fixed a Windows thread-starvation bug where a thread that never yielded voluntarily could hold the runtime lock forever, blocking preemptive switching between systhreads, by Nicolás Ojeda Bär, reported by Daniel Larraz (ocaml/ocaml#15029, fixing ocaml/ocaml#15028, backported to trunk in ocaml/ocaml#15034)
  • Haiku/BeOS native-code backend activated, with Unix socket tests and single-threaded setlocale/signal handling, by Anarchos (ocaml/ocaml#14773)
  • Security fix: Marshal.data_size now guards against integer overflow when computing header_len + data_len, by Xavier Leroy (ocaml/ocaml#15030), shipped in the OCaml 5.5.1 release published this week
  • Fixed an uncaught Sys_error raised when flushing standard formatters at program exit, by Olivier Nicole, reported by Olivier Andrieu (ocaml/ocaml#15026, fixing ocaml/ocaml#14765)
  • Runtime_events.runtime_phase gained the missing EV_MINOR_EPHE_CLEAN constructor, and the EV_C_MINOR_ALLOCATED_WORDS counter now reports the correct unit, by Tim McGilchrist (ocaml/ocaml#14966, ocaml/ocaml#14969)

  • Architecture-specific native code generation continued to replace C fallbacks, spanning arm64/power rounding instructions (ocaml/ocaml#15017), the POWER frame-offset assembler fix (ocaml/ocaml#15021), and a bit-counting primitives proposal under design review (ocaml/ocaml#15018).
  • Five new unmerged PRs were opened, including a Weak.blit optimization (ocaml/ocaml#15033) and a GADT-equation fix in Translcore (ocaml/ocaml#15035).
