    • Emerging Trends

  • Architecture-specific native code generation keeps replacing calls into C, spanning arm64/power rounding instructions (ocaml/ocaml#15017), power fsqrt (ocaml/ocaml#15006), the POWER frame-offset assembler fix (ocaml/ocaml#15021), and the proposed bit-counting primitives (ocaml/ocaml#15018)
  • Integer-overflow hardening in low-level runtime paths continued, following the ring-buffer file-size fix (ocaml/ocaml#15000) with the Marshal.data_size overflow guard shipped in OCaml 5.5.1 (ocaml/ocaml#15030)
  • Windows platform work clustered this week, with two Win32-specific merges (ocaml/ocaml#15025, ocaml/ocaml#15029) and two fresh Windows-only reports opened in the same window (ocaml/ocaml#15040, ocaml/ocaml#15042)
  • CI platform tiering is an active theme, from enabling KVM for Android emulation (ocaml/ocaml#15003) to activating the Haiku native backend (ocaml/ocaml#14773) to debating whether to retire macOS x86_64 (ocaml/ocaml#15036)
  • ocaml/RFCs saw no recorded activity for the second consecutive week

    • Multicore

    Activity this week was confined to ocaml-multicore/eio: a new Process.Env API merged and Windows-parity fixes were opened.

    New Features

  • ocaml-multicore/eio: Added a new Eio.Process.Env module providing a typed representation of process environments (empty, of_bindings, get_opt, override, of_array, to_array), replacing the raw string array previously used by ?env on Process.spawn, Process.run and Process.parse_out (ocaml-multicore/eio#930) by Thomas Leonard
  • Process.Env performs case-insensitive name comparisons on Windows while preserving original case, following discussion between Thomas Leonard and Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#930)
  • Expanded process-spawning tests in tests/process.md, lib_eio_linux/tests/spawn.md and lib_eio_posix/test/spawn.md to exercise the new Env bindings API (ocaml-multicore/eio#930)

    • Overview

  • Of the nine repositories in the multicore group, only ocaml-multicore/eio recorded activity for week 36 (2026-08-31 to 2026-09-06); ocaml-multicore/domainslib, ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring, ocaml-multicore/meio, ocaml-multicore/saturn, ocaml-multicore/eio-trace, ocaml-multicore/picos, ocaml-multicore/kcas and ocaml-multicore/ocaml-iomux had no recorded changes
  • eio's week centered on merging a typed Eio.Process.Env API (ocaml-multicore/eio#930) and opening two Windows-parity items: an anonymous-pipe fix (ocaml-multicore/eio#929) and an NtCreateFile path-qualification bug report (ocaml-multicore/eio#931)
  • Design discussion continued on an Eio.Vars.t accessor for Stdenv that builds on the newly merged Process.Env (ocaml-multicore/eio#923)

    • Activity

  • Anil Madhavapeddy opened a draft PR fixing anonymous pipes on Windows after a transfer test case started failing with an Eio.Io exception, reproducing the failure in both CI and locally (ocaml-multicore/eio#929)
  • Kento Okura's PR adding Eio.Fiber.List.partition_map remains open, with Thomas Leonard suggesting the helper could instead live in the submitter's own code since Limiter isn't part of the public interface (ocaml-multicore/eio#927)
  • Patrick Ferris's PR adding Eio.Vars.t to Stdenv for reading environment variables without depending on Eio_unix continued extensive design discussion covering read-only vs. mutable environments, lazy evaluation under large environments (e.g. Nix), naming (get/get_opt/get_paths), and how it should build on Process.Env (ocaml-multicore/eio#923, building on ocaml-multicore/eio#930)
  • Kento Okura reported that NtCreateFile requires fully-qualified paths on Windows, causing Unix.ENOENT for relative-looking paths that Sys.file_exists reports as present; Thomas Leonard suggested adding absolute-path tests to lib_eio_windows/test/test_fs.ml, while Anil Madhavapeddy began investigating a fix involving symlink-following complexities (ocaml-multicore/eio#931)

    • Notable Discussions

  • Thomas Leonard, Anil Madhavapeddy and Patrick Ferris debated whether environment-variable name comparisons should be case-insensitive across all platforms versus only on Windows, settling on Windows-only case-insensitivity plus a convention of upper-case names (ocaml-multicore/eio#930)
  • Discussion on ocaml-multicore/eio#923 weighed use cases for mutating the global environment (subprocess inheritance, passing values within a process, interop with legacy Unix-based code) and concluded a read-only Stdenv.vars accessor layered on Process.Env covers most needs while avoiding Unix.putenv races

    • Emerging Trends

  • Windows compatibility remained the dominant theme in eio this week, spanning a path-qualification bug in NtCreateFile calls (ocaml-multicore/eio#931), an anonymous-pipe transfer failure (ocaml-multicore/eio#929), and case-insensitive environment-variable handling in Process.Env (ocaml-multicore/eio#930)
  • Environment-variable handling in eio is being layered incrementally: a low-level Process.Env type merged first (ocaml-multicore/eio#930), with a higher-level Eio.Vars.t read/write accessor for Stdenv still under discussion on top of it (ocaml-multicore/eio#923)
  • The other eight repositories in the group (domainslib, ocaml-uring, meio, saturn, eio-trace, picos, kcas, ocaml-iomux) had no recorded activity this week
entry.summary: OCaml 5.5.1 and opam 2.6.0~beta2 shipped alongside Dune's RPC-based dynamic actions, new oxcaml atomic pointers/DWARF-5, and eio's typed Process.Env.

entry.title: Week 35, 2026: Core fixed Marshal/runtime_events overflow bugs, OxCaml added idx_atomic ops, and tools shipped dune sandboxing hardening plus opam 2.6.0~beta1.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Core ocaml/ocaml closed an integer-overflow hole in Marshal.from_string/from_bytes's bounds check on untrusted data, validated with AFL fuzzing and backported to the 5.5 branch and 4.14 (ocaml/ocaml#15019, ocaml/ocaml#15030) by Xavier Leroy.
  • OCaml Core ocaml/ocaml widened the runtime_events ring buffer's size computation from int to size_t, fixing a SIGBUS/truncated-offset bug once the ring exceeds 2 GiB (ocaml/ocaml#15000) by Tim McGilchrist.
  • OxCaml oxcaml/oxcaml added new Idx_atomic operations (exchange, compare_and_set, fetch_and_add, and more) implementing the previously-missing idx_atomic primitives, by Joe Kerrigan (oxcaml/oxcaml#6743).
  • OxCaml oxcaml/oxcaml added a new -cfg-block-layout compiler flag for static CFG block-layout optimization, by Xavier Clerc (oxcaml/oxcaml#6918), and parsetree compiler hooks that let external tooling edit the AST before typing, by Stephen Dolan (oxcaml/oxcaml#6826).
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/dune gated a sandboxing hardening sweep behind Dune language 3.25/MDX 0.6, covering pkg-config, PPX lint, MDX, and Ctypes actions (ocaml/dune#16178, ocaml/dune#16176, ocaml/dune#16223), and removed the experimental (fdo ...) OCamlFDO integration as a breaking change (ocaml/dune#16198), mostly by Rudi Grinberg.
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/ocaml-lsp added ocp-indent as an alternative document/range formatter with config auto-discovery and textDocument/onTypeFormatting support via a new ocp-indent-rpc helper, by Rudi Grinberg (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2148, ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1986).
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/opam merged reproducible Windows release binaries (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0/LC_ALL=C) and a pinning-scan performance fix that avoids recursively scanning entire project directories, by Kate (ocaml/opam#7097, ocaml/opam#7101); the dev version was bumped to 2.6.0~beta1.
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/odoc now renders OxCaml mode annotations (@ local, @ unique, @ once) on values and arrow types, and fixed a crash compiling docs for packages like base on OxCaml, both by @art-w (ocaml/odoc#1454, ocaml/odoc#1466).
  • OCaml Ecosystem ocaml/opam-repository published opam 2.6.0~beta1 as eight packages by Kate (ocaml/opam-repository#30542), alongside mirage-crypto 2.4.1 (CCM/RSA/poly1305 fixes) and a coordinated Miou/mnet/Solo5 unikernel-stack release, all by Hannes Mehnert and Calascibetta Romain (ocaml/opam-repository#30568, ocaml/opam-repository#30582, ocaml/opam-repository#30581).
  • Multicore ocaml-multicore/eio merged a hand-written index.mld documentation landing page grouping the API by purpose, replacing the auto-generated odoc index, by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#926).
  • OCaml Ecosystem ocaml/ocaml.org hardened the planet feed scraper with a 30s fetch timeout (up from 3s), a descriptive User-Agent, and retries with exponential backoff, by Cuihtlauac Alvarado (ocaml/ocaml.org#3752); its weekly automated scraper build also published a new scraper-latest release (ocaml/ocaml.org releases).

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    Cuihtlauac Alvarado hardened ocaml.org planet-feed scraping while opam-repository shipped opam 2.6.0~beta1 and Miou/Solo5/mirage-crypto releases.

    New Features

  • ocaml/opam-repository: the opam 2.6.0~beta1 toolchain was published as eight packages by Kate (ocaml/opam-repository#30542)
  • ocaml/opam-repository: mirage-crypto 2.4.1 shipped CCM/RSA/poly1305 fixes and avoided reusing registered entropy sources, by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#30568)
  • ocaml/opam-repository: miou 0.9.0 fixed an assert false in Miou.Ownership.transfer and enforced ownership atomicity, and mnet 0.0.5 fixed double-close of TCP connections and IPv6 router selection, both by Calascibetta Romain (ocaml/opam-repository#30582, ocaml/opam-repository#30584)
  • ocaml/opam-repository: Solo5 0.13.0 fixed Alpine compilation, added a --no-net-ring memory-bounding option, and added riscv64 support for the spt target, by Calascibetta Romain (ocaml/opam-repository#30581)
  • ocaml/opam-repository: new packages cdp/cdp-gen (Chrome DevTools Protocol bindings) by Vitalii Shapoval (ocaml/opam-repository#30594), hpke (Hybrid Public Key Encryption) by Ville Vesilehto (ocaml/opam-repository#30590), and eio-based aws-eio, https-eio, kafka-eio clients by Logan B. Nielsen (ocaml/opam-repository#30589, ocaml/opam-repository#30570, ocaml/opam-repository#30557)
  • ocaml/opam-repository: conan 0.0.8 (content/mime-type analyzer) by Calascibetta Romain (ocaml/opam-repository#30565) and colibri2 0.6 SMT-LIB solver with soundness fixes by François Bobot (ocaml/opam-repository#30097)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: the planet feed scraper gained a 30s fetch timeout (up from 3s), a descriptive User-Agent, and retries with exponential backoff, reducing spurious scrape failures, by Cuihtlauac Alvarado (ocaml/ocaml.org#3752)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: dead planet sources ocaml-book and emilpriver marked disabled: true so they stop failing nightly scrapes, by Cuihtlauac Alvarado (ocaml/ocaml.org#3755)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: Dune 3.24.1 platform release changelog added by Ali Caglayan (ocaml/ocaml.org#3723), and the opam 2.5.2 release announcement added by Kate (ocaml/ocaml.org#3712)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/opam-repository merged opam 2.6.0~beta1 (ocaml/opam-repository#30542) plus coordinated MirageOS-stack releases (miou, mnet, Solo5, mirage-crypto) and a wave of new package submissions
  • ocaml/ocaml.org focused on planet aggregator reliability (timeouts, retries, dead-feed cleanup) driven by Cuihtlauac Alvarado (ocaml/ocaml.org#3752, ocaml/ocaml.org#3755), alongside Dune 3.24.1 and opam 2.5.2 platform release announcements (ocaml/ocaml.org#3723, ocaml/ocaml.org#3712)
  • Both repositories saw a new repository-level policy or process discussion: opam-repository debated requiring human review of automated-tooling package submissions (ocaml/opam-repository#30367), while ocaml.org resolved a multi-feed triage issue via direct author outreach (ocaml/ocaml.org#3753)

    • Activity

  • ocaml/opam-repository: Samuel Hym has an open PR teaching x-ci-accept-failures to Windows CI tests, aligning naming with setup-ocaml after feedback from Kate and Jan Midtgaard (ocaml/opam-repository#28856)
  • ocaml/opam-repository: Logan B. Nielsen opened two more obs-eio ecosystem packages (obs-prometheus-eio, obs-loki-eio) extending the Obs_eio.backend interface (ocaml/opam-repository#30596, ocaml/opam-repository#30597)
  • ocaml/opam-repository: Dmitrii Kosarev opened and merged a cluster of CI-driven constraint fixes surfaced by check.ci.ocaml.org, covering yojson-bench, guile, tplib, lambda-runtime, inquire, taglib, and qrencode (ocaml/opam-repository#30587, ocaml/opam-repository#30585, ocaml/opam-repository#30592)
  • ocaml/opam-repository: Fermin Reig normalized data-structures tag variants and added missing discoverability tags for the opam web UI (ocaml/opam-repository#30561)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: Cuihtlauac Alvarado opened an opt-in feed-repair PR pinning an unreleased river branch to work around the MirageOS feed's malformed HTML, but closed it unmerged after Hannes Mehnert reported the feed had already been fixed upstream by Reynir Björnsson in mirage/mirage-www#868 (ocaml/ocaml.org#3756)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: the automated [scrape] New OCaml Planet posts workflow continued weekly, pulling in new blog content while logging recurring scrape errors for several YouTube feeds and the still-unresolved dinosaure and patricoferris feeds (ocaml/ocaml.org#3750, ocaml/ocaml.org#3754)

    • Notable Discussions

  • ocaml/opam-repository: Calascibetta Romain proposed a policy requiring that, once a project is submitted via automated tooling such as opam-publish, all subsequent maintainer/release-manager responses come from a human, guarding against automated release-and-CI-fix loops; Marcello Seri agreed (ocaml/opam-repository#30367)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: on ocaml/ocaml.org#3753, Cuihtlauac Alvarado surveyed the authors of five failing planet feeds; John Whitington and Emil Priver confirmed their blogs are gone and can be delisted, while Hannes Mehnert clarified the MirageOS feed was valid Atom rejected only for unclosed tags, opening dbuenzli/cmarkit#32 upstream before it was fixed directly in mirage/mirage-www#868
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: Calascibetta Romain noted their blog.osau.re feed remains down pending a rewrite staged at dinosaure.github.io/blogger, suggesting the feed URL be updated once ready rather than disabled outright (ocaml/ocaml.org#3753)

    • Emerging Trends

  • The robur-coop MirageOS/unikernel stack (miou, mnet, Solo5, mirage-crypto) advanced together in opam-repository with coordinated bug-fix releases from Calascibetta Romain and Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#30582, ocaml/opam-repository#30584, ocaml/opam-repository#30581)
  • Growth in the eio-based ecosystem continued in opam-repository with Logan B. Nielsen publishing a family of obs-eio/aws-eio/https-eio/kafka-eio packages (ocaml/opam-repository#30589, ocaml/opam-repository#30570, ocaml/opam-repository#30557)
  • Across both repositories, maintainers favored conservative, source-scoped fixes and upstream coordination over broad changes: opam-repository's CI-driven constraint fixes targeted individual packages (ocaml/opam-repository#30587), and ocaml.org pushed a feed-parsing fix back to the MirageOS site generator rather than patching the scraper globally (ocaml/ocaml.org#3756)
  • The opam 2.6.0~beta1 package set landed in opam-repository ahead of a stable release (ocaml/opam-repository#30542), while ocaml.org published the opam 2.5.2 stable release announcement (ocaml/ocaml.org#3712), reflecting the two repositories' complementary roles in the opam release pipeline

    • OCaml Tools

    Dune shipped a sandboxing hardening sweep and RPC fixes, ocaml-lsp added ocp-indent support, and opam/odoc landed release and OxCaml fixes.

    New Features

  • ocaml/dune gated a sandboxing hardening sweep behind Dune language 3.25/MDX 0.6, covering pkg-config queries (ocaml/dune#16178), PPX lint actions (ocaml/dune#16176), MDX generator/dependency actions (ocaml/dune#16177, ocaml/dune#16183), and Ctypes stub/link actions (ocaml/dune#16223, ocaml/dune#16243); it also removed the experimental (fdo ...) OCamlFDO integration as a breaking change (ocaml/dune#16198), fixed RPC build requests in watch mode to no longer wait on unrelated concurrent builds (ocaml/dune#15191), and made portable lock directories select a single package version across all requested platforms (ocaml/dune#15982), all mostly by Rudi Grinberg
  • ocaml/ocaml-lsp added ocp-indent as an alternative document/range formatter with config auto-discovery (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2148) and implemented textDocument/onTypeFormatting via a new ocp-indent-rpc helper process (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1986), both by Rudi Grinberg
  • ocaml/opam merged reproducible Windows release binaries with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0/LC_ALL=C and a reproducibility check step, closing ocaml/opam#6752 (ocaml/opam#7097), a hardened release/ssh-auto.sh retry wrapper replacing raw sshpass calls (ocaml/opam#7096), and a pinning-scan performance fix that avoids recursively scanning entire project directories (ocaml/opam#7101), all by Kate; the dev version was bumped to 2.6.0~beta1
  • ocaml/odoc now renders OxCaml mode annotations (@ local, @ unique, @ once) on values and arrow types (ocaml/odoc#1454) and fixed a crash compiling docs for packages like base on OxCaml caused by with-bound expressions referencing arbitrary types (ocaml/odoc#1466), both by @art-w; odoc_driver's stdlib detection was fixed to support lib64/ install layouts (ocaml/odoc#1474 by @katrinafyi)
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml fixed Wasm asset resolution in the Node runtime to locate .wasm files relative to module.filename instead of require.main.filename, fixing lookups behind CLI wrappers, symlinks, and worker threads (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2389 by Jérôme Vouillon)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/dune landed a coordinated sandboxing hardening sweep gated to lang 3.25/MDX 0.6, removed experimental FDO support, and merged a batch of engine/RPC reliability fixes (ocaml/dune#16198, ocaml/dune#16267); Rudi Grinberg also pruned a cluster of long-dormant backlog PRs
  • ocaml/ocaml-lsp added ocp-indent as an alternative formatter with persistent on-type indentation (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2148, ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1986) and ran a sweep of fixes aligning client codecs with LSP 3.18's nullable/union result contracts, almost entirely authored by Rudi Grinberg
  • ocaml/opam merged release-hardening work — reproducible Windows binaries and a retrying SSH wrapper (ocaml/opam#7097, ocaml/opam#7096) — plus a pinning-scan performance fix (ocaml/opam#7101) and a 2.6.0~beta1 version bump, driven almost entirely by Kate with review from R. Boujbel
  • ocaml/odoc merged OxCaml mode-annotation rendering and a with-bounds crash fix (ocaml/odoc#1454, ocaml/odoc#1466), continuing the broader OxCaml-support tracking effort (ocaml/odoc#1411)
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml fixed Wasm asset resolution in the Node runtime (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2389) while seven PRs on Wasm sourcemaps, typed arrays, and CI remained open, alongside two large Claude-Code-assisted Web API binding PRs pending review (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2400, ocsigen/jsofocaml#2401)
  • ocaml/merlin saw a single PR fixing a false "already at definition point" result from locate (ocaml/merlin#2118 by @aryemans)
  • No recorded activity this week in ocaml/ocamlfind, ocaml/opam-file-format, or ocaml-dune/spawn

    • Activity

  • ocaml/dune: Ali Caglayan opened several package-management fixes still under review, covering findlib tool definitions, lock directory paths, and compiler package comparison (ocaml/dune#16239, ocaml/dune#16218, ocaml/dune#16173); Shon Feder merged a planning PR that broke a "discretionary tools" package-management feature into nine tracked design/implementation sub-issues (ocaml/dune#16043, ocaml/dune#16185-ocaml/dune#16196); Antonio Nuno Monteiro merged a long refactor series sharing code across the Melange, jsofocaml, opam, package, and preprocessing backends (ocaml/dune#16147-ocaml/dune#16165); Rudi Grinberg closed a cluster of long-dormant PRs as backlog cleanup, inviting reopening once work resumes
  • ocaml/opam: four new PRs opened by Kate, including a directory-scan follow-up (ocaml/opam#7106) and a proposed opam install --no-lint flag (ocaml/opam#7111); ongoing performance work on the opam show/cache path continued on ocaml/opam#7100, with Kate and Török Edwin discussing Marshal.from_channel memory growth
  • ocaml/odoc: include functor rendering (ocaml/odoc#1452) and OxCaml kind-abbreviation support (ocaml/odoc#1467) remained under active review; a Forward-constructor dead-code removal (ocaml/odoc#1478) and an id-wrapper simplification cutting output size ~30% (ocaml/odoc#1479) were opened, while a Stdlib-polyfill proposal was closed as not worth the added uncertainty (ocaml/odoc#1476)
  • ocaml/ocaml-lsp: a test-then-fix pattern dominated the week — regression tests merged first, immediately followed by fixes — covering trailing-newline edit ranges (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2158 → ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2159) and out-of-range inlay hints (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2039 → ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2155); a record-pun rename corruption bug was exposed by a merged regression test and intentionally left unfixed (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2040); an automated flake.lock update PR remained the only PR open at week's end (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2144)
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml: seven PRs opened by Jérôme Vouillon covering Windows sourcemap detection (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2418), per-function sourcemap mappings (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2417), BOM preservation (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2414), and typed array constructors (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2416), plus continued consolidation of the Wasm runtime to a single linear memory for Safari compatibility (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2405); Hugo Heuzard has two large Web API binding PRs pending review (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2400, ocsigen/jsofocaml#2401) and merged a stdlib 5.6 test-snapshot refresh (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2412)
  • ocaml/merlin: @aryemans fixed locate returning a false already-at-definition result, adding a regression test covering both value and type declarations (ocaml/merlin#2118, fixing ocaml/merlin#2033)

    • Notable Discussions

  • On ocaml/dune ocaml/dune#15381 (narrowing binary lookups to declared dependencies), Ali Caglayan repeatedly pressed Puneeth Chaganti to clarify which test demonstrated the narrowing behavior, leading to revised prose and an improved test
  • On ocaml/dune ocaml/dune#13758 (preserving multi-line strings when formatting), Rudi Grinberg questioned why the parser only produces the new constructor for the CST rather than the AST; Ali Caglayan explained the AST change would require touching more consumers, leaving the PR unfinished
  • On ocaml/opam ocaml/opam#7103, Hannes Mehnert reported that OpamFilename.in_dir, used by the orb reproducible-build tool, was removed in 2.6.0~beta1; Kate provided a three-line Unix.chdir/Fun.protect replacement
  • On ocaml/odoc ocaml/odoc#1452, Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac prototyped an alternative "alias desugaring" approach for rendering include functor, questioning the current DUMMY__ module approach's functor-argument substitution
  • On ocaml/odoc ocaml/odoc#1476, Daniel Bünzli and @art-w discussed the tradeoffs of relying on Stdlib polyfills versus maintaining odoc's own implementations, concluding the refactor wasn't worth the added uncertainty

    • Emerging Trends

  • A parallel hardening push across repos: dune gated build-action sandboxing behind lang 3.25 (ocaml/dune#16176, ocaml/dune#16223) while opam hardened its release process with reproducible builds and retrying SSH tooling (ocaml/opam#7097, ocaml/opam#7096)
  • OxCaml compatibility churn recurred across repos, with odoc merging mode-annotation rendering and compiler-version compatibility fixes (ocaml/odoc#1454, ocaml/odoc#1469) the same week dune fixed OxCaml-related Odoc generation (ocaml/dune#16200)
  • AI/LLM-assisted contributions surfaced across the group: jsofocaml's large Web API binding PRs are tagged "🤖 Generated with Claude Code" (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2400, ocsigen/jsofocaml#2401), and dune's Jan-Oliver Kaiser cited ongoing large-scale LLM-assisted code changes at their organization as motivation for an experimental scheduler (ocaml/dune#15991)
  • A test-first workflow was prominent in both dune (regression tests backing engine/RPC fixes, ocaml/dune#16244-ocaml/dune#16260) and ocaml-lsp (dedicated bug-reproduction PRs merged before their fixes, e.g. ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2158 → ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2159)
  • Design-first planning continued in dune's package management, with a single planning PR spawning nine tracked design/implementation sub-issues for a new "discretionary tools" stanza feature (ocaml/dune#16043, ocaml/dune#16185-ocaml/dune#16196)

    • OxCaml

    oxcaml/oxcaml added idx_atomic ops and a CFG block-layout pass while advancing mode-system, DWARF-5, and in-tree Merlin integration work.

    New Features

  • New atomic operations (exchange, compare_and_set, compare_exchange, fetch_and_add, add, sub, logand, and more) added to Stdlib_stable.Idx_atomic, implementing the previously-missing idx_atomic primitives by Joe Kerrigan (oxcaml/oxcaml#6743), building on a cleanup of the %atomic_load_idx/%atomic_set_idx lowering (oxcaml/oxcaml#6746)
  • New -cfg-block-layout compiler flag adding a static CFG block-layout optimization pass by Xavier Clerc (oxcaml/oxcaml#6918)
  • Recursive uses are now permitted within non-value fields of mixed blocks, relaxing a restriction for unboxed types code by Ryan Tjoa (oxcaml/oxcaml#6847)
  • Parsetree compiler hooks can now edit the AST, letting external tooling transform the parse tree before typing runs, by Stephen Dolan (oxcaml/oxcaml#6826)
  • Mode-implication inference improved for functor arguments/returns and external declarations by @dkalinichenko-js (oxcaml/oxcaml#6745)
  • Continued build-out of the mode-variable-levels infrastructure covering update-level, generalize, copy, locality alloc_mode, and comonadic curry mode by @ainageorges (oxcaml/oxcaml#5478, oxcaml/oxcaml#6966)
  • Fixed a memory leak from tail-calling a local-returning function by @ainageorges (oxcaml/oxcaml#6396)
  • Fixed continuations being invoked with invalid kinds in from_lambda, a Flambda2 bug, by Nathanaëlle Courant (oxcaml/oxcaml#6291)
  • Fixed young effect handlers being forgotten between update/continue by Max Slater (oxcaml/oxcaml#6768)
  • Reduced CAML_GC_MESSAGE overhead and many-domain CPU overhead by Nick Barnes (oxcaml/oxcaml#6888), plus smaller minor-GC tables and a simplified "reserve" algorithm (oxcaml/oxcaml#6840)
  • Faster compilation of encode_instruction.ml by flipping a match's argument order by Stephen Dolan (oxcaml/oxcaml#6936)
  • Fixed caching of DWARF type DIEs, cutting redundant debug-info generation, by Mark Shinwell (oxcaml/oxcaml#6916), and DIEs for the immediate-or-pointer discriminant enum are now shared per compilation unit (oxcaml/oxcaml#6945)
  • Fixed incorrect DWARF file paths by Kevin Svetlitski (oxcaml/oxcaml#6882)
  • Documentation for mode implications rewritten to distinguish "fixed" sites (where every axis must be pinned) from "flexible" sites (where only written axes are constrained), alongside the inference fix by @dkalinichenko-js (oxcaml/oxcaml#6745)

    • Overview

  • This week's recorded activity across the oxcaml group was concentrated almost entirely in oxcaml/oxcaml; no issue or PR activity was recorded in oxcaml/opam-repository, oxcaml/merlin, oxcaml/jsofocaml, or janestreet/opam-repository
  • New atomic idx_atomic operations landed in Stdlib_stable.Idx_atomic (oxcaml/oxcaml#6743), alongside a new -cfg-block-layout optimization pass (oxcaml/oxcaml#6918) and relaxed recursion rules for non-value mixed-block fields (oxcaml/oxcaml#6847)
  • The bulk of open-PR activity centered on four large, multi-PR efforts: importing Merlin diagnostics into the compiler (oxcaml/oxcaml#6891 and related PRs), DWARF-5 support (oxcaml/oxcaml#6926 and related PRs), link-time optimization via Reaper/.ltosol (oxcaml/oxcaml#6895 and related PRs), and the functorize/parameterized-libraries project (oxcaml/oxcaml#6917 and related PRs)
  • The long-running mode-system stacked series from @ainageorges continued to merge incrementally (oxcaml/oxcaml#5478, oxcaml/oxcaml#6966)

    • Activity

  • Gavin Gray opened a series of PRs importing structured-diagnostics and provenance information from Merlin into the compiler frontend, covering uniqueness errors, modality implications, and function-argument provenance (oxcaml/oxcaml#6891, oxcaml/oxcaml#6892, oxcaml/oxcaml#6893, oxcaml/oxcaml#6896, oxcaml/oxcaml#6897, oxcaml/oxcaml#6900, oxcaml/oxcaml#6901, oxcaml/oxcaml#6941), also opening tooling PRs to expose module-type information and a module-type-impls query for compiler artifacts (oxcaml/oxcaml#6801, oxcaml/oxcaml#6811)
  • Mark Shinwell opened a run of DWARF-5 PRs including base-address/offset-pair location and range lists (oxcaml/oxcaml#6926), LLDB DWARF-5 test variants (oxcaml/oxcaml#6957), a selectable -gdwarf-version flag (oxcaml/oxcaml#6923), optional DWARF-4 type units in .debug_types (oxcaml/oxcaml#6920), and enabling --enable-oxcaml-dwarf-on-compiler by default (oxcaml/oxcaml#6911), plus a fix for unit# and unboxed-type DWARF shapes (oxcaml/oxcaml#6969)
  • Miriam Vellacott opened further link-time optimization PRs to store Reaper solutions in .ltosol files and rebuild from them (oxcaml/oxcaml#6895, oxcaml/oxcaml#6964) and to load .reaped.cmx files during -reaper-rebuild (oxcaml/oxcaml#6965), following merged work on .ltosol file writing (oxcaml/oxcaml#6752) and naive dependency-graph merging (oxcaml/oxcaml#6731)
  • Zesen Qian opened several functorize/parameterized-libraries PRs deriving block formats from .cmi coercions, fixing argument-block projection on mixed module blocks, and checking arg_param during projection (oxcaml/oxcaml#6917, oxcaml/oxcaml#6912, oxcaml/oxcaml#6925, oxcaml/oxcaml#6924), plus lazy loading of hidden manifests in the load path (oxcaml/oxcaml#6951) and a magic-number bump for ox6 that merged this week (oxcaml/oxcaml#6906)
  • Liam Stevenson opened PRs vendoring csexp and yojson and including the Merlin libraries in the install, continuing the in-tree Merlin effort (oxcaml/oxcaml#6938, oxcaml/oxcaml#6939, oxcaml/oxcaml#6954), and merged a fix for Merlin jump-to-definition in the compiler frontend (oxcaml/oxcaml#6932) and a CI check for committed ignored files (oxcaml/oxcaml#6546)
  • Xavier Clerc opened jump-table support for unboxed values in pattern matching, an AFL-based fuzzer for CFG dominators, and a [@table] attribute forcing jump-table dispatch (oxcaml/oxcaml#6963, oxcaml/oxcaml#6930, oxcaml/oxcaml#6887), while merging CFG configuration-compatibility checks and frame/prologue-decision storage (oxcaml/oxcaml#6907, oxcaml/oxcaml#6324)
  • Ryan Tjoa opened Box kinds, a new kind constructor for the boxed version of a kind (oxcaml/oxcaml#6956), plus PRs making non-scanned layouts cross externality inherently rather than syntactically and moving any-fields to stable (oxcaml/oxcaml#6973, oxcaml/oxcaml#6970)
  • Robin Ricard opened a PR importing the full upstream js_of_ocaml history into external/js_of_ocaml as a subtree merge, in preparation for integrating OxCaml patches on top of it (oxcaml/oxcaml#6968)
  • @hwasilewskijs opened a fuzzer MVP containing a random program generator for a small subset of OxCaml (oxcaml/oxcaml#6933)
  • Joe Kerrigan opened a PR adding atomic ext_ptr support and removing a caml_domain_alone optimization from user atomics (oxcaml/oxcaml#6937)
  • Additional merged infrastructure work included the Claude Code CI integration and PR-secrets deployment environments by Jacob Van Buren (oxcaml/oxcaml#6415, oxcaml/oxcaml#6441) and a broadened tool allowlist (oxcaml/oxcaml#6958), a dependency bump for GitHub Actions (oxcaml/oxcaml#6819), and build cleanups such as untangling the CamlinternalQuote build and avoiding building ocamlj during boot-compiler by Stephen Dolan (oxcaml/oxcaml#6928, oxcaml/oxcaml#6929)
  • Several draft or exploratory PRs were closed without merging as the underlying work was superseded, including early structured-diagnostics drafts by Gavin Gray (oxcaml/oxcaml#6818, oxcaml/oxcaml#6890, oxcaml/oxcaml#6898, oxcaml/oxcaml#6899, oxcaml/oxcaml#6878), dynamic-binding prototypes by Max Slater (oxcaml/oxcaml#6709, oxcaml/oxcaml#6710, oxcaml/oxcaml#6711), and a draft mode-error-hints PR and -nondep flag exploration by Zesen Qian (oxcaml/oxcaml#4686, oxcaml/oxcaml#6229)

    • Notable Discussions

  • Extended review discussion on Addressable kinds between Ryan Tjoa and Jakub Bachurski covering the Le_result design and constrain_*_addressable helpers, working through several rounds to keep the core lattice logic clean (oxcaml/oxcaml#6712)
  • Review of Middle modality mode crossing with input from Jules Jacobs (oxcaml/oxcaml#6272)
  • Marek Kubica reported unexpected typing of include functor applications inside signature contexts, and Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac followed up showing the same surprising behavior arises more generally from functors and module aliases, not just include functor (oxcaml/oxcaml#6931)
  • Detailed review threads on exposing module-type information for compiler artifacts and a new module-type-impls query, both opened by Gavin Gray as part of the Merlin-integration effort (oxcaml/oxcaml#6801, oxcaml/oxcaml#6811)
  • Review discussion on the DWARF-5 base-address/offset-pair location-list encoding and on DWARF type-DIE caching, both from Mark Shinwell (oxcaml/oxcaml#6926, oxcaml/oxcaml#6916)

    • Emerging Trends

  • The mode system continues to receive sustained, incremental investment through a long stacked-PR series from @ainageorges (update level, generalize, copy, locality alloc_mode, comonadic curry mode) (oxcaml/oxcaml#5478, oxcaml/oxcaml#5479, oxcaml/oxcaml#5480, oxcaml/oxcaml#5481, oxcaml/oxcaml#5482, oxcaml/oxcaml#6249, oxcaml/oxcaml#6279, oxcaml/oxcaml#6572, oxcaml/oxcaml#6966) alongside inference improvements from @dkalinichenko-js (oxcaml/oxcaml#6745)
  • DWARF debug-info quality is a recurring focus, with Mark Shinwell driving a long series toward DWARF-5 support and reduced debug-info size (oxcaml/oxcaml#6916, oxcaml/oxcaml#6945, oxcaml/oxcaml#6517, oxcaml/oxcaml#6915, oxcaml/oxcaml#6926, oxcaml/oxcaml#6957, oxcaml/oxcaml#6923, oxcaml/oxcaml#6920, oxcaml/oxcaml#6911) plus fixes from Kevin Svetlitski (oxcaml/oxcaml#6882)
  • Bringing Merlin in-tree is an active theme: Gavin Gray is importing structured-diagnostics and provenance features from Merlin into the compiler (oxcaml/oxcaml#6891-oxcaml/oxcaml#6941), while Liam Stevenson is vendoring Merlin's dependencies and adjusting its install footprint (oxcaml/oxcaml#6938, oxcaml/oxcaml#6939, oxcaml/oxcaml#6954, oxcaml/oxcaml#6932)
  • The link-time optimization subsystem is under active construction by Miriam Vellacott, progressing from dependency-graph merging to .ltosol solution files and Reaper-solution rebuilds (oxcaml/oxcaml#6731, oxcaml/oxcaml#6752, oxcaml/oxcaml#6895, oxcaml/oxcaml#6964, oxcaml/oxcaml#6965)
  • Growing use of AI-assisted contributions is visible from several PRs labeled "100% vibe" this week (oxcaml/oxcaml#6879, oxcaml/oxcaml#6922, oxcaml/oxcaml#6908, oxcaml/oxcaml#6962, oxcaml/oxcaml#6945, oxcaml/oxcaml#6958, oxcaml/oxcaml#6918), alongside new Claude Code CI integration set up by Jacob Van Buren (oxcaml/oxcaml#6415, oxcaml/oxcaml#6441, oxcaml/oxcaml#6958)
  • Recorded activity across the group remained concentrated in oxcaml/oxcaml this week, with no tracked issues or PRs in oxcaml/opam-repository, oxcaml/merlin, oxcaml/jsofocaml, or janestreet/opam-repository

    • OCaml Core

    ocaml/ocaml merged Marshal and runtime_events overflow fixes and fixed Windows regressions; ocaml/RFCs had no activity this week.

    New Features

  • Marshal.from_string/from_bytes gained a guard against integer overflow when computing header_len + data_len from untrusted marshaled data, which could previously make bounds checks ineffective (ocaml/ocaml#15019) by Xavier Leroy, reviewed by Nicolás Ojeda Bär and Antonin Décimo; validated with roughly 2 hours of AFL fuzzing that reproduced a crash on trunk and found none with the fix. The fix was also cherry-picked to the 5.5 branch and backported to 4.14 (ocaml/ocaml#15030).
  • The runtime_events ring buffer's total size computation was changed from int to size_t, fixing an overflow that could SIGBUS the producer or silently write custom-event registrations through a truncated offset once the ring exceeded 2 GiB (OCAMLRUNPARAM=e=21 and above) (ocaml/ocaml#15000, fixes ocaml/ocaml#14999) by Tim McGilchrist, reviewed by Sadiq Jaffer.
  • Utf8_lexeme was extracted out of the Misc module into its own utils/utf8_lexeme.ml(i) files, so tools that vendor the parser no longer need to pull in all of misc.ml to get UTF-8 lexeme handling (ocaml/ocaml#15023) by Thomas Refis, reviewed by Nicolás Ojeda Bär.
  • AI.md gained a new "Guidelines relevant to AI-assisted bug reports" section advising against mixing LLM-generated content into bug reports and cautioning about LLM-shrunk reproduction cases (ocaml/ocaml#14899) by Florian Angeletti.

    • Overview

  • ocaml/ocaml merged overflow-guard fixes for Marshal unmarshaling (ocaml/ocaml#15019) and the runtime_events ring buffer (ocaml/ocaml#15000), alongside Windows-specific regression fixes for Unix.select (ocaml/ocaml#15025) and thread scheduling (ocaml/ocaml#15029).
  • POWER/arm64 codegen work (ocaml/ocaml#15017, ocaml/ocaml#15018, ocaml/ocaml#15021) and several longer-running language-design proposals — nested record fields (ocaml/ocaml#14527), implicit source positions (ocaml/ocaml#13886), link-time linking (ocaml/ocaml#14895), and relocatable cross compilers (ocaml/ocaml#14929) — continued under review in ocaml/ocaml.
  • ocaml/RFCs had no recorded issue or pull-request activity during this week.

    • Activity

  • Two Windows-specific bug fixes were opened and merged just after the week's end: a fix for Unix.select mapping polling results to the wrong file descriptor when a socket appears in multiple lists or a list has duplicates (ocaml/ocaml#15025, fixes ocaml/ocaml#14758), and a fix for a 5.5.0 regression where a thread that never yields starves other threads of its domain, caused by an invalid backup-thread handle after CloseHandle (ocaml/ocaml#15029, fixes ocaml/ocaml#15028) — both by Nicolás Ojeda Bär, with the thread fix confirmed on Windows CI by Daniel Larraz.
  • POWER and arm64 codegen work continued: a fix for assembler errors when frame-management offsets exceed the 16-bit immediate field on POWER (ocaml/ocaml#15021) by Tim McGilchrist, and native rounding instructions for Float.round, Float.trunc, ceil and floor on arm64 and power (ocaml/ocaml#15017) by Zane Hambly — both opened before and merged just after this week.
  • Format.flush_standard_formatters was opened for changes to silence Sys_error, matching Stdlib.flush_all's existing behaviour and fixing an uncaught exception at exit when stdout is a closed pipe (ocaml/ocaml#15026, fixes ocaml/ocaml#14765) by Olivier Nicole, reviewed by Gabriel Scherer.
  • The GitHub issue template was updated to discourage posting AI-generated text in bug reports, linking to the new AI.md guidance (ocaml/ocaml#15031) by Gabriel Scherer, following the discussion on ocaml/ocaml#14899.
  • Int.popcount, leading_zeros and trailing_zeros gained %popcount, %clz and %ctz primitives with arm64 code generation for clz/ctz (popcount stays a C call pending SIMD-only cnt), measured at roughly 2x faster for leading_zeros/trailing_zeros on an X-Gene (ocaml/ocaml#15018, draft) opened by Zane Hambly, building on the pure-OCaml versions added in ocaml/ocaml#14433.
  • Romain Beauxis opened a PR adding global-roots debugging support: an XOR-stamped pointer check plus a provenance skiplist recording where each root was registered, exposed through a new ocaml roots gdb command and a Gc.check_roots function, currently gated behind DEBUG (ocaml/ocaml#15027).
  • Vincent Laviron opened a fix for the ocamldebug protocol clamping remote object headers to 32 bits, sending the full 64-bit header on request following Xavier Leroy's suggestion (ocaml/ocaml#15022, fixes ocaml/ocaml#15012).
  • Ongoing runtime_events reliability work continued from Tim McGilchrist: a consumer-side "corrupt stream" fix plus a producer-side memory-ordering fence addressing intermittent test-suite failures under small ring buffers (ocaml/ocaml#15016, fixes ocaml/ocaml#14151), and a proposal to widen the lost_words counter from int to uint64_t so it no longer wraps once more than 2^31 events are lost (ocaml/ocaml#15010).
  • Longer-running proposals saw continued review: nested/inline record fields for record types (ocaml/ocaml#14527) by David Sancho, the implicit source positions RFC (ocaml/ocaml#13886) by Olivier Nicole, link-time linking (ocaml/ocaml#14895) by Raphaël Proust, and relocatable cross compilers (ocaml/ocaml#14929) by @shym.

    • Notable Discussions

  • Repeated friction over LLM-generated content in issue reports: Gabriel Scherer asked whether Nikos Gorogiannis's detailed runtime-event-spam report was LLM-drafted (ocaml/ocaml#15024), and Daniel Larraz's thread-starvation report and follow-up comments (ocaml/ocaml#15028, ocaml/ocaml#15029) drew a direct request from Nicolás Ojeda Bär to stop posting raw LLM output, which fed into merging ocaml/ocaml#14899 and the follow-up issue-template change (ocaml/ocaml#15031).
  • On ocaml/ocaml#14977, exposing that Atomic.t is not a float in the interface, Gabriel Scherer and Daniel Bünzli discussed keeping the type abstract via a possible [@@not_float] attribute versus a @deprecated-field workaround that Daniel Bünzli proposed and Török Edwin implemented.
  • On ocaml/ocaml#15022, Xavier Leroy and Vincent Laviron discussed backward compatibility for the ocamldebug wire protocol and byte order for the new full-header encoding.

    • Emerging Trends

  • Runtime-events reliability received sustained attention, with overflow and corruption fixes/proposals spanning this week and last (ocaml/ocaml#15000, ocaml/ocaml#15016, ocaml/ocaml#15010) plus a new spam report (ocaml/ocaml#15024), mostly driven by Tim McGilchrist.
  • Architecture-specific codegen work kept expanding primitive support on arm64 and power, covering float rounding (ocaml/ocaml#15017), bit-counting primitives (ocaml/ocaml#15018), and a POWER assembler-offset fix (ocaml/ocaml#15021), largely from Zane Hambly and Tim McGilchrist.
  • Windows support saw two distinct regression fixes land for Unix.select (ocaml/ocaml#15025) and thread scheduling (ocaml/ocaml#15029), both from Nicolás Ojeda Bär.
  • Maintainers are actively formalizing pushback on AI-generated content in issue reports, via the new AI.md guidelines (ocaml/ocaml#14899) and the issue template change (ocaml/ocaml#15031).

    • Multicore

    Eio merged a curated documentation index and reviewed proposals for chown id validation and a concurrent partition_map helper; the other eight repos were quiet.

    New Features

  • ocaml-multicore/eio: added a hand-written documentation index page grouping the API by purpose (fibers/switches/cancellation, host resources, files, networking, time, concurrency primitives, collections, domains, exceptions, and private/backend-only modules), replacing the default auto-generated odoc index, merged by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#926)

    • Overview

  • Only one of the nine group repositories had recorded activity this week — ocaml-multicore/eio; ocaml-multicore/domainslib, ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring, ocaml-multicore/meio, ocaml-multicore/saturn, ocaml-multicore/eio-trace, ocaml-multicore/picos, ocaml-multicore/kcas, and ocaml-multicore/ocaml-iomux had no recorded activity in this period
  • ocaml-multicore/eio merged a curated index.mld documentation landing page, replacing the auto-generated odoc index (ocaml-multicore/eio#926)
  • Two eio PRs remained open under review: a chown uid/gid range check (ocaml-multicore/eio#928) and a Fiber.List.partition_map proposal whose concurrency implementation was questioned (ocaml-multicore/eio#927)

    • Activity

  • Anil Madhavapeddy opened a PR to reject out-of-range chown uid/gid values in eio_unix while still allowing -1 to mean "leave unchanged", per POSIX semantics (ocaml-multicore/eio#928); Thomas Leonard questioned whether the kernel already validates this and noted uid_t is unsigned on Linux, and Anil Madhavapeddy argued a portable-layer check is still prudent given uid_t/gid_t signedness varies across platforms, citing python/cpython#46289
  • Kento Okura's proposal to add Eio.Fiber.List.partition_map to ocaml-multicore/eio remained open for review (ocaml-multicore/eio#927); Anil Madhavapeddy and Thomas Leonard noted the fork-then-immediately-wait pattern in the initial implementation was not actually concurrent, and suggested a simpler one-liner built on the existing map function instead

    • Notable Discussions

  • On ocaml-multicore/eio#927, Anil Madhavapeddy and Thomas Leonard identified that forking a fiber and immediately waiting on it does not provide real concurrency, using the test output as evidence, and recommended a simpler List.partition_map Fun.id (map ?max_fibers fn items) implementation as a starting point
  • On ocaml-multicore/eio#928, Thomas Leonard raised whether kernel-side checks make an explicit uid/gid range check redundant and noted uid_t's unsigned representation on Linux, prompting Anil Madhavapeddy to explain the cross-platform signedness rationale for validating in the portable layer, drawing a parallel to python/cpython#46289

    • Emerging Trends

  • Reviewers in ocaml-multicore/eio are pushing back on complexity in new concurrency helpers, preferring simple compositions of existing primitives (e.g. building partition_map from map) unless a performance need is demonstrated (ocaml-multicore/eio#927)
  • Continued attention to portability edge cases in the eio_unix POSIX bindings, including signedness differences in system types across platforms (ocaml-multicore/eio#928)
  • Investment in documentation discoverability continued in ocaml-multicore/eio with a curated API index replacing auto-generated docs (ocaml-multicore/eio#926)
  • Eight of the nine group repositories recorded no activity this week, concentrating all visible work in ocaml-multicore/eio
entry.summary: Core fixed Marshal/runtime_events overflow bugs, OxCaml added idx_atomic ops, and tools shipped dune sandboxing hardening plus opam 2.6.0~beta1.

entry.title: Week 34, 2026: Eio 1.5 and opam 2.6.0~beta1 shipped, ocaml/ocaml gained native FMA/sqrt codegen, and opam-repository merged cohttp/mirage-crypto security fixes.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • Multicore ocaml-multicore/eio released Eio 1.5 (ocaml-multicore/eio#924), bundling pre-connect socket options on Eio.Net.connect via ?bind_to/?options (ocaml-multicore/eio#875) by Anil Madhavapeddy building on @art-w's draft, Windows path support, and an opam available-constraint fix by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#921).
  • Multicore ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring added Iovec.to_bigarray, a zero-copy Bigarray.Array1.t alias over the library's new bytes-backed buffers, part of its ongoing migration off bigarray/cstruct (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153).
  • OCaml Core ocaml/ocaml added Sys.filepath_exists, a stricter alternative to Sys.file_exists that reports permission and other system errors via Sys_error instead of silently returning false (ocaml/ocaml#14974) by Khalid.
  • OCaml Core ocaml/ocaml gained native codegen for FMA, square root and byte swap on arm64, power, riscv and s390x instead of C fallbacks, driven by Zane Hambly (ocaml/ocaml#15008, ocaml/ocaml#15002, ocaml/ocaml#15005); 32-bit builds now default to large-file and year-2038-safe time_t support (ocaml/ocaml#14997) by Antonin Décimo.
  • OxCaml oxcaml/oxcaml added a runtime API for heap extensions (caml_add_extent) letting embedders register externally-allocated GC-scannable memory, by Nick Barnes (oxcaml/oxcaml#6248), reduced native-code frame table size via de-duplicated debuginfo and bitmap encoding, also by Barnes (oxcaml/oxcaml#6399), and fixed a stack-growth use-after-free in caml_tick_fiber_res by Max Slater (oxcaml/oxcaml#6764).
  • OxCaml oxcaml/oxcaml flipped the default shape format to Debugging_shapes and added -gupstream-dwarf fidelity flags by Simon Spies (oxcaml/oxcaml#5103), and made DW_AT_call_{file,line,column} report the call site for inlined calls, by Kevin Svetlitski (oxcaml/oxcaml#6877); Merlin gained destruct support for unboxed tuples by Liam Stevenson (oxcaml/oxcaml#6849).
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/opam released 2.6.0~beta1 (ocaml/opam#7095) by Kate, bundling switch-list repair on opam init --reinit and git gc.autoDetach/maintenance.autoDetach hardening to avoid a race with opam's own directory removal (ocaml/opam#7073).
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/dune added the dune ocaml inferred-mli MODULE command (ocaml/dune#16111) and Linux Landlock sandboxing for sandboxed actions (ocaml/dune#15858), both by Rudi Grinberg; a breaking change now disallows : in context names for Windows/Cygwin path portability (ocaml/dune#16085).
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/merlin's destruct command can now generate case splits directly on a let-binding's pattern, previously only possible inside match expressions, by Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac (ocaml/merlin#2117).
  • OCaml Ecosystem ocaml/opam-repository merged cohttp 6.3.0, fixing a path-traversal vulnerability in Cohttp.Path.resolve_local_file (ocaml/opam-repository#30528), and mirage-crypto 2.4.0, fixing a timing leak in elliptic-curve lookup tables (OSEC-2026-17) (ocaml/opam-repository#30507), both by Hannes Mehnert for the latter and Anil Madhavapeddy for the former.
  • OCaml Ecosystem ocaml/ocaml.org added mdx-based automatic testing of tutorial code blocks, wiring a test_code_examples Makefile target into CI across 14 tutorials, by Yassine Haouzane, extended by Cuihtlauac Alvarado (ocaml/ocaml.org#3622).

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    Security fixes in cohttp, eio and mirage-crypto shipped in opam-repository, while ocaml.org added mdx-tested tutorial code blocks.

    New Features

  • cohttp 6.3.0 fixes a path-traversal vulnerability in Cohttp.Path.resolve_local_file and adds Cohttp.Path.normalise for safe access-control checks, by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml/opam-repository#30528)
  • mirage-crypto 2.4.0 fixes a timing leak in elliptic-curve lookup tables (OSEC-2026-17) and a hardcoded Diffie-Hellman group, by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#30507)
  • eio 1.5 adds Windows path support to Eio.Path.t, pre-connect socket options on Eio.Net.connect, and Eio.Path.of_dir, by Thomas Leonard and Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml/opam-repository#30518)
  • prometheus 2.0 splits the client into prometheus-eio and a cohttp-free prometheus-reporter, removing Lwt from the core registry, by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml/opam-repository#30535)
  • cascade 1.1.0 ships breaking CSS-engine changes including stricter Css.hex parsing and corrected cascade-layer handling, by Thomas Gazagnaire (ocaml/opam-repository#30524)
  • New opam packages this week include fuse3 FUSE bindings by Alessandro Strada (ocaml/opam-repository#30547), ascon, a dependency-free NIST Ascon AEAD/hash implementation, by Ville Vesilehto (ocaml/opam-repository#30549), and rpmfile/bytream by Михаил (ocaml/opam-repository#30533, ocaml/opam-repository#30534)
  • ocaml.org added mdx-based automatic testing of code blocks in tutorials and exercises, wiring a test_code_examples Makefile target into CI across 14 tutorials, by Yassine Haouzane, extended by Cuihtlauac Alvarado (ocaml/ocaml.org#3622)
  • ocaml.org added an industrial users entry for Amazon Web Services describing its use of HOL Light to verify the s2n-bignum cryptography project, by adith nk (ocaml/ocaml.org#3681)
  • ocaml.org corrected the wasmofocaml tool page to state it targets WebAssembly GC rather than plain WebAssembly, by Akhil Indurti (ocaml/ocaml.org#3719)

    • Overview

  • Security-driven releases in ocaml/opam-repository dominated the week, with cohttp fixing a path-traversal bug and mirage-crypto fixing a timing leak, both merged ahead of full CI completion given the security impact (ocaml/opam-repository#30528, ocaml/opam-repository#30507)
  • OCaml 5.5 compatibility triage continued at scale in opam-repository, with Dmitrii Kosarev adding bounds and depext fixes to over a dozen older packages (ocaml/opam-repository#30489, ocaml/opam-repository#30500)
  • Package archival policy was formalised, with several archived-upstream packages marked non-maintained following a triage discussion (ocaml/opam-repository#30550)
  • Doc-quality tooling landed in ocaml/ocaml.org via mdx-based testing of tutorial code blocks, which immediately surfaced pre-existing tutorial breakage (ocaml/ocaml.org#3622, ocaml/ocaml.org#3745)

    oxcaml/oxcaml merged debug-info/DWARF, heap-extension, and frametable-size work while 52 PRs opened; oxcaml/opam-repository reviewed two pending dune/eio/mdx version-guard PRs.

    New Features

  • oxcaml/oxcaml: new runtime API for heap extensions by Nick Barnes adds caml_add_extent, letting embedders register externally-allocated memory as valid OCaml blocks the GC can scan (oxcaml/oxcaml#6248).
  • oxcaml/oxcaml: frame table size reduced for native code by Nick Barnes through de-duplicated debuginfo strings, a shorter descriptor format, and a bitmap encoding for scannable stack slots (oxcaml/oxcaml#6399).
  • oxcaml/oxcaml: fixed a stack-growth use-after-free in caml_tick_fiber_res where tick handlers could invalidate the stack pointer during a stack grow, by Max Slater (oxcaml/oxcaml#6764); runtime atoms now get linker symbols caml_atom_, also by Nick Barnes (oxcaml/oxcaml#6779).
  • oxcaml/oxcaml: backported the idle-phase major GC algorithm from upstream OCaml, by @julesjacobs; tuning OCAMLRUNPARAM='o=200,Xsmall_heap_limit=128M' was measured at roughly 20% aggregate compile-time improvement on a large tree (oxcaml/oxcaml#6484).
  • oxcaml/oxcaml: default shape format flipped to Debugging_shapes and debug-info fidelity levels increased, adding -type-to-shape-max-depth and -gupstream-dwarf/-gno-upstream-dwarf flags, by Simon Spies (oxcaml/oxcaml#5103, oxcaml/oxcaml#5199); DW_AT_call_{file,line,column} now reports the call site rather than the definition site for inlined calls, by Kevin Svetlitski (oxcaml/oxcaml#6877).
  • oxcaml/oxcaml: fixed fatal errors and incorrect dummy block sizing when compiling recursive mixed blocks, by Ryan Tjoa (oxcaml/oxcaml#6844, oxcaml/oxcaml#6843); Merlin gained destruct support for unboxed tuples, by Liam Stevenson (oxcaml/oxcaml#6849), and can now be built via Nix, also by Liam Stevenson/Gavin Gray (oxcaml/oxcaml#6814).
