    • OCaml Core

    New `Sys.filepath_exists`, native FMA/sqrt codegen for arm64/power/riscv/s390x, and runtime_events corrupt-stream fixes landed in ocaml/ocaml.

    New Features

  • Added Sys.filepath_exists, a stricter alternative to Sys.file_exists that reports permission and other system errors via a Sys_error exception instead of silently returning false, and clarified the documentation of file_exists to recommend the new function (ocaml/ocaml#14974, closing ocaml/ocaml#12393) by Khalid.
  • Hardened bytecode executable loading in caml_read_section_descriptors against overflow when a corrupted or malicious file declares 2^29 or more table-of-contents entries (ocaml/ocaml#14872) by Xavier Leroy.
  • Float.fma now emits a native fused multiply-add instruction on arm64, power, riscv and s390x instead of calling into C (ocaml/ocaml#15008) by Zane Hambly.
  • The s390x backend now emits sqdbr for square root and lrvgr/lrvr for byte swap natively rather than going through C (ocaml/ocaml#15002) by Zane Hambly.
  • The riscv backend now emits fsqrt.d for square root natively (ocaml/ocaml#15005) by Zane Hambly.
  • 32-bit builds now default to and recommend large-file (LFS) and year-2038-safe time_t support via configure, with --disable-largefile and --disable-year2038 available to opt out (ocaml/ocaml#14997) by Antonin Décimo.
  • Added a cross-backend testsuite check for sqrt covering zeros, infinities, NaN, denormals and exact squares, pinning behaviour used by the s390x and riscv sqrt changes (ocaml/ocaml#15007) by Zane Hambly.

    • Overview

  • Activity was concentrated entirely in ocaml/ocaml this week; ocaml/RFCs recorded no activity.
  • Sys.filepath_exists was added as a stricter alternative to Sys.file_exists (ocaml/ocaml#14974), and native codegen for FMA, square root and byte swap landed on arm64, power, riscv and s390x (ocaml/ocaml#15008, ocaml/ocaml#15002, ocaml/ocaml#15005).
  • A cluster of runtime_events correctness fixes was opened, including two competing fixes for the long-standing "corrupt stream" race (ocaml/ocaml#15015, ocaml/ocaml#15016) tracked against ocaml/ocaml#14151, and a lost_words overflow fix (ocaml/ocaml#15010).
  • Five PRs opened this week remain unmerged: native rounding instructions (ocaml/ocaml#15017), the two runtime_events corrupt-stream fixes (ocaml/ocaml#15015, ocaml/ocaml#15016), the lost_words widening (ocaml/ocaml#15010), and physical-equality fast paths for Set.union/inter/diff (ocaml/ocaml#15009).

    • Activity

  • Five newly opened PRs remain unmerged: native rounding instructions (Float.round, trunc, ceil, floor) for arm64 and power (ocaml/ocaml#15017) by Zane Hambly; a fix for the runtime_events "corrupt stream" failure that adds a producer-side memory fence and consumer re-check, with detailed reproduction data across amd64, arm64, riscv64 and ppc64le (ocaml/ocaml#15016) by Tim McGilchrist; an earlier, narrower fix for the same corrupt-stream issue (ocaml/ocaml#15015) by Sadiq Jaffer, which the two authors are now discussing combining; widening lost_words from int to uint64_t in the runtime-events lost-events callback to avoid wraparound past INT_MAX (ocaml/ocaml#15010) by Tim McGilchrist; and physical-equality fast paths for Set.union, Set.inter and Set.diff that improve complexity for sets with structural sharing, carried internally at LexiFi for over a decade (ocaml/ocaml#15009) by Nicolás Ojeda Bär.
  • The runtime_events subsystem received concentrated attention beyond the corrupt-stream PRs: a size_t fix for ring-buffer file-size overflow past 2 GiB (ocaml/ocaml#15000, fixing ocaml/ocaml#14999) and a proposal to expose EV_C_MAJOR_DIRECT_ALLOCATED_WORDS and related direct/suspended/resume counters (ocaml/ocaml#15001), both by Tim McGilchrist, remain open.
  • The minor-GC rewrite that inlines the oldify_one fast path and upstreams work from OxCaml continues under review, with Eduardo Souza publishing a benchmarking dashboard showing mostly improvements with one workload regression tied to glibc malloc tuning (ocaml/ocaml#14571) by Nick Barnes.
  • Native atomic exchange and compare-and-set generation across all architectures, follow-up to the fetch-and-add work, remains open for review with a call for extra eyes on the riscv and power fences (ocaml/ocaml#14980) by Zane Hambly.
  • Type-checker cleanup continues in draft form: removing an unnecessary unify_var call in enforce_current_level (ocaml/ocaml#14995) and making abstract types defined directly in structures injective, a follow-up to ocaml/ocaml#14982 and ocaml/ocaml#14990 (ocaml/ocaml#14991), both by Jacques Garrigue.
  • Jeremy Yallop proposed fixing Weak.get_copy so it no longer shallow-duplicates continuations, which can otherwise crash a program with a segmentation fault (ocaml/ocaml#14988).
  • Build and CI work continued from Antonin Décimo: enabling KVM for hardware-accelerated Android emulation in CI, saving roughly 40 seconds per job (ocaml/ocaml#15003), and switching configure to Autoconf's own C++ compiler detection to fix a -std=gnu23 build failure (ocaml/ocaml#14996).

    • Notable Discussions

  • The runtime_events "corrupt stream" bug (ocaml/ocaml#14151) prompted parallel investigation: Sadiq Jaffer proposed a consumer-side re-check (ocaml/ocaml#15015), while Tim McGilchrist traced a second, independent cause — a release-store ordering bug in write_to_ring — and added a producer-side fence (ocaml/ocaml#15016); Zane Hambly independently reproduced the failure on riscv64 and confirmed the combined fix eliminates it while the consumer-only fix does not.
  • Wording for the new Sys.filepath_exists and revised Sys.file_exists documentation went through several rounds between Xavier Leroy, Daniel Bünzli and Khalid, settling on plain-language phrasing that avoids POSIX-specific terms like stat, ENOTDIR and ENOENT since Sys module readers are not assumed to know POSIX systems programming (ocaml/ocaml#14974).
  • Jeremy Yallop found that Weak.get_copy shallow-duplicates effect-handler continuations, producing two continuations sharing one fiber and causing a segmentation fault when both are resumed (ocaml/ocaml#14988).
  • Ryan Tjoa reported that [%atomic.loc] on a polymorphic mutable record field can be used to implement Obj.magic, an unsoundness hole credited in part to a discussion with Nathan Farlow (ocaml/ocaml#14987).
  • Whether runtime_events constructor indices should be covered by a maintained wire-format version field was debated by Gabriel Scherer, Sadiq Jaffer, Tim McGilchrist and Anil Madhavapeddy, converging on bumping the version now and enforcing an append-only policy for constructors going forward (ocaml/ocaml#15011).
  • Reviewers debated whether the new sharing-based fast paths in Set.union/inter/diff warrant documenting the resulting complexity guarantees, with Vincent Laviron and Daniel Bünzli leaning toward leaving the documentation unchanged since the guarantee is not simple to state precisely (ocaml/ocaml#15009).
  • Vincent Laviron found that the ocamldebug wire protocol clamps object headers to 32 bits, which can silently truncate large array sizes during remote debugging, surfaced while investigating support for the Introcaml tool (ocaml/ocaml#15012).
  • Tim McGilchrist and Zane Hambly confirmed the flambda+ThreadSanitizer test combination fails on ppc64le, amd64 Linux and arm64 macOS due to flambda's anonymous-function symbol naming and missing race reports, with McGilchrist taking on the fix (ocaml/ocaml#15014).

    • Emerging Trends

  • Systematic replacement of C-call fallbacks with native instructions on arm64, power, riscv and s390x continues, covering FMA, square root, byte swap and now rounding operations, largely driven by Zane Hambly (ocaml/ocaml#14980, ocaml/ocaml#15002, ocaml/ocaml#15005, ocaml/ocaml#15006, ocaml/ocaml#15008, ocaml/ocaml#15017).
  • Several independent integer-overflow and correctness bugs in runtime_events were reported and fixed in the same period — ring-buffer size overflow, lost_words truncation, constructor-index versioning and the corrupt-stream race — indicating active hardening of that subsystem by Tim McGilchrist and Sadiq Jaffer (ocaml/ocaml#14999, ocaml/ocaml#15000, ocaml/ocaml#15001, ocaml/ocaml#15010, ocaml/ocaml#15011, ocaml/ocaml#15015, ocaml/ocaml#15016).
  • Build-system modernization keeps moving toward standard Autoconf idioms rather than hand-rolled checks, for large-file/year-2038 support and C++ compiler detection (ocaml/ocaml#14997, ocaml/ocaml#14996) by Antonin Décimo.

    • Multicore

    Eio 1.5 was released with pre-connect socket options, while ocaml-uring's bytes-based buffer migration gained a zero-copy bigarray bridge.

    New Features

  • ocaml-multicore/eio: Eio.Net.connect gained optional ?bind_to and ?options arguments so a socket can be bound to a local address and have Sockopt.settings (e.g. SO_REUSEADDR, SO_KEEPALIVE) applied before connecting, letting multi-homed hosts pick the local address for an outbound connection; built on @art-w's draft (ocaml-multicore/eio#713) and merged by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#875)
  • ocaml-multicore/eio: eio_posix and eio_windows opam files gained available constraints so eio_posix no longer attempts to install on Windows and vice versa, now that ocaml-ci has Windows support, by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#921)
  • ocaml-multicore/eio: Eio 1.5 was released (ocaml-multicore/eio#924) by Thomas Leonard, bundling the pre-connect socket options, the opam availability fix, and previously-landed Windows path support and Eio.Path.of_dir — see the v1.5 release notes
  • ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring: added Iovec.to_bigarray, a zero-copy Bigarray.Array1.t alias over an Iovec.t's underlying bytes, letting bigarray-based interfaces interoperate with the library's new bytes-backed buffers without copying, part of the ongoing buffer-type migration from bigarray/cstruct to bytes (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153, 4116ced)
  • ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring: implementation adds a hand-built bigarray proxy with a GC finaliser chain on the aliased bytes buffer, plus a new internal stub ocaml_uring_ba_family_refs tracking live bigarray references so the buffer is only freed once all derived views are unreachable, with aliasing tests added in tests/buffer_test.ml (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153)

    • Overview

  • Two of the nine group repositories had recorded activity this week — ocaml-multicore/eio and ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring; ocaml-multicore/domainslib, ocaml-multicore/meio, ocaml-multicore/saturn, ocaml-multicore/eio-trace, ocaml-multicore/picos, ocaml-multicore/kcas, and ocaml-multicore/ocaml-iomux had no recorded activity in this period
  • ocaml-multicore/eio shipped the 1.5 release (ocaml-multicore/eio#924), merging pre-connect socket options for Eio.Net.connect (ocaml-multicore/eio#875) and a Windows opam availability fix (ocaml-multicore/eio#921)
  • ocaml-multicore/eio also saw three new PRs opened: Fiber.List.partition_map (ocaml-multicore/eio#927), a curated documentation index (ocaml-multicore/eio#926), and an Eio.Vars environment-variables API (ocaml-multicore/eio#923)
  • ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring's draft buffer-type migration PR (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153) progressed with a zero-copy bigarray-aliasing mechanism, moving the library from bigarray/cstruct toward plain bytes buffers

    • Activity

  • Kento Okura opened a PR adding Eio.Fiber.List.partition_map to eio, noting it could not be implemented standalone since Limiter is hidden from the interface (ocaml-multicore/eio#927)
  • Thomas Leonard opened a PR adding a curated index.mld to eio's documentation, replacing the hard-to-navigate auto-generated index, with review from Anil Madhavapeddy on grouping Eio.Fs with Path and clarifying Eio_unix/Eio_mock descriptions (ocaml-multicore/eio#926)
  • Patrick Ferris opened Eio.Vars.t on Stdenv for portable get/put/get_all access to environment variables, following design discussion in ocaml-multicore/eio#922; Anil Madhavapeddy reviewed extensively, raising thread-safety of putenv across domains, an off-by-one in the A=b parsing case, and missing test coverage (ocaml-multicore/eio#923)
  • In ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring, Anil Madhavapeddy's draft PR switching the buffer type to bytes instead of bigarray/cstruct remains open, with this week's update adding the bigarray-aliasing mechanism so existing bigarray-based consumers can still be supported, reported as passing stress testing so far (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153)

    • Notable Discussions

  • Patrick Ferris proposed a portable System/environment-variable interface for eio, prompting Thomas Leonard to suggest Vars over System to avoid confusion with Stdenv, adopted in the follow-up PR (ocaml-multicore/eio#922, ocaml-multicore/eio#923)
  • On the same PR, Anil Madhavapeddy raised whether Eio.Vars.put should be synchronised with a mutex given putenv is not thread-safe across domains, and Patrick Ferris discussed whether start-of-day usage makes the race window practically significant (ocaml-multicore/eio#923)
  • Thomas Gazagnaire requested a capability-safe hard-link primitive (linkat-style, taking two dirfds) for use in OCI image extraction, contrasting it with the check-then-use race of flattening paths and calling Unix.link directly (ocaml-multicore/eio#925)
  • Thomas Gazagnaire reported that Eio.Private.Trace allocates 23 words per event once the runtime_events ring is active, affecting allocation-profile readings of fiber-dense programs; Anil Madhavapeddy noted this will be fixed once OCaml 5.6 ships with ocaml/ocaml#14984 merged upstream (ocaml-multicore/eio#914)
  • In ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring, Anil Madhavapeddy relayed design feedback from Thomas Leonard describing a technique that aliases non-moving bytes as a bigarray via a proxy and finaliser, noting it did not obviously crash under stress testing despite still being evaluated (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Portability work continues to land in small, targeted increments in ocaml-multicore/eio — opam available constraints for Windows this week (ocaml-multicore/eio#921) following the Windows path support already released in 1.5
  • Requests are trending toward closing capability-safety gaps in eio's filesystem API, exemplified by the hard-link request explicitly modeled on how ~follow:false closed a similar gap for chmod (ocaml-multicore/eio#925)
  • New API surface in eio (Eio.Vars, Fiber.List.partition_map) is being proposed and reviewed with attention to domain-safety and hidden internals like Limiter, rather than merged quickly (ocaml-multicore/eio#923, ocaml-multicore/eio#927)
  • Across both active repositories, buffer- and memory-lifetime safety on the OCaml 5 runtime is a shared design concern — eio's per-event trace allocation overhead (ocaml-multicore/eio#914) and ocaml-uring's non-moving bytes/GC-finaliser/bigarray-proxy scheme (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153) both hinge on precise control of allocation and object lifetime
  • Ongoing shift from bigarray/cstruct to plain bytes-based buffers in ocaml-uring is balancing zero-copy interop against GC lifetime safety rather than dropping bigarray support outright (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153)
entry.summary: Eio 1.5 and opam 2.6.0~beta1 shipped, ocaml/ocaml gained native FMA/sqrt codegen, and opam-repository merged cohttp/mirage-crypto security fixes.

entry.title: Week 33, 2026: MirageOS/Solo5 releases, a prometheus core/Lwt split, and OCaml Workshop 2026 site build-out were the week's only reported group activity.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Ecosystem New affect 0.0.0 package published, a streamlined effects-based concurrency model for OCaml supported by an OCaml Software Foundation grant, by Daniel Bünzli (ocaml/opam-repository#30469)
  • OCaml Ecosystem New dune-rpc-eio 0.1.0 package: an Eio client for dune's RPC protocol that can spawn or attach to a dune server, build paths/aliases, run tests, and read diagnostics, by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml/opam-repository#30453)
  • OCaml Ecosystem prometheus 1.4 splits the library into a synchronous core and a new prometheus-lwt package, deprecating the Lwt-typed timing helpers in core ahead of their eventual removal, by Anil Madhavapeddy with Mark Elvers (ocaml/opam-repository#30452)
  • OCaml Ecosystem mirage-xen 9.0.1 adds Import.copy_from/Import.copy_to, hypervisor-mediated grant-copy primitives that speed up transfers such as the qubes-mirage-firewall, by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#30493)
  • OCaml Ecosystem jsont 0.3.0 narrows the safely encodable integer range for Jsont.int/Jsont.int64 from [-2^53;2^53] to [-2^53+1;2^53-1] (a breaking change, with legacy variants provided for migration), and fixes nested out-of-order case-member decoding, by Daniel Bünzli (ocaml/opam-repository#30485)
  • OCaml Ecosystem sqlite3 5.4.2 fixes OCaml GC rooting across runtime-released SQLite calls, preventing statement/database wrappers from being finalized while blocked inside SQLite, by Markus Mottl (ocaml/opam-repository#30475)
  • OCaml Ecosystem ocamlmig updated to OCaml 5.5, and its [@@migrate] attribute now accepts a ~min_version for dependencies, by v-gb (ocaml/opam-repository#30396)
  • OCaml Ecosystem New packages published this week include checked_oint 2.1.0 checked integer arithmetic by @hirrolot (ocaml/opam-repository#30505); bitflyer and gmocoin cryptocurrency-exchange API clients by YOSHIHIRO Imai (ocaml/opam-repository#30459, ocaml/opam-repository#30460); the 4-package pure-OCaml Neo4j driver neodriver by Tomasz Barański (ocaml/opam-repository#30448); and p4spectec 0.1.2, a P4-language mechanization toolchain, by Haechan Kwon (ocaml/opam-repository#30455)
  • OCaml Ecosystem Added a dedicated OCaml Workshop 2026 schedule page at /ocaml-workshop-2026/schedule, wiring up a new Schedule section in the workshop navigation layout, URL, handler, and router, by Sudha Parimala (ocaml/ocaml.org#3740), followed by speaker authors, talk abstracts, and a timing fix (ocaml/ocaml.org#3742)

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    MirageOS/Solo5 releases, a prometheus core/Lwt split, and OCaml Workshop 2026 site build-out defined ecosystem activity this week.

    New Features

  • New affect 0.0.0 package published, a streamlined effects-based concurrency model for OCaml supported by an OCaml Software Foundation grant, by Daniel Bünzli (ocaml/opam-repository#30469)
  • New dune-rpc-eio 0.1.0 package: an Eio client for dune's RPC protocol that can spawn or attach to a dune server, build paths/aliases, run tests, and read diagnostics, by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml/opam-repository#30453)
  • prometheus 1.4 splits the library into a synchronous core and a new prometheus-lwt package, deprecating the Lwt-typed timing helpers in core ahead of their eventual removal, by Anil Madhavapeddy with Mark Elvers (ocaml/opam-repository#30452)
  • mirage-xen 9.0.1 adds Import.copy_from/Import.copy_to, hypervisor-mediated grant-copy primitives that speed up transfers such as the qubes-mirage-firewall, by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#30493)
  • jsont 0.3.0 narrows the safely encodable integer range for Jsont.int/Jsont.int64 from [-2^53;2^53] to [-2^53+1;2^53-1] (a breaking change; legacy variants provided for migration), and fixes nested out-of-order case-member decoding, by Daniel Bünzli (ocaml/opam-repository#30485)
  • sqlite3 5.4.2 fixes OCaml GC rooting across runtime-released SQLite calls, preventing statement/database wrappers from being finalized while blocked inside SQLite, by Markus Mottl (ocaml/opam-repository#30475)
  • ocamlmig updated to OCaml 5.5 and its [@@migrate] attribute now accepts a ~min_version for dependencies, by v-gb (ocaml/opam-repository#30396)
  • New packages published this week: checked_oint 2.1.0 checked integer arithmetic by @hirrolot (ocaml/opam-repository#30505); bitflyer and gmocoin cryptocurrency-exchange API clients by YOSHIHIRO Imai (ocaml/opam-repository#30459, ocaml/opam-repository#30460); the 4-package pure-OCaml Neo4j driver neodriver by Tomasz Barański (ocaml/opam-repository#30448); and p4spectec 0.1.2, a P4-language mechanization toolchain, by Haechan Kwon (ocaml/opam-repository#30455)
  • Added a dedicated OCaml Workshop 2026 schedule page at /ocaml-workshop-2026/schedule, wiring up a new Schedule section in the workshop navigation layout, URL, handler, and router, by Sudha Parimala (ocaml/ocaml.org#3740), followed by speaker authors, talk abstracts, and a timing fix (ocaml/ocaml.org#3742)

    • Overview

  • Package ecosystem activity in ocaml/opam-repository centered on MirageOS/Solo5 releases, a prometheus core/Lwt split (ocaml/opam-repository#30452), and new effects-based/Eio tooling packages
  • Sustained CI-constraint triage by Dmitrii Kosarev targeting old or under-maintained packages surfaced by check.ci.ocaml.org failures
  • Website build-out in ocaml/ocaml.org focused on the OCaml Workshop 2026 event site, with a new schedule page and content additions (ocaml/ocaml.org#3740, ocaml/ocaml.org#3742)
  • Incremental internationalization work on ocaml.org's site search, replacing ASCII-only lowercasing with Unicode-aware case folding (ocaml/ocaml.org#3739)

    • Activity

  • Dmitrii Kosarev opened a cluster of CI/depext maintenance PRs tracking check.ci.ocaml.org failures, including an OCaml upper bound for errpy (ocaml/opam-repository#30500), Ubuntu depexts for conf-lua (ocaml/opam-repository#30498), and upper-bound constraints for qrencode (ocaml/opam-repository#30488), oclock (ocaml/opam-repository#30489) and tplib (ocaml/opam-repository#30484)
  • Package submissions opened this week and still awaiting review include snoke 0.3.2, a Snake-style game, by 珊瑚 (ocaml/opam-repository#30495) and oxbow 0.1.0, a river-compositor window manager, by @3L0C (ocaml/opam-repository#30497)
  • The Hegel property-based testing PPX suite iterated through three release attempts this week (0.16.0 merged, 0.16.1 closed, 0.16.2 merged), by Ethan Chou (ocaml/opam-repository#30457, ocaml/opam-repository#30467, ocaml/opam-repository#30468)
  • MirageOS/Solo5 ecosystem releases merged this week include ocaml-solo5/ocaml-solo5-cross-aarch64 1.3.4 (ocaml/opam-repository#30492), Solo5 v0.12.1 (ocaml/opam-repository#30470), and mirage-qubes 2.0.1 (ocaml/opam-repository#30483), by Hannes Mehnert and Pierre Alain, alongside deprecation of most mirage-crypto-rng-* variant packages (ocaml/opam-repository#30478)
  • Draft/pending releases include Caqti 3.0.1 fixing a PostgreSQL reconnect bug, by Petter A. Urkedal (ocaml/opam-repository#30477), and fsevents 0.4.0 flagged "do not merge" pending an OCaml 5.5 compatibility fix, by Calascibetta Romain (ocaml/opam-repository#30479)
  • An open ocaml.org PR replaces String.lowercase_ascii with Unicode-aware case folding (Uucp.Case.Fold) across seven search call sites, fixing case-insensitive matching for non-ASCII text such as "école" vs "ÉCOLE", by Tai Nguyen, addressing ocaml/ocaml.org#2444 (ocaml/ocaml.org#3739)
  • A documentation typo fix in the ocaml.org Lists tutorial was reviewed and merged, by QuantumMango and Cuihtlauac Alvarado (ocaml/ocaml.org#3741)
  • Routine ocaml.org Planet blog scrape updates picked up new posts including OCaml Weekly News and workshop-related entries (ocaml/ocaml.org#3738, ocaml/ocaml.org#3743), and the automated platform-releases scraper PR remained open (ocaml/ocaml.org#3693)
  • Governance discussion continued on a proposed policy requiring human responses on package-submission PRs even when the submission itself is machine-generated, led by Calascibetta Romain with Anil Madhavapeddy and Shon Feder (ocaml/opam-repository#30367)

    • Notable Discussions

  • Policy discussion on requiring human responses to package-submission PRs, even when auto-generated, converged on wording that distinguishes machine-generated PR creation from machine-generated comments, with Calascibetta Romain, Anil Madhavapeddy and Shon Feder iterating on the text (ocaml/opam-repository#30367)
  • Reviewer Jan Midtgaard raised naming/attribution concerns about bisectppxng, a fork of the original bisect_ppx, asking for the synopsis to clarify the fork relationship before merge, addressed by Dmitrii Kosarev (ocaml/opam-repository#30463)
  • A debugging thread on qrencode 0.2 traced compile failures on OCaml 5.0+ to the removal of unprefixed C runtime function names (alloc_custom → caml_alloc_custom); Dmitrii Kosarev and Jan Midtgaard worked through gcc-14-specific errors before splitting conf-qrencode into its own patched package (ocaml/opam-repository#30488)
  • Jérôme Vouillon clarified with Dmitrii Kosarev that the newly released wax toolchain's all-red CI matrix stems from an unrelated avoid-version-flagged preview lsp package being pulled in, not from wax itself (ocaml/opam-repository#30278)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Dmitrii Kosarev continues a sustained wave of OCaml-upper-bound and depext maintenance PRs discovered via check.ci.ocaml.org, targeting old or under-maintained packages such as tplib (ocaml/opam-repository#30484), qrencode (ocaml/opam-repository#30488), oclock (ocaml/opam-repository#30489) and errpy (ocaml/opam-repository#30500)
  • Multiple opam-repository packages are decoupling from Lwt or deprecating Lwt-coupled variants, including prometheus's core/Lwt split (ocaml/opam-repository#30452) and the deprecation of most mirage-crypto-rng-* variant packages (ocaml/opam-repository#30478)
  • OCaml 5.5 readiness work continues across the ecosystem, visible in introcaml's flambda-alpha1 release (ocaml/opam-repository#30415), modelkit's restored 5.5 builds (ocaml/opam-repository#30462), and ocamlmig's move to 5.5 (ocaml/opam-repository#30396)
  • Continued build-out of the OCaml Workshop 2026 event site on ocaml.org across multiple PRs in the same week, moving from a schedule page to enriched abstracts/authors content (ocaml/ocaml.org#3740, ocaml/ocaml.org#3742)
  • Ongoing internationalization work on ocaml.org replacing ASCII-only string comparisons with Unicode-aware case folding for search features, following on from ocaml/ocaml.org#2444 (ocaml/ocaml.org#3739)
  • Automated maintenance (Planet blog scraping, platform release scraping, Dependabot updates) continues to account for a steady share of weekly ocaml.org PR activity (ocaml/ocaml.org#3737, ocaml/ocaml.org#3738, ocaml/ocaml.org#3743, ocaml/ocaml.org#3693)

    • OCaml Tools

    OxCaml

    OCaml Core

    Multicore
entry.summary: MirageOS/Solo5 releases, a prometheus core/Lwt split, and OCaml Workshop 2026 site build-out were the week's only reported group activity.

entry.title: Week 32, 2026: ocaml/ocaml landed Uchar ASCII/Latin-1 helpers and soundness fixes while opam-repository shipped OCaml 5.6 preview builds and dune 3.24.2.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Core New Uchar.is_ascii, Uchar.ascii_to_char, Uchar.is_latin1, and Uchar.latin1_to_char functions were merged, clarifying the ambiguous latin1-vs-ASCII behaviour of the existing Uchar.is_char/Uchar.to_char (now deprecated in their favour) ocaml/ocaml#14981, closing ocaml/ocaml#14962, by @copy.
  • OCaml Core Weak.get_copy no longer shallow-copies continuations, fixing a segmentation fault that could occur when a weakly-held continuation was duplicated and both copies were resumed ocaml/ocaml#14988, by Jeremy Yallop.
  • OCaml Core The runtime now sizes the alternate signal stack from sysconf(_SC_MINSIGSTKSZ) when available, fixing a fatal "Failed to allocate signal stack" error on musl libc 1.2.6+ on certain Intel CPUs ocaml/ocaml#14933, by Nat Mote, reviewed by Florian Angeletti.
  • OCaml Core A soundness bug allowing Obj.magic-style casts via abstract types defined by module include was fixed, removing the wrong assumption that abstract types defined in the current module are always injective ocaml/ocaml#14982, by Jeremy Yallop.
  • OCaml Core The let-rec check now gives generic (unknown-type) arrays dynamic size, fixing a segfault on 32-bit systems where flat float arrays and boxed arrays have different word sizes but were previously assumed equal ocaml/ocaml#14993, by Jeremy Yallop.
  • OCaml Core The build now requires and generates configure with Autoconf 2.72, gaining large-file (LFS) and year-2038 (_TIME_BITS=64) support checks and updated C++-compiler detection ocaml/ocaml#14953, addressing ocaml/ocaml#14937, by David Allsopp.
  • OCaml Core printast now prints a trailing newline after Pexp_unreachable, fixing malformed AST dumps ocaml/ocaml#14992, by David Allsopp.
  • OCaml Ecosystem ocaml/dune released 3.24.2, adding the implicit unix dependency required by MDX 2.6+ for generated MDX test executables (dune#15592, by Anil Madhavapeddy) and rescanning the RPC registry on directory-mtime change so clients that poll before Dune registers can discover the new instance (dune#15634, fixes dune#15630, by Rudi Grinberg).
  • OCaml Ecosystem OCaml 5.6 preview compatibility releases landed for ppxlib ocaml/opam-repository#30424 by Nathan Rebours and for merlin/ocaml-lsp ocaml/opam-repository#30382 by Ulysse.
  • OCaml Ecosystem Seven new opam packages were submitted, including floatml (f16/f32/f64/f128 float types) by opale (opam-repository#30437) and opam-audit (switch security auditing) by Hannes Mehnert (opam-repository#30443).
  • OCaml Ecosystem ocaml/ocaml.org reworked package version pages so get_versions returns explicit Avoided/Deprecated version_status tags instead of a bare date, grouping entries into Latest, Previous, and Not-normally-selected versions ocaml/ocaml.org#3713, by Sora Morimoto.

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    Opam-repository had a heavy release week with OCaml 5.6 preview builds, while ocaml.org reworked package version-status pages to flag avoided/deprecated releases.

    New Features

  • ocaml/ocaml.org: Package version pages reworked so get_versions returns explicit Avoided/Deprecated version_status tags instead of a bare date, sharing latest-version selection logic between package pages and the package index, by Sora Morimoto (ocaml/ocaml.org#3713)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: Version pages now group entries into Latest version, Previous versions, and Versions not normally selected by opam, with dates relabelled Added to opam-repository as accessible UTC timestamps, plus new package_versions_test.ml coverage (ocaml/ocaml.org#3713)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: OCaml Workshop 2026 page updated with the confirmed INRIA Paris venue and a live registration link, and the call-for-talks page now shows a closed-submissions notice, by Sudha Parimala (ocaml/ocaml.org#3734)
  • ocaml/opam-repository: Seven new packages submitted — floatml (f16/f32/f64/f128 float types) by opale (ocaml/opam-repository#30437), opam-audit (switch security auditing) by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#30443), p4spectec by Haechan Kwon (ocaml/opam-repository#30430), ravel by Kayo Tei (ocaml/opam-repository#30450), readabilitymetrics by Michael Lip (ocaml/opam-repository#30449), requisite by Stephen Olesen (ocaml/opam-repository#30400), and smajiglyph_path by ZAN DoYe (ocaml/opam-repository#30444)
  • ocaml/opam-repository: dune and its 18-package toolchain released at 3.24.2 by Ali Caglayan (ocaml/opam-repository#30392), and the mirage-crypto family released at 2.3.0 across 6 packages by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#30436)
  • ocaml/opam-repository: OCaml 5.6 preview compatibility releases landed for ppxlib by Nathan Rebours (ocaml/opam-repository#30424) and for merlin/ocaml-lsp by Ulysse (ocaml/opam-repository#30382)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/opam-repository: seven new package submissions merged, plus point releases for dune 3.24.2, mirage-crypto 2.3.0, and carton 1.3.0; ongoing migration of packages with disappeared upstream archives to the opam-source-archives mirror
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: the package version-status page rework merged (ocaml/ocaml.org#3713), alongside OCaml Workshop 2026 logistics updates (ocaml/ocaml.org#3734) and routine scraper/dependency automation
  • OCaml 5.6 preview compatibility builds appeared across the toolchain (ppxlib, merlin, ocaml-lsp) in opam-repository ahead of the upcoming release (ocaml/opam-repository#30424, ocaml/opam-repository#30382)

    • Activity

  • ocaml/opam-repository: Anil Madhavapeddy opened a prometheus 1.4 release covering 3 packages (ocaml/opam-repository#30452), superseding a closed attempt by Thomas Leonard (ocaml/opam-repository#30439), and opened a new dune-rpc-eio 0.1.0 package (ocaml/opam-repository#30453)
  • ocaml/opam-repository: the hegel ecosystem shipped two point releases, 0.13.1 (ocaml/opam-repository#30408) and 0.14.1 (ocaml/opam-repository#30423), by Ethan Chou, after earlier point-version submissions were closed and resubmitted
  • ocaml/opam-repository: Calascibetta Romain merged carton (ocaml/opam-repository#30390), git-kv (ocaml/opam-repository#30391), stem (ocaml/opam-repository#30389), arc (ocaml/opam-repository#30427), and httpcats (ocaml/opam-repository#30426)
  • ocaml/opam-repository: Dmitrii Kosarev fixed the coq-lsp bad-checksum build by re-hosting its archive on the opam-source-archives mirror (ocaml/opam-repository#30401, closes ocaml/opam-repository#30241) and migrated pxshot (ocaml/opam-repository#30385), vecosek (ocaml/opam-repository#30386), rfsm (ocaml/opam-repository#30363), pgsolver (ocaml/opam-repository#30404), and simlog (ocaml/opam-repository#30402)
  • ocaml/opam-repository: several submissions never merged, including three attempts at a new par package by JC (ocaml/opam-repository#30406, ocaml/opam-repository#30417, ocaml/opam-repository#30429) and a modelkit submission by Clyde (ocaml/opam-repository#30411)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: an automated Platform Releases scraper PR remains open, tracking new upstream platform release entries pending merge (ocaml/ocaml.org#3693)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: routine automated maintenance merged, including OCaml Planet blog/video scrapes (ocaml/ocaml.org#3733, ocaml/ocaml.org#3735, ocaml/ocaml.org#3736) and a Dependabot bump of DavidAnson/markdownlint-cli2-action (ocaml/ocaml.org#3732)

    • Notable Discussions

  • ocaml/opam-repository: Hannes Mehnert questioned why creating a second opam switch with OCaml 5.5.0 triggered a full compiler rebuild instead of reusing a relocatable build; closed after being unable to reproduce consistently, CC'ing David Allsopp (ocaml/opam-repository#30407)
  • ocaml/opam-repository: a three-year-old request from Jacob Reinhold to stop hardcoding cc in the conf-openblas build (instead honoring $CC) was closed this week (ocaml/opam-repository#23495)

    • Emerging Trends

  • ocaml/opam-repository: Dmitrii Kosarev is systematically migrating packages with disappeared or unstable upstream archives onto a dedicated opam-source-archives GitHub mirror, covering coq-lsp, curses, pgsolver, simlog, pxshot, vecosek, and rfsm, closing several bad-checksum reports along the way (ocaml/opam-repository#30241, ocaml/opam-repository#30244, ocaml/opam-repository#30240)
  • ocaml/opam-repository: new-package submissions are commonly iterated through several closed-then-reopened PRs before merging as CI feedback drives version bumps, seen with soteria, hegel, p4spectec, and ocaml-neo4j-driver (ocaml/opam-repository#30438, ocaml/opam-repository#30423, ocaml/opam-repository#30430, ocaml/opam-repository#30448), while others like par (ocaml/opam-repository#30429) never make it through
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: metadata-presentation work is increasingly framed around avoiding misleading not just human readers but also search crawlers and LLMs about which package versions are current, as reflected in the accessibility and semantic-labelling work in ocaml/ocaml.org#3713
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: content/event pages continue to be kept in sync with real-world logistics (venue confirmation, registration going live, CFP closing) close to the event date, as seen in the OCaml Workshop 2026 updates (ocaml/ocaml.org#3734)

    • OCaml Tools

    OxCaml

    OCaml Core

    New Uchar ASCII/Latin-1 helpers and typing-soundness fixes landed in ocaml/ocaml, while the RFCs source-positions proposal was updated.

    New Features

  • New Uchar.is_ascii, Uchar.ascii_to_char, Uchar.is_latin1, and Uchar.latin1_to_char functions were merged, clarifying the ambiguous latin1-vs-ASCII behaviour of the existing Uchar.is_char/Uchar.to_char (now deprecated in their favour) (ocaml/ocaml#14981, closing ocaml/ocaml#14962), by @copy.
  • Weak.get_copy no longer shallow-copies continuations, fixing a segmentation fault that could occur when a weakly-held continuation was duplicated and both copies were resumed (ocaml/ocaml#14988) by Jeremy Yallop.
  • The runtime now sizes the alternate signal stack from sysconf(_SC_MINSIGSTKSZ) when available, fixing a fatal "Failed to allocate signal stack" error on musl libc 1.2.6+ on certain Intel CPUs (ocaml/ocaml#14933) by Nat Mote, merged with review from Florian Angeletti.
  • printast now prints a trailing newline after Pexp_unreachable, fixing malformed AST dumps (ocaml/ocaml#14992) by David Allsopp.
  • The let-rec check now gives generic (unknown-type) arrays dynamic size, fixing a segfault on 32-bit systems where flat float arrays and boxed arrays have different word sizes but were previously assumed to have the same static size (ocaml/ocaml#14993) by Jeremy Yallop.
  • A soundness bug allowing Obj.magic-style casts via abstract types defined by module include was fixed, removing the wrong assumption that abstract types defined in the current module are always injective (ocaml/ocaml#14982) by Jeremy Yallop.
  • The build now requires and generates configure with Autoconf 2.72, gaining large-file (LFS) and year-2038 (_TIME_BITS=64) support checks and updated C++-compiler detection (ocaml/ocaml#14953, addressing ocaml/ocaml#14937) by David Allsopp.
  • The Makefile now avoids a build-reproducibility race where otherlibs/str and otherlibs/unix .cmi/.cmx files could be compiled from two different rules recording different source paths, changing interface digests non-deterministically (ocaml/ocaml#14989) by Bernhard M. Wiedemann, cherry-picked to the 5.5 branch by David Allsopp.

    • Overview

  • Activity was concentrated in ocaml/ocaml, with sixteen new PRs opened this week; ocaml/RFCs saw a single RFC update.
  • New stdlib helpers (Uchar.is_ascii/Uchar.ascii_to_char/Uchar.is_latin1/Uchar.latin1_to_char, ocaml/ocaml#14981) and several typing-soundness and memory-safety fixes landed on trunk, including an abstract-type injectivity fix (ocaml/ocaml#14982) and a Weak.get_copy continuation-safety fix (ocaml/ocaml#14988).
  • Native atomic exchange/compare-and-set codegen (ocaml/ocaml#14980) and a Weak.Make open-addressing rewrite (ocaml/ocaml#14979) were opened, continuing performance-focused work from prior weeks.
  • In ocaml/RFCs, the 'Implicit source positions' RFC (ocaml/RFCs#52) by Olivier Nicole was updated while remaining open for review.

    • Activity

  • Antonin Décimo opened two configure-related PRs following up on the Autoconf 2.72 switch: defaulting to large-file and year-2038 support on 32-bit systems (ocaml/ocaml#14997) and switching C++ compiler detection to Autoconf's own machinery to fix a -std=gnu23 flag conflict (ocaml/ocaml#14996), plus a set of small Cygwin build fixes (ocaml/ocaml#14921).
  • Jacques Garrigue opened a draft simplifying enforce_current_level to avoid a spurious unify_var call (ocaml/ocaml#14995), and follow-ups to the injectivity fix: removing the now-redundant in_current_module/in_pervasives helpers (ocaml/ocaml#14990, folded into ocaml/ocaml#14982) and a draft making abstract types defined directly in structures injective (ocaml/ocaml#14991).
  • Zane Hambly opened a PR generating native atomic exchange/compare-and-set instructions across amd64, arm64, riscv, POWER, and s390x for immediate-typed atomics, avoiding the C call and its write barrier when the payload is known non-pointer, with per-architecture hardware benchmarking (ocaml/ocaml#14980, follow-up to ocaml/ocaml#14575); they also reviewed Anil Madhavapeddy's stack-reallocation size PR (ocaml/ocaml#14812) with detailed notes on RISC-V displacement limits.
  • Gabriel Scherer opened a rewrite of Weak.Make ("weak hashsets") using open-addressing with linear probing instead of bucket arrays, reporting a 30% speedup on an alt-ergo benchmark and up to 2.8x on some ocaml-hashcons workloads (ocaml/ocaml#14979), and continued discussion on enabling -g by default in the bytecode compiler (ocaml/ocaml#14971) and disabling a benchmark mistakenly run as a test (ocaml/ocaml#14960).
  • Anil Madhavapeddy opened a change making Runtime_events.User.write non-allocating by replacing a per-domain closure-based write-buffer cache with a single atomic bytes slot in DLS, removing roughly 23 words of allocation per event (ocaml/ocaml#14984), discussed with Thomas Leonard.
  • Jeremy Yallop also opened a fix so the expansiveness check considers effect-handler cases, fixing a segfault from an unhandled expansive allocation inside an effect match case (ocaml/ocaml#14986).
  • Alistair opened a PR adding typing support for optional polymorphic parameters, encoding them as Tpoly under an option type (ocaml/ocaml#14985), discussed with Florian Angeletti and Kate.
  • Ongoing typing-internals refactoring continued with Samuel Vivien's merge of eqtype with moregen (ocaml/ocaml#14739) and the change to make unify return a result rather than raise (ocaml/ocaml#14425), alongside Jacques Garrigue's fix for the type_newtype regression reported in ocaml/ocaml#14842 (ocaml/ocaml#14983).
  • Other open work under review this week includes Tim McGilchrist's POWER frame-pointer support (ocaml/ocaml#14505), agrn's comballoc peephole optimisation merging pointer-bump instructions (ocaml/ocaml#14812), shym's relocatable cross-compiler support (ocaml/ocaml#14929), Jeannalyse's draft reimplementation of Hashtbl with deterministic iteration order via dynamic arrays (ocaml/ocaml#14956), and Nick Barnes's proof-of-concept moving systhreads into the runtime (ocaml/ocaml#14965).
  • Stdlib feature-wish PRs continued to accumulate review, including Khalid's Sys.filepath_exists (ocaml/ocaml#14974), Brian Ward's Result.all/Option.all (ocaml/ocaml#14964), Benoit's Char.Ascii.is_punct (ocaml/ocaml#14957), and Jeannalyse's Atomic.compare_and_exchange (ocaml/ocaml#14912).
  • In ocaml/RFCs, the 'Implicit source positions' RFC (ocaml/RFCs#52), opened by Olivier Nicole on behalf of Tarides and Jane Street, was updated; it proposes a [%call_pos] arrow type so a labeled Lexing.position parameter is automatically filled with the call site's location when not explicitly supplied, aimed at stack-trace-free tracing of monadic binds, testing frameworks, and error reporting in embedded languages.

    • Notable Discussions

  • Ryan Tjoa reported that [%atomic.loc] on a polymorphic record field can be used to implement Obj.magic, producing a genuine unsoundness (ocaml/ocaml#14987); Gabriel Scherer analysed the typing gap around Tpoly instantiation for atomic-record primitives.
  • The Ctype.Unify typechecker crash reported by Eduardo Souza (ocaml/ocaml#14842) drew a multi-round discussion between Stefan Muenzel and Jacques Garrigue about where update_level/enforce_current_level should be called around locally-abstract module scopes, resulting in the fix PR ocaml/ocaml#14983 and the related simplification ocaml/ocaml#14995.
  • Török Edwin raised that int Atomic.t still emits polling points and a C call to caml_atomic_fetch_add_field instead of inlined machine instructions (ocaml/ocaml#14976), motivating a companion PR exposing that Atomic.t is not a float in the .mli (ocaml/ocaml#14977) and connecting to Zane Hambly's native atomic-exchange/CAS work (ocaml/ocaml#14980).

    • Emerging Trends

  • Several fixes credited LLM-assisted bug discovery, including the injectivity soundness fix (ocaml/ocaml#14982), the effect-case expansiveness fix (ocaml/ocaml#14986), the Weak.get_copy continuation fix (ocaml/ocaml#14988), and the win32 select handle leak fix (ocaml/ocaml#14975), each disclosed per the project's AI policy.
  • Atomic-operation performance work is converging on inlining native instructions in place of C calls when the payload type is statically known non-pointer, spanning fetch-and-add (referenced from ocaml/ocaml#14575), exchange/compare-and-set (ocaml/ocaml#14980), and .mli type exposure to aid the optimizer (ocaml/ocaml#14977).
  • Reworking of core data structures for both performance and determinism continued with a Weak.Make open-addressing rewrite (ocaml/ocaml#14979) and a Hashtbl reimplementation targeting deterministic iteration order (ocaml/ocaml#14956).
  • Build-system hygiene work is ongoing around the Autoconf 2.72 migration, with follow-up PRs for large-file/year-2038 support (ocaml/ocaml#14997) and C++ compiler detection (ocaml/ocaml#14996) landing the same week as the base switch (ocaml/ocaml#14953).

    • Multicore
entry.summary: ocaml/ocaml landed Uchar ASCII/Latin-1 helpers and soundness fixes while opam-repository shipped OCaml 5.6 preview builds and dune 3.24.2.

entry.title: Week 31, 2026: Merlin 5.8.1 and an ocaml-lsp 1.28.0 preview shipped, oxcaml/oxcaml landed AVX-512 SIMD, and core resolved a typechecker performance pathology.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Core Occurs-check elision and type-path equivalence normalization work by Stefan Muenzel and Gabriel Scherer cut a pathological jsofocaml/Lwt compile from 10 minutes to 170ms (ocaml/ocaml#14913, ocaml/ocaml#14952, building on ocaml/ocaml#14947 and ocaml/ocaml#14950).
  • OCaml Core Stdlib gained Dynarray.append_iarray and Pqueue.of_iarray from Nicolás Ojeda Bär (ocaml/ocaml#14909) and Option.try_value/Result.try_value (ocaml/ocaml#14941); a pattern-matching switch overflow bug was fixed by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml#14890) and a runtime memory leak from an unbounded stack cache was fixed (ocaml/ocaml#14940).
  • OxCaml AVX-512 support landed in oxcaml/oxcaml's amd64 SIMD backend, with Max Slater adding EVEX instruction encoding (oxcaml/oxcaml#6294) and opmask/ZMM mask-layout plumbing (oxcaml/oxcaml#6293), closing the original tracking request (oxcaml/oxcaml#6257).
  • OxCaml New compiler flags landed: -omit-leaf-frame-pointers from Xavier Clerc (oxcaml/oxcaml#6679) and -X (Flambda2 inlining-meet control) from Nathanaëlle Courant (oxcaml/oxcaml#6640); atomic fields in mixed blocks can now be loaded and stored, by Joe Kerrigan (oxcaml/oxcaml#6545).
  • Multicore ocaml-multicore/eio directory traversal sped up roughly 30% on directories with around a million files by enlarging the getdents64 stack buffer, by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#910), and path split/join moved into per-backend Eio.Fs.Pi.PATH modules laying groundwork for Windows support, by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#913, ocaml-multicore/eio#915); a bug causing fstat/mkdir/chmod/chown to fail on unconfined eio_posix handles was fixed (ocaml-multicore/eio#907, fixes ocaml-multicore/eio#906).
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/merlin released 5.8.1, fixing ocaml-index staleness for ppx-preprocessed files (ocaml/merlin#2110), a load_path invalidation race across concurrent typers (ocaml/merlin#2109), and a document query bug (ocaml/merlin#2092) by Liam Stevenson, plus a 5.8.1-506~preview with experimental OCaml 5.6 support.
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/ocaml-lsp enabled function-parameter inlay hints by default (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2097, fixes ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1371) and published the 1.28.0-506~preview release, by Rudi Grinberg and Ulysse.
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/dune added --include-empty to dune describe external-lib-deps (ocaml/dune#15585), fixed an action-leak bug between target-less multi-alias rules (ocaml/dune#15581), and fixed RPC registry polling so ocaml-lsp reliably discovers new instances, by Rudi Grinberg (ocaml/dune#15634).
  • OCaml Ecosystem opam 2.6.0~alpha1 preview shipped covering 8 packages, by Kate (ocaml/opam-repository#30284), alongside release trains for mirage-crypto/tls (12 packages, ocaml/opam-repository#30344, ocaml/opam-repository#30350) and cohttp (15 packages), by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml/opam-repository#30339).
  • OCaml Ecosystem ocaml/ocaml.org switched its documentation-build backend from sage to dill and added build-status links on package pages, by Jon Ludlam (ocaml/ocaml.org#3716).

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    Opam-repository had a heavy release week (opam 2.6.0 alpha, MirageOS/TLS/cohttp trains) while ocaml.org migrated its docs backend from sage to dill.

    New Features

  • opam 2.6.0~alpha1 preview published covering 8 packages (opam-client, opam-core, opam-devel, opam-format, opam-installer, opam-repository, opam-solver, opam-state) by Kate (ocaml/opam-repository#30284)
  • First release of CamlSurf (CamlSurf-wayland, CamlSurf-x11), a new windowing/graphics package, by Christophe Raffalli (ocaml/opam-repository#30356)
  • hedgehog and hedgehog-alcotest property-based testing libraries published as new packages by Tim McGilchrist (ocaml/opam-repository#30369)
  • jsonkit and jsonkit-melange added as new JSON libraries ported from melange-community/jsonkit by Pedro Lisboa (ocaml/opam-repository#30377)
  • bcfg and bcfgt configuration libraries introduced as new packages by Calascibetta Romain (ocaml/opam-repository#30373)
  • granary and granary_repl 0.0.3 published as new packages by Tej Pochiraju (ocaml/opam-repository#30362)
  • Gles3 bindings refreshed with new X11 and Wayland backends and an updated conf-gles2 depext fixing openSUSE builds, by Christophe Raffalli (ocaml/opam-repository#30334)
  • mirage-crypto, mirage-crypto-ec/pk/rng (6 packages) released at 2.2.0 and tls/tls-async/tls-eio/tls-lwt/tls-miou-unix/tls-mirage (6 packages) released at 2.1.2, by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#30344, ocaml/opam-repository#30350)
  • mirage and mirage-runtime 4.11.2 released by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#30354)
  • cohttp release train (15 packages including cohttp, cohttp-eio, cohttp-lwt-unix, cohttp-mirage, cohttp-curl-*) published at 6.2.2 by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml/opam-repository#30339)
  • capnp-rpc, capnp-rpc-net, capnp-rpc-unix released at 2.1.2 by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml/opam-repository#30375)
  • merlin, merlin-lib, ocaml-index, dot-merlin-reader released at 5.8.1-505 by Ulysse (ocaml/opam-repository#30380)
  • mnet-dhcp added as a new sub-package of the mnet (7-package) release 0.0.4 by Calascibetta Romain (ocaml/opam-repository#30374)
  • Introcaml 5.5.0 published as an alpha preview of OCaml with polymorphic printing support by Frédéric Bour (ocaml/opam-repository#30379)
  • dscheck 0.6.0 released by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml/opam-repository#30387)
  • Fixed bad checksum on res_tailwindcss.0.1.3 after its upstream repo moved from green-labs to mununki, by Dmitrii Kosarev (ocaml/opam-repository#30349, closes ocaml/opam-repository#30243)
  • Added an OCaml 5.5-compatible ocamlfind preview package (ocamlfind.1.9.9~preview) to work around ld.conf parsing and MSYS2 gaps, by David Allsopp (ocaml/opam-repository#30285)
  • ocaml.org now links package pages to a documentation build-status page on the new docs server: the "No Docs" indicator and the documentation-not-found page both point to package.documentation_status_url instead of a static message or a "Report Missing Docs" GitHub-issue link, by Jon Ludlam (ocaml/ocaml.org#3716)
  • ocaml.org added a new OCAMLORG_DOC_STATUS_URL configuration variable and Ocamlorg_package.Documentation.doc_status_url API, switching the default documentation source from sage.ci.dev to dill.caelum.ci.dev (ocaml/ocaml.org#3716)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/opam-repository: heavy package-release week including an opam 2.6.0~alpha1 preview (8 packages, ocaml/opam-repository#30284), MirageOS/TLS release trains, a 15-package cohttp release (ocaml/opam-repository#30339), and at least six brand-new packages
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: migrated the package documentation backend from sage to dill and added build-status links on package pages (ocaml/ocaml.org#3716), alongside routine security and library team roster updates (ocaml/ocaml.org#3728, ocaml/ocaml.org#3725)
  • Combined, the group merged roughly 30 package-release PRs on opam-repository and 5 code/config PRs on ocaml.org this week, with several open PRs awaiting review on each side
  • A new opam-repository policy proposal on requiring human authorship for maintainer replies to AI-generated submissions was opened by Calascibetta Romain (ocaml/opam-repository#30367)

    • Activity

  • Newly opened opam-repository PRs not yet merged include mirror fixes for rfsm.1.5 and archiving of pxshot.0.1.2/vecosek by Dmitrii Kosarev (ocaml/opam-repository#30363, ocaml/opam-repository#30385, ocaml/opam-repository#30386), a more flexible libcurl depext for Debian/Ubuntu by madroach (ocaml/opam-repository#30360), and OCaml 5.6 previews of merlin/ocaml-lsp by Ulysse (ocaml/opam-repository#30382)
  • Other open opam-repository submissions awaiting review include mariadb.2.0.0 by Petter A. Urkedal (ocaml/opam-repository#30343), lmdb.1.1.2 by madroach (ocaml/opam-repository#30198), Windows x-ci-accept-failures CI support by shym (ocaml/opam-repository#28856), and colibri2 (4 packages) by François Bobot (ocaml/opam-repository#30097)
  • Frama-C ecosystem releases landed on opam-repository: frama-c-metacsl 0.10 (ocaml/opam-repository#29308), frama-c-lannotate 0.2.5 (ocaml/opam-repository#29344), and Frama-C itself at 32.1-Germanium (stable) and 33.0~beta-Arsenic by Allan Blanchard (ocaml/opam-repository#30016, ocaml/opam-repository#30136)
  • Several first-time opam-repository package submissions were closed without merging: shibboleth.0.0.5 by Asher Frost (ocaml/opam-repository#29402), par/par_cli.0.4.8 by JC (ocaml/opam-repository#30086), and product.0.1.1 by José Serratos (ocaml/opam-repository#30359)
  • An automated ocaml.org platform releases PR from scrape_platform_releases.yml remains open, tracking new OCaml Platform tool releases (ocaml/ocaml.org#3693)
  • ocaml.org security team roster updated by Hannes Mehnert, adding Reynir Björnsson and refining his robur.coop affiliation (ocaml/ocaml.org#3728, ocaml/ocaml.org#3729); the Standard Library team page was also updated by Nicolás Ojeda Bär (ocaml/ocaml.org#3725)
  • Routine OCaml Planet blog aggregation on ocaml.org picked up new posts, including Anil Madhavapeddy's .plan-26-30 update, OCaml Weekly News for 28 Jul 2026, and a robur.coop post on autoscaling MirageOS unikernels (ocaml/ocaml.org#3726, ocaml/ocaml.org#3727)

    • Notable Discussions

  • On the proposed revert of the ocaml.org docs-server switch (ocaml/ocaml.org#3731), Cuihtlauac Alvarado documented the root cause — the new dill docs server omitted the doc/README.html, doc/CHANGES.html and doc/LICENSE.html pages that the old sage server produced — before Jon Ludlam confirmed the issue had since been resolved server-side, avoiding the need for a revert

    • Emerging Trends

  • Coordinated multi-package release trains remain common on opam-repository: cohttp (15 packages, ocaml/opam-repository#30339), mnet (7 packages, ocaml/opam-repository#30374), mirage-crypto (6 packages, ocaml/opam-repository#30344), tls (6 packages, ocaml/opam-repository#30350), and opam itself (8 packages, ocaml/opam-repository#30284)
  • Hannes Mehnert and Calascibetta Romain account for a large share of this week's MirageOS-adjacent releases (mirage, mirage-crypto, tls, utcp, mnet, miou, vif, flux, mkernel, mtbox, crunch), reflecting ongoing coordinated maintenance across that ecosystem
  • Several first-time opam-repository package submissions were auto-generated via opam-publish and closed without merge (ocaml/opam-repository#29402, ocaml/opam-repository#30086, ocaml/opam-repository#30359), prompting a new policy proposal on AI-generated maintainer responses (ocaml/opam-repository#30367)
  • Packages continue adding explicit upper bounds ahead of opam 2.6, and OCaml 5.5/5.6 previews (ocamlfind, merlin, Introcaml) are being staged alongside stable releases (ocaml/opam-repository#30284, ocaml/opam-repository#30285, ocaml/opam-repository#30382, ocaml/opam-repository#30379)
  • Continued reliance on the external ocaml-docs-ci pipeline for package documentation, with ocaml.org adapting quickly (config, UI links, and a near-revert) as that pipeline's backend server changed from sage to dill (ocaml/ocaml.org#3716, ocaml/ocaml.org#3731)
  • Routine upkeep of team governance pages (security and library teams) on ocaml.org, keeping data/governance.yml and data/pages/security.md in sync with team membership (ocaml/ocaml.org#3725, ocaml/ocaml.org#3728, ocaml/ocaml.org#3729)

    • OCaml Tools

    Merlin released 5.8.1 with race and staleness fixes, dune fixed RPC and alias bugs, and ocaml-lsp enabled inlay hints by default this week.

    New Features

  • ocaml/dune: added an --include-empty flag to dune describe external-lib-deps so dependency-free libraries are still listed, by Nat Karmios (ocaml/dune#15585, fixes ocaml/dune#15566); fixed a rule/alias bug that leaked actions between aliases on target-less multi-alias rules, by Nat Karmios (ocaml/dune#15581, fixes ocaml/dune#15576); dune pkg enabled now queries a running RPC server for transient --pkg enabled/disabled settings, by Ali Caglayan (ocaml/dune#15589); fixed RPC registry polling to reliably rescan on mtime changes so clients like ocaml-lsp discover new instances, by Rudi Grinberg (ocaml/dune#15634); added Windows Proc.wait support for the typed process API (ocaml/dune#15536); and roughly halved time/allocation for module alias generation via String_builder, by Antonio Nuno Monteiro (ocaml/dune#15657)
  • ocaml/merlin: released 5.8.1, fixing ocaml-index staleness detection for ppx-preprocessed files (ocaml/merlin#2110) by Liam Stevenson, a loadpath invalidation race across concurrent typer instances (ocaml/merlin#2109), and a document query that returned a neighboring constructor's or field's doc comment (ocaml/merlin#2092) by Liam Stevenson; also published a 5.8.1-506~preview build with experimental OCaml 5.6 support (https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/releases/tag/v5.8.1-506preview)

    • OCaml Core

    Coordinated typechecker-performance fixes resolved a js_of_ocaml compile-time blowup; native-atomics and Hashtbl-determinism work advanced.

    New Features

  • Typechecking-performance work on the js_of_ocaml/Lwt compilation-time blowup continued, with occurs-check elision for fresh type variables during instantiation by Stefan Muenzel cutting the offending file from 10 minutes to 5 seconds (ocaml/ocaml#14913), and further type-path equivalence normalization optimizations by Gabriel Scherer merged via ocaml/ocaml#14952 (building on ocaml/ocaml#14947 and ocaml/ocaml#14950), bringing the same case down to 170ms (ocaml/ocaml#14897).
  • Stdlib additions: Dynarray.append_iarray and Pqueue.of_iarray by Nicolás Ojeda Bär close a gap for converting immutable arrays without unsafe code (ocaml/ocaml#14909, fixes ocaml/ocaml#14320), and Option.try_value/Result.try_value were added (ocaml/ocaml#14941).
  • Fixed a pattern-matching switch overflow bug where the integer-overflow guard failed to account for abs min_int = min_int, by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml#14890).
  • Fixed a memory leak in the runtime caused by an unbounded internal cache of stacks (ocaml/ocaml#14940).
  • Fixed the generated compiler-cloning script used by opam to work inside opam's sandbox on macOS, where an old bash version broke here-document handling, by David Allsopp (ocaml/ocaml#14923).
  • OCAMLTOP_INCLUDE_PATH is now ignored during the build, preventing environment leakage into build steps (ocaml/ocaml#14871, ocaml/ocaml#14914).
  • Fixed a docstring typo in Bigarray.Array2.init that reversed the description of dim1/dim2, by Tristan F.-R. (ocaml/ocaml#14973).
  • Added documentation on the ocamllex -w command-line argument to the man page (ocaml/ocaml#14902, ocaml/ocaml#14944).

    • Overview

  • Activity this week was concentrated entirely in ocaml/ocaml; ocaml/RFCs recorded no repository activity.
  • A coordinated multi-contributor effort resolved a typechecker performance pathology surfaced by jsofocaml/Lwt builds, cutting compilation time on the offending file from 10 minutes to 170ms (ocaml/ocaml#14897, ocaml/ocaml#14913, ocaml/ocaml#14952).
  • Nine new PRs were opened, spanning native atomics, a new Hashtbl implementation, win32/Sys fixes, and stdlib proposals.
  • Design discussion continued on a new Hashtbl implementation for deterministic iteration order, feeding a broader RFC discussion on hash-flooding protection (ocaml/ocaml#14956, ocaml/ocaml#14967).
  • Build-system and POWER-architecture maintenance continued alongside stdlib additions such as Dynarray.append_iarray (ocaml/ocaml#14909) and a runtime memory-leak fix (ocaml/ocaml#14940).

    • Activity

  • Nine PRs opened this week span runtime, typing, and stdlib work: Zane Hambly proposed generating native atomic exchange/compare_and_set instructions across all five backends, replacing C calls with inline assembly on amd64/arm64/riscv/power/s390x (ocaml/ocaml#14980); Gabriel Scherer opened a re-implementation of Weak.Make hashsets using open-addressing with linear probing, reporting a 30% speedup on alt-ergo-free (ocaml/ocaml#14979); 314eter proposed fixing with module type precedence so = and := behave consistently, a breaking change for existing uses of the old precedence (ocaml/ocaml#14978); Romain Beauxis fixed a win32 select handle leak reported by liquidsoap users (ocaml/ocaml#14975); Khalid proposed Sys.filepath_exists as a safer alternative to Sys.file_exists (ocaml/ocaml#14974); Gabriel Scherer proposed enabling -g by default in the bytecode compiler to close the debugging gap with ocamlopt (ocaml/ocaml#14971); Tim McGilchrist opened two runtime-events fixes, correcting a minor_allocated_bytes unit-conversion bug (ocaml/ocaml#14969) and adding a missing EV_MINOR_EPHE_CLEAN constructor that crashed consumers on out-of-range values (ocaml/ocaml#14966); Xavier Van de Woestyne continued the typing-recovery work needed for Merlin (ocaml/ocaml#14963); and Török Edwin opened a draft exposing that Atomic.t is not a float in the interface to improve code generation (ocaml/ocaml#14977, following ocaml/ocaml#14976).
  • The typechecker path-equivalence and occurs-check performance work triggered by ocaml/ocaml#14897 (jsofocaml compile-time blowup) was resolved this week through coordinated contributions from Stefan Muenzel (ocaml/ocaml#14900, ocaml/ocaml#14913) and Gabriel Scherer/Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml#14927, ocaml/ocaml#14947, ocaml/ocaml#14950, ocaml/ocaml#14952), taking typechecking time on the offending file from 10 minutes to 170ms.
  • Ongoing native atomics work builds on the earlier fetch-and-add landing (ocaml/ocaml#14575), with Zane Hambly's new exchange/compare_and_set PR (ocaml/ocaml#14980) discussing a follow-up to unify with Gabriel Scherer's proposed compare_and_exchange (ocaml/ocaml#14912), while Török Edwin separately proposes exposing that Atomic.t excludes floats for better inlining (ocaml/ocaml#14977).
  • Extensive design discussion continued on a new Hashtbl implementation guaranteeing deterministic iteration order by Jeannalyse (ocaml/ocaml#14956), with detailed benchmarking trade-offs explored by Gabriel Scherer and Stefan Muenzel, feeding into the broader RFC (ocaml/ocaml#14967) and the older randomized-seeding proposal by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/ocaml#14291).

    • Notable Discussions

  • Make unlabeled applications fine again? by Gabriel Scherer revisits whether OCaml's existing (but discouraged since warning 6) support for calling labeled functions unlabeled could ease adding labels to existing APIs without breaking callers, spun out of the Atomic.compare_and_exchange labeling debate (ocaml/ocaml#14912).
  • RFC: Hashtbl: remember insertion order to guarantee deterministic iteration by Gabriel Scherer proposes an internal doubly-linked list to make Hashtbl iteration deterministic even with randomized seeding, weighing a roughly 42% memory overhead against enabling hash-flooding protection by default, with alternatives (a new Hashmap module, Go-style intentional randomization) surveyed against Python/PHP/Ruby/Java precedent; it directly informs ocaml/ocaml#14956 and ocaml/ocaml#14291.
