  • Disclosed LLM-assisted contributions are becoming more visible in PR descriptions, for example a bug investigation credited to LLM assistance in ocaml/ocaml#14975 and disclosed LLM use per OCaml's AI policy in ocaml/ocaml#14933.

    • Multicore

    Eio split path handling into per-backend modules and sped up directory traversal; ocaml-uring triaged a Debian flaky-test report.

    New Features

  • Directory traversal sped up roughly 30% on directories with around a million files by increasing the getdents64 stack buffer from PATH_MAX + sizeof(dirent64) to a fixed 65536 bytes, cutting syscalls by an order of magnitude and also helping network filesystems, by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#910)
  • Path splitting and joining moved out of the frontend into per-backend Eio.Fs.Pi.PATH implementations, with a new Eio_utils.Posix_path module providing POSIX behavior and laying groundwork for Windows-specific path support, by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#913)
  • Eio.Path.split for POSIX paths reworked to scan the string directly instead of allocating intermediate lists, reducing allocation, by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#915)
  • Fixed fstat, mkdir, symlink creation/reading, chmod, chown and directory listing failing on eio_posix when applied directly to an unconfined fs handle, since fstatat(AT_FDCWD, "", ...) rejects empty paths, by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#907, fixes ocaml-multicore/eio#906)

    • Overview

  • ocaml-multicore/eio merged four PRs reworking path handling into per-backend modules and speeding up directory traversal, plus opened three more still under review or in draft
  • ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring had no commits merged; activity was limited to a single issue thread about a Debian-packaging test failure (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#161)
  • ocaml-multicore/domainslib, ocaml-multicore/meio, ocaml-multicore/saturn, ocaml-multicore/eio-trace, ocaml-multicore/picos, ocaml-multicore/kcas, and ocaml-multicore/ocaml-iomux recorded no activity for this period

    • Activity

  • ocaml-multicore/eio: a 32-bit build fix was opened for MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC overflowing OCaml's native int on 32-bit platforms, by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#917, addressing ocaml-multicore/eio#909)
  • ocaml-multicore/eio: a draft implementing Eio.Path.native as a backend interface with Windows support was split off from a larger patch, by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#916), alongside the original Windows path-handling draft it was split from, now marked conflicting, by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#908); review between the two converged on treating paths lexically and possibly rejecting drive-relative paths like C:foo
  • ocaml-multicore/eio: a draft adding device mknod support for creating device files beyond FIFOs was opened by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#911), prompting discussion on sharing the feature with eio_linux, a portable Eio.File.Dev.t type, and handling device numbers on platforms like Wayland where they don't fit a fixed-width field
  • ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring: Stéphane Glondu opened an issue describing intermittent failures in tests/main.md when packaging ocaml-uring 2.15.0 for Debian, where a section of tests hangs on almost all Debian build machines though not on his own workstation, and proposed a patch tolerating read/write failures instead of asserting exact results (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#161); no PRs were opened or merged, and main saw no new commits since the v2.15.0 release

    • Notable Discussions

  • On ocaml-multicore/eio#909, whether Eio should support 32-bit at all was debated: Thomas Leonard suggested restricting eio.unix to 64-bit only, Stéphane Glondu noted Debian still officially supports armhf and i386, and Anil Madhavapeddy proposed following OCaml upstream's guidance of bytecode-only on 32-bit, which ocaml-multicore/eio#917 later addressed pragmatically
  • On ocaml-multicore/eio#914, an allocation of 23 words per trace event was traced to Runtime_events.User.write; Thomas Gazagnaire reported the repro, Thomas Leonard pinpointed an unnecessary closure allocation in upstream runtime_events.ml, and Anil Madhavapeddy began benchmarking a single-buffer fix, looping in Sadiq Jaffer
  • On ocaml-multicore/eio#912, the need for directory fsync was raised to make journal-then-rename patterns durable in an embedded database; Anil Madhavapeddy agreed a path-based sync in Fs.Pi.DIR is reasonable and noted fdatasync may also be needed
  • On ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#161, Thomas Leonard asked what kernel version was running on the affected CI machines, suggesting a hanging pipe read likely indicates a prior write failed rather than a kernel-specific bug, and Stéphane Glondu replied with the kernel version (6.12.96+deb13-arm64) from his debugging session

    • Emerging Trends

  • Path handling is being restructured into backend-specific modules in ocaml-multicore/eio (POSIX now, Windows next), spanning ocaml-multicore/eio#908, ocaml-multicore/eio#913, ocaml-multicore/eio#915, and ocaml-multicore/eio#916
  • Large draft PRs are being split into smaller reviewable pieces, as with Anil Madhavapeddy's ocaml-multicore/eio#908 being carved into ocaml-multicore/eio#913, ocaml-multicore/eio#915, and ocaml-multicore/eio#916
  • Debian packaging surfaced portability friction independently in two repositories, with Stéphane Glondu reporting a 32-bit build failure in eio (ocaml-multicore/eio#909) and a Debian arm64 flaky test in ocaml-uring (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#161)
  • Renewed focus on allocation profiling of hot paths continued in eio, spanning the tracing, getdents, and path-split work (ocaml-multicore/eio#914, ocaml-multicore/eio#910, ocaml-multicore/eio#915)
  • Activity across the group remained concentrated in eio, with seven of the nine tracked repositories (ocaml-multicore/domainslib, ocaml-multicore/meio, ocaml-multicore/saturn, ocaml-multicore/eio-trace, ocaml-multicore/picos, ocaml-multicore/kcas, ocaml-multicore/ocaml-iomux) showing no recorded activity
entry.summary: Merlin 5.8.1 and an ocaml-lsp 1.28.0 preview shipped, oxcaml/oxcaml landed AVX-512 SIMD, and core resolved a typechecker performance pathology.

entry.title: Week 30, 2026: Eio 1.4, dune 3.24.1 and opam 2.6.0-alpha1 all released this week, while oxcaml/oxcaml opened a coordinated wave of Flambda 2 planning issues and core landed new Option/Result stdlib helpers.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • Multicore ocaml-multicore/eio published the v1.4 release (ocaml-multicore/eio#904), adding Flow.null by Anil Madhavapeddy and Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#894), a macOS select() fallback for poll()'s POLLNVAL misreporting (ocaml-multicore/eio#893, fixes ocaml-multicore/eio#757), and hostname-qualified Net.getaddrinfo error messages by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#900)
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/dune released 3.24.1 (ocaml/dune#15539), fixing build_runtime_flags being silently ignored for js_of_ocaml/wasm_of_ocaml executables in separate compilation (ocaml/dune#15455) and %{bin:...} PATH resolution on Windows (ocaml/dune#15518); separately merged fish-shell completion by Chizy (ocaml/dune#15515) and dune promote tab completion by Ali Caglayan (ocaml/dune#15338)
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/opam released 2.6.0-alpha1 (ocaml/opam#7047) by Kate, bundling .install root/rootexec sections for prefix-relative installs (ocaml/opam#6938) and a new --ignore-available-on flag by Brian Ward (ocaml/opam#6836)
  • OxCaml oxcaml/oxcaml landed layout-polymorphic functions (let poly_ f x = ...) by Jack Rickard (oxcaml/oxcaml#5870) and distinct unsigned unboxed integer primitive types (uint8_u, uint16_u, uint32_u, uint64_u) by Max Slater (oxcaml/oxcaml#6534), later gated behind the small_numbers extension with a new unativeint_u type (oxcaml/oxcaml#6634)
  • OCaml Core ocaml/ocaml merged new Option.try_value/Result.try_value stdlib functions by Michael Neumann (ocaml/ocaml#14941) and a public Obj.hash_variant function by David Allsopp (ocaml/ocaml#14939), plus a runtime fiber/stack-cache memory-leak fix by Vesa Karvonen and Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml#14940)
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/merlin shipped destructuring of open record patterns by Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac, resolving a request open since 2015 (ocaml/merlin#2103, fixes ocaml/merlin#436)
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/ocaml-lsp added LSP trace notifications for Dune RPC and build-progress activity (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1899) and a code action to open the closest Dune file (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1817), both by Rudi Grinberg
  • OCaml Ecosystem ocaml/opam-repository added eight new packages, including cascade and tw by Thomas Gazagnaire (ocaml/opam-repository#30280, ocaml/opam-repository#30314) and ocaml-sbom by Martin Jambon (ocaml/opam-repository#30292), and merged Frama-C 33.0 "Arsenic" by Allan Blanchard (ocaml/opam-repository#30323)

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    Opam-repository shipped dune 3.24.1, eio 1.4 and frama-c 33.0 plus eight new packages, while ocaml.org published the Dune 3.24.0 release page.

    New Features

  • Eight new packages added to opam-repository: cascade and tw by Thomas Gazagnaire (ocaml/opam-repository#30280, ocaml/opam-repository#30314); theo and wax/wax-lib by Jérôme Vouillon (ocaml/opam-repository#30279, ocaml/opam-repository#30278); noise by Race (ocaml/opam-repository#30288); ocaml-sbom by Martin Jambon (ocaml/opam-repository#30292); robotstxt by Albert Peschar (ocaml/opam-repository#30307); and termaid by Alex Leighton (ocaml/opam-repository#30287)
  • Dune 3.24.1 patch release merged across 18 opam-repository packages by Ali Caglayan (ocaml/opam-repository#30298), with its ocaml.org changelog announcement opened the same week (ocaml/ocaml.org#3723)
  • Eio 1.4 released across 5 packages by Thomas Leonard (ocaml/opam-repository#30318)
  • Frama-C 33.0 "Arsenic" released by Allan Blanchard (ocaml/opam-repository#30323)
  • OCaml 5.5 readiness in opam-repository: a macOS switch-creation fix disabling compiler cloning by Kate (ocaml/opam-repository#30317), and an ocamlfind 1.9.9~preview package adding 5.5 compatibility by David Allsopp (ocaml/opam-repository#30285)
  • ocaml.org published the Dune 3.24.0 platform release page covering the new %{pkg::
    :} pform and the relocatable compiler now enabled by default for package management, by Shon Feder (ocaml/ocaml.org#3704)
  • ocaml.org added Jérôme Vouillon's blog to the OCaml Planet aggregator (ocaml/ocaml.org#3722)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/opam-repository: added eight new packages and shipped major upstream releases — dune 3.24.1 across 18 packages (ocaml/opam-repository#30298), eio 1.4 across 5 packages (ocaml/opam-repository#30318), and frama-c 33.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#30323)
  • OCaml 5.5 compatibility work continued with a macOS switch-creation fix (ocaml/opam-repository#30317) and a 5.5-compatible ocamlfind preview (ocaml/opam-repository#30285)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: published the Dune 3.24.0 platform release page (ocaml/ocaml.org#3704), continued the opam package version display rework (ocaml/ocaml.org#3713), and added a new Planet aggregator blog feed (ocaml/ocaml.org#3722)
  • Group activity centered on opam-repository's package growth and release triage, while ocaml.org's work focused on documenting those releases and clarifying how package version data is presented to end users

    • Activity

  • opam-repository merged package updates for cvc5, goblint-cil, ppx_deriving/ppx_deriving_hash, decompress 1.6.0, gmp, ca-certs-nss, qcow, docfd, and the hegel/ppx_hegel_* group, alongside new menhir tooling (menhirformat, menhir-lsp) and other new packages (lstar/lstar-rocq, fungi, shakuhachi, sqlgg, ppx_matches, ppx_deriving_melange, jingoo) (ocaml/opam-repository#30289, ocaml/opam-repository#30321, ocaml/opam-repository#30300, ocaml/opam-repository#30302)
  • Several new package submissions remained blocked on CI: Philippe Strauss's plcairo, sndfile and dspml trio failing on missing system dependencies (ocaml/opam-repository#30297, ocaml/opam-repository#30296, ocaml/opam-repository#30295); Christophe Raffalli's conf-gles2/conf-gles3 rework (ocaml/opam-repository#30334); and François Bobot's colibri2 0.6 update awaiting rebase (ocaml/opam-repository#30097)
  • Earlier quickjs 0.5.0 and server-reason-react 0.5.0 submissions by David Sancho were superseded by 0.5.1 releases merged this week (ocaml/opam-repository#30311, ocaml/opam-repository#30312)
  • On ocaml.org, Nicolás Ojeda Bär opened a library team governance documentation update (ocaml/ocaml.org#3725); Akhil Indurti opened a wasm-gc documentation fix for the WebAssembly tutorial (ocaml/ocaml.org#3719); the opam package version display rework by Sora Morimoto continued under review awaiting Jon Ludlam (ocaml/ocaml.org#3713); the automated platform-releases scrape PR remained open (ocaml/ocaml.org#3693); and three automated Planet scrape runs merged new community blog and video content (ocaml/ocaml.org#3720, ocaml/ocaml.org#3721, ocaml/ocaml.org#3724)

    • Notable Discussions

  • opam-repository reviewers debated whether to remove simple_httpd.1.0 outright after a checksum error, favoring available: false per repository policy, with input from Jan Midtgaard, Hannes Mehnert, Marcello Seri and Dmitrii Kosarev (ocaml/opam-repository#30330, ocaml/opam-repository#30123)
  • Naming and licensing of the new ocaml-sbom package were discussed against the policy discouraging ocaml-prefixed names, with Jan Midtgaard and Raphaël Proust weighing an exception (ocaml/opam-repository#30292)
  • Christophe Raffalli detailed platform-specific gaps in conf-gles2/conf-gles3 coverage across openSUSE, FreeBSD and macOS, with a companion fix proposed (ocaml/opam-repository#30336, ocaml/opam-repository#30334)
  • Dmitri Volkov raised whether conf-sdl2 should depend on sdl2-compat rather than sdl2 on macOS, since Homebrew aliases the two (ocaml/opam-repository#30337)
  • A forum report that the opam package versions page could be misread as listing release dates and recommending every version shown, when dates actually reflect opam-repository submission times, led Sora Morimoto to rework the page's version selection and labeling (ocaml/ocaml.org#3713)

    • Emerging Trends

  • OCaml 5.5 readiness work continues across opam-repository, including the macOS compiler-cloning fix (ocaml/opam-repository#30317) and the ocamlfind 5.5-compatible preview package (ocaml/opam-repository#30285)
  • Maintainers Jan Midtgaard and Raphaël Proust are actively triaging revdeps CI failures before merging, catching regressions in soteria (ocaml/opam-repository#30315), server-reason-react (ocaml/opam-repository#30311) and menhirformat (ocaml/opam-repository#30327)
  • opam-repository's package-lifecycle policy favors available: false over deletion for broken submissions, and duplicate re-submitted PRs are closed rather than left open (ocaml/opam-repository#30330, ocaml/opam-repository#30331, ocaml/opam-repository#30333)
  • Contributors continue to submit grouped multi-package releases in single PRs, such as dune's 18 packages (ocaml/opam-repository#30298), eio's 5 packages (ocaml/opam-repository#30318), and the hegel/ppx_hegel_* group (ocaml/opam-repository#30302)
  • Growing attention to accuracy of package/version metadata shown to end users, seen in ocaml.org's version-page rework prompted by forum feedback (ocaml/ocaml.org#3713) and its wasm-gc documentation fix (ocaml/ocaml.org#3719)
  • ocaml.org continues weekly automation of content sync via the Planet blog/video scraper (ocaml/ocaml.org#3720, ocaml/ocaml.org#3721, ocaml/ocaml.org#3724) and dune platform release announcements kept in sync with upstream (ocaml/ocaml.org#3704, ocaml/ocaml.org#3723)

    • OCaml Tools

    Dune shipped 3.24.1 and opam released 2.6.0-alpha1, fixing a same-day signing-key mixup, while merlin and ocaml-lsp advanced protocol work.

    New Features

  • ocaml/dune released 3.24.1 (ocaml/dune#15539) bundling several backports, and separately merged fish-shell completion by Chizy (ocaml/dune#15515), dune promote pending-file tab completion by Ali Caglayan (ocaml/dune#15338), and a move of artifact-substitution I/O onto the background thread pool by Antonio Nuno Monteiro (ocaml/dune#15559, ocaml/dune#15598)
  • ocaml/merlin shipped destructuring of open record patterns by Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac, resolving a request open since 2015 (ocaml/merlin#2103, fixes ocaml/merlin#436), and exposed a parse_warnings API by PixieDust (ocaml/merlin#2088)
  • ocaml/opam released 2.6.0-alpha1 by Kate, bundling .install root/rootexec sections (ocaml/opam#6938) and a new --ignore-available-on flag (ocaml/opam#6836)
  • ocaml/ocaml-lsp added LSP trace notifications for Dune RPC and build-progress activity (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1899), a code action to open the closest Dune file (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1817), and operator-aware semantic highlighting (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1831), all by Rudi Grinberg

    • Overview

  • ocaml/dune: released 3.24.1 (ocaml/dune#15539) after an opam-CI triage across 1,314 variants, shipped fish completion and promote completion, and opened dune describe/dune shell tooling PRs
  • ocaml/merlin: merged open-record destructuring and two occurrences-staleness fixes (ocaml/merlin#2104, ocaml/merlin#2097), plus an .mli open-path locate fix (ocaml/merlin#2089)
  • ocaml/ocamlfind: no merges this week; detailed commit-by-commit review continued on David Allsopp's relocatable-install PR (ocaml/ocamlfind#122)
  • ocaml/odoc: three OxCaml-compatibility PRs opened by @art-w (ocaml/odoc#1464, ocaml/odoc#1466, ocaml/odoc#1467); only a CI-action bump merged (ocaml/odoc#1463)
  • ocaml/opam: released 2.6.0-alpha1 (ocaml/opam#7047), then same-day triaged a release-signature mixup (ocaml/opam#7049) and a git fsmonitor bug (ocaml/opam#7054)
  • ocaml/opam-file-format: no recorded activity this week
  • ocaml-dune/spawn: no recorded activity this week
  • ocaml/ocaml-lsp: Rudi Grinberg shipped trace notifications, a Dune-file code action, and dozens of protocol fixes, and closed the OCaml-native test-suite rewrite tracker (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1063)
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml: Jérôme Vouillon's Wasm/WASI asset-resolution fix remained under review (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2389); Dependabot merged a changelog-action bump (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2408)

    • Activity

  • ocaml/dune: new unmerged PRs cover anonymous-action/alias semantics (ocaml/dune#15581), a dune describe --include-empty flag (ocaml/dune#15585), and a dune shell debugging prototype by Ali Caglayan (ocaml/dune#15597); Kris De Volder's report of a silent dune exec hang on execve failure (ocaml/dune#15602) was covered with regression tests the same day by Antonio Nuno Monteiro (ocaml/dune#15603)
  • ocaml/merlin: six PRs opened remain unmerged, including a typing-recovery preview by Xavier Van de Woestyne (ocaml/merlin#2087) and a regression test reproducing stale load paths by Rudi Grinberg (ocaml/merlin#2109); seven long-dormant issues from 2015-2021 were closed after backlog review led by Ulysse
  • ocaml/opam: Brian Ward's multi-PR cmdliner-based completion rewrite continued across four dependent PRs (ocaml/opam#6812, ocaml/opam#6867, ocaml/opam#6868, ocaml/opam#6869), and yannl35133 opened a clearer opam repo add error message (ocaml/opam#7014)
  • ocaml/ocaml-lsp: the OCaml-native test-suite rewrite (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1063) closed this week after converting dozens of bug reproductions into property-based tests; twenty further PRs opened on diagnostics pulls, code-action resolution, and semantic-token classification, and a batch of a dozen-plus long-standing issues were triaged and closed
  • ocaml/odoc: review continued on Tim ats's multi-line link-parsing fix, with detailed feedback from Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac on escaping semantics (ocaml/odoc#1439)

    • Notable Discussions

  • On the dune 3.24.1 release tracker, Ali Caglayan posted a detailed opam-CI triage summary covering 18 packages across 1,314 variants with no Dune-attributable regressions, and explained that a DragonFlyBSD support fix would wait for 3.25 rather than the patch release (ocaml/dune#15439)
  • Rudi Grinberg and Nat Karmios debated why anonymous dune actions attached to multiple aliases produce surprising inter-alias dependencies, agreeing human-readable action IDs were worth adding for dune shell (ocaml/dune#15576)
  • Akhil reported merlin-lib failing to build against OCaml 5.5.0; Ulysse and Kate discussed possible stale-stdlib causes without reproducing it on macOS (ocaml/merlin#2108)
  • @shym suggested in review that relocatable installation should become Findlib's default behaviour rather than an opt-in mode (ocaml/ocamlfind#122)
  • Benjamin Canou disclosed that his odoc fix was developed with AI assistance, with the regression test written by Claude (ocaml/odoc#1465)
  • The opam 2.6.0-alpha1 release signature was found to use the wrong GPG subkey shortly after publishing; Andriy Sultanov reported the failure and Kate traced it to a key-transfer mistake and re-signed the release the same day (ocaml/opam#7049)
  • Sora Morimoto documented a git fsmonitor socket breaking opam repository set-url and repository updates (ocaml/opam#7054)

    • Emerging Trends

  • AI-assisted contributions recurred across repos: a Windows fix authored directly by the copilot-swe-agent bot in merlin (ocaml/merlin#2095), Carine Morel disclosing Claude-assisted diagnosis before hand-authoring a merlin fix (ocaml/merlin#2089), and a Claude-written regression test in odoc (ocaml/odoc#1465)
  • Relocatable, reproducible installs are a shared theme ahead of OCaml 5.5: ocamlfind's in-progress relocatable-install PR (ocaml/ocamlfind#122) follows the definition proposed in ocaml/RFCs#53, while opam 2.6.0-alpha1 shipped root/rootexec .install sections for prefix-relative installs (ocaml/opam#6938)
  • Parallel shell-completion rewrites: dune shipped fish-shell completion and opened an issue to upstream it into cmdliner itself (ocaml/dune#15583), while opam's independent cmdliner-based completion overhaul continued across four PRs (ocaml/opam#6812, ocaml/opam#6867, ocaml/opam#6868, ocaml/opam#6869)
  • Backlog grooming of long-dormant issues stood out in both merlin (seven issues from 2015-2021 closed, ocaml/merlin#436, ocaml/merlin#1384) and ocaml-lsp (a dozen-plus old reports closed alongside the ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1063 test-suite rewrite)
  • OxCaml compiler compatibility continued incrementally in odoc, with three of four PRs opened this week addressing kind abbreviations, with-bounds handling, and parameterized libraries (ocaml/odoc#1467, ocaml/odoc#1466, ocaml/odoc#1464)
  • Concentrated solo maintenance in ocaml-lsp, where nearly all merged and opened work this week came from Rudi Grinberg

    • OxCaml

    oxcaml/oxcaml landed layout-polymorphic functions and unsigned unboxed integers; a Flambda 2 planning push began; opam-repository had one pending PR.

    New Features

  • Layout-polymorphic functions (let poly_ f x = ...) implemented across typedtree-to-tlambda and tlambda-to-slambda translation, along with application of such functions, by Jack Rickard (oxcaml/oxcaml#5870)
  • Distinct unsigned unboxed integer primitive types (uint8_u, uint16_u, uint32_u, uint64_u) added with the same kinds as their signed counterparts, letting the compiler distinguish signed and unsigned unboxed integers, by Max Slater (oxcaml/oxcaml#6534), which were then guarded behind the small_numbers extension along with a new unativeint_u type in the same follow-up (oxcaml/oxcaml#6634)
  • New -modules-only flag for ocamldep that behaves like -modules but omits the leading file: prefix from each output line, letting build rules consume dependency output directly without shell postprocessing, by Jakub Staroń (oxcaml/oxcaml#6540)
  • -dprofile now works in combination with -stop-after middle_end, fixing a case where profiling output was previously suppressed by the early exit, by Basile Clément (oxcaml/oxcaml#6550)
  • Emitter plumbing added across backend code emitters to enable compact frametables, laying groundwork for shorter frametables tracked in oxcaml/oxcaml#6399, by Nick Barnes (oxcaml/oxcaml#6488)
  • New split statement added to ocamltest, by Luke Maurer (oxcaml/oxcaml#6422)
  • Type shapes for any fields implemented, allowing a type shape to be constructed even when field layouts of an any-kinded field are unknown, by Luke Maurer (oxcaml/oxcaml#6403)
  • Fixed a crash when an any type variable resolves to an unboxed product, by Luke Maurer (oxcaml/oxcaml#6436)
  • Fixed unsound argument value kinds in partial GADT matches, where calling-convention specialization could select the wrong value representation across GADT cases, by Ryan Tjoa (oxcaml/oxcaml#6356, oxcaml/oxcaml#6533)
  • Fixed reversed logic in contains_no_escaping_local_allocs for unboxed function wrappers, by Jules Jacobs (oxcaml/oxcaml#6558)
  • Fixed float32 double-rounding bug, by Luke Maurer (oxcaml/oxcaml#6474)
  • Fixed %makearray_dynamic for float kinds under -no-flat-float-array, by Jules Jacobs (oxcaml/oxcaml#6486)
  • Fixed missing safepoints (polls) in loops that only allocate locally, with a codegen test added to exhibit the bug before the fix, by Xavier Clerc (oxcaml/oxcaml#6469)
  • Removed unnecessary caml_modify calls for existential immediate types in mixed blocks and via better value kinds for type variables, reducing write-barrier overhead, by Ryan Tjoa (oxcaml/oxcaml#6631, oxcaml/oxcaml#6633)
  • Recursive-module unroll depth is now chosen adaptively for large module groups instead of using a fixed bound, by Jules Jacobs (oxcaml/oxcaml#6532)
  • Parameter allocation modes are now kept in sync when unboxing closures in the reaper, by Miriam Vellacott (oxcaml/oxcaml#6543), who also split the reaper into stages for LTO and added reaper-rebuild/reaper-solve entry points (oxcaml/oxcaml#6627, oxcaml/oxcaml#6632)
  • Dissector link-input resolution reworked to parse each partition once and parallelize partial linking, by Simon Spies (oxcaml/oxcaml#6447), building on resolving link inputs' object files through manifests by Jakub Staroń (oxcaml/oxcaml#6468)
  • Custom [@@or_null] variants now get the same precise kind as or_null, by Jules Jacobs (oxcaml/oxcaml#6500)
  • Platform symbol prefix stripped from DW_AT_linkage_name in DWARF debug info, by Mark Shinwell (oxcaml/oxcaml#6506)

    • Overview

  • Two of the five repositories in the group had recorded activity this week: oxcaml/oxcaml and oxcaml/opam-repository; oxcaml/merlin, oxcaml/jsofocaml, and janestreet/opam-repository had no tracked commits or pull requests.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml landed layout-polymorphic functions (oxcaml/oxcaml#5870), distinct unsigned unboxed integer types (oxcaml/oxcaml#6534, oxcaml/oxcaml#6634), and a series of backend/Flambda2 correctness fixes, with 87 PRs open at week's end.
  • Mark Shinwell and Pierre Chambart opened a large, coordinated wave of Flambda 2 design and roadmap issues (oxcaml/oxcaml#6581-oxcaml/oxcaml#6629), the dominant theme of the week.
  • oxcaml/opam-repository saw a single PR from David Allsopp adding OxCaml compatibility for mdx.2.6.0 (oxcaml/opam-repository#55), left open pending a dune version fix.
  • Liam Stevenson continued Merlin synchronization work in oxcaml/oxcaml, landing the "Merlin for 5.4.0-ox3" sync (oxcaml/oxcaml#6557) even though the oxcaml/merlin repository itself recorded no activity this week.

    • Activity

  • Notable open, unmerged PRs from this week include Nick Barnes's rework of faulting safepoints (oxcaml/oxcaml#6551) and a #include cleanup in the runtime (oxcaml/oxcaml#6562); Vlad Turcuman's draft -runtime-variant baremetal (oxcaml/oxcaml#6549); Max Slater's draft AVX-512 intrinsics work (oxcaml/oxcaml#6578); Zesen Qian's -no-crc flag to drop a dependency's import-table rows for byte-stable artifacts (oxcaml/oxcaml#6561) and generic mode-axis exhaustion in out_type (oxcaml/oxcaml#6569); and Vincent Laviron's removal of mutable-string support in Flambda2 (oxcaml/oxcaml#6570)
  • @zhizhuoxin opened several related PRs on noalloc primitives and allocation-mode checking, including forcing allocation to be local (oxcaml/oxcaml#6548), a quick check for the allocation-mode axis (oxcaml/oxcaml#6559), and preventing noalloc primitives from forcing closures to allocate (oxcaml/oxcaml#6571), after an earlier no-stack variant was closed without merging (oxcaml/oxcaml#6547)
  • Jakub Bachurski opened a cluster of PRs on metaprogramming internals: consistent naming of quotes and splices (oxcaml/oxcaml#6575), renaming code to expr in Predef (oxcaml/oxcaml#6576), enabling ocamlformat in camlinternalQuote (oxcaml/oxcaml#6577), a dynamic scope extrusion check (oxcaml/oxcaml#6579), refactoring quoting of predefined names (oxcaml/oxcaml#6635), and fixes for mode constraints in quotes (oxcaml/oxcaml#6647), and merged an earlier fix avoiding ambiguous use of the phrase "top-level" in metaprogramming docs (oxcaml/oxcaml#6565)
  • Liam Stevenson continued Merlin synchronization work, merging an updated import script, build rules for Merlin, and enforcement that Merlin stays in sync (oxcaml/oxcaml#6034, oxcaml/oxcaml#6042, oxcaml/oxcaml#6245), landing the larger "Merlin for 5.4.0-ox3" sync (oxcaml/oxcaml#6557), and opening further synchronization changes and jkind-annotation fixups still under review (oxcaml/oxcaml#6563, oxcaml/oxcaml#6566); Kostia Balytskyi also merged an import of upstream ocaml/merlin PR 2104 (oxcaml/oxcaml#6555)
  • Backend and codegen work merged this week spans Xavier Clerc's CFG block merging for identical blocks differing only in debug info (oxcaml/oxcaml#6541), a Simplify_terminator fix (oxcaml/oxcaml#6370), skipping prologue/epilogue when computing liveness for stack checks (oxcaml/oxcaml#6472), and factoring a shared dead-code predicate into Cfg.is_dead_basic (oxcaml/oxcaml#6301), alongside Nathanaëlle Courant's x86 TEST-instead-of-CMP optimization for boolean materialization, co-authored with @ttebbi-janestreet (oxcaml/oxcaml#6552)
  • Flambda2 fixes merged include Basile Clément's restriction of relation recovery to relations that hold globally (oxcaml/oxcaml#6502) and a fix to stop silently forgetting about bottom (oxcaml/oxcaml#6347), and Basile Clément's in-progress work on Tmod type_desc infrastructure merged by Jules Jacobs (oxcaml/oxcaml#6430)
  • Flambda2 export info's table of contents was moved into CMX file sections by Jack Rickard (oxcaml/oxcaml#6455), and Is_parameter was moved to middle_end/ and recorded in Backend_var.Provenance by Mark Shinwell (oxcaml/oxcaml#6504), who also merged a fix comparing dinfo_uid in Debuginfo.Dbg.compare (oxcaml/oxcaml#6503)
  • Codegen test coverage expanded with James Rayman's tests for matching on unboxed ints (oxcaml/oxcaml#6391) and sign-extension fix for Typedtree.Const_untagged_char payloads (oxcaml/oxcaml#6535), and Xavier Clerc's [%%expect_asm_full] codegen-test attribute plus a stack-check/SIMD fix (oxcaml/oxcaml#6334)
  • Two mode-polymorphism PRs from Jules Jacobs on closure conventions when compiling against a .cmi and lowering generic mode variables in lower_nongen were closed without merging after review (oxcaml/oxcaml#6567, oxcaml/oxcaml#6568), alongside closures of a lock-free skiplist race-condition fix by Nick Barnes (oxcaml/oxcaml#6346) and driver flags -X gc-space-overhead/-X gc-idle-floor by Jules Jacobs (oxcaml/oxcaml#6485)
  • Mark Shinwell opened a large set of Flambda 2 design and planning issues covering breadth-first meet (oxcaml/oxcaml#6581), n-way join and its performance (oxcaml/oxcaml#6583, oxcaml/oxcaml#6586), lifted-constants restrictions (oxcaml/oxcaml#6588), enabling match-in-match, the reaper, functor size limits, and the new zero-alloc analysis in production on the JS tree (oxcaml/oxcaml#6589, oxcaml/oxcaml#6590, oxcaml/oxcaml#6591, oxcaml/oxcaml#6599), and closed a batch of older reaper/testing-infrastructure design issues as resolved (oxcaml/oxcaml#4693, oxcaml/oxcaml#4694, oxcaml/oxcaml#4696, oxcaml/oxcaml#4698, oxcaml/oxcaml#4700, oxcaml/oxcaml#5253, oxcaml/oxcaml#5271)
  • Pierre Chambart opened companion Flambda 2 issues on speculative inlining, argument-use estimation, code-size/cost-metric correctness, reducing and delaying CMX loading, lazy join, and splitting the typing environment between toplevel and function level (oxcaml/oxcaml#6582, oxcaml/oxcaml#6585, oxcaml/oxcaml#6587, oxcaml/oxcaml#6601, oxcaml/oxcaml#6602, oxcaml/oxcaml#6605, oxcaml/oxcaml#6607); Vincent Laviron opened related issues on Flambda2 logging, removing binary join, speculative variables, variant unboxing, better closure types, and dominator scoping during Simplify (oxcaml/oxcaml#6594, oxcaml/oxcaml#6600, oxcaml/oxcaml#6603, oxcaml/oxcaml#6604, oxcaml/oxcaml#6606, oxcaml/oxcaml#6608)
  • In oxcaml/opam-repository, David Allsopp opened a PR adding OxCaml compatibility for mdx.2.6.0 (oxcaml/opam-repository#55), a small four-line change across four files mirroring ocaml/opam-repository#30305, noting its second commit will be superseded once that upstream PR merges; the PR remains open and unmerged pending a dune-side fix.

    • Notable Discussions

  • Basic functorization support drew extended review discussion (oxcaml/oxcaml#5903)
  • Translating Flambda 2 phantom lets to Cmm generated substantial review commentary before landing (oxcaml/oxcaml#6519)
  • Simon Spies's Dissector rework to parse each partition once and parallelize partial linking prompted detailed review before merging (oxcaml/oxcaml#6447)
  • Tracking staticity of functors and their applications was actively discussed (oxcaml/oxcaml#6194)
  • The Datalog-based validator for cfg_simplify drew review feedback while still in draft (oxcaml/oxcaml#6564)
  • A new [unused-alert-disable] warning for alert disables that suppress nothing was discussed at length (oxcaml/oxcaml#6524)
  • On oxcaml/opam-repository#55, Anil Madhavapeddy noted the change needs a newer dune or else mdx rules break, pointing to ocaml/dune#15592 as the relevant fix.

    • Emerging Trends

  • Mark Shinwell and Pierre Chambart opened a coordinated wave of design and tracking issues for Flambda 2 (join algorithms, inlining, closure types, compilation-time improvements), suggesting a planning phase ahead of deeper Flambda 2 work (oxcaml/oxcaml#6581-oxcaml/oxcaml#6629)
  • Continued investment in Merlin synchronization with the upstream OCaml compiler, spanning import scripts, build rules, and jkind-annotation fixups, driven mainly by Liam Stevenson (oxcaml/oxcaml#6034, oxcaml/oxcaml#6042, oxcaml/oxcaml#6245, oxcaml/oxcaml#6557, oxcaml/oxcaml#6563, oxcaml/oxcaml#6566)
  • The reaper is being restructured for LTO in stages, with new reaper-rebuild/reaper-solve entry points, by Miriam Vellacott (oxcaml/oxcaml#6627, oxcaml/oxcaml#6632)
  • Unsigned unboxed integer types are being fleshed out and gated behind the small_numbers extension, indicating active refinement of the numeric-types surface area by Max Slater (oxcaml/oxcaml#6534, oxcaml/oxcaml#6634)
  • oxcaml/opam-repository activity remained minimal, with a single OxCaml-compatibility PR left open pending an external dune dependency (oxcaml/opam-repository#55), while oxcaml/merlin, oxcaml/jsofocaml, and janestreet/opam-repository had no recorded activity at all.

    • OCaml Core

    Stdlib gained `Option.try_value`/`Result.try_value` while a Hashtbl redesign proposal and a closed IO-channels PR drove an RFC removal.

    New Features

  • Standard library gains Option.try_value and Result.try_value, returning a fallback value or an error handler's result respectively, implemented by Michael Neumann with review by Daniel Bünzli and David Allsopp (ocaml/ocaml#14941)
  • Btype.hash_variant (the compiler's implementation of the runtime's caml_hash_variant) moved to a new public Obj.hash_variant function by David Allsopp (ocaml/ocaml#14939)
  • Toplevel gains limited support for tracing module-dependent functions via modular explicits, implemented by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml#14707)
  • Fixed a memory leak in the runtime by bounding the size of the internal fiber/stack cache, work by Vesa Karvonen and Florian Angeletti, merged by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml#14940)
  • Fixed RISC-V assembler errors from Ireturn_addr and Iextcall with stack arguments when the offset exceeds a 12-bit immediate, by Tim McGilchrist (ocaml/ocaml#14943)
  • Typing recovery mechanism extended to keep continuation information inside the Typedtree via a dedicated type, helping editors report more than one typing error, by Xavier Van de Woestyne (ocaml/ocaml#14946, ocaml/ocaml#14945)
  • Added a level to abbreviations in Texpand as part of the ongoing expansion/well-foundedness rework, by Jacques Garrigue (ocaml/ocaml#14801)
  • Overhauled the locale-handling code used for mingw/msvc float-to-string and string-to-float conversions in runtime/floats.c, by David Allsopp (ocaml/ocaml#10258)
  • OCAMLTOP_INCLUDE_PATH is now ignored during the build, fixing opam installation failures when the variable holds an invalid value, by David Allsopp (ocaml/ocaml#14914)
  • Added documentation for the ocamllex -w warning-list argument to the man page, covering the missing-case warning, by Jeannalyse (ocaml/ocaml#14944, closing ocaml/ocaml#14902)
  • Updated documentation for runtime functions using nanosleep, by David Allsopp (ocaml/ocaml#14948)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/ocaml merged nine PRs this week, including new Option.try_value/Result.try_value stdlib functions (ocaml/ocaml#14941) and a runtime fiber-cache memory-leak fix (ocaml/ocaml#14940)
  • A draft Hashtbl reimplementation for deterministic iteration order, submitted as a closing internship contribution by Jeannalyse, drew pushback over generic-structure performance tradeoffs (ocaml/ocaml#14956)
  • A cluster of typechecker path-equivalence refactors landed in ctype.ml from Gabriel Scherer and Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml#14947, ocaml/ocaml#14950, ocaml/ocaml#14952)
  • ocaml/RFCs saw two PRs: one proposing removal of the rejected modular-IOs RFC (ocaml/RFCs#63) and continued revision of the Destinations API RFC by Gabriel Radanne (ocaml/RFCs#62)

    • Activity

  • Jeannalyse opened a draft reimplementation of Hashtbl giving deterministic iteration order regardless of the random seed, as a final contribution from a research internship with Gabriel Scherer (ocaml/ocaml#14956); Florian Angeletti pushed back on trading generic-structure performance for this safety property
  • Gabriel Scherer opened a series of typechecker path-equivalence refactors in ctype.ml, including normalizing types in tconstr-equivalence fast paths (ocaml/ocaml#14950), clarifying uses of Env_unscoped.path_equiv (ocaml/ocaml#14947), and an optimization for path-equivalence checks modulo normalization built on top of those (ocaml/ocaml#14952), following on from Florian Angeletti's path-equivalence-modulo-aliases work (ocaml/ocaml#14927)
  • David Allsopp opened a PR to bump the required autoconf version to 2.72 (ocaml/ocaml#14953), addressing an issue about CI/local autoconf version mismatches (ocaml/ocaml#14937)
  • Khalid opened a PR adding Sys.file_exists', a variant raising Sys_error on failure instead of returning false (ocaml/ocaml#14951), addressing a long-standing request (ocaml/ocaml#12393)
  • Benoit opened a PR adding Stdlib.Char.Ascii.is_punct, completing the set of ASCII predicates left out of an earlier PR (ocaml/ocaml#14957)
  • Stefan Muenzel opened PRs for smaller generated code for stack reallocation on AMD64 (ocaml/ocaml#14954) and a fix for expect-test trailing output (ocaml/ocaml#14959), alongside earlier open work inlining the full-application part of caml_apply (ocaml/ocaml#14925) and eliding the occurs-check for fresh-variable parameters (ocaml/ocaml#14913)
  • Gabriel Scherer opened a PR disabling testsuite/tests/misc/sorts.ml, noting it is a benchmark rather than a correctness test (ocaml/ocaml#14960), and briefly opened then closed a ocamlc -g reoptimization attempt (ocaml/ocaml#14961)
  • Simon Cruanes closed his extensible IO channels RFC implementation, noting stdlib-committee discussion had stalled (ocaml/ocaml#14775), and closed Buffer.iter_chunks (ocaml/ocaml#12931)
  • Gabriel Scherer closed Dynarray.unsafe_{get,set} after concluding the safety-reasoning tradeoffs were not worth the 1.4-2.5x microbenchmark speedup, following questions from Daniel Bünzli (ocaml/ocaml#14864)
  • v-gb closed a PR improving Map/Set.union complexity on related maps after Gabriel Scherer identified it violated the union specification when the merge function is non-trivial; Nicolás Ojeda Bär noted the Set.union fast path remained valid and that LexiFi has related inter/diff optimizations to offer (ocaml/ocaml#14949)
  • Ongoing open work continues on structured compiler diagnostics for developer tooling by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml#13766), new GC-pacing logic by Damien Doligez (ocaml/ocaml#14796), link-time linking support by Raphaël Proust (ocaml/ocaml#14895), exposing caml_ba_compare and related bigarray functions by David Allsopp (ocaml/ocaml#14804), and POWER-architecture frame-pointer support by Tim McGilchrist (ocaml/ocaml#14505)
  • Cross-platform build maintenance continued with David Allsopp's build-environment sanitization (ocaml/ocaml#14915) and macOS opam-sandbox compiler-cloning fix (ocaml/ocaml#14923), Antonin Décimo's Cygwin build fixes (ocaml/ocaml#14921) and CAMLthread_local C/C++ interoperability improvement (ocaml/ocaml#14934), and Kate's macOS fix for opam clone (ocaml/ocaml#14901)
  • Runtime fixes remain open for a musl/Intel sigaltstack issue by Nat Mote (ocaml/ocaml#14933), printing errno on sigaltstack errors by Nathan Taylor (ocaml/ocaml#14928), and dropping redundant memory-model fences around atomic RMWs on AArch64 by Sebastian Pop (ocaml/ocaml#14936)
  • Gabriel Scherer has an open fix for record updates with unchanged [@atomic] fields (ocaml/ocaml#14935), addressing a reported issue where functional updates of atomic records fail to emit atomic loads (ocaml/ocaml#14918)
  • Simon Cruanes opened a PR proposing to remove the RFC on modular IOs (ocaml/RFCs#63)
  • Gabriel Radanne continued work on the Destinations API RFC, updating the proposal for an API to manipulate destinations (ocaml/RFCs#62)

    • Notable Discussions

  • Jeannalyse's draft Hashtbl reimplementation for deterministic iteration order drew disagreement from Florian Angeletti, who argued against slowing down a performance-sensitive generic data structure to guard against programmer error (ocaml/ocaml#14956)
  • Daniel Bünzli opened a "Show and tell" discussion proposing new String search functions (find_sub/rfind_sub) based on a two-way string-search algorithm, following up on ocaml/ocaml#14068, with a gist and benchmark script for feedback (ocaml/ocaml#14099)
  • Austin Theriault described Semgrep's need for per-domain timeouts and discussed with Gabriel Scherer whether Domain.interrupt can safely interact with effect handlers, referencing the asynchronous-exception-masking work in ocaml/ocaml#8961 (ocaml/ocaml#14955)
  • The autoconf version mismatch between CI and local hygiene checks was debated by Antonin Décimo, David Allsopp, and others, weighing bleeding-edge autoconf against long-term stability (ocaml/ocaml#14937)
  • Simon Cruanes's extensible IO channels RFC implementation was closed after stdlib-committee discussion stalled without a resolution (ocaml/ocaml#14775)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Repeated tension between performance and safety/reasoning guarantees in stdlib data structures, seen in the closed Dynarray.unsafe_{get,set} PR (ocaml/ocaml#14864) and the contested Hashtbl redesign (ocaml/ocaml#14956)
  • An active cluster of typechecker path-equivalence refactoring in ctype.ml from Gabriel Scherer and Florian Angeletti, building incrementally on each other's PRs (ocaml/ocaml#14927, ocaml/ocaml#14947, ocaml/ocaml#14950, ocaml/ocaml#14952)
  • David Allsopp driving a cluster of cross-platform build and locale maintenance across Windows/mingw, Cygwin, and macOS opam sandboxing (ocaml/ocaml#14914, ocaml/ocaml#14915, ocaml/ocaml#14923, ocaml/ocaml#14953, ocaml/ocaml#10258)
  • Continued incremental progress on the typing-recovery mechanism for multi-error editor integration, spanning several small merged PRs in the same week (ocaml/ocaml#14945, ocaml/ocaml#14946)
  • ocaml/RFCs activity was reactive to ocaml/ocaml decisions this week, with the modular-IOs RFC removal following directly from the closed IO-channels PR (ocaml/RFCs#63, ocaml/ocaml#14775)

    • Multicore

    Eio published v1.4 with Flow.null and macOS fixes; ocaml-uring saw only issue discussion, and seven other group repos had no recorded activity.

    New Features

  • ocaml-multicore/eio: Added Flow.null, a sink/source pair modeled on /dev/null, by Anil Madhavapeddy and Thomas Leonard, suggested by Jon Sterling (ocaml-multicore/eio#894)
  • ocaml-multicore/eio: eio_posix now falls back to a custom select() stub when poll() returns POLLNVAL, fixing a macOS crash writing to /dev/null, by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#893, fixes ocaml-multicore/eio#757)
  • ocaml-multicore/eio: Net.getaddrinfo and related lookups now include the queried hostname/service in error messages, by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#900)
  • ocaml-multicore/eio: eio_linux directory reading no longer returns an empty batch before end-of-file, preventing truncated listings on FUSE filesystems, by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#897)
  • ocaml-multicore/eio: eio_linux now surfaces the real underlying error when chmod on a symlink fails via /proc/self/fd/, by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#901, test fix ocaml-multicore/eio#903)
  • ocaml-multicore/eio: fork_action now rejects uid/gid/pid values that overflow the underlying C types instead of silently truncating them, by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#895)
  • ocaml-multicore/eio: Function applications were eta-expanded to support compilation under OxCaml, by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#898)
  • ocaml-multicore/eio: eio_unix_fork_error now calls _exit automatically instead of relying on every caller to do so, by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#896, fixes ocaml-multicore/eio#818)
  • ocaml-multicore/eio: Published the v1.4 release, consolidating the above fixes and features into CHANGES.md, by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#904)

    • Overview

  • ocaml-multicore/eio published its v1.4 release, merging eight PRs covering Flow.null, a macOS select() fallback, error-message improvements, and OxCaml compatibility work
  • ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring had no commits merged; activity was limited to two issue threads, one resolved as a false positive (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#160) and one still open (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#156)
  • ocaml-multicore/domainslib, ocaml-multicore/meio, ocaml-multicore/saturn, ocaml-multicore/eio-trace, ocaml-multicore/picos, ocaml-multicore/kcas, and ocaml-multicore/ocaml-iomux recorded no activity for this period

    • Activity

  • ocaml-multicore/eio: A PR converting tty EIO errors into End_of_file for Eio_unix.Pty was opened by Anil Madhavapeddy, addressing reads from a closed pty raising an unhandled I/O error (ocaml-multicore/eio#905, fixes ocaml-multicore/eio#902)
  • ocaml-multicore/eio: Thomas Gazagnaire reported a relative-path bug in Eio.Path.mkdirs, closed after investigation (ocaml-multicore/eio#906), and opened a request to add a ~follow argument to open_in/open_out (ocaml-multicore/eio#899)
  • ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring: Vesa Karvonen opened and then closed a suspected double-free/dangling-pointer report in uring_stubs.c, surfaced by an AI-assisted code review, after confirming the leftover pointer is never referenced (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#160)
  • ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring: Isaac Freund added a comment to the open vendored-liburing portability issue, describing a build failure on Chimera Linux and requesting a system-liburing build option for Debian packaging (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#156)

    • Notable Discussions

  • On ocaml-multicore/eio#899, Thomas Gazagnaire and Thomas Leonard discussed adding ~follow to open_in/open_out, covering use cases like opening raw block devices with O_NOFOLLOW and safely building disk images from a source tree
  • On ocaml-multicore/eio#902, Anil Madhavapeddy and Thomas Leonard debated wrapping Eio_unix.Pty specifically versus converting EIO to end-of-file generically whenever isatty() is true, settling on the general approach implemented in ocaml-multicore/eio#905
  • On ocaml-multicore/eio#893, review of the macOS select() fallback covered fd_set sizing beyond 1024 descriptors, whether to restrict the workaround to __APPLE__ only, and correct CAMLparam usage in the new C stub
  • On ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#160, Vesa Karvonen raised a memory-safety concern about Ring_val(v_uring) potentially dangling after a failed io_uring_queue_init_params call, then self-corrected once it was clear the leftover pointer is never dereferenced

    • Emerging Trends

  • Error message quality was a recurring focus in ocaml-multicore/eio this week, adding hostnames and underlying errno values to exceptions rather than generic failures (ocaml-multicore/eio#900, ocaml-multicore/eio#901, ocaml-multicore/eio#903)
  • Platform-specific edge-case hardening continued in eio, spanning macOS poll()/select() behavior (ocaml-multicore/eio#893) and forward compatibility with the OxCaml compiler (ocaml-multicore/eio#898)
  • Packaging and portability friction around vendored C dependencies surfaced in ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring, with Stéphane Glondu and Isaac Freund both requesting a system-liburing build option across different distributions (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#156)
  • AI-assisted code review produced at least one false-positive memory-safety report this week, self-diagnosed and closed by the reporter (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#160)
  • Activity across the group remained concentrated in eio, with seven of the nine tracked repositories (ocaml-multicore/domainslib, ocaml-multicore/meio, ocaml-multicore/saturn, ocaml-multicore/eio-trace, ocaml-multicore/picos, ocaml-multicore/kcas, ocaml-multicore/ocaml-iomux) showing no recorded activity
entry.summary: Eio 1.4, dune 3.24.1 and opam 2.6.0-alpha1 all released this week, while oxcaml/oxcaml opened a coordinated wave of Flambda 2 planning issues and core landed new Option/Result stdlib helpers.

entry.title: Week 29, 2026: RISC-V frame pointers landed in ocaml/ocaml, opam shipped 2.6.0~alpha1, and oxcaml/oxcaml added unsigned division primitives and a safe effects API.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Core Frame pointer support for the RISC-V (riscv64) Linux backend merged, adding configure-time detection and prologue/epilogue handling, by Tim McGilchrist (ocaml/ocaml#14506)
  • OCaml Core arm64 mutable-field write barriers now emit a store-release (stlr/stlur) instead of dmb ishld; str, with older Cortex cores kept on the fenced path, by Sebastian Pop and Xavier Leroy (ocaml/ocaml#14922)
  • OCaml Core caml_program is now generated as a loop over a table of module entry points, making startup code size independent of the number of linked modules, by Tim McGilchrist and Pierre Oechsel (ocaml/ocaml#13217)
  • OxCaml Added unsigned division and remainder primitives (%int64#_unsigned_div/_mod) for native and bytecode, rewiring Int8/Int16 onto them, by James Rayman (oxcaml/oxcaml#4936)
  • OxCaml Added a "safe" effects API requiring a local, yielding Handler.t phantom value to perform effects, by Aspen Smith (oxcaml/oxcaml#6281)
  • OxCaml Added alloc_regions to alloc_modes, threaded through every allocating primitive as groundwork for zero-alloc-with-regions checking, by Nathanaëlle Courant (oxcaml/oxcaml#6121)
  • OxCaml Allowed definition of atomic fields in mixed records, by Joe Kerrigan (oxcaml/oxcaml#6423); five new oxcaml-compiler releases (5.2.0minus-38/39/40, 5.4.0-ox1/ox2 previews) shipped in oxcaml/opam-repository#54 by David Allsopp
  • Multicore Eio added macOS TCP_KEEPIDLE support and a new Eio_unix.Err module by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#890, ocaml-multicore/eio#887), while Eio_linux.Low_level gained iouring-backed socket/bind/listen/ftruncate/fdatasync, with fsync/shutdown now routed through iouring, by Leonard and Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#884, ocaml-multicore/eio#850) ahead of a v1.4 release (ocaml-multicore/eio#892)

    • OxCaml

    oxcaml/oxcaml added unsigned division primitives, a safe effects API, and DWARF groundwork; opam-repository shipped five new compiler releases.

    New Features

  • Added unsigned division and remainder primitives (e.g. %int64#_unsigned_div, %int64#_unsigned_mod) for native and bytecode, rewiring Int8/Int8_u/Int16/Int16_u onto them, by James Rayman (oxcaml/oxcaml#4936)
  • Added a "safe" effects API requiring a local, yielding Handler.t phantom value to perform effects, making it impossible (short of silencing alerts) to perform an effect from an unyielding context, by Aspen Smith (oxcaml/oxcaml#6281)
  • Added alloc_regions to alloc_modes, threaded through every allocating primitive as groundwork for future zero-alloc-with-regions checking, by Nathanaëlle Courant (oxcaml/oxcaml#6121)
  • Allowed definition of atomic fields in mixed records (use still prohibited pending field-offset support), by Joe Kerrigan (oxcaml/oxcaml#6423)
  • Added Dynamic to the Stdlib, exposing the dynamics implementation previously internal to the test suite, by Max Slater (oxcaml/oxcaml#6412)
  • Added float32_u to the predef types as type float32_u = float32#, by Ryan Tjoa (oxcaml/oxcaml#6459)
  • New -ddebug-avail-sets dump flag prints register-availability sets when dumping Linear/CFG, part of the ongoing dwarf202607 DWARF-debugging series, by Mark Shinwell (oxcaml/oxcaml#6511)
  • -gdwarf-compression now also applies to standard -g DWARF output rather than only inlined-frame builds, by Simon Spies (oxcaml/oxcaml#6490)
  • Fixed 3 CFG peephole bugs, including a potential miscompilation from integer overflow in a mul/lsl simplification, and a CSE bug hoisting mutable loads across atomic fences, by Xavier Clerc (oxcaml/oxcaml#6424, oxcaml/oxcaml#6433)
  • Fixed missing CFI_SIGNAL_FRAME annotations in GC entry points on amd64/arm64, which had been breaking gdb backtraces starting inside the GC, by Max Slater (oxcaml/oxcaml#6456)
  • oxcaml/opam-repository added five new oxcaml-compiler releases (5.2.0minus-38/39/40 bundling Jane Street 130.100+614 and 130.106+341, plus 5.4.0-ox1/ox2 previews), closing the long-standing request to bump the repository to 130.100+614, by David Allsopp (oxcaml/opam-repository#54, oxcaml/opam-repository#46)

    • Overview

  • Two of the five repositories in the group had recorded activity this week: oxcaml/oxcaml and oxcaml/opam-repository; oxcaml/merlin, oxcaml/jsofocaml, and janestreet/opam-repository had no tracked commits or pull requests.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml landed unsigned division primitives, a safe effects API, and alloc_regions groundwork, while a 24-PR DWARF debugging series (oxcaml/oxcaml#6503 through oxcaml/oxcaml#6523) from Mark Shinwell remained mostly open, with 63 PRs open at week's end.
  • oxcaml/opam-repository merged oxcaml/opam-repository#54 the same day it was opened, adding five new oxcaml-compiler releases across 1197 changed files and closing oxcaml/opam-repository#46.
  • Continued frontend/backend decomposition work in oxcaml/oxcaml (splitting ocamlcommon) and dissector partitioning fixes progressed alongside typing micro-optimizations.

    • Activity

  • Mark Shinwell's dwarf202607 series (24 PRs) adds end-to-end DWARF debugging support for Flambda 2 code — phantom lets, inlined-frame attribution, and DWARF call-site information — with most of the stack still open (oxcaml/oxcaml#6503, oxcaml/oxcaml#6504, oxcaml/oxcaml#6513, oxcaml/oxcaml#6519, oxcaml/oxcaml#6523)
  • Xavier Clerc opened several CFG/register-allocation correctness PRs covering prologue clarification, hardened terminator simplification, stack-check liveness, and a vectorizer audit (oxcaml/oxcaml#6461, oxcaml/oxcaml#6462, oxcaml/oxcaml#6465, oxcaml/oxcaml#6469, oxcaml/oxcaml#6472, oxcaml/oxcaml#6531, oxcaml/oxcaml#6541)
  • Julesjacobs merged three typing micro-optimizations (skipping Result boxing, physical-equality shortcuts, exception-free Env lookup) and opened work on adaptive recursive-module unroll depth and custom [@@or_null] variant kinds (oxcaml/oxcaml#6478, oxcaml/oxcaml#6479, oxcaml/oxcaml#6480, oxcaml/oxcaml#6532, oxcaml/oxcaml#6500)
  • David Allsopp continued splitting the frontend out of ocamlcommon, merging the Env.Current_unit factoring and opening a further ocamlfrontend split and compiler-libs reshuffle (oxcaml/oxcaml#6491, oxcaml/oxcaml#6470, oxcaml/oxcaml#6530)
  • Max Slater opened distinct unsigned unboxed integer primitive types (uint{8,16,32,64}_u), building on this week's merged unsigned divmod work, so the compiler can distinguish signed and unsigned types as GADT indices (oxcaml/oxcaml#6534, oxcaml/oxcaml#4936)
  • Jane Street's dissector saw partitioning and robustness work from Jakub Staroń and Simon Spies: resolving link inputs' object files through manifests, robustness to manifest-resolved link inputs, and linking only relevant compilation units (oxcaml/oxcaml#6468, oxcaml/oxcaml#6501, oxcaml/oxcaml#6526)
  • Ten oxcaml/oxcaml PRs closed without merging this week, including duplicate driver-flag attempts and an arm64 store-release attempt superseded by oxcaml/oxcaml#6538 (oxcaml/oxcaml#6481, oxcaml/oxcaml#6443)
  • In oxcaml/opam-repository, David Allsopp followed the oxcaml/opam-repository#54 merge with three commits extending overlay packages (merlin, ocaml-lsp-server, ocamlformat) to the new compiler and raising conflict upper bounds for the 130.106+341 package set ahead of 5.4.0-ox1 (aa0b5c8, 3a0e9e3)

  • DWARF debugging infrastructure and unsigned-integer support are each being built up as staged, independently-reviewable multi-PR series: Mark Shinwell's 24-PR dwarf202607 series (oxcaml/oxcaml#6503-oxcaml/oxcaml#6523) and Max Slater's follow-up to this week's merged unsigned divmod primitives with distinct unsigned unboxed integer types (oxcaml/oxcaml#6534, oxcaml/oxcaml#4936)

  • oxcaml/opam-repository is bridging the older 5.2.0minus compiler line to the upcoming 5.4.0-ox1/ox2 releases incrementally, deferring patch-dependent packages like angstrom and faraday until the patches build on the newer compilers rather than fixing them immediately (oxcaml/opam-repository#54, 1b6e86c)

    • OCaml Core

    RISC-V frame pointers and arm64 store-release codegen merged in ocaml/ocaml; atomic-field record-update semantics were debated. ocaml/RFCs was quiet.

    New Features

  • Frame pointer support for the RISC-V (riscv64) Linux backend, adding emit_store_word_with_barrier-style prologue/epilogue handling and configure-time detection, by Tim McGilchrist (ocaml/ocaml#14506)
  • On arm64, mutable-field-assignment write barriers now emit a store-release (stlr, or stlur when FEAT_LRCPC2 is available) instead of dmb ishld; str, with older cores (Cortex-A53/-A57/-A72/-A73) kept on the fenced path and the default chosen at configure time, by Sebastian Pop and Xavier Leroy (ocaml/ocaml#14922)
  • caml_program is now generated as a loop over a table of module entry points instead of one call block per module, making startup code size independent of the number of linked modules, by Tim McGilchrist and Pierre Oechsel (ocaml/ocaml#13217)
  • Fixed -dtypedtree output incorrectly printing Twith_modtypesubst as Twith_modtype, by Corentin De Souza (ocaml/ocaml#14932)
  • Documentation for Gc.stat corrected to state that stack_size (unlike heap_chunks, free_blocks, and largest_free) is now populated again in OCaml 5.5, by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/ocaml#14942)
  • Memory-model manual documentation clarified on how domain-frontier updates behave, by Olivier Nicole (ocaml/ocaml#14924)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/ocaml merged RISC-V frame pointer support (ocaml/ocaml#14506), arm64 store-release write-barrier codegen (ocaml/ocaml#14922), and a loop-based rewrite of caml_program startup (ocaml/ocaml#13217)
  • Eleven new PRs were opened in ocaml/ocaml, spanning an Atomic.compare_and_exchange proposal (ocaml/ocaml#14912), GC-pacing rework (ocaml/ocaml#14796), a fiber-cache leak fix (ocaml/ocaml#14940), and several build/portability fixes
  • Discussion converged on how atomic record fields interact with functional record updates, closing ocaml/ocaml#14931 in favor of ocaml/ocaml#14935
  • ocaml/RFCs recorded no issue or PR activity during this period

    • Activity

  • Eleven new PRs opened this week, including Jeannalyse's Atomic.compare_and_exchange proposal (ocaml/ocaml#14912), Gabriel Scherer's fix for record updates with unchanged atomic fields (ocaml/ocaml#14935), shym's support for relocatable cross compilers (ocaml/ocaml#14929), David Allsopp's move of Btype.hash_variant into Obj (ocaml/ocaml#14939) and exposure of caml_ba_compare (ocaml/ocaml#14804), and Michael Neumann's {Option,Result}.try_value implementation (ocaml/ocaml#14941)
  • Damien Doligez opened the new GC-pacing logic PR completing the last item of ocaml/ocaml#14324, prompting Török Edwin to benchmark space-overhead and RSS effects against 5.5 and trunk (ocaml/ocaml#14796)
  • Florian Angeletti opened a fiber cache leak fix for OCaml 5.5, cherry-picking a fix from oxcaml after Daniel Bünzli reported the leak on Discuss, and separately enabled module-dependent function tracing (#trace) for modular explicits in the toplevel (ocaml/ocaml#14940, ocaml/ocaml#14707)
  • Sebastian Pop opened a PR to drop redundant memory-model fences around atomic RMWs on AArch64, backed by herd7 litmus-test analysis distinguishing LSE from LL/SC atomics, discussed in depth with Olivier Nicole (ocaml/ocaml#14936)
  • Portability and build fixes opened this week include Nat Mote's sigaltstack/musl fix for certain Intel CPUs with review from Miod Vallat and Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml#14933), Nathan Taylor's errno-printing patch for sigaltstack errors (ocaml/ocaml#14928), Antonin Décimo's CAMLthread_local C/C++ interoperability improvements and Cygwin build fixes (ocaml/ocaml#14934, ocaml/ocaml#14921), Anarchos's Haiku Unix-socket/setlocale/signal test adaptations (ocaml/ocaml#14773), and Tim McGilchrist's frame-pointer support for the POWER architecture, reviewed by Zane Hambly who flagged a TSAN interaction to investigate later (ocaml/ocaml#14505)
  • Stdlib additions proposed this week include Nicolás Ojeda Bär's Dynarray.append_iarray and Pqueue.of_iarray (ocaml/ocaml#14909, fixing ocaml/ocaml#14320) and Gabriel Scherer's caml_result_find_exception helper for mlvalues.h (ocaml/ocaml#14814)
  • Tim McGilchrist's PR pinning the Ubuntu version in HACKING.adoc to 24.04 (for autoconf 2.71 compatibility) merged, and Antonin Décimo noted a related Cygwin CI fix depends on the CAMLthread_local PR (ocaml/ocaml#14926, ocaml/ocaml#14921)
  • Török Edwin added a testsuite case that fragments sizeclass pools, tracing a behavior difference between OCaml 5.4.1 and 5.5/trunk back to a major-GC work-accounting fix (ocaml/ocaml#14818)

    • Notable Discussions

  • Whether functional record updates that implicitly copy atomic fields should be forbidden or should perform an implicit atomic read: Ryan Tjoa reported the missing atomic load (ocaml/ocaml#14918); Joe Kerrigan opened a PR to forbid the pattern citing OxCaml's precedent (ocaml/ocaml#14931), but after further discussion with Gabriel Scherer, Daniel Bünzli, and Aspen Smith concluded that record updates are more constrained than pattern-matching (fields are read exactly once, unconditionally), so ocaml/ocaml#14931 was closed in favor of Gabriel Scherer's alternative that implicitly performs the atomic read (ocaml/ocaml#14935)
  • A related question on the unspecified evaluation order of fields in { r with ... } record-update expressions, raised by Guillaume Bury, which Daniel Bünzli linked to the atomic-field discussion above (ocaml/ocaml#14129, ocaml/ocaml#14918, ocaml/ocaml#14931)
  • Michael Neumann's request for point-free {Option,Result}.andthen/orelse combinators was closed by Daniel Bünzli, who explained the stdlib team's preference for a try_value-style combinator (previously discussed in ocaml/ocaml#13937) over andthen/orelse, after which Neumann agreed and opened ocaml/ocaml#14941 implementing try_value (ocaml/ocaml#14893)
  • Török Edwin raised that Gc.Memprof does not track the lifetime of bigarray subarrays, causing memory-profiling tools like memtrace to underestimate live memory in applications such as Mirage (ocaml/ocaml#14938)
  • Sebastian Pop and Olivier Nicole debated whether the PLDI'18 Bounding Data Races in Space and Time compilation scheme's fences around AArch64 atomic RMWs are stronger than necessary, backed by herd7 litmus tests distinguishing LSE and LL/SC atomic forms (ocaml/ocaml#14936)
  • Chet Murthy reported that Scanf.unescaped accepts hex (\x41) but rejects octal (\o101) escapes, which Daniel Bünzli confirmed matches the documented spec but agreed is surprising behavior (ocaml/ocaml#14930)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Multiple concurrent efforts to refine low-level memory-ordering guarantees: arm64 store-release barrier codegen (ocaml/ocaml#14922), dropping redundant AArch64 RMW fences (ocaml/ocaml#14936), and updated memory-model documentation for domain frontiers (ocaml/ocaml#14924, ocaml/ocaml#14134)
  • Growing attention to atomic record fields interacting with existing language features (functional updates, pattern matching, evaluation order), spanning ocaml/ocaml#14918, ocaml/ocaml#14931, ocaml/ocaml#14935, and ocaml/ocaml#14129
  • Continued cross-architecture portability work landing frame-pointer support architecture by architecture, following RISC-V this week (ocaml/ocaml#14506) with POWER proposed in parallel (ocaml/ocaml#14505)
  • Runtime portability fixes are increasingly driven by libc and platform edge cases reported by external users (musl on Intel CPUs in ocaml/ocaml#14933, Haiku in ocaml/ocaml#14773, Cygwin in ocaml/ocaml#14921)

    • Multicore

    Eio advanced io_uring socket support toward v1.4; ocaml-uring closed a false double-free report; saturn fixed qcheck test compatibility.

    New Features

  • TCP_KEEPIDLE socket option support added for macOS by Thomas Leonard, alongside disabling TCP_FASTOPEN on non-Linux platforms where it produced unreliable results (ocaml-multicore/eio#890).
  • New Eio_unix.Err module by Thomas Leonard exposes a public Err.v function for wrapping Unix_error exceptions as Eio.Io errors, replacing ad-hoc duplicated logic across eio_linux, eio_posix, and eio_windows (ocaml-multicore/eio#887).
  • Eio_linux.Low_level gained socket, bind, and listen functions with io_uring support, falling back to plain syscalls on older kernels, by Thomas Leonard building on Anil Madhavapeddy's work (ocaml-multicore/eio#884, ocaml-multicore/eio#850).
  • Eio_linux.Low_level also gained ftruncate and fdatasync, and now routes fsync/shutdown through io_uring, by Anil Madhavapeddy; a new Eio.Exn.Not_available exception was added for operations unsupported on a given backend (ocaml-multicore/eio#850).
  • Socket-option stubs were moved into eio.unix so extended options can be shared between eio_linux and eio_posix, by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#889), followed by a fix ensuring sockopt functions always raise proper Eio exceptions instead of leaking a raw Unix_error (ocaml-multicore/eio#891).
  • CHANGES.md and library documentation updated to describe the accumulated v1.4 feature set, including the Sockopt module, Path.chmod/chown, Path.with_dir_entries, and Eio_unix.Pty, by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#892).

    • Overview

  • Across the nine repositories in the multicore group, recorded activity this week was limited to three: ocaml-multicore/eio, ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring, and ocaml-multicore/saturn.
  • ocaml-multicore/eio was the most active, merging socket-option and io_uring PRs and reorganizing eio_linux ahead of a v1.4 release (ocaml-multicore/eio#892).
  • ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring's only activity was a suspected double-free report that was investigated and closed as not a bug (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#160).
  • ocaml-multicore/saturn merged a single maintenance PR restoring test-suite compatibility with recent qcheck releases (ocaml-multicore/saturn#188).
  • No activity was recorded this week in ocaml-multicore/domainslib, ocaml-multicore/meio, ocaml-multicore/eio-trace, ocaml-multicore/picos, ocaml-multicore/kcas, or ocaml-multicore/ocaml-iomux.

    • Activity

  • In eio, Thomas Leonard merged the eio_linux reorganisation splitting net.ml, process.ml, fs.ml, and time.ml to mirror eio_posix (ocaml-multicore/eio#886), building on the uring-backed Low_level.{socket,bind,listen} work (ocaml-multicore/eio#884).
  • Anil Madhavapeddy opened a PR proposing a select() fallback for macOS file descriptors where poll() incorrectly returns POLLNVAL (e.g. /dev/tty, /dev/null), fixing an assertion failure in sched.ml and following on from ocaml-multicore/eio#757 (ocaml-multicore/eio#893).
  • Anil Madhavapeddy continued iterating on a pre-connect socket options design exposing a GADT-based options list for bind_to, building on @art-w's earlier work (ocaml-multicore/eio#875, ocaml-multicore/eio#713), plus an open proposal to add an SO_TYPE query to the portable socket interface (ocaml-multicore/eio#860).
  • Cleanup in eio removed the obsolete [@@@alert "-unstable"] Merlin workaround (ocaml-multicore/eio#885), deleted leftover test files after test runs (ocaml-multicore/eio#883), and fixed a compiler warning via added switch-case braces, contributed by Olaf Hering (ocaml-multicore/eio#882).
  • In ocaml-uring, Vesa Karvonen reported a suspected double-free in the error path of io_uring_queue_init_params, flagged during AI-assisted code review; Thomas Leonard investigated and closed the issue after confirming the custom block's NULL finalizer prevents any second free (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#160).
  • In saturn, Carine Morel fixed the test-suite build against qcheck >= 0.90, renaming deprecated generators across 13 test files and bumping dependency version constraints in dune-project and saturn.opam (ocaml-multicore/saturn#188).

    • Notable Discussions

  • Marijan Petričević raised a question about persistently high iowait/IO pressure reported by the kernel for an otherwise idle Eio io_uring-backed service, despite no visible disk activity or blocked processes (ocaml-multicore/eio#862).
  • Cross-platform testing results shared on ocaml-multicore/eio#890 showed several "Linux-only" socket options also work on macOS and Windows, and surfaced a likely errno-message bug in FreeBSD's tcp_usrreq.c where ESRCH is reported as a process-not-found error, discussed by Thomas Leonard and Anil Madhavapeddy.
  • On ocaml-multicore/eio#884, Anil Madhavapeddy and Thomas Leonard discussed design alternatives for tracking uring feature support, weighing storing the probe itself against per-feature booleans or a functor-based dispatch, and settled on storing the probe directly.
  • The double-free report on ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#160 was notable for being spotted by AI during code review rather than manual inspection; Thomas Leonard resolved it by pointing to the existing finalizer documentation in uring_stubs.c, which explains why the custom block's NULL finalizer prevents an actual double free.

    • Emerging Trends

  • Consolidation of socket-option handling into a shared eio.unix layer continued in eio, so eio_linux, eio_posix, and eventually eio_windows reuse the same C stubs and exception handling (ocaml-multicore/eio#889, ocaml-multicore/eio#891, ocaml-multicore/eio#890).
  • Broader adoption of io_uring for operations previously done with plain syscalls extended to socket, bind, listen, shutdown, and fsync in eio (ocaml-multicore/eio#850, ocaml-multicore/eio#884).
  • AI-assisted code review surfaced a memory-safety question in ocaml-uring's C stubs, an explicitly noted first instance for the group this week (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#160).
  • Dependency-compatibility maintenance continued, with a qcheck generator rename in saturn prompting a coordinated update across its entire test suite rather than a single module (ocaml-multicore/saturn#188).
entry.summary: RISC-V frame pointers landed in ocaml/ocaml, opam shipped 2.6.0~alpha1, and oxcaml/oxcaml added unsigned division primitives and a safe effects API.

entry.title: Week 28, 2026: Opam 2.5.2 fixed a symlink CVE while ocaml/ocaml gained configurable stack sizes and js_of_ocaml shipped WebGL2 and OCaml 5.6 support.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Core A new OCAMLRUNPARAM='S=' option lets programs configure the minimum system stack size used when spawning a Thread or Domain, useful for FFI code needing a larger native stack, by Jeannalyse, reviewed by Antonin Décimo (ocaml/ocaml#14195, ocaml/ocaml#14860)
  • OCaml Core Sys.file_exists and related primitives now use GetFileAttributes instead of stat_os on Windows, avoiding a kernel bug that made paths like C:\...\repro:xxx wrongly report as existing, and Filename functions now treat : strictly as the drive separator, by David Allsopp (ocaml/ocaml#14919, ocaml/ocaml#14916)
  • OCaml Core Fixed a hang in caml_shutdown() under cleanup-at-exit mode where orphaned ephemerons from a terminated domain were never adopted by the final GC cycle, by Olivier Nicole (ocaml/ocaml#14906), alongside a fix so the multicore GC waits for all domains to finish marking before another ephemeron-marking round, by Gabriel Scherer (ocaml/ocaml#14774)
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/opam released opam 2.5.2, fixing a symlink bypass of the switch-prefix check tracked as CVE-2026-57825 (ocaml/opam#7005, backported in ocaml/opam#7006), and switched internal repository storage to gzipped tar archives to speed up update/init on NTFS and IO-constrained machines (ocaml/opam#6625); the release also landed in OCaml Ecosystem opam-repository across 8 packages by Kate (ocaml/opam-repository#30237, ocaml/opam-repository#30238)
  • OCaml Tools ocsigen/jsofocaml merged WebGL2 bindings closing a long-standing request (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2388, ocsigen/jsofocaml#1226), fixed an if-fusion miscompilation in js_simpl that could collapse two evaluations of an effectful expression into one (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2393), and merged initial OCaml 5.6 support (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2227)
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/ocamlfind now installs .cmx files alongside .cmi files during make install, resolving warning-58 reports in downstream projects such as Rocq, by David Allsopp (ocaml/ocamlfind#120, fixes ocaml/ocamlfind#117)
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/ocaml-lsp reworked ppx hover expansion to call Merlin's expand-ppx command directly, fixing broken hover text for [@@deriving ...] on mutually recursive types, by Rudi Grinberg (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1615, fixes ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1614)
  • Multicore ocaml-multicore/eio added Address_lookup_failed errors to Eio.Net.getaddrinfo instead of silently returning [], reworked Eio.Path.load to fix reads of zero-size files such as /proc entries, hardened Eio.Path.chown/chmod against sandbox escape via symlinks, and added blksize/blocks fields to Eio.File.Stat.t, by Thomas Leonard and Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#866, ocaml-multicore/eio#869, ocaml-multicore/eio#877, ocaml-multicore/eio#865)
  • OxCaml oxcaml/oxcaml extended the reaper's unboxing transformation to boxed int32/int64/nativeint numbers via a new Boxed_number field constructor, by Mark Shinwell (oxcaml/oxcaml#6437), and now rejects functional record updates that implicitly read an [@atomic] field nonatomically, by Joe Kerrigan (oxcaml/oxcaml#6453)
  • OCaml Ecosystem New union-find-lattice persistent union-find/lattice library based on the authors' SAS 2026 paper, by Dorian Lesbre (ocaml/opam-repository#30207), and Caqti 3.0.0 released as a breaking API change requiring existing users to add caqti.classic to their link lines, by Petter A. Urkedal (ocaml/opam-repository#30174)

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    Opam 2.5.2 shipped in opam-repository with its ocaml.org announcement pending, alongside new packages and a breaking Caqti 3.0.0 release.

    New Features

  • opam 2.5.2 toolchain released across 8 packages by Kate in opam-repository (ocaml/opam-repository#30237, ocaml/opam-repository#30238), with the corresponding release-announcement page opened on ocaml.org, still awaiting merge (ocaml/ocaml.org#3712)
  • New union-find-lattice persistent union-find/lattice library, based on the authors' SAS 2026 paper, submitted by Dorian Lesbre (ocaml/opam-repository#30207)
  • New pidgin/pidgin_pp packages for describing and validating data structures, first release by Xavier Van de Woestyne (ocaml/opam-repository#30208)
  • New hegel property-based testing library plus ppxhegelcompat, ppxhegelgenerator, and ppxhegeltest, submitted by Ethan Chou at 0.8.0 and updated to 0.9.0 within the week (ocaml/opam-repository#30185, ocaml/opam-repository#30246, ocaml/opam-repository#30239)
  • New micro_httpd no-dependency HTTP server package by Kate (ocaml/opam-repository#30251)
  • New ocamlgrep/ocamlgrep-lib structural grep tool for OCaml source by Martin Jambon, reaching 0.1.1 with a fix removing test-only build dependencies and a new --dune-root option (ocaml/opam-repository#30201, ocaml/opam-repository#30200)
  • Caqti 3.0.0 released as a breaking API change by Petter A. Urkedal: the caqti library now holds the Caqti 3 API while caqti.classic provides a Caqti 2 compatibility wrapper, requiring existing users to add caqti.classic to their link lines (ocaml/opam-repository#30174)
  • OCaml/Unikraft 1.2.0 released by @shym adding OCaml 5.4.1/5.5.0 support, a relocatable cross compiler, and a new option-9pfs filesystem package (ocaml/opam-repository#30209)
  • Frama-C 33.0~beta (Arsenic) released by Allan Blanchard, removing deprecation of logic declarations outside axiomatic blocks (ocaml/opam-repository#30136)
  • caisar 6.0 released by caisar-platform, replacing --prover-altern/--prover-precision with a combined -p PROVER[:ALTERN][:PRECISION] syntax (ocaml/opam-repository#30165)
  • Automated OCaml Planet aggregator on ocaml.org syndicated the blog post "Notes from week 27" by Mark Elvers (ocaml/ocaml.org#3710), and the markdown-lint CI workflow was bumped from markdownlint-cli2-action v23 to v24 (ocaml/ocaml.org#3709)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/opam-repository: five new packages landed (union-find-lattice, pidgin/pidginpp, hegel family, microhttpd, ocamlgrep) alongside an opam 2.5.2 toolchain release and a breaking Caqti 3.0.0 API overhaul (ocaml/opam-repository#30207, ocaml/opam-repository#30174)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: automated Planet content sync and a CI dependency bump merged, while the opam 2.5.2 announcement page and a longstanding AWS industrial-users addition remained open for review (ocaml/ocaml.org#3712, ocaml/ocaml.org#3681)
  • Package-release volume in opam-repository (raylib, MirageOS tools, melange, dap, and others) far outweighed ocaml.org's mostly bot-driven PR activity this week (ocaml/opam-repository#30219, ocaml/ocaml.org#3711)

    • Activity

  • Newly opened opam-repository PRs awaiting merge include syguslib-utils 0.3.0 by Victor Nicolet (ocaml/opam-repository#30043), quickjs 0.5.0 with breaking RegExp.exec changes by David Sancho (ocaml/opam-repository#30212), ocamlformat-mlx 0.29.0.0 adding OCaml 5.5 syntax support by @mlx-automation (ocaml/opam-repository#30216), and lmdb 1.1.2 switching to ocamlbuild by @madroach (ocaml/opam-repository#30198)
