  • A cluster of graphics/game-engine bindings released: raylib/raylib-callbacks 2.2.0 then 2.2.1 by Tobias Mock (ocaml/opam-repository#30219, ocaml/opam-repository#30257), plus raygui and wayland 2.3 by Thomas Leonard (ocaml/opam-repository#30222)
  • MirageOS/network-tooling releases from Hannes Mehnert: tuntap 2.0.2, orb 1.0.1, ocaml-solo5 1.3.2, and patch 3.1.2 (ocaml/opam-repository#30204, ocaml/opam-repository#30205, ocaml/opam-repository#30202, ocaml/opam-repository#30203)
  • JS/AI-tooling releases: melange 7.0.1 by Antonio Nuno Monteiro (ocaml/opam-repository#30253), ppxderivingmelange 0.1.0 by Vitalii Shapoval (ocaml/opam-repository#30255), dap 1.1.0 by Tim McGilchrist (ocaml/opam-repository#30233), and ocaml-ai-sdk 0.5 by José Nogueira (ocaml/opam-repository#30210)
  • Seven-part dependency-bound cleanup converting to the v-prefix convention across a broad set of unrelated packages by Jan Midtgaard (ocaml/opam-repository#30225–ocaml/opam-repository#30231), and core/core_unix OpenBSD/Alpine availability guards backported to older releases by Thomas Gazagnaire (ocaml/opam-repository#30224, ocaml/opam-repository#30217)
  • On ocaml.org, Kate opened the opam 2.5.2 announcement page, still unmerged (ocaml/ocaml.org#3712); the automated Planet scraper opened a further batch of blog posts and videos, including "OCaml Weekly News, 07 Jul 2026", though several source feeds returned timeouts or unsupported-format errors (ocaml/ocaml.org#3711)
  • The industrial users page proposing AWS as an OCaml adopter (citing AWS's use of HOL Light in the s2n-bignum project) remains open from a prior week under adith nk (ocaml/ocaml.org#3681)

    • Notable Discussions

  • Dmitrii Kosarev reported bad checksums across multiple riot releases in opam-repository (ocaml/opam-repository#30242); Leandro Ostera replied that the repository moved to leostera/riot-lib and he no longer maintains the libraries, prompting a follow-up PR marking riot unmaintained and its bad-checksum versions unavailable (ocaml/opam-repository#30252)
  • Dmitrii Kosarev resolved a bad checksum on synopsis.1.0 after confirming with upstream developers, marking that version unavailable (ocaml/opam-repository#30113, ocaml/opam-repository#30245)
  • Juneyoung Lee followed up on the AWS industrial users PR on ocaml.org, asking whether an extra step is needed to get it merged (ocaml/ocaml.org#3681)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Jan Midtgaard is running a systematic, multi-part campaign converting dependency bounds to the v-prefix convention across a broad swath of unrelated opam-repository packages in a single week (ocaml/opam-repository#30225–ocaml/opam-repository#30231)
  • Continued investment in unikernel and embedded targets, with OCaml/Unikraft gaining a new 9pfs filesystem option and relocatable cross-compiler support (ocaml/opam-repository#30209), alongside the ongoing ocaml-solo5 release cadence (ocaml/opam-repository#30202)
  • Property-based testing tooling is actively growing, with the hegel/ppxhegel* family moving from a 0.8.0 first release to 0.9.0 within the same week (ocaml/opam-repository#30185, ocaml/opam-repository#30246)
  • On ocaml.org, automated bots (the Planet scraper and Dependabot) accounted for most PR volume (ocaml/ocaml.org#3709, ocaml/ocaml.org#3710, ocaml/ocaml.org#3711), while manually authored content PRs such as the AWS industrial-users addition have awaited review for over a month (ocaml/ocaml.org#3681)
  • Recurring Planet scraper failures for several feed sources (timeouts, unsupported formats) continue to appear across weekly scrape runs on ocaml.org (ocaml/ocaml.org#3710, ocaml/ocaml.org#3711)

    • OCaml Tools

    Opam 2.5.2 fixed CVE-2026-57825 while OCaml 5.5 compatibility work continued across dune, ocamlfind, opam, and ocaml-lsp.

    New Features

  • ocaml/opam released opam 2.5.2, fixing a symlink bypass of the switch-prefix check tracked as CVE-2026-57825 (ocaml/opam#7005, backported in ocaml/opam#7006), and switched internal repository storage from plain directories to gzipped tar archives to speed up update/init on NTFS and IO-constrained machines (ocaml/opam#6625)
  • ocaml/ocamlfind now installs .cmx files alongside .cmi files during make install, resolving warning-58 reports in downstream projects such as Rocq (ocaml/ocamlfind#120, fixes ocaml/ocamlfind#117), and fixed threads package lookup to catch the correct exception, restoring ocamlfind ocamlopt -config on compilers built without systhreads (ocaml/ocamlfind#99)
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml merged WebGL2 bindings closing a long-standing request (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2388, ocsigen/jsofocaml#1226), consolidated five duplicate messageEvent class types into one (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2390), fixed an if-fusion miscompilation in js_simpl that could collapse two evaluations of an effectful expression into one (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2393), and merged initial OCaml 5.6 support (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2227)
  • ocaml/ocaml-lsp reworked ppx hover expansion to call Merlin's expand-ppx command directly instead of hand-reconstructing output, fixing broken hover text for [@@deriving ...] on mutually recursive types (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1615, fixes ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1614), and switched its nix sandbox's default OCaml version to 5.5 (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1616)
  • ocaml/dune fixed relocatable-compiler detection for OCaml >= 5.5 (ocaml/dune#15444, fixes ocaml/dune#15443), aligned C compiler vendor detection with the OCaml compiler's own identifiers (ocaml/dune#15423), and stopped crashing when ~/.config/dune is a regular file rather than a directory (ocaml/dune#15475, fixes ocaml/dune#15406)
  • ocaml/odoc removed dead compatibility code for OCaml versions older than 4.08 from the loader and model (ocaml/odoc#1458)
  • ocaml/merlin added a regression test confirming project-wide occurrences/renaming correctly resolves a module name mid-path, alongside a GitHub Actions checkout v6→v7 upgrade across all workflows (ocaml/merlin#2081)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/opam shipped 2.5.2 with a CVE fix and a repository-archive storage change, while a new .install reftest suite surfaced Windows follow-up bugs
  • ocaml/ocamlfind landed cmx-file installation and a thread-lookup fix, and the maintainer closed nine long-standing issues
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml merged WebGL2 bindings, a messageEvent type consolidation, compiler-correctness fixes, and OCaml 5.6 support, with three more Web API/ESM PRs opened
  • ocaml/ocaml-lsp reworked ppx hover to delegate to Merlin and continued a multi-PR removal of internal Stdune modules
  • ocaml/dune fixed several OCaml 5.5 compatibility regressions, progressed the 3.24.1 patch release, and continued an internal stdune process-spawning refactor
  • ocaml/odoc removed legacy pre-4.08 compatibility code and continued OxCaml-related work on modes rendering and include functor support
  • ocaml/merlin had a CI-maintenance week, with six new PRs opened covering doc comments, locate/shadowing, and LRgrep
  • ocaml/opam-file-format and ocaml-dune/spawn had no recorded activity this week

    • Activity

  • ocaml/dune: Rudi Grinberg drove a multi-PR refactor of stdune's process-spawning code, unvendoring the spawn library (ocaml/dune#15470) and changing it to return Pid.t (ocaml/dune#15473, ocaml/dune#15474); the 3.24.1 patch release progressed under tracker ocaml/dune#15439, with a js_of_ocaml/enabled_if backport (ocaml/dune#15451) and an odoc build-dir path fix backport (ocaml/dune#15293) both merging
  • ocaml/ocaml-lsp: Rudi Grinberg opened and merged a batch of PRs removing internal Stdune modules in favor of standalone packages — Stdune.Int (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1619), Stdune.Pid (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1631) — with Stdune.Map removal (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1620) and others still open; Sora Morimoto fixed Dune S-expression formatting being applied to non-Dune documents (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1621)
  • ocaml/ocamlfind: David Allsopp closed nine long-standing issues dating to 2019-2022, including a Gentoo linker error (ocaml/ocamlfind#24) and an unreachable source-tarball mirror (ocaml/ocamlfind#108); Rodolphe Lepigre opened a fix to make ld.conf paths absolute for OCaml 5.5.0 support (ocaml/ocamlfind#119)
  • ocaml/opam: an exhaustive .install field reftest suite merged (ocaml/opam#6956), surfacing three Windows-specific follow-up bugs around file cleanup and libexec installs (ocaml/opam#7021, ocaml/opam#7022, ocaml/opam#7023)
  • ocaml/merlin: six new PRs opened, including a draft typing-recovery preview (ocaml/merlin#2087) and a locate fix for module resolution under shadowing, closing ocaml/merlin#1748 (ocaml/merlin#2089)
  • ocaml/odoc: art-w continued rendering OxCaml modes in generated docs (ocaml/odoc#1454), and Marek Kubica extended include functor support with review from Jon Ludlam (ocaml/odoc#1452)
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml: three new PRs opened by hhugo — an experimental ESM output mode (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2402), Web Audio/Media Capture bindings (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2401), and BroadcastChannel/SharedWorker bindings (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2400) — plus a cluster of CI-restructuring merges (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2394, ocsigen/jsofocaml#2395, ocsigen/jsofocaml#2396)

    • Notable Discussions

  • On ocaml/dune#15472, Ali Caglayan opened a design discussion on supporting Bazel's Remote Execution API for distributed builds, noting incompatibility with dune's current DAP-based action runner
  • On ocaml/dune#15458, Rodolphe Lepigre, Ali Caglayan, and Gaëtan Gilbert traced why dune exec -- prog now resolves binaries under _build/default instead of the install directory, to an intentional %{bin:...} semantics change from a previous release
  • On ocaml/merlin#2072, Ulysse reported an lrgrep compile step hanging for over 20 minutes after rebasing onto OCaml 5.5, worked around by pinning lrgrep to its main branch after Frédéric Bour helped diagnose menhir-generated naming issues
  • On ocaml/ocamlfind#118, David Allsopp narrowed a Fedora "package not found" report from Kabir G down to the dnf-packaged camlidl missing its META file, a distro packaging gap rather than an ocamlfind bug
  • On ocaml/odoc#1450, Vincent Balat raised how odoc_driver resolves same-named modules across sibling libraries (Eliom's eliom.client/eliom.server), with Jon Ludlam proposing to separate odoc compile and odoc link dependency scoping to fix it
  • On ocaml/opam#6866, Kate mentioned the project has opened a yet-to-be-formally-advertised mirror at codeberg.org/ocaml/opam, from which a patch for ocaml/opam#6999 was itself sourced (ocaml/opam#7012)
  • On ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1604, Kate explained why opam upgrade attempts to downgrade ocaml-lsp-server on OCaml 4.14, suggesting pinning or the builtin-0install solver
  • On ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1622, Sora Morimoto documented workspace/symbol taking over 13 seconds and returning empty results in a ~50,000-file monorepo, traced to a full re-scan of every .cmt/.cmti file with no retained symbol index
  • On ocsigen/jsofocaml#2399, hhugo and Brian Ward traced an unexpected ~12k-line Temporal polyfill in compiled JS to a downstream dependency bump rather than a jsofocaml defect

    • Emerging Trends

  • OCaml 5.5 compatibility was the dominant cross-cutting theme, driving fixes in ocaml/dune#15444, ocaml/ocamlfind#119, ocaml/opam#6988/ocaml/opam#7007, and ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1616
  • Process-spawning/internal-module refactors ran in parallel across two repos, both led by Rudi Grinberg: unvendoring spawn in dune's stdune (ocaml/dune#15470) and stripping Stdune modules from ocaml-lsp in favor of standalone packages (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1619, ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1631)
  • Delegating to Merlin rather than reimplementing logic recurred in ocaml-lsp: the ppx-hover rewrite calls Merlin's expand-ppx directly (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1615), and merlin itself exposed a warnings-parsing function to unblock ocaml-lsp's own hover work (ocaml/merlin#2088)
  • Legacy-code and backlog removal appeared in both odoc (dropping OCaml <4.08 compatibility branches, ocaml/odoc#1458) and ocamlfind (closing nine multi-year-old issues, e.g. ocaml/ocamlfind#24)
  • Security and correctness fixes fast-tracked to stable branches: opam backported its CVE-2026-57825 fix and several path-resolution bugs directly to the 2.5 branch the same week they landed on default (ocaml/opam#7005/ocaml/opam#7006, ocaml/opam#6953/ocaml/opam#7003)
  • AI-assisted development disclosure continued to surface explicitly, with Carine Morel noting she used Claude to fix a merlin module-shadowing bug (ocaml/merlin#2089) and several jsofocaml PR descriptions noting Claude Code generation (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2401, ocsigen/jsofocaml#2400)

    • OxCaml

    oxcaml/oxcaml advanced reaper unboxing, jkind/ikind precision, and atomic-field safety, while opam-repository packaged the 5.2.0minus-39 toolchain.

    New Features

  • Fibers now store dynamic bindings in a growable stack table with new caml_dynamic_push/caml_dynamic_pop primitives, by Max Slater (oxcaml/oxcaml@5b3304c)
  • Functional record updates that implicitly read an [@atomic] field nonatomically are now rejected at typecheck time, closing upstream ocaml/ocaml#14918, by Joe Kerrigan (oxcaml/oxcaml#6453)
  • Mode coercion on function return values is now allowed for non-local axes (e.g. int -> int :> int -> int @ portable), by @dkalinichenko-js (oxcaml/oxcaml#6407)
  • Correctness fixes for the -x86-peephole-optimize pass, plus a restructuring of X86_proc so rewrites also reach the internal-assembler output, by Xavier Clerc (oxcaml/oxcaml#6426)
  • Reaper's unboxing transformation extended to boxed int32/int64/nativeint numbers via a new Boxed_number field constructor, by Mark Shinwell (oxcaml/oxcaml#6437)
  • New imprecise-kind-annotation warning (191) flags kind annotations that differ from the inferred jkind, by @dkalinichenko-js (oxcaml/oxcaml#5362)
  • First-class modules are now supported inside quotes, with automatic annotation insertion for packing/unpacking, by Jakub Bachurski (oxcaml/oxcaml#5884)
  • oxcaml/opam-repository added the oxcaml-compiler.5.4.0-ox2 variant and corrected its download URL, by David Allsopp (oxcaml/opam-repository@fe691dc)
  • Landed the v0.18~preview.130.106+341 Jane Street package snapshot, adding several hundred packages spanning core, async, bonsai, and hardcaml via the janestreet public-release automation (oxcaml/opam-repository@3dce94a)
  • odoc/sherlodoc 3.2.0+ox2, jsonrpc/lsp/ocaml-lsp-server 1.19.0+ox2, and merlin/merlin-lib 5.2.1-502+ox2 added for the 5.2.0minus-39 compiler, by Diana Kalinichenko (oxcaml/opam-repository@42d7cdab, oxcaml/opam-repository@49ed501)

    • Overview

  • oxcaml/oxcaml advanced reaper unboxing to boxed numbers, added atomic-field safety checks, and shipped x86 peephole correctness fixes, alongside jkind/ikind precision groundwork (oxcaml/oxcaml#6437, oxcaml/oxcaml#6453, oxcaml/oxcaml#6426)
  • oxcaml/opam-repository pushed direct-to-main commits registering the oxcaml-compiler.5.4.0-ox2 variant, landing a large Jane Street v0.18~preview.130.106+341 package snapshot, and rebuilding dev tooling (merlin, ocaml-lsp-server, odoc, ocamlformat) against 5.2.0minus-39 (oxcaml/opam-repository@fe691dc, oxcaml/opam-repository@3dce94a)
  • No recorded activity this week in oxcaml/merlin, oxcaml/jsofocaml, or janestreet/opam-repository

    • Activity

  • James Rayman opened a series of Cmm/codegen PRs covering machtype checking, cast-constructor renaming, and adding returns : bool to Capply (oxcaml/oxcaml#6435, oxcaml/oxcaml#6448, oxcaml/oxcaml#6449, oxcaml/oxcaml#6457)
  • @julesjacobs opened work-in-progress PRs toward ikind unification, adding a Tmod type_desc constructor and starting removal of the legacy engine (oxcaml/oxcaml#6430, oxcaml/oxcaml#6451, oxcaml/oxcaml#6460)
  • Tim McGilchrist opened PRs on structured name mangling for data-section symbols and unknown debug locations (oxcaml/oxcaml#6408, oxcaml/oxcaml#6418)
  • Jacob Van Buren opened PRs to set up Claude Code integration, workflow static analysis, and deployment environments for PR secrets (oxcaml/oxcaml#6415, oxcaml/oxcaml#6416, oxcaml/oxcaml#6441)
  • Stack-check/SIMD-save correctness for the backend was completed by Xavier Clerc, fixing the live set used by Stack_check and adding a regression codegen test (oxcaml/oxcaml#6337, oxcaml/oxcaml#6336)
  • Allocation-mode inference gained heap-allocation detection to constrain modes, merged by @zhizhuoxin after review from @dkalinichenko-js (oxcaml/oxcaml#6319)
  • AVX512 instruction encoding and backend support remained under active review between Max Slater and Xavier Clerc, still open (oxcaml/oxcaml#6294, oxcaml/oxcaml#6339)
  • Closed-without-merge activity included Aspen Smith's Dynamic stdlib implementation (oxcaml/oxcaml#5172) and @julesjacobs's four-part mode-bitfields series, superseded by the ikind-unification work (oxcaml/oxcaml#5677, oxcaml/oxcaml#5673, oxcaml/oxcaml#5672, oxcaml/oxcaml#5671)
  • oxcaml/opam-repository extended the test workflow to also run on the 5.2.0minus39 branch and to test wasm_of_ocaml-compiler and previously-broken odoc/sherlodoc/utop packages, by David Allsopp (oxcaml/opam-repository@354043e)
  • Disabled wasm_of_ocaml-compiler on the Arch Linux CI runner to work around an unreleased GCC 16 upstream fix, and added ocamlformat/ocamlformat-lib to the CI broken-packages allowlist since they fail under 5.2.0minus39, by David Allsopp (oxcaml/opam-repository@e04414e, oxcaml/opam-repository@527cf13)

    • Notable Discussions

  • Extended review of the Merlin typing-recovery mechanism in oxcaml/oxcaml, with Liam Stevenson giving detailed feedback to Xavier Van de Woestyne across 90+ comments on how the mechanism integrates with the type checker (oxcaml/oxcaml#6366)
  • Aspen Smith, Joe Kerrigan, Jacob Van Buren, and David Allsopp discussed scope and workflow concerns around setting up Claude Code integration for oxcaml/oxcaml (oxcaml/oxcaml#6415)
  • Design discussion on defunctionalizing %resume between Aspen Smith and Max Slater, resolved and merged after review (oxcaml/oxcaml#6440)
  • Review of atomic-field definitions in mixed records between Joe Kerrigan and Ryan Tjoa, covering record-representation and typechecking edge cases (oxcaml/oxcaml#6423)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Continued investment in the reaper (Flambda2 unboxing pass) in oxcaml/oxcaml: new documentation, poison-value handling, unboxing counters, and boxed-number support all landed this week (oxcaml/oxcaml#6419, oxcaml/oxcaml#6409, oxcaml/oxcaml#6437)
  • Ongoing jkind/ikind precision work spanning a new imprecise-annotation warning and an emerging ikind-unification effort aiming to replace the legacy engine (oxcaml/oxcaml#5362, oxcaml/oxcaml#6430, oxcaml/oxcaml#6451, oxcaml/oxcaml#6460)
  • Atomic-field safety hardening in the type system, restricting both functional updates and definitions of atomic fields in mixed records (oxcaml/oxcaml#6453, oxcaml/oxcaml#6423)
  • Across the group, toolchain consolidation is the dominant theme in opam-repository: dev tools (merlin, ocaml-lsp-server, ocamlformat, odoc) are being rebuilt and re-tested against 5.2.0minus-39 in a tight commit sequence while early 5.4.0-ox2 packaging groundwork is laid (oxcaml/opam-repository@42d7cdab, oxcaml/opam-repository@fe691dc)
  • Growing internal tooling investment in oxcaml/oxcaml: Claude Code integration, workflow static analysis, and cachix caching for nix builds (oxcaml/oxcaml#6415, oxcaml/oxcaml#6416, oxcaml/oxcaml#6414)

    • OCaml Core

    Configurable domain/thread stack sizes, Windows filename hardening, and an ephemeron-termination fix landed in ocaml/ocaml.

    New Features

  • New OCAMLRUNPARAM='S=' option lets programs configure the minimum system stack size used when spawning a Thread or Domain, useful for FFI code that needs a larger native stack; documented in man/ocamlrun.1, the reference manual, Thread.create and Domain.spawn (ocaml/ocaml#14195, ocaml/ocaml#14860) by @Jeannalyse, reviewed by Antonin Décimo
  • Sys.file_exists/related Sys primitives now use GetFileAttributes instead of stat_os on Windows, avoiding a kernel bug in GetFileInformationByName that made Sys.file_exists "C:\\...\\repro:xxx" wrongly return true (ocaml/ocaml#14919, reported as ocaml/ocaml#14911-adjacent) by David Allsopp
  • Filename functions on Windows now treat : strictly as the drive/volume separator rather than sometimes as a directory separator, fixing surprising results from Filename.concat on paths like C:\Foo: (ocaml/ocaml#14871, ocaml/ocaml#14916) by David Allsopp
  • Fixed a hang in caml_shutdown() under OCAMLRUNPARAM="c=1" (cleanup-at-exit mode) where the final GC cycle could get stuck in Phase_sweep_and_mark_main because orphaned ephemerons from a terminated domain were never adopted (ocaml/ocaml#14906) by Olivier Nicole
  • Multicore GC now waits for all domains to finish marking before starting another round of ephemeron marking, avoiding unnecessary marking work at the cost of potentially longer GC cycles in some workloads (ocaml/ocaml#14774) by Gabriel Scherer, reviewed by Damien Doligez
  • Unix.EACCES documentation typo fixed (previously misspelled EACCESS) in unix.mli/unixLabels.mli (ocaml/ocaml#14920) by Kate
  • Memory-model documentation comments in runtime/memory.c clarified to be more precise about how GC frontiers update (ocaml/ocaml#14857, ocaml/ocaml#14924) by Olivier Nicole
  • HACKING.adoc build documentation pinned to Ubuntu 24.04 for reproducible dev-environment setup (ocaml/ocaml#14926) by Tim McGilchrist

    • Overview

  • ocaml/ocaml merged a configurable thread/domain system-stack-size option (ocaml/ocaml#14860), two Windows path-handling fixes (ocaml/ocaml#14916, ocaml/ocaml#14919), and a multicore-GC ephemeron/shutdown correctness fix (ocaml/ocaml#14906, ocaml/ocaml#14774)
  • Ten further PRs were opened in ocaml/ocaml spanning a new Atomic.compare_and_exchange function (ocaml/ocaml#14912), compiler-backend inlining and typechecker changes (ocaml/ocaml#14925, ocaml/ocaml#14913, ocaml/ocaml#14910, ocaml/ocaml#14927), and macOS/Cygwin build fixes (ocaml/ocaml#14921, ocaml/ocaml#14923)
  • The GC-pacing rework tracked in ocaml/ocaml#14796 remains open with test failures still to debug
  • ocaml/RFCs recorded no activity this week

    • Activity

  • @Jeannalyse opened a PR adding Atomic.compare_and_exchange : 'a t -> expected:'a -> set:'a -> 'a to the standard library, following up on a request from Daniel Bünzli (ocaml/ocaml#14889, ocaml/ocaml#14912)
  • Antonin Décimo opened a set of small build fixes discovered while testing on Cygwin (ocaml/ocaml#14921)
  • Nathan Taylor opened a runtime fix to print errno when sigaltstack fails, aiding diagnosis of signal-handling setup errors (ocaml/ocaml#14928)
  • Stefan Muenzel opened two compiler-backend PRs: inlining the full-application part of caml_apply (ocaml/ocaml#14925) and eliding the occurs-check for parameters that are fresh type variables (ocaml/ocaml#14913)
  • Gabriel Scherer opened a PR compressing the definition of union-find path compression used in the type-checker (ocaml/ocaml#14910)
  • Florian Angeletti opened a typechecker PR on path equivalence modulo aliases (ocaml/ocaml#14927)
  • David Allsopp opened three build/packaging PRs: fixing compiler cloning in the opam sandbox on macOS (ocaml/ocaml#14923), sanitizing the build environment (ocaml/ocaml#14915), and fixing installation in opam when OCAMLTOP_INCLUDE_PATH is invalid (ocaml/ocaml#14914)
  • Ongoing GC-pacing rework by Damien Doligez, implementing new GC-pacing logic as the last item of an earlier tracking issue, remains open with test failures still to debug and a rebase pending (ocaml/ocaml#14324, ocaml/ocaml#14796), related to community reports of GC behavior differences between 4.14 and 5.x in ocaml/ocaml#14533
  • Cross-architecture backend work continued outside PR-merge boundaries this week, with Tim McGilchrist tracking frame-pointer support for RiscV and POWER (ocaml/ocaml#14506, ocaml/ocaml#14505)

    • Notable Discussions

  • Ryan Tjoa reported that functional record updates ({ r with j }) on records with [@atomic] fields silently emit implicit atomic loads without the same protection as pattern matching; Gabriel Scherer and Joe Kerrigan agreed this was an oversight that should be forbidden, while updates that fully overwrite all atomic fields (with no implicit load) should remain accepted (ocaml/ocaml#14918)
  • Christophe Raffalli proposed a #x pattern-matching syntax for constant patterns as sugar for a when clause; after triage-meeting discussion, Olivier Nicole, Stefan Muenzel and Florian Angeletti judged the syntactic translation brittle and a likely source of bugs, recommending explicit when clauses or a PPX instead; the issue was closed (ocaml/ocaml#14908)
  • Alain Frisch investigated counter-intuitive Format module wrapping behavior where a smaller indentation produced more line-wrapping than a larger one, and closed the issue after confirming it reflects documented (if surprising) behavior of the default structural box type distinct from hov boxes (ocaml/ocaml#14917)
  • Romain Beauxis and Pierre-Yves Strub discussed GC pacing and default parameter regressions between OCaml 4.14 and 5.x, with custom_major_ratio tuning reported to resolve a 5x checking-time blow-up seen in EasyCrypt on 5.5, feeding into the GC-pacing rework tracked in ocaml/ocaml#14796 (ocaml/ocaml#14533)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Continued Windows platform hardening, with three related fixes/reports this week touching Sys.file_exists, Filename.concat, and colon handling in paths, several stemming from the same underlying report (ocaml/ocaml#14871, ocaml/ocaml#14911, ocaml/ocaml#14916, ocaml/ocaml#14919)
  • Ongoing focus on multicore GC and ephemeron correctness, with two merged fixes this week (ocaml/ocaml#14774, ocaml/ocaml#14906) plus documentation clarification (ocaml/ocaml#14857) and the broader GC-pacing rework in progress (ocaml/ocaml#14796)
  • Several small compiler-backend performance/typechecker PRs opened by different authors in the same week (inlining caml_apply, occurs-check elision, path compression, path equivalence) suggest active parallel work on typechecker and native-code-generation internals (ocaml/ocaml#14925, ocaml/ocaml#14913, ocaml/ocaml#14910, ocaml/ocaml#14927)
  • ocaml/RFCs had no new proposals or discussion this week, in contrast to prior weeks' RFC activity

    • Multicore

    Eio hardened sandbox/error handling with 15+ PRs; saturn opened qcheck/ocamlformat PRs; ocaml-uring discussed system liburing support.

    New Features

  • Eio.Net.getaddrinfo, getaddrinfo_stream, and getaddrinfo_datagram now raise a descriptive Address_lookup_failed error instead of silently returning [] on failure, implemented by Thomas Leonard building on Christiano Haesbaert's earlier work (ocaml-multicore/eio#866, fixing ocaml-multicore/eio#776 and ocaml-multicore/eio#351)
  • Eio.Path.load reworked to use a buffered reader instead of pre-sizing from stat, fixing reads of zero-size files such as /proc entries, by Patrick Ferris and Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#869, ocaml-multicore/eio#878)
  • Eio.File.Stat.t gained blksize/blocks fields for on-disk usage, with fstat switched to statx on Linux, by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#865)
  • Eio.Path.chown and chmod hardened against sandbox escape via symlinks, by Thomas Leonard and Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#877, ocaml-multicore/eio#872)
  • Windows build fixed by declaring unixsupport functions CAMLextern, unblocking mdx tests, by Anil Madhavapeddy with a fix suggested by David Allsopp (ocaml-multicore/eio#881)

    • Overview

  • ocaml-multicore/eio had the most substantive activity, with hardening of getaddrinfo error reporting, sandbox-escape resistance for chown/chmod, and eio_linux error-handling robustness across roughly 17 merged or closed PRs
  • ocaml-multicore/saturn had two PRs opened by Carine Morel: a qcheck compatibility fix and an ocamlformat update (ocaml-multicore/saturn#188, ocaml-multicore/saturn#189)
  • ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring saw a maintainer follow-up on the long-open request to support building against a system-installed liburing (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#156)
  • No recorded activity in domainslib, meio, eio-trace, picos, kcas, or ocaml-iomux this week

    • Activity

  • An open ocaml-multicore/eio#875 PR proposes a GADT-based DSL for pre-connect socket options, opened by Anil Madhavapeddy; Thomas Leonard questioned whether the DSL was becoming too complex and suggested exposing a lower-level BSD-sockets-style API alongside it
  • ocaml-multicore/eio#873, a getsockopt_string truncation-check PR, was closed without merging after discussion showed the existing bounds check was already correct
  • Several long-standing eio issues were closed as a result of this week's fixes, including the umbrella "Finish eio_posix backend" tracker (ocaml-multicore/eio#456) and the /proc read-failure reports (ocaml-multicore/eio#835, ocaml-multicore/eio#798)
  • Carine Morel opened two PRs in ocaml-multicore/saturn: a test-suite fix for qcheck compatibility (ocaml-multicore/saturn#188) and an ocamlformat update (ocaml-multicore/saturn#189); neither merged within the week
  • In ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring, Anil Madhavapeddy responded to Stéphane Glondu's request to support building against a system-installed liburing (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#156), noting he is still working out build-system changes to support both vendored and system configurations

    • Notable Discussions

  • On the pre-connect socket options PR in ocaml-multicore/eio, Thomas Leonard questioned the shape of the growing options DSL and suggested a lower-level setsockopt/bind_socket/connect_socket API; Anil Madhavapeddy argued Eio's DSLs exist so backends can interpret portable intent, citing performance, portability (an in-progress mirage-eio effort by Thomas Gazagnaire), and tracing/backpressure motivations (ocaml-multicore/eio#875)
  • The eio README's framing versus Lwt/Async was debated after @redianthus argued that describing Eio as "replacing" existing concurrency libraries overstates adoption, citing Ocsigen's continued use of Lwt; the discussion converged on describing Eio as implementing similar functionality via effects (ocaml-multicore/eio#879)
  • The chmod/chown sandbox-escape fixes prompted a detailed thread on kernel/glibc behaviour of fchmodat2, AT_EMPTY_PATH, and ENOSYS fallbacks across Linux kernel versions, including strace evidence from a 6.1 kernel VM, between Anil Madhavapeddy and Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#872)
  • In ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring, Anil Madhavapeddy confirmed to Stéphane Glondu that system-liburing packaging support has not been dropped but requires further build-system work (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#156)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Sandbox-escape hardening continues in eio, following chown with chmod symlink fixes this week, both flagged as related to a possible move to a modern glibc/kernel minimum (ocaml-multicore/eio#877, ocaml-multicore/eio#872, ocaml-multicore/eio#845)
  • eio_linux error-handling robustness is being incrementally tightened via the Uring.Res module, fd-lifetime fixes, and socket-option bounds checks (ocaml-multicore/eio#868, ocaml-multicore/eio#871, ocaml-multicore/eio#876)
  • Toolchain modernization continued in eio with the uring minimum bumped to 2.15.0+ and CI/bench Dockerfiles moved to OCaml 5.5 (ocaml-multicore/eio#867), alongside similar formatter/dependency maintenance in ocaml-multicore/saturn (ocaml-multicore/saturn#188, ocaml-multicore/saturn#189)
  • Group activity this week was concentrated almost entirely in ocaml-multicore/eio, with the remaining eight repositories showing minimal (ocaml-uring, saturn) or no recorded activity
entry.summary: Opam 2.5.2 fixed a symlink CVE while ocaml/ocaml gained configurable stack sizes and js_of_ocaml shipped WebGL2 and OCaml 5.6 support.

entry.title: Week 27, 2026: A typechecking speedup and ephemeron GC fix landed in ocaml/ocaml, while Dune 3.24.0 and coordinated MirageOS releases shipped in opam-repository.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Core Typechecking performance improved by removing closure allocations from deep_occur_rec, the routine that traverses type expressions during unification; benchmarks on a large js_of_ocaml file show up to a 45% wall-clock speedup with flambda and 20% without, by Stefan Muenzel (ocaml/ocaml#14900), motivated by the regression reported in ocaml/ocaml#14897
  • OCaml Core Major GC ephemeron marking reworked so ephe_mark() calls mark() directly on markable data instead of only scheduling it, avoiding quadratic-looking marking behaviour for long ephemeron dependency chains, by Gabriel Scherer (ocaml/ocaml#14688), a safer follow-up to the previously reverted ocaml/ocaml#14657
  • OCaml Core Fixed a scope error in ctype where non-dependent module-type application could erase the whole result type after the first package type was encountered, causing incorrect types to be accepted for anonymous module type structs, by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml#14892, fixing ocaml/ocaml#14891)
  • OCaml Core Removed a useless Option.map call in Btype.fold_row, a small internal cleanup noticed while working on the typechecking performance PR, by Vincent Laviron (ocaml/ocaml#14904)
  • OCaml Ecosystem Dune 3.24.0 released (18 packages) by Shon Feder in opam-repository (ocaml/opam-repository#30092), with a companion announcement PR opened on ocaml.org (ocaml/ocaml.org#3704)
  • OCaml Ecosystem Coordinated MirageOS ecosystem releases by Hannes Mehnert covering x509 1.1.1, tls 2.1.1, charrua 3.1.2/3.2.0, mirage 4.11.1, and kdf 1.1.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#30154, ocaml/opam-repository#30155, ocaml/opam-repository#30156)
  • OCaml Ecosystem jsofocaml/wasmofocaml 6.4.1 released (8 packages) by @hhugo (ocaml/opam-repository#30173), fixing wasm module-name derivation and test path handling broken by dune 3.24's leading-./ path form (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2371, ocsigen/jsofocaml#2384)
  • Multicore ocaml-uring 2.15.0 released by Anil Madhavapeddy, updating to liburing 2.15, adding shutdown, socket, renameat, symlinkat, fallocate, ftruncate ops and vectored readv/writev on fixed buffers, and raising the minimum OCaml version to 5.2 (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#157, ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#144)
  • OCaml Ecosystem New hegel property-based testing library with Antithesis support submitted by Ethan Chou (ocaml/opam-repository#30185), and new ocgtk GTK4 bindings by Chris Armstrong (ocaml/opam-repository#30134)

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    Dune 3.24.0 shipped in opam-repository and was announced on ocaml.org, alongside coordinated MirageOS releases and new packages.

    New Features

  • Dune 3.24.0 released (18 packages) by Shon Feder in opam-repository (ocaml/opam-repository#30092), with a companion announcement PR opened on ocaml.org (ocaml/ocaml.org#3704)
  • Coordinated MirageOS ecosystem releases by Hannes Mehnert covering x509 1.1.1, tls 2.1.1, charrua 3.1.2/3.2.0, mirage 4.11.1, and kdf 1.1.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#30154, ocaml/opam-repository#30155, ocaml/opam-repository#30156)
  • New hegel property-based testing library with Antithesis support, plus PPX helpers, submitted by Ethan Chou after several iterations (ocaml/opam-repository#30185)
  • New ocgtk GTK4 bindings and conf-gtk4 dependency by Chris Armstrong (ocaml/opam-repository#30134)
  • jsofocaml/wasmofocaml 6.4.1 release (8 packages) by @hhugo (ocaml/opam-repository#30173)
  • Around a dozen further new packages submitted, including chatoyant, soteria, playwright, menhirformat, keyseq, melange-edn, starpath, and opam-minver (ocaml/opam-repository#30190, ocaml/opam-repository#30150, ocaml/opam-repository#30146)
  • Fixed the OCaml Workshop 2026 "Important Dates" panel on ocaml.org, correcting the submission deadline to 12 Jul and the notification date to 3 Aug by Sudha Parimala (ocaml/ocaml.org#3707, ocaml/ocaml.org#3708)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/opam-repository: dune 3.24.0 (18 packages) and a coordinated MirageOS release round (x509, tls, charrua, mirage, kdf) shipped alongside roughly 15 new package submissions (ocaml/opam-repository#30092, ocaml/opam-repository#30154)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org: corrected OCaml Workshop 2026 deadline dates, continued automated Planet-blog and platform-release ingestion, and had a broken cookbook link reported (ocaml/ocaml.org#3707, ocaml/ocaml.org#3703)
  • Dune's 3.24.0 release (ocaml/opam-repository#30092) was the week's shared thread, prompting both downstream package fixes in opam-repository and a pending announcement post on ocaml.org (ocaml/ocaml.org#3704)

    • Activity

  • Several opam-repository release PRs remain unmerged, including lmdb 1.1.2, caisar 6.0, Frama-C 33.0~beta-Arsenic, Caqti 3.0.0, colibri2 0.6, and ocsigen-toolkit 4.3.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#30198, ocaml/opam-repository#30136, ocaml/opam-repository#30174)
  • The dune 3.24.0 release prompted a wave of downstream maintenance PRs in opam-repository bounding dune versions or disabling brittle tests (ocaml/opam-repository#30157, ocaml/opam-repository#30162, ocaml/opam-repository#30161)
  • On ocaml.org, three Planet scrape PRs merged bringing in new blog posts and an OCaml Weekly News edition, while an automated platform-releases scrape PR (212 lines, four files) remains open from before this week (ocaml/ocaml.org#3702, ocaml/ocaml.org#3705, ocaml/ocaml.org#3693)
  • A broken link in the ocaml.org Dream web-server cookbook was reported, pointing to a stale aantron.github.io/dream URL needing redirection to camlworks.github.io/dream (ocaml/ocaml.org#3703)

    • Notable Discussions

  • Contributors debated ownership of revdep breakage following the dune 3.24.0 release, with Hannes Mehnert asking whether fixing packages broken by a dune release falls to opam-repository maintainers, dune maintainers, or the affected package's own maintainer (ocaml/opam-repository#30157)
  • Christophe Raffalli and Marcello Seri agreed to mark the old simple_httpd 1.0 as unavailable rather than resolve a disputed checksum (ocaml/opam-repository#30123)
  • Florian Angeletti tracked OCaml 5.5.0 release readiness (ocaml/opam-repository#29463), while a related macOS second-switch build failure for 5.5.0~alpha was reported by @jrfondren and traced to an upstream fix by Kate (ocaml/opam-repository#29496)
  • Romain Beauxis asked the community to stop running dune runtest unconditionally in CI, with Dmitrii Kosarev and Shon Feder discussing existing mechanisms for running a subset of tests (ocaml/opam-repository#29166)
  • Tibor reported the broken Dream cookbook link and attempted a fix, but hit a make switch build failure where topkg referenced an unrelated local opam switch instead of the default one (ocaml/ocaml.org#3703)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Coordinated multi-package release rounds continued, exemplified by Hannes Mehnert's MirageOS-ecosystem releases spanning x509, tls, charrua, mirage, and kdf within the same week (ocaml/opam-repository#30154, ocaml/opam-repository#30184)
  • The dune 3.24.0 release (ocaml/opam-repository#30092) triggered downstream compatibility fixes in opam-repository and surfaced an open question about who owns fixing revdep breakage (ocaml/opam-repository#30157)
  • Preparation for the OCaml 5.5.0 release continued in opam-repository, including a release-readiness tracking issue and a camlp5 fix for a test broken by 5.5.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#29463, ocaml/opam-repository#30163)
  • ocaml.org content this week was driven mainly by recurring automated ingestion (Planet blog scraping, platform release tracking) rather than new manual authoring (ocaml/ocaml.org#3702, ocaml/ocaml.org#3693)
  • Event-logistics upkeep for the OCaml Workshop 2026 page required a second date correction shortly after the first, suggesting details were still being finalised with organisers (ocaml/ocaml.org#3707, ocaml/ocaml.org#3708)
  • Local dev-environment setup (make switch/opam) surfaced as an onboarding barrier for a prospective ocaml.org contributor attempting a small documentation fix (ocaml/ocaml.org#3703)

    • OCaml Tools

    OxCaml

    OCaml Core

    A typechecking speedup and an ephemeron GC fix merged in ocaml/ocaml, while ocaml/RFCs received a new proposal for a destinations API.

    New Features

  • Typechecking performance improved by removing closure allocations from deep_occur_rec, which traverses type expressions during unification; benchmarks on a large js_of_ocaml file show up to a 45% wall-clock speedup with flambda and 20% without, by Stefan Muenzel (ocaml/ocaml#14900), motivated by the regression reported in ocaml/ocaml#14897
  • Major GC ephemeron marking reworked so ephe_mark() calls mark() directly on markable data instead of only scheduling it, avoiding quadratic-looking marking behaviour for long ephemeron dependency chains, by Gabriel Scherer (ocaml/ocaml#14688), a safer follow-up to the previously reverted ocaml/ocaml#14657
  • Fixed a scope error in ctype where non-dependent module-type application could erase the whole result type after the first package type was encountered, causing incorrect types to be accepted for anonymous module type structs, by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml#14892, fixing ocaml/ocaml#14891)
  • Removed a useless Option.map call in Btype.fold_row, a small internal cleanup noticed while working on the typechecking performance PR, by Vincent Laviron (ocaml/ocaml#14904)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/ocaml merged a typechecking performance fix (ocaml/ocaml#14900, up to 45% wall-clock speedup on large types) and an ephemeron GC marking fix (ocaml/ocaml#14688)
  • A ctype scope-error fix (ocaml/ocaml#14892) and a small internal cleanup (ocaml/ocaml#14904) also landed in ocaml/ocaml
  • New PRs were opened in ocaml/ocaml for stdlib additions (ocaml/ocaml#14909), a caml_shutdown/ephemeron termination bug (ocaml/ocaml#14906), large-interval pattern matching (ocaml/ocaml#14907), and an opam clone macOS fix targeted for 5.5.1 (ocaml/ocaml#14901)
  • Design discussion continued on a static-linking / link-time parameter resolution proposal in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#14895), with reviewers requesting a formal design document
  • ocaml/RFCs received one new proposal, ocaml/RFCs#62, for a compiler-assisted API exposing destinations (write-once pointers) to PPXs, opened by Gabriel Radanne

    • Activity

  • Nicolás Ojeda Bär opened Dynarray.append_iarray and Pqueue.of_iarray stdlib additions to avoid copying an iarray into a mutable array or resorting to unsafe code (ocaml/ocaml#14909, fixing ocaml/ocaml#14320)
  • Olivier Nicole opened a fix for caml_shutdown() termination with ephemerons, addressing an infinite loop in Phase_sweep_and_mark_main when the last domain is terminated with OCAMLRUNPARAM=c=1, joint work with Damien Doligez that has been affecting CI for weeks (ocaml/ocaml#14906, related to ocaml/ocaml#14594)
  • Florian Angeletti opened a pattern-matching compiler change to support switches over very large integer intervals (beyond the previous $[-2^{16}; 2^{16}]$ limit), with Vincent Laviron and Stefan Muenzel reviewing edge cases around interval overflow (ocaml/ocaml#14907)
  • Kate opened a fix for opam clone on macOS, where the default /bin/sh (old bash) mishandles heredocs and creates temporary files in the wrong directory, targeted for the 5.5.1 release per David Allsopp (ocaml/ocaml#14901, fixing ocaml/opam-repository#29496)
  • Ongoing design discussion on Raphaël Proust's static linking and link-time linking parameter resolution proposal (-cclib-static, -cclib-variant, -static, -linking-variant), with Daniel Bünzli requesting a proper design document referencing his own OCaml library linking RFC and Calascibetta Romain noting relevance to MirageOS/Solo5 unikernel toolchains (ocaml/ocaml#14895)
  • Jeannalyse continued iterating on the "Signature mismatch" error message rewrite (renaming "is not included"/"does not include" to subtype/supertype terminology), with extensive wording feedback from Florian Angeletti and Brandon Stride (ocaml/ocaml#14896, following discussion in ocaml/ocaml#11937)
  • Florian Angeletti opened a guideline for LLM usage in bug reports, recommending against mixing LLM-generated content with bug reports and cautioning about LLM-shrunk reproduction cases losing the original bug, reviewed by Olivier Nicole, Daniel Bünzli, Stefan Muenzel, and Miod Vallat (ocaml/ocaml#14899)
  • Anarchos continued the Haiku port PR covering unix socket tests, single-threaded setlocale, and signal handling differences on Haiku, still marked as conflicting (ocaml/ocaml#14773)
  • Tim McGilchrist's PR on missing minor-heap allocation statistics for the main domain at exit remains under review, with Gabriel Scherer proposing alternatives to the extra minor-GC-at-exit approach (ocaml/ocaml#14522)
  • Tim McGilchrist's s390x CFI/backtrace fix, merged earlier this year, was confirmed and its tracking issue closed this week (ocaml/ocaml#14500, closing ocaml/ocaml#13509)
  • Gabriel Radanne opened a new RFC proposing to expose destinations (write-once pointers used in tail-modulo-cons and related destination-passing-style transformations) so they can be manipulated from PPXs rather than only from the compiler's internal Lambda IR (ocaml/RFCs#62); the proposal remains open and awaiting review, with no comments yet recorded

    • Notable Discussions

  • Extensive back-and-forth on rewording the "Signature mismatch" compiler error message, weighing "subtype"/"supertype" terminology against readability and consistency with existing messages about include, involving Jeannalyse, Florian Angeletti, and Brandon Stride (ocaml/ocaml#14896)
  • Daniel Bünzli pushed back on the static/link-time linking proposal, arguing that adding new .cma metadata fields and a shell-command-based pkg-config resolution mechanism needs a design document before merging, citing past problems with ad-hoc META file metadata and raising a security concern about archives embedding shell commands run at link time; Calascibetta Romain offered a MirageOS/Solo5 use case as a concrete test (ocaml/ocaml#14895)
  • Deep investigation into the typing performance regression in js_of_ocaml's lwt_xmlHttpRequest.ml, with Stefan Muenzel, Jacques Garrigue, and Gabriel Scherer diagnosing that unification of deeply nested object types causes repeated, non-shared expansion of type abbreviations (ocaml/ocaml#14897, related to ocaml/ocaml#11648 and ocaml/ocaml#14801)
  • Simmo Saan shared updated Goblint benchmark results comparing OCaml 4.14 against 5.6.0+trunk (including ocaml/ocaml#14885 and ocaml/ocaml#14894), showing average CPU time regression down to +4% from earlier measurements, prompting Gabriel Scherer to ask about remaining outlier tests (ocaml/ocaml#13733)

    • Emerging Trends

  • A cluster of typechecking and GC performance work landed or progressed in ocaml/ocaml this week, including deep_occur_rec allocation removal (ocaml/ocaml#14900), ephemeron marking (ocaml/ocaml#14688), and ongoing Goblint/Frama-C regression tracking (ocaml/ocaml#13733, ocaml/ocaml#11733), with Vincent Laviron also reporting -O3 and inlining-attribute experiments that cut deep_occur_rec time further
  • Maintainers are formalizing process around AI-assisted contributions to ocaml/ocaml, with Florian Angeletti's bug-report guideline proposal (ocaml/ocaml#14899) following earlier discussion in ocaml/ocaml#14842
  • Recurring pattern of closure-allocation elimination in the typechecker (renamings in recursive definitions from ocaml/ocaml#14885/ocaml/ocaml#14894, and deep_occur_rec from ocaml/ocaml#14900) as a recurring technique for compile-time speedups, motivated by real-world regressions reported by users of js_of_ocaml and Goblint
  • The single ocaml/RFCs proposal this week (ocaml/RFCs#62) continues a pattern of exposing compiler-internal mechanisms (here, destinations) to library and PPX authors rather than keeping them restricted to the compiler's internal IR

    • Multicore
entry.summary: A typechecking speedup and ephemeron GC fix landed in ocaml/ocaml, while Dune 3.24.0 and coordinated MirageOS releases shipped in opam-repository.

entry.title: Week 26, 2026: OCaml 5.5 support shipped in merlin and ocaml-lsp releases while oxcaml retired its OCaml-4 runtime and eio gained a portable Sockopt API.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Tools ocaml/merlin published release v5.8-505 with OCaml 5.5 support, by Ulysse (ocaml/merlin#2077, release), bundling a signature-help fix for type aliases (ocaml/merlin#2067) and a locate fix for punned let bindings (ocaml/merlin#2066)
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/ocaml-lsp published release 1.27.0, adding OCaml 5.5 support (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1609, release) and no longer forcing Merlin's real_paths = false, letting full type-alias paths show in errors, fixed by Gaëtan Gilbert (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1579, closes ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1395)
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/dune added command/subcommand/flag completion for bash, zsh, and pwsh via dune completion [shell], by Ambre Austen Suhamy (ocaml/dune#14779), and made dune build --auto-promote/dune fmt exit 0 on success, by Rudi Grinberg (ocaml/dune#15284)
  • OCaml Tools ocaml/opam added a native OpamTar module reading/writing tar.gz archives via the tar library instead of shelling out, by R. Boujbel building on work by Kate (ocaml/opam#6945)
  • OCaml Tools ocsigen/jsofocaml merged new Crypto (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2380) and Notification/Clipboard (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2379) Web API bindings, and Lwt_js_events.mutation/mutations for MutationObserver (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2376), all by @hhugo
  • OxCaml oxcaml/oxcaml added a new -experimental-optimizations compiler flag bundling off-by-default codegen improvements (CFG prologue shrink-wrap, x86 peephole, irc allocator, CFG block merging), by @ttebbi-janestreet (oxcaml/oxcaml#6174)
  • OxCaml Nick Barnes removed the legacy OCaml-4 runtime and dual-runtime switch from oxcaml/oxcaml (oxcaml/oxcaml#6218), and Tim McGilchrist landed ocamlfilt, a demangler for compiler symbol names (oxcaml/oxcaml#5100)
  • Multicore ocaml-multicore/eio added an extensible Eio.Net.Sockopt API with portable socket-option constructors (SO_REUSEADDR, TCP_NODELAY, and others) and Linux-specific TCP_*/IP_* options, by Thomas Leonard based on Anil Madhavapeddy's original design (ocaml-multicore/eio#858, ocaml-multicore/eio#859, ocaml-multicore/eio#575)
  • Multicore ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring added readv_fixed/writev_fixed for multi-buffer reads/writes against registered fixed buffers, by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#155)
  • OCaml Core ocaml/ocaml improved compilation of recursive function definitions to avoid allocating pseudo-closure blocks for local aliases, fixing a code-generation regression (ocaml/ocaml#14876), by Vincent Laviron (ocaml/ocaml#14885) and Gabriel Scherer (ocaml/ocaml#14894)
  • OCaml Core RISC-V code generation now uses compressed instructions (the "C" ISA extension) when supported, by Xavier Leroy (ocaml/ocaml#14873); native codegen for Atomic.fetch_and_add was extended to all remaining backends by Zane Hambly (ocaml/ocaml#14575)
  • OCaml Ecosystem ocaml/opam-repository added four new packages including soteria (ocaml/opam-repository#30150) and playwright OCaml bindings (ocaml/opam-repository#30146), released dune 3.24.0 across 18 packages by Shon Feder (ocaml/opam-repository#30092), added the OCaml 5.5.0 manual by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/opam-repository#30095), and shipped melange 7.0.0 by Antonio Nuno Monteiro (ocaml/opam-repository#30094)
  • OCaml Ecosystem ocaml/ocaml.org's watch.ocaml.org video scraper now catches per-source fetch failures as a non-fatal error instead of aborting the whole Planet scrape job, by Cuihtlauac Alvarado (ocaml/ocaml.org#3695)

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    Opam-repository shipped new packages plus dune 3.24.0 and OCaml 5.5.0 support, while ocaml.org hardened its watch.ocaml.org scraper.

    New Features

    ocaml/opam-repository
    - New packages: soteria by opale (ocaml/opam-repository#30150), playwright OCaml bindings by Dmytro Melnychuk (ocaml/opam-repository#30146), osx-keychain by Alex Leighton (ocaml/opam-repository#30148), and forcamla by Christopher Sumnicht, iterated from 0.1.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#30124, closed) to 0.2.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#30142)
    - Preview release of ocgtk and conf-gtk4 GTK4 bindings by Chris Armstrong (ocaml/opam-repository#30134)
    - dune 3.24.0 released across 18 packages by Shon Feder (ocaml/opam-repository#30092)
    - OCaml 5.5.0 reference manual package added by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/opam-repository#30095), with merlin 5.8-505 and ocaml-lsp-server 1.27.0 adding 5.5 support from Ulysse (ocaml/opam-repository#30117)
    - jsofocaml/wasmofocaml-compiler 6.4.0 (8 packages) by @hhugo (ocaml/opam-repository#30088) and melange 7.0.0 (from 6.0.1) by Antonio Nuno Monteiro (ocaml/opam-repository#30094)
    - core and its dependencies made installable on arm32 by Brian Ward (ocaml/opam-repository#30147)

    ocaml/ocaml.org
    - The watch.ocaml.org video scraper now catches per-source fetch failures (network outage, expired TLS cert, malformed response) as a non-fatal Scrape_report.Error instead of aborting the whole Planet scrape job, by Cuihtlauac Alvarado (ocaml/ocaml.org#3695)
    - Bumped actions/checkout from v6 to v7 across all CI workflows (ocaml/ocaml.org#3691)
    - Added the platform newsletter covering February-May 2026, by sabine (ocaml/ocaml.org#3680)
    - Automated Planet blog aggregation and platform-release scrapes pulled in new posts and release data (ocaml/ocaml.org#3677, ocaml/ocaml.org#3692, ocaml/ocaml.org#3697)

    Overview

  • ocaml/opam-repository had a high-volume week: four new packages, dune 3.24.0 across 18 packages (ocaml/opam-repository#30092), the OCaml 5.5.0 manual with matching merlin/ocaml-lsp-server support (ocaml/opam-repository#30095, ocaml/opam-repository#30117), and melange 7.0.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#30094)
  • The dune 3.24.0 release forced immediate downstream upper-bound pins (ocaml/opam-repository#30143, ocaml/opam-repository#30132), and several packages needed source tarballs recovered into opam-source-archives after upstream links broke, led by Marcello Seri
  • ocaml/ocaml.org had lighter, incident-driven activity: Cuihtlauac Alvarado fixed and closed out a scraper outage (ocaml/ocaml.org#3695, ocaml/ocaml.org#3694) and a site-downtime report prompted an uptime-monitoring question (ocaml/ocaml.org#3699)
  • Five ocaml.org content PRs remain open awaiting merge, covering AWS industrial users, a sqlite3 FTS5 cookbook example, and a GC tutorial clarification (ocaml/ocaml.org#3681, ocaml/ocaml.org#3698, ocaml/ocaml.org#3682)

    • Activity

    ocaml/opam-repository
    - Five PRs opened this week remain unmerged: Frama-C 33.0~beta-Arsenic by Allan Blanchard (ocaml/opam-repository#30136), colibri2 0.6 (4 packages) by François Bobot (ocaml/opam-repository#30097), a simplehttpd.1.0 checksum fix by Christophe Raffalli (ocaml/opam-repository#30123), ocaml-r 0.7.0 by pveber (ocaml/opam-repository#30007), and syguslib-utils 0.3.0 by Victor Nicolet (ocaml/opam-repository#30043)
    - The dune 3.24.0 release (ocaml/opam-repository#30092) prompted upper-bound pins on cppo, lablgtk3 and wasmof_ocaml-compiler (ocaml/opam-repository#30143) and camomile (ocaml/opam-repository#30132) from Shon Feder
    - Marcello Seri recovered several packages' source tarballs into opam-source-archives after upstream links broke (ocaml/opam-repository#30129, ocaml/opam-repository#30126, ocaml/opam-repository#30127, ocaml/opam-repository#30128, ocaml/opam-repository#30102, ocaml/opam-repository#30103)
    - Package release volume stayed high: ocsipersist 2.1.0 and eliom 12.1.0 by Vincent Balat (ocaml/opam-repository#30046, ocaml/opam-repository#30098), awskit 0.2.0 (10 packages) by Abdullah Elsayed (ocaml/opam-repository#30149), x509 1.1.0 by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#30130), and lwt 5.10.1 by Raphaël Proust (ocaml/opam-repository#30145)

    ocaml/ocaml.org
    - Cuihtlauac Alvarado merged the watch.ocaml.org scraper resilience fix (ocaml/ocaml.org#3695), closed the incident report (ocaml/ocaml.org#3694), and opened a follow-up hardening issue (ocaml/ocaml.org#3696)
    - Open PRs pending merge: a sqlite3 FTS5 search cookbook example by Jones Melton (ocaml/ocaml.org#3698), a GC tutorial clarification about Gc.tune's Core dependency by adith nk (ocaml/ocaml.org#3682), and an AWS industrial-users addition approved by Juneyoung Lee (ocaml/ocaml.org#3681, fixing ocaml/ocaml.org#3652)
    - Routine merges: the LexiFi job listing refresh by Nicolás Ojeda Bär (ocaml/ocaml.org#3701) and the platform newsletter addition by sabine (ocaml/ocaml.org#3680)
    - Lemonsity reported the Emacs tooling guide binds eglot-ensure to an obsolete hook variable, triggering a warning in Emacs 30.2 (ocaml/ocaml.org#3700)

    Notable Discussions

  • ocaml/opam-repository#30089: a bad checksum on the wol packages was traced to a change in how the tangled.org forge generates git-archive tarballs; Dmitrii Kosarev reported it, Marcello Seri and akshay diagnosed the cause, Hannes Mehnert cited repository policy against modifying source-archive checksums, and Anil Madhavapeddy and Ryan Gibb discussed publishing a static, annotated-tag archive instead
  • ocaml/opam-repository#30121: David Allsopp and Hannes Mehnert discussed whether OCaml "trunk" compiler-variant packages that intentionally omit checksums should be archived, concluding most are git-branch sources that don't need it
  • ocaml/ocaml.org#3699: Rafał reported ocaml.org was down and asked whether the project uses an uptime monitor, suggesting StatusCake or Pulsetic
  • ocaml/ocaml.org#3694: Cuihtlauac Alvarado traced the Planet scrape job failure to an expired watch.ocaml.org TLS certificate, noting the blog scraper already isolated per-source failures while the video scraper did not
  • ocaml/ocaml.org#3682: Cuihtlauac Alvarado and adith nk discussed preserving Anil Madhavapeddy's and Yaron Minsky's original Real World OCaml GC tutorial text while adding a preamble and appendix for Stdlib equivalents to Core

    • Emerging Trends

  • Dune version-bound fallout: the 3.24.0 release (ocaml/opam-repository#30092) required immediate upper-bound pins on cppo, lablgtk3, wasmofocaml-compiler (ocaml/opam-repository#30143) and camomile (ocaml/opam-repository#30132) to keep existing packages installable

    • OxCaml

    oxcaml/oxcaml retired the OCaml-4 runtime, added an -experimental-optimizations flag, and opened AVX512 backend and runtime concurrency work.

    New Features

  • New -experimental-optimizations compiler flag bundling off-by-default codegen improvements (CFG prologue shrink-wrap, x86 peephole, irc allocator, CFG block merging), added by @ttebbi-janestreet in oxcaml/oxcaml#6174.
  • Nick Barnes removed the OCaml-4 runtime and the dual-runtime switch from oxcaml/oxcaml, retiring the associated technical debt (oxcaml/oxcaml#6218).
  • Tim McGilchrist landed ocamlfilt, a demangler for compiler symbol names that auto-detects pre-5.3, post-5.3, and new structured mangling schemes (oxcaml/oxcaml#5100).
  • Jérémie Dimino added an explicit Punspecializedarray array kind, replacing an overloaded use of Pgenarray that misbehaved with the flat float array optimization disabled (oxcaml/oxcaml#6101).
  • @zhizhuoxin introduced a new Allocation mode axis to improve static support for the zero_alloc checker (oxcaml/oxcaml#6269).
  • @dkalinichenko-js enabled implicit kind declarations inside structures, previously restricted to signatures (oxcaml/oxcaml#6114).
  • @julesjacobs allowed zero-parameter, unused-parameter, and multi-parameter custom [@@or_null] payload shapes (oxcaml/oxcaml#5830).
  • Ryan Tjoa fixed inline-record representation for any-kind fields that had caused incorrect variant match-arm selection (oxcaml/oxcaml#6240).
  • Mark Shinwell fixed a bad movz instruction emitted for arm64 stack reallocation (oxcaml/oxcaml#6311) and added bounds checks to arm64 AST constructors (oxcaml/oxcaml#6313).

    • Overview

  • oxcaml/oxcaml was the only repository in the group with recorded activity in week 26; oxcaml/opam-repository, oxcaml/merlin, oxcaml/jsofocaml, and janestreet/opam-repository had no tracked commits or pull requests this week.
  • Two cleanups of note landed in oxcaml/oxcaml: removal of the legacy OCaml-4 runtime (oxcaml/oxcaml#6218) and a new -experimental-optimizations flag bundling several off-by-default codegen improvements (oxcaml/oxcaml#6174).
  • New backend work opened this week includes a multi-PR AVX512 vector/mask support effort from Max Slater (oxcaml/oxcaml#6293, oxcaml/oxcaml#6294, oxcaml/oxcaml#6339, oxcaml/oxcaml#6340) and a new compiler-performance CI from @julesjacobs (oxcaml/oxcaml#6365).

  • Nathanaëlle Courant reported that [@zero_alloc assume never_returns_normally] is accepted by the checker on code that actually allocates when an inlined function raises an exception, and that plain [@zero_alloc assume] has the same unsoundness (oxcaml/oxcaml#6297); a related report showed the checker can also accept an allocating raise_notrace under -Oclassic (oxcaml/oxcaml#6261).
  • Basile Clément opened a design discussion proposing to rework [@inline] attribute semantics, arguing the current meaning conflates cross-compilation-unit availability with automatic-inlining heuristics (oxcaml/oxcaml#6312).

  • David Allsopp reviewed the runtime-4 retirement commit-by-commit, questioning whether some mechanisms (e.g. ocamlc -config parsing behavior) should be preserved for diff-reduction with upstream OCaml (oxcaml/oxcaml#6218).

    • OCaml Core

    Twelve PRs merged in ocaml/ocaml covering codegen, GC, and cross-compilation fixes; ocaml/RFCs had no recorded activity this week.

    New Features

  • Better compilation of recursive function definitions that avoids allocating pseudo-closure blocks for local aliases introduced before the function, addressing a code-generation regression reported in ocaml/ocaml#14876; implemented by Vincent Laviron (ocaml/ocaml#14885) and extended by Gabriel Scherer to cover redefinitions of identifiers from other modules (ocaml/ocaml#14894)
  • RISC-V code generation now takes advantage of compressed instructions (the "C" ISA extension) when supported by the host processor, by Xavier Leroy (ocaml/ocaml#14873, ocaml/ocaml#14799)
  • Native code generation for Atomic.fetch_and_add (Iatomic_fetch_add) now emits direct assembly instead of going through a C call, extended to all remaining backends (amd64, arm64, riscv, power) by Zane Hambly (ocaml/ocaml#14575)
  • Fixed an assertion failure in out_type when external types carry a manifest subject to module constraints, by Stefan Muenzel (ocaml/ocaml#14882, closes ocaml/ocaml#14881)
  • Fixed mislabeled Pmty_extension in the -dparsetree dump, which had incorrectly printed module type extensions with the Pmod_extension label, by @hhugo (ocaml/ocaml#14880)
  • Fixed a runtime memory leak: pthread attribute objects are now correctly destroyed after use, by @Jeannalyse (ocaml/ocaml#14875)
  • Major GC now adopts orphaned ephemerons early and often (except when terminating), part of an ongoing ephemeron-simplification effort by Gabriel Scherer (ocaml/ocaml#14877, ocaml/ocaml#14813)
  • Fixed a cross-compilation build failure on older mingw32-gcc toolchains caused by a missing errno.h include, by Brian Ward (ocaml/ocaml#14884, closes ocaml/ocaml#14883)
  • More concise printing of non-exhaustiveness warning counter-examples, e.g. A (_,_) now prints as A _, by Luc Maranget (ocaml/ocaml#14887)
  • Expect tests now also run with -rectypes in addition to -principal, exercising recursive types in more of the test suite, by Stefan Muenzel (ocaml/ocaml#14643)

    • Multicore

    Eio gained a portable Sockopt API for socket options while ocaml-uring merged vectored fixed-buffer read/write bindings.

    New Features

  • Added an extensible Eio.Net.Sockopt type with Eio.Net.setsockopt/getsockopt, a register_printer mechanism, and an Invalid_option error case, laying groundwork for typed socket options across all Eio backends, by Thomas Leonard based on Anil Madhavapeddy's original design (ocaml-multicore/eio#858, ocaml-multicore/eio#575)
  • Added portable socket-option constructors (SO_REUSEADDR, SO_KEEPALIVE, TCP_NODELAY, SO_LINGER, SO_RCVTIMEO, and others) usable even outside Unix processes, by Thomas Leonard, closing ocaml-multicore/eio#322 and ocaml-multicore/eio#376 (ocaml-multicore/eio#859)
  • Added Linux-specific TCP_*/IP_* socket options (TCP_CORK, TCP_KEEPIDLE, TCP_FASTOPEN, IP_FREEBIND, IP_MTU, and others) implemented via getsockopt/setsockopt C stubs in lib_eio_linux, by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#575)
  • Relaxed the return type of Eio.Process.pipe from a fixed closable-source/sink pair to a polymorphic-variant subtype, allowing use with libraries such as Cohttp_eio.Body.t, by Isaac Arogbonlo with casts by Thomas Leonard, closing ocaml-multicore/eio#750 (ocaml-multicore/eio#775)
  • Added readv_fixed and writev_fixed to the Uring API for multi-buffer reads/writes against a ring's registered fixed buffer, with Invalid_argument validation against buffers not belonging to the ring, by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#155)
  • Fixed misnamed C stubs (submit_readv_fixed/submit_writev_fixed, which never performed vectored I/O, renamed to submit_read_fixed/submit_write_fixed), freeing the vectored names for the new operations (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring@5669961)
