  • Of the nine repositories in the multicore group, only ocaml-multicore/eio and ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring had recorded activity during 2026-06-22 to 2026-06-28
  • ocaml-multicore/domainslib, ocaml-multicore/meio, ocaml-multicore/saturn, ocaml-multicore/eio-trace, ocaml-multicore/picos, ocaml-multicore/kcas, and ocaml-multicore/ocaml-iomux had no tracked commits, PRs, or issues this week
  • Eio's work centered on a new portable/Linux socket-options API (ocaml-multicore/eio#858, ocaml-multicore/eio#859, ocaml-multicore/eio#575) and relaxed typing for Eio.Process.pipe (ocaml-multicore/eio#775)
  • ocaml-uring merged vectored fixed-buffer read/write bindings (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#155), while a related per-operation RWF-flags PR (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#154) and a liburing-vendoring issue (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#156) remain open

    • Activity

  • Anil Madhavapeddy opened add SO_TYPE query to the portable Eio socket interface, exploring whether querying a socket's type belongs in the portable Sockopt API (ocaml-multicore/eio#860)
  • Thomas Leonard closed the long-stale eio_linux: add support for integration with Async draft, citing lack of continued interest (ocaml-multicore/eio#221)
  • The pseudoterminal (Eio_unix.Pty) and login_tty fork-action work by Anil Madhavapeddy continued, with a FreeBSD-specific test failure (pty buffers discarded on close, unlike Linux) diagnosed with shell access from Mark Elvers, plus design discussion with Thomas Leonard on re-exporting Unix.tcgetattr (ocaml-multicore/eio#531)
  • The per-operation RWF flags PR by Anil Madhavapeddy, exposing preadv2/pwritev2-style flags such as dsync and nocache at the uring layer, remains open; Thomas Leonard asked for a rebase after the fixed-buffer bindings merged, and Patrick Ferris reviewed the changes favorably (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#154)
  • Discussion continues on whether ocaml-uring should support building against system liburing instead of only the vendored copy, following a Debian build failure caused by a missing io_uring_prep_readv_fixed declaration (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#156)

    • Notable Discussions

  • Stéphane Glondu and Thomas Leonard discussed whether ocaml-uring should support building against system liburing rather than only a vendored copy, after Debian's patched build failed with an implicit-declaration error for io_uring_prep_readv_fixed; opam-installed uring often needs a newer liburing than stable distributions ship (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#156)
  • Thomas Leonard and Anil Madhavapeddy debated whether Eio's portable Sockopt API should expose SO_TYPE as a raw integer, agreeing to omit it until it can be mapped to a proper variant type rather than an unhelpful platform-dependent integer (ocaml-multicore/eio#859)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Both ocaml-multicore/eio and ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring continued building typed, portable OCaml wrappers around raw Unix/kernel interfaces — Eio's socket-options and pty/login_tty work (ocaml-multicore/eio#858, ocaml-multicore/eio#859, ocaml-multicore/eio#531) and ocaml-uring's fixed-buffer vectored I/O (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#155) — rather than requiring users to drop to raw syscalls
  • Large single-author PRs are being split during review to ease landing, as when Thomas Leonard divided Anil Madhavapeddy's Sockopt PR (ocaml-multicore/eio#575) into a base API PR (ocaml-multicore/eio#858) and a portable-options PR (ocaml-multicore/eio#859)
  • Packaging/distribution tension around vendored vs. system dependencies surfaced in ocaml-uring's liburing-vendoring discussion (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#156), as newer kernel-feature bindings require liburing versions ahead of what stable distributions package
  • Seven of the nine group repositories (ocaml-multicore/domainslib, ocaml-multicore/meio, ocaml-multicore/saturn, ocaml-multicore/eio-trace, ocaml-multicore/picos, ocaml-multicore/kcas, ocaml-multicore/ocaml-iomux) had no recorded activity this week, concentrating all visible work in eio and ocaml-uring
entry.summary: OCaml 5.5 support shipped in merlin and ocaml-lsp releases while oxcaml retired its OCaml-4 runtime and eio gained a portable Sockopt API.

entry.title: Week 25, 2026: OCaml 5.5.0 and 4.14.4 shipped alongside dune 3.24.0 and js_of_ocaml 6.4.0, with opam-repository and ocaml.org publishing matching packages and docs.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Core Released OCaml 5.5.0, a feature release adding module-dependent functions, polymorphic functions as function arguments, a relocatable compiler, generalized local definitions, substring search/replace functions, external types, garbage collector improvements, and around 60 new standard library functions, by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml release 5.5.0)
  • OCaml Core Released OCaml 4.14.4, a security bugfix release addressing CVE-2026-34353 (caml_ba_reshape size-overflow) and CVE-2026-41083 (Filename.quote_command Windows argument quoting), by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml release 4.14.4)
  • OCaml Tools Released dune 3.24.0, promoting directory targets from experimental to generally available, enabling the relocatable compiler by default for package management, and adding the %{pkg::
    :} pform for resolving package install files, by Shon Feder (ocaml/dune release 3.24.0)
  • OCaml Tools Released jsofocaml 6.4.0, adding initial OCaml 5.5.0 and OxCaml compiler support, WASI 0.1 support, a new variable-coalescing compiler pass, a pure-Wasm zstd/BLAKE2b runtime, and new Promise and Fetch library bindings, by @hhugo (ocsigen/jsofocaml release 6.4.0)
  • OCaml Ecosystem Official OCaml 5.5.0 compiler packages (ocaml-compiler, ocaml-base-compiler, ocaml-variants, ocaml-system, ocaml-src) added to ocaml/opam-repository, by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/opam-repository#30075), with a follow-up fix restoring the relocatable compiler build template (ocaml/opam-repository#30085)
  • OCaml Ecosystem Matching OCaml 5.5.0 release page published on ocaml/ocaml.org, by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml.org#3688)
  • OCaml Ecosystem Official OCaml 4.14.4 packages added to opam-repository, by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/opam-repository#30054), with a matching ocaml.org release page documenting both CVEs (ocaml/ocaml.org#3684)
  • OCaml Ecosystem conf-pkg-config fixed for OpenBSD to use the base-system pkg-config, by Marcello Seri (ocaml/opam-repository#30082, closing ocaml/opam-repository#30080)
  • OCaml Ecosystem Windows CI reworked in opam-repository to reduce depext-driven switch recompilations, by David Allsopp (ocaml/opam-repository#30040, ocaml/opam-repository#30058)
  • OCaml Ecosystem New package ktdeque, a purely-functional double-ended queue extracted from a machine-checked Rocq proof, added by Yann Régis Gianas (ocaml/opam-repository#30060)

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    OCaml 5.5.0 and 4.14.4 compiler releases and their ocaml.org release-page documentation landed the same week.

    New Features

  • Official OCaml 5.5.0 compiler packages (ocaml-compiler, ocaml-base-compiler, ocaml-variants, ocaml-system, ocaml-src) added to ocaml/opam-repository, by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/opam-repository#30075), with a follow-up fix restoring the relocatable compiler build template (ocaml/opam-repository#30085)
  • Matching OCaml 5.5.0 release page published on ocaml/ocaml.org, covering module-dependent functions, polymorphic function parameters, GC improvements and around 60 new standard library functions, by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml.org#3688)
  • Official OCaml 4.14.4 security bugfix release packages added to opam-repository, containing two standard-library security fixes and an ARM64 compilation fix, by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/opam-repository#30054)
  • Matching OCaml 4.14.4 release page published on ocaml.org, documenting CVE-2026-34353 (caml_ba_reshape size-overflow) and CVE-2026-41083 (Filename.quote_command Windows argument quoting), by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml.org#3684)
  • conf-pkg-config fixed for OpenBSD to use the base-system pkg-config, by Marcello Seri (ocaml/opam-repository#30082, closing ocaml/opam-repository#30080)
  • Windows CI reworked in opam-repository to reduce depext-driven switch recompilations, replacing a temporary conf-pkg-config workaround with a new conf-allegro5.2 package, by David Allsopp (ocaml/opam-repository#30040, ocaml/opam-repository#30058)
  • New package ktdeque, a purely-functional double-ended queue extracted from a machine-checked Rocq proof, added by Yann Régis Gianas (ocaml/opam-repository#30060)

    • Overview

  • The week's central event was the OCaml 5.5.0 feature release and OCaml 4.14.4 security bugfix release, packaged in ocaml/opam-repository (ocaml/opam-repository#30075, ocaml/opam-repository#30054) and documented with new release pages on ocaml/ocaml.org (ocaml/ocaml.org#3688, ocaml/ocaml.org#3684)
  • ocaml/opam-repository merged dozens of package releases, including upstream batch releases from ocurrent, savonet and landmarks, alongside continued Windows CI hardening (ocaml/opam-repository#30069, ocaml/opam-repository#30065, ocaml/opam-repository#30040)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org activity centered on reviewing and merging the two compiler release pages, plus routine automated Planet blog aggregation and a documentation-gap report for patricia-tree (ocaml/ocaml.org#3685)

    • Activity

  • Newly opened opam-repository PRs awaiting merge include dune 3.24.0 by Shon Feder (ocaml/opam-repository#30092), par/par_cli (a Programmable Agent Runtime for OCaml) by JC (ocaml/opam-repository#30086), and an ocaml-r 0.7.0 update for R 4.5/4.6 by pveber (ocaml/opam-repository#30007)
  • Bulk upstream batch releases merged: 10 packages from ocurrent by Mark Elvers (ocaml/opam-repository#30069), 8 from savonet/ocaml-ffmpeg and 4 from savonet/liquidsoap-release-assets by Romain Beauxis (ocaml/opam-repository#30065, ocaml/opam-repository#30057), and 3 from LexiFi/landmarks by Marc Lasson (ocaml/opam-repository#30071)
  • Individual package releases merged include jsofocaml 6.4.0 by @hhugo (ocaml/opam-repository#30088), tiny_httpd 0.21 by Simon Cruanes (ocaml/opam-repository#30074), goblint 2.8.0 by Simmo Saan (ocaml/opam-repository#30052), and docfd 13.0.0 by Darren Li (ocaml/opam-repository#30047)
  • Closed without merge in opam-repository: the stdcompat multi-version update abandoned pending an upstream 5.5 compat branch, by Dmitrii Kosarev (ocaml/opam-repository#30090); and the name-reservation submissions ioqwerty (ocaml/opam-repository#30049) and aslplifterocaml (ocaml/opam-repository#30051)
  • Review of the ocaml.org 5.5.0 release page involved extensive wording and code-example corrections from Anil Madhavapeddy before Cuihtlauac Alvarado merged it (ocaml/ocaml.org#3688); the 4.14.4 release page was reviewed by sabine before merging (ocaml/ocaml.org#3684)
  • Routine Planet feed scraping on ocaml.org continued to surface new community blog posts, including pieces from Ocsigen and robur.coop, while repeatedly flagging the same unreachable mirage, ocaml-book, dinosaure, emilpriver and patricoferris feeds (ocaml/ocaml.org#3686, ocaml/ocaml.org#3687, ocaml/ocaml.org#3689, ocaml/ocaml.org#3690)
  • Dorian Lesbre opened an ocaml.org issue noting the two most recent patricia-tree package releases have no documentation, possibly related to earlier documentation-generation issues (ocaml/ocaml.org#3685, ocaml/ocaml.org#3437, ocaml/ocaml.org#3451)

    • Notable Discussions

  • The dune 3.24.0 release thread in opam-repository surfaced test-suite regressions in cppo, camomile and lablgtk3 tied to a breaking change in %{bin:...} variable handling, with Shon Feder confirming the change should only affect invalid usage (ocaml/opam-repository#30092)
  • opam-repository maintainers reaffirmed the utility-for-users policy for package submissions, questioning the standalone agentxm-example-tinyflags package by Craig Smitham (ocaml/opam-repository#29905) and rejecting the ioqwerty name-reservation package by Anton Matiash (ocaml/opam-repository#30049)
  • On the ocaml.org 5.5.0 release PR, Florian Angeletti asked about the process for updating the online manual and observed that ocaml.org appeared to block merging while a change request was outstanding, which Anil Madhavapeddy said was not intended behavior (ocaml/ocaml.org#3688)
  • Sebastien Marie and Marcello Seri clarified that pkg-config has shipped in the OpenBSD base system since release 7.8, resolving the conf-pkg-config special-casing question in opam-repository (ocaml/opam-repository#30080, fixed by ocaml/opam-repository#30082)
  • Dorian Lesbre raised missing documentation for the latest patricia-tree releases on ocaml.org, linking it to two previously reported documentation-generation issues (ocaml/ocaml.org#3685, ocaml/ocaml.org#3437, ocaml/ocaml.org#3451)

    • Emerging Trends

  • OCaml 5.5 ecosystem migration: the official 5.5.0 compiler release and its ocaml.org documentation (ocaml/opam-repository#30075, ocaml/ocaml.org#3688), a relocatable-build fix (ocaml/opam-repository#30085), and compatibility updates in baby and omod all landed the same week (ocaml/opam-repository#30084, ocaml/opam-repository#30063)
  • Continued Windows CI hardening in opam-repository reducing depext-driven switch recompilation and modernizing the workflow (ocaml/opam-repository#30040, ocaml/opam-repository#30058, ocaml/opam-repository#30076)
  • AI/agent-tooling packages entering opam-repository — a Programmable Agent Runtime SDK (ocaml/opam-repository#30086) and an AgentXM example package (ocaml/opam-repository#29905) — prompting maintainers to reaffirm the submission bar
  • Automated batch releases from upstream CI bots continue to make up a large share of opam-repository merges (ocurrent ocaml/opam-repository#30069, ocaml-ffmpeg ocaml/opam-repository#30065, liquidsoap ocaml/opam-repository#30057)
  • On ocaml.org, automated [scrape] Planet PRs continued at a near-daily cadence, repeatedly reporting the same unresolved unreachable feeds (ocaml/ocaml.org#3686, ocaml/ocaml.org#3687, ocaml/ocaml.org#3689, ocaml/ocaml.org#3690)

    • OCaml Tools

    OxCaml

    OCaml Core

    Multicore
entry.summary: OCaml 5.5.0 and 4.14.4 shipped alongside dune 3.24.0 and js_of_ocaml 6.4.0, with opam-repository and ocaml.org publishing matching packages and docs.

entry.title: Week 24, 2026: OCaml 5.4 merged into OxCaml; two CVEs fixed in core; OCaml 5.5.0~rc1 landed in opam-repository; eio gains incremental directory reading.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Core Fixed shell injection vulnerability in Filename.quote_command on Windows (CVE-2026-41083, OSEC-2026-05) — filenames with special characters like & in redirection arguments were not properly quoted; implemented by David Allsopp, reviewed by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml#14853)
  • OCaml Core Fixed inverted mark_header lazy tag check — a regression from ocaml/ocaml#14816 causing corruption and segfaults in multi-domain programs using laziness (ocaml/ocaml#14856)
  • OCaml Core Fixed infinite loop in runtime_events.c write_to_ring when an event exceeds ring buffer size; runtime now emits a fatal error with the minimum required e= value (Michael Bacarella, reviewed by Gabriel Scherer, ocaml/ocaml#13335)
  • OCaml Core Fixed Flambda infinite recursive stub inlining miscompilation discovered by Nathanaëlle Courant and Vincent Laviron, fixed by Pierre Chambart (ocaml/ocaml#14828, ocaml/ocaml#14839)
  • OCaml Core Fixed modular explicit type expansion to correctly update expansion nodes containing tfunctor arguments, resolving an uncaught exception from ocaml/ocaml#14842 (Florian Angeletti, ocaml/ocaml#14845)
  • OCaml Core Added AR and ARFLAGS export in Makefile.config, deprecating ARCMD to improve build system integration (Antonin Décimo, ocaml/ocaml#14552)
  • OxCaml OCaml 5.4 upstream merge (oxcaml/oxcaml#5325) landed on June 12 in oxcaml/oxcaml, bringing in the full 5.4 branch including stdlib updates, runtime changes, and toolchain improvements with a magic number bump
  • OxCaml Fixed correct handling of concurrent lazy header marking in the major GC, backported from ocaml/ocaml#14856: resolves potential SEGVs or heap corruption when two domains race on a lazy block (oxcaml/oxcaml#6228)
  • OxCaml Dune 3.22.2+ox package family (16 sub-packages including chrome-trace, dune-build-info, dune-rpc, stdune, xdg) added to oxcaml/opam-repository with oxcaml-dune.patch compatibility (oxcaml/opam-repository#49)
  • Multicore Path.with_dir_entries in ocaml-multicore/eio provides incremental directory entry reading as a lazy Seq.t of (File.Stat.kind * string) pairs, with 10–13× speedups on Linux for recursive walks (ocaml-multicore/eio#821)
  • Multicore Path.read_dir_entries returns a sorted (File.Stat.kind * string) list with file type information, eliminating separate kind calls per entry (ocaml-multicore/eio#821)
  • Multicore Path.open_subtree and Path.with_subtree replace open_dir/with_open_dir with names communicating capability-confinement semantics, merged by Thomas Leonard (ocaml-multicore/eio#853)
  • Multicore Socket CLOEXEC default in ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring: socket now uses Sock_flags.cloexec as default, preventing fd leaks into child processes (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#151)
  • OCaml Tools WASI 0.1 runtime added to wasm_of_ocaml via --enable wasi flag (ocsigen/jsofocaml#1831) by Jérôme Vouillon; supports Wizard engine and wasmtime
  • OCaml Tools OxCaml modalities rendered across all odoc output backends (HTML, LaTeX, man pages, markdown) via ocaml/odoc#1420 by @art-w
  • OCaml Tools Configurator query_variable adds Pkg_config.query_variable to query arbitrary pkg-config variables per package in ocaml/dune (ocaml/dune#15078) by Rudi Grinberg
  • OCaml Tools Let-punning locate fix in ocaml/merlin: locate on punned bindings like let x in or let+ x in now jumps to the source binding correctly (ocaml/merlin#2066) by Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac
  • OCaml Tools 13 jsofocaml runtime correctness fixes merged including Ephemeron.blit_key data corruption (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2264), Int64.shift_right sign extension (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2278), BLOCK32 unsigned shift (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2275), Sys.rename-to-self deletion (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2268), and Str SIMPLEOPT infinite loop (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2277)
  • OCaml Ecosystem OCaml 5.5.0~rc1 packaged in ocaml/opam-repository with ocaml-compiler, ocaml-base-compiler, and variants (ocaml/opam-repository#30023)
  • OCaml Ecosystem 25+ new or updated packages in opam-repository including awskit 0.1.0 (AWS infrastructure with Eio/Lwt adapters, ocaml/opam-repository#29980), migra 1.0.0 (database migrations, ocaml/opam-repository#30002), cabal 0.1.0 (agent execution primitives, ocaml/opam-repository#30008), ocaml-ai-sdk 0.4 (ocaml/opam-repository#30005), transom 0.2.0 (WebView desktop apps, ocaml/opam-repository#30037), and miou 0.7.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#30009)
  • OCaml Ecosystem Published Backstage article on wasm_of_ocaml WASI prototype covering WASI preview1 backend, CPS effects compilation, and a call for production users or sponsors (ocaml/ocaml.org#3667)
  • OCaml Ecosystem Added CLAUDE.md developer guide to ocaml/ocaml.org with AI-assisted development context covering build commands, architecture, EML templating, data flow, and CI/deployment (ocaml/ocaml.org#3585)

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    OCaml 5.5.0~rc1 landed in opam-repository with 25+ new packages; ocaml.org added AI dev docs and a wasm_of_ocaml WASI backstage post.

    New Features

    ocaml/opam-repository
    - OCaml 5.5.0~rc1 packaged ocaml-compiler, ocaml-base-compiler, and ocaml-variants...+options with runtime fixes and a Windows filename quoting security fix (ocaml/opam-repository#30023)
    - awskit (10 packages, 0.1.0) — AWS infrastructure library with signing, credentials, S3 client, and Eio/Lwt adapters (ocaml/opam-repository#29980)
    - migra (1.0.0, 1.0.1, 2.0.0) — database migration tool for PostgreSQL, MariaDB/MySQL, and SQLite with checksum validation (ocaml/opam-repository#30002, #30012, #30033)
    - mnet (0.0.3, 6 packages) — TCP implementation for Miou and Solo5 unikernels, now including mnet-ssh for SSH in unikernels (ocaml/opam-repository#30011)
    - cabal (0.1.0) — backend-agnostic agent execution primitives for OCaml applications driving agentic CLI backends (ocaml/opam-repository#30008)
    - ocaml-ai-sdk (0.4, 2 packages) — provider abstraction for AI models with Anthropic and OpenRouter prompt caching support (ocaml/opam-repository#30005)
    - transom (0.2.0) — OCaml backend for desktop WebView apps with typed IPC and generated glue code (ocaml/opam-repository#30037)
    - contract (0.2.0) — typed HTTP API contract library with OpenAPI 3.0.3 output (ocaml/opam-repository#30014)
    - doctor (0.4.0) — diagnostic CLI checking opam, dune, LSP, and editor integration for OCaml development environments (ocaml/opam-repository#30015)
    - liquid-ml (0.1.4, 5 packages) — Shopify Liquid templating language implementation in OCaml (ocaml/opam-repository#30004)
    - melange-edn (0.1.0 and 0.3.0) — EDN reader and writer for Melange targeting JavaScript (ocaml/opam-repository#29999, #30028)
    - kind2 (3.0.0) — SMT-based automatic model checker for Lustre programs (ocaml/opam-repository#30019)
    - notty-miou (0.0.2, 4 packages) — terminal library using Miou with new mkernel/mnet support (ocaml/opam-repository#30027)
    - miou (0.7.0) — composable concurrency primitives adding Miou.get and Miou.Promise.state (ocaml/opam-repository#30009)
    - caqti and caqti-lwt (2.3.2) — database access library fixing timed cleanup of idle connection pool entries (ocaml/opam-repository#30026)
    - Frama-C (32.1-Germanium) — static analysis platform for C (ocaml/opam-repository#30016)
    - goblint-cil (2.1.0) — C frontend for program analysis with cast kinds, _Static_assert checking, and attribute handling improvements (ocaml/opam-repository#30022)
    - hxd (0.5.0) — hexdump library with new introspection API for cfg values (ocaml/opam-repository#30010)
    - ca-certs-nss (3.125) — X.509 trust anchors updated to NSS 3.125 (2026-06-11) (ocaml/opam-repository#30038)
    - checkedoint (2.0.1) — library for checked integer arithmetic (ocaml/opam-repository#30031)
    - timedesc and related (3.1.2, 6 packages) — OCaml datetime handling library suite (ocaml/opam-repository#29995)
    - mcrunch (0.0.3) — file crunching tool now handling empty files (ocaml/opam-repository#30025)
    - dockerfile (8.4.1, 3 packages) — Dockerfile eDSL with a libzstd packaging fix (ocaml/opam-repository#30018)
    - mingw-w64-shims (1.0.1) — Windows shims package with clarified conf- usage (ocaml/opam-repository#30040)
    - embeddedocaml_templates (0.8.1) — template library making ppx_inline_test a test-only dependency (ocaml/opam-repository#29929)

    ocaml/ocaml.org
    - Fixed contrast on OCaml Workshop 2026 date pills — switched from text-title to text-white on orange background badges across both /ocaml-workshop-2026 and /ocaml-workshop-2026/cfp pages (ocaml/ocaml.org#3673)
    - Added CLAUDE.md developer guide with AI-assisted development context covering build commands, architecture, EML templating, data flow, dependency pinning, and CI/deployment (ocaml/ocaml.org#3585)
    - Expanded HACKING.md with a "Before Submitting a PR" section, updated tool/ directory tree, and corrected dependency pinning file list (ocaml/ocaml.org#3585)
    - Published Backstage article on wasm_of_ocaml WASI prototype covering WASI preview1 backend, CPS effects compilation, and a call for production users or sponsors (ocaml/ocaml.org#3667)
    - Added seven new OCaml Planet blog posts via automated scraping across three merged PRs (ocaml/ocaml.org#3674, #3676, #3678)

    Overview

  • ocaml/opam-repository had its highest-volume week in months: OCaml 5.5.0~rc1 landed via ocaml/opam-repository#30023, accompanied by 25+ new or updated packages spanning AWS SDKs, database tooling, unikernel networking, AI/agent libraries, static analysis, and developer tooling
  • ocaml/ocaml.org saw lighter activity focused on content and developer documentation: UI contrast fixes, a new CLAUDE.md guide, a backstage post on wasm_of_ocaml WASI, and seven new Planet blog posts
  • Infrastructure work in opam-repository hardened Windows CI (ocaml/opam-repository#29998), updated conf-* packages for 0install solver compatibility on Windows (ocaml/opam-repository#30029), and addressed dune 3.24 install layout changes affecting multiple packages
  • The MirageOS unikernel ecosystem had a coordinated release week: miou, mnet, mcrunch, and notty-miou all landed together
  • Four ocaml.org PRs remain open pending review: platform newsletter, llms.txt endpoint, GC tutorial clarification, and AWS industrial users addition

    • Activity

    ocaml/opam-repository infrastructure and compatibility
    - Windows CI hardened: ocaml/opam-repository#29998 updated CI to install edited packages by upgrading from the master version first, catching state regressions and lockfile issues; includes a lint error 46 suppression for conf-flagged packages with install sections
    - conf-* packages updated for 0install solver compatibility on Windows, tweaking many conf-* packages and adding conf-pkg-config.5 via ocaml/opam-repository#30029
    - dune 3.24 compatibility: tests for crunch.4.0.0 ocaml/opam-repository#30035, lintcstubs.0.4.7 ocaml/opam-repository#30032, and merlin ocaml/opam-repository#30044 conditionally gated on dune < 3.24 due to install layout changes
    - OxCaml compatibility: ocaml/opam-repository#30041 adds missing constraints to async_websocket.v0.13.0 to prevent selection in OxCaml switches
    - Dependency fixes: mazeppa.0.7.2's checked_oint dependency corrected via ocaml/opam-repository#30034; diffast-core 0.2/0.4 incompatibility patched via ocaml/opam-repository#30039

    • OxCaml

    OCaml 5.4 upstream merge landed in oxcaml/oxcaml; Dune 3.22.2+ox packages added to oxcaml/opam-repository.

    New Features

  • The OCaml 5.4 upstream merge (oxcaml/oxcaml#5325) landed on June 12, bringing in the full 5.4 branch including stdlib updates, runtime changes, and toolchain improvements, accompanied by a magic number bump.
  • Correct handling of concurrent lazy header marking in the major GC, backported from ocaml/ocaml#14856: fixes potential SEGVs or heap corruption when two domains race on a lazy block (oxcaml/oxcaml#6228).
  • Graceful degradation for OCAMLRUNPARAM=d= values exceeding valid range, avoiding a fatal error in the runtime (oxcaml/oxcaml#6215).
  • Post-5.4-merge typing fixes by Chris Casinghino: corrected @untagged error messages on externals with int8/int16, updated format strings in typetexp.ml, and unified duplicate solve_Pexp_field/type_label_projection functions (oxcaml/oxcaml#6247).
  • CFG merge-blocks register equality strengthened: structural equality now used instead of physical equality in the merge-blocks pass (oxcaml/oxcaml#6223).
  • Merlin updated to 5.2.0minus-40 with a merlin-specific diff added to out_type.ml (oxcaml/oxcaml#6211, oxcaml/oxcaml#6216, oxcaml/oxcaml#6225).
  • Dune 3.22.2+ox package family (16 sub-packages including chrome-trace, dune-build-info, dune-rpc, stdune, xdg, etc.) added to oxcaml/opam-repository with oxcaml-dune.patch compatibility (oxcaml/opam-repository#49).
  • Version constraint fixes in oxcaml/opam-repository for stdune, extlib, eio_linux, cmarkit, omd, yojson, and cmdliner to correctly scope 5.2.0minus31 vs 5.2.0minus31+ builds (oxcaml/opam-repository#52).

  • oxcaml/oxcaml had the highest activity: the OCaml 5.4 upstream merge (oxcaml/oxcaml#5325) completed on June 12 after months of work, triggering 40+ new PRs for post-merge cleanup, unboxed types, mode error improvements, runtime API, and name mangling test infrastructure.
  • oxcaml/opam-repository completed the Dune 3.22.2+ox package additions (oxcaml/opam-repository#49) and merged accumulated constraint fixes (oxcaml/opam-repository#52), while oxcaml/opam-repository#51 remains open pending an upstream Dune fix.

    • OCaml Core

    Two CVE security fixes landed in ocaml/ocaml alongside a GC mark_header regression fix and Flambda miscompilation correction.

    New Features

  • Fixed shell injection vulnerability in Filename.quote_command on Windows (CVE-2026-41083, OSEC-2026-05): filenames with special characters like & in redirection arguments were not properly quoted, potentially allowing unintended command execution. David Allsopp implemented the fix, reviewed by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/ocaml#14853)
  • Fixed inverted check in mark_header for lazy tags — a regression from ocaml/ocaml#14816 that could cause corruption and segfaults in multi-domain programs using laziness, verified by Sadiq Jaffer and KC Sivaramakrishnan (ocaml/ocaml#14856) by Anil Madhavapeddy
  • Fixed infinite loop in runtime_events.c's write_to_ring when an event exceeds the configured ring buffer size; the runtime now emits a fatal error suggesting the minimum required e= value (Michael Bacarella, review by Gabriel Scherer, ocaml/ocaml#13335)
  • Fixed infinite recursive inlining of stub functions with Flambda, a miscompilation discovered by Nathanaëlle Courant and Vincent Laviron, fixed by Pierre Chambart (ocaml/ocaml#14828, ocaml/ocaml#14839)
  • Fixed modular explicit type expansion to correctly update expansion nodes containing tfunctor arguments in instance_tfunctor, resolving an uncaught exception from ocaml/ocaml#14842 (Florian Angeletti, ocaml/ocaml#14845)
  • Updated Changes file to assign CVE numbers to the intern.c robustness fix (CVE-2026-28364, OSEC-2026-01 by Xavier Leroy and Nicolás Ojeda Bär) and fill in reviewer credits for the relocatable compiler feature (ocaml/ocaml#13728, ocaml/ocaml#14014, ocaml/ocaml#14243)
  • Added AR and ARFLAGS export in Makefile.config, deprecating ARCMD to improve build system integration (Antonin Décimo, review by David Allsopp, ocaml/ocaml#14552)
  • Corrected stdlib documentation: Option.is_some self-referential typo (ocaml/ocaml#14855) and List.find_opt clarification (ocaml/ocaml#14851) by adith nk
  • Corrected Patterns.deconstruct documentation to reflect the function is total and does not raise exceptions (Florian Angeletti, ocaml/ocaml#14859)

    • Activity

  • Antonin Décimo opened cross-compilation fixes for Windows addressing dummy file extensions in installcross, CC variable quoting for Flexlink, and preventing clang-cl from synthesizing wcslen calls via -fno-builtin-wcslen (ocaml/ocaml#14850)
  • @Jeannalyse opened a PR implementing configurable domain stack size via a new S= parameter in OCAMLRUNPARAM, addressing a feature request for C FFI-heavy workloads (ocaml/ocaml#14860, related to ocaml/ocaml#14195)
  • @Jeannalyse also opened a PR implementing Dynarray.sort, Dynarray.stable_sort, and Dynarray.stable_sort_sub by delegating to Array.stable_sort_sub on the backing array (ocaml/ocaml#14848)
  • Olivier Nicole opened a PR adding memory model documentation comments in memory.c explaining release fences and "publication safety" for initialising writes, drawing on ocaml/ocaml#10995 (ocaml/ocaml#14857)
  • Zane Hambly continues work on native Iatomic_fetch_add across amd64, arm64, RISC-V, and POWER, with review from Olivier Nicole on release fence correctness (ocaml/ocaml#14575)
  • Romain Beauxis continues seeking feedback on Weak.{iter, iteri, foldi_left} additions, with foldi_left implemented as a C primitive to avoid per-element option wrapping allocations (ocaml/ocaml#14792)
  • Simon Cruanes maintains an open draft PR for extensible IO channels implementing the modular IO RFC, under stdlib team discussion (ocaml/ocaml#14775)
  • Stefan Muenzel has two open PRs: -rectypes testing in expect tests (ocaml/ocaml#14643) and allowing aliases in signature inclusion checks (ocaml/ocaml#14746)
  • Gabriel Scherer has an open PR adding weak pointer and ephemeron repro test cases for multicoretests failures from ocaml/ocaml#14349, noting tests now pass on trunk (ocaml/ocaml#14745)
  • Antonin Décimo merged a fix for the GHA cygwin-packages download directory causing CI cache misses (~20 seconds per run saved) (ocaml/ocaml#14852)
  • Long-standing soundness bug with polymorphism and row types (ocaml/ocaml#10840) was closed by Florian Angeletti, noting the reported crash examples are now rejected by the typechecker

    • Notable Discussions

  • Yotam Barnoy proposed lighter syntax for deep record updates in ocaml/ocaml#14854, suggesting {bar with {foo with x=2}} as an alternative to {bar with foo={bar.foo with x=2}}, with comparisons to the dotted-path syntax from ocaml/ocaml#290
  • Two newcomers opened contribution guidance discussions: @gperdutoutmoncodetipe in ocaml/ocaml#13901 and adith nk in ocaml/ocaml#14849; adith nk subsequently contributed two documentation fixes (ocaml/ocaml#14851, ocaml/ocaml#14855) that were merged the same week
  • Romain Beauxis opened ocaml/ocaml#14861 reporting that object finalizers declared in initializer can prevent GC collection
  • Nicolás Ojeda Bär opened ocaml/ocaml#14858 on the broken make world && make install workflow

    • Emerging Trends

  • Windows and cross-compilation work received sustained attention: David Allsopp landed a security fix (ocaml/ocaml#14853), Antonin Décimo merged a CI cache fix (ocaml/ocaml#14852) and opened further installcross fixes (ocaml/ocaml#14850)
  • Security hardening received formal CVE assignments for two previously merged fixes: CVE-2026-28364 / OSEC-2026-01 for intern.c robustness and CVE-2026-41083 / OSEC-2026-05 for Filename.quote_command Windows injection
  • Newcomer contributions translated into merged work: adith nk went from a newcomer Q&A discussion to having two documentation PRs merged within the same week (ocaml/ocaml#14851, ocaml/ocaml#14855), and @Jeannalyse submitted PRs for both a domain stack size feature (ocaml/ocaml#14860) and Dynarray.sort (ocaml/ocaml#14848)
  • Memory model documentation is being actively improved: Olivier Nicole's open PR (ocaml/ocaml#14857) and the ongoing Iatomic_fetch_add review (ocaml/ocaml#14575) both reflect careful attention to documenting and correctly implementing the OCaml multicore memory model guarantees

    • Multicore

    eio gains incremental directory reading and subtree rename; ocaml-uring adds socket CLOEXEC default and new I/O bindings.

    New Features

  • Path.open_subtree and Path.with_subtree replace open_dir/with_open_dir in ocaml-multicore/eio#853 with names that communicate capability-confinement semantics, merged by Thomas Leonard
  • Path.with_dir_entries provides incremental directory entry reading as a lazy Seq.t of (File.Stat.kind * string) pairs, avoiding sort overhead and showing 10–13× speedups on Linux for recursive walks (ocaml-multicore/eio#821)
  • Path.read_dir_entries returns a sorted (File.Stat.kind * string) list including file type information, eliminating the need for a separate kind call per entry (ocaml-multicore/eio#821)
  • Eio_linux.Low_level.read_some_dir exposes batched directory entry reading with kind from the Linux backend (ocaml-multicore/eio#821)
  • Eio_posix.Low_level.with_dir_entries provides the POSIX-backend counterpart with batched reads and worker-thread directory opening (ocaml-multicore/eio#821)
  • eio_linux ENOMEM fallback: when io_uring_queue_init fails with ENOMEM on memory-constrained systems, eio_linux now falls back to eio_posix (ocaml-multicore/eio#852)
  • Socket CLOEXEC default in ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#151: socket now uses Sock_flags.cloexec as the default ?flags value, preventing fd leaks into child processes; merged by Anil Madhavapeddy
  • Per-operation RWF flags proposed in ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#154: exposes preadv2/pwritev2 flags (RWF_DSYNC, RWF_NOCACHE) for use by eio_linux on recent 6.x kernels
  • Vectored fixed-buffer bindings proposed in ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#155: corrects misnamed C stubs and adds proper readv/writev for fixed-buffer operations

    • Overview

  • Activity this week was concentrated in ocaml-multicore/eio and ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring; the remaining seven repositories (domainslib, meio, saturn, eio-trace, picos, kcas, ocaml-iomux) had no recorded commits or PRs
  • In eio, five PRs merged: incremental directory reading (ocaml-multicore/eio#821), Path.open_subtree rename (ocaml-multicore/eio#853), ENOMEM fallback (ocaml-multicore/eio#852), scheduler simplification (ocaml-multicore/eio#849), and removal of unused retry logic (ocaml-multicore/eio#851)
  • In ocaml-uring, one PR merged (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#151), two new PRs opened (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#154, ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#155), one draft PR active (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153), and two older PRs closed (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#152, ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#101)
  • Three contributors were active: Thomas Leonard, Anil Madhavapeddy, and Patrick Ferris

    • Activity

  • eio scheduler simplification (ocaml-multicore/eio#849): read/write retries moved out of the scheduler into calling fibers, removing the Read/Write job types, file_offset type, and amount type; merged by Thomas Leonard
  • Removal of unused fixed-buffer retry logic (ocaml-multicore/eio#851): EAGAIN/EINTR retries that cannot trigger since switching to DEFER_TASKRUN removed; merged by Thomas Leonard
  • add ftruncate/fdatasync and use uring for fsync/shutdown/socket (ocaml-multicore/eio#850): opened by Anil Madhavapeddy, adds ftruncate/fdatasync to the Linux backend and wires newer io_uring operations for fsync, shutdown, and socket calls; awaiting review
  • Eio_unix.Sockopt module (ocaml-multicore/eio#575): rebased by Anil Madhavapeddy this week; adds a GADT-based socket options interface and is seeking design feedback on SOCKET module type integration
  • chmod support in Eio_linux and Eio_posix (ocaml-multicore/eio#785): originally by Patrick Ferris, rebased by Anil Madhavapeddy with uring nofollow flag usage and File.Unix_perm.t alignment; awaiting final review
  • Long-standing deadlock issue closed (ocaml-multicore/eio#700): "Occasional deadlocks with systhreads" resolved this week
  • bytes buffer migration draft (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153): Anil Madhavapeddy shared microbenchmarks showing improved large-buffer allocation and I/O throughput but worse small-buffer performance due to a 2KB minimum allocation floor; ongoing
  • Experimental Cstruct-to-Bstruct PR closed (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#101): closed by Patrick Ferris in favour of the broader bytes migration in ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153

    • Notable Discussions

  • Path.open_subtree naming debate (ocaml-multicore/eio#853): Anil Madhavapeddy questioned whether the confusion was a documentation problem; Thomas Leonard argued with_open_dir sounds like a directory-listing API rather than a capability-confinement primitive; Patrick Ferris cited mirage/ocaml-tar#177 as a concrete real-world security confusion caused by the old name
  • Distinct types for confined vs. unconfined directory handles (ocaml-multicore/eio#853): Thomas Leonard argued static typing cannot track whether symlink traversal escapes a subtree; Anil Madhavapeddy proposed renaming Path.(/) to Path.extend_unconfined as a use-site signal instead
  • Minimum kernel version proposal for eio_linux (ocaml-multicore/eio#845): Anil Madhavapeddy and Patrick Ferris discussed requiring kernel 6.17+/7.x+ to eliminate many op-probe workarounds needed for newer io_uring features
  • bytes vs bigarray performance tradeoffs (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153): Thomas Leonard asked for benchmark evidence; Anil Madhavapeddy reported improved large-buffer allocation (avoiding bigarray finalizer overhead) but worse small-buffer performance due to a 2KB GC-pinning minimum; conclusion was to coalesce small writes before submission
  • caml_hash_variant compile-time evaluation (ocaml-multicore/eio#821): Thomas Leonard tested in Compiler Explorer and found gcc/clang optimise the call away, but this does not work in OCaml C stubs since caml_hash_variant is defined in a .c file rather than a header
  • Linux errno module utility (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#152): Thomas Leonard and Anil Madhavapeddy concluded that since Unix_error is always needed for Low_level fallback paths in Eio, a Linux-specific errno module adds limited value; preference expressed for contributing useful errnos upstream to OCaml

    • Emerging Trends

  • Filesystem API surface expansion: with_dir_entries/read_dir_entries (ocaml-multicore/eio#821) and pending PRs for ftruncate, fdatasync, fsync, chmod, and socket options (ocaml-multicore/eio#850, ocaml-multicore/eio#785) continue a pattern of broadening eio's low-level filesystem and I/O coverage
  • Capability-confinement terminology tightening: the open_subtree/with_subtree rename (ocaml-multicore/eio#853) and discussion of Path.extend_unconfined suggest ongoing effort to surface security semantics at the API level rather than relying on documentation
  • io_uring scheduler internalization: moving retry logic from the scheduler into fibers (ocaml-multicore/eio#849) and removing dead retry paths (ocaml-multicore/eio#851) reflect a deliberate simplification of the eio_linux scheduler toward a leaner design
  • Migration from Cstruct/bigarray to bytes: closure of ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#101 in favour of ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#153 shows a deliberate effort to reduce C-backed memory dependencies and improve standard OCaml library interoperability
  • Safer-by-default API conventions: the CLOEXEC change in ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#151 reflects a pattern of making secure behavior opt-out rather than opt-in, consistent with modern Linux socket best practices
  • Minimum kernel version consideration: discussion in ocaml-multicore/eio#845 about requiring kernel 6.17+/7.x+ for eio_linux suggests willingness to drop older kernel support in exchange for significantly simpler backend code
entry.summary: OCaml 5.4 merged into OxCaml; two CVEs fixed in core; OCaml 5.5.0~rc1 landed in opam-repository; eio gains incremental directory reading.

entry.title: Week 23, 2026: Dune 3.24.0 alpha1/alpha2 released; OxCaml minus-40 bump and typing fixes; uring gains six syscalls; OCaml Workshop 2026 site launched.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Core Fixed infinite loop in runtime_events write_to_ring when events exceed ring buffer size — runtime now terminates with a fatal error (ocaml/ocaml#14834, fixes ocaml/ocaml#13335)
  • OCaml Core Fixed warning 60 (unused-module) source location for non-aliasable module substitutions — now points to substitution site rather than original declaration (ocaml/ocaml#14831, fixes ocaml/ocaml#12745)
  • OCaml Core Fixed infinite recursive stub inlining in flambda when optional argument defaults reference the enclosing function (ocaml/ocaml#14839, fixes ocaml/ocaml#14828)
  • OCaml Core Added DragonFly BSD frame pointer support for AMD64, resolving assembler errors with gcc 8.3 and binutils 2.34 (ocaml/ocaml#14840)
  • OCaml Core AR and ARFLAGS now exported in Makefile.config with configure-time override support; ARCMD deprecated as of OCaml 5.5 (ocaml/ocaml#14552)
  • OCaml Core Fixed type recovery error messages: paths are now deep-copied when freezing type expressions, preventing later unification from changing module names in earlier errors (ocaml/ocaml#14824)
  • OCaml Core Corrected singular/plural grammar in warning 57 message, upstreamed from OxCaml (ocaml/ocaml#14843)
  • OCaml Core Fixed configure.ac incorrect break statements that broke default-argument detection, resolving broken installation on OpenSUSE (ocaml/ocaml#14846)
  • OxCaml Match-in-match heuristic landed in flambda2 (oxcaml/oxcaml#4374), enabling continuation specialisation across nested match expressions via new -flambda2-match-in-match flag
  • OxCaml Normal-form mode morphisms merged (oxcaml/oxcaml#5453), refactoring the mode solver's internal representation for more precise mode error hints via concrete modality propagation
  • OxCaml Frametables now placed in .rodata section by default (oxcaml/oxcaml#6094), separating instruction and data pages to improve iTLB efficiency
  • OxCaml %%expect_fexpr annotations now available in toplevel expect tests (oxcaml/oxcaml#5837), allowing flambda2 IR snapshot testing inline
  • OxCaml New OXCAML_RUNTIME C preprocessor symbol added (oxcaml/oxcaml#6203) by Nick Barnes, giving external stubs a canonical way to detect an OxCaml runtime
  • Multicore New Eio_linux.Low_level.Fixed module introduced by Thomas Leonard, replacing Uring.Region API with an Eio-managed fixed-buffer abstraction (ocaml-multicore/eio#848)
  • Multicore Six new io_uring syscall bindings in ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring: fallocate, ftruncate, shutdown, socket, renameat, and symlinkat (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#149, ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#147)
  • Multicore Statx.Attr API overhauled — inverted check replaced by mem_checked ~mask; typed Attr.t/Mask.t return types replace Int64.t; FLAGS.t made abstract (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#142)
  • Multicore io_uring_submit errors now raised as exceptions instead of returning raw negative integers (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#144)
  • Multicore meio CLI migrated to cmdliner with --help, --version, man pages with examples, and proper positional argument handling (ocaml-multicore/meio#75)
  • OCaml Tools %{git-sha} rule variable added to dune, expanding to the short git SHA of current HEAD (ocaml/dune#14810)
  • OCaml Tools dune-configurator gains optional ?static argument to Configurator.V1.Pkg_config.get for static linking options (ocaml/dune#14947, Raphaël Proust)
  • OCaml Tools (enabled_if) in (executable) and (install) stanzas now allows any available variable, matching (library) behaviour (ocaml/dune#14860, fixes ocaml/dune#14789)
  • OCaml Tools Melange rules for multi-mode libraries now only generated when melc is available in the switch, avoiding build errors for native-only setups (ocaml/dune#15021)
  • OCaml Tools Parallel dependency cutoffs restored concurrently in watch mode; cutoffs_that_reduce_concurrency_in_watch_mode knob removed (ocaml/dune#15012)
  • OCaml Tools New Memo public API additions: Memo.create_rec, Memo.Var.Unit, Invalidation.custom, on_event node lifecycle callbacks, and reset_if_necessary with non-reproducible error tracking (ocaml/dune#14960, ocaml/dune#14965, ocaml/dune#14967, ocaml/dune#14987)
  • OCaml Tools --error-reporting=twice now prints an ==== Error Summary ==== header before repeated error list (ocaml/dune#15016, fixes ocaml/dune#14757)
  • OCaml Tools OxCaml @@zero_alloc annotations now rendered in generated odoc documentation; new Zero_alloc model type with opt, strict, arity, and custom_error_msg fields (ocaml/odoc#1422, closes ocaml/odoc#1418)
  • OCaml Tools New Intl.RelativeTimeFormat OCaml bindings in jsofocaml with format, formatToParts, and resolvedOptions methods (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2070)
  • OCaml Ecosystem OCaml Workshop 2026 mini-site launched on ocaml/ocaml.org with three new routes (/ocaml-workshop-2026, /ocaml-workshop-2026/cfp, /ocaml-workshop-2026/committee) featuring tab navigation and a "Submit a Talk" CTA (ocaml/ocaml.org#3670)
  • OCaml Ecosystem raylib 2.0.0 — OCaml bindings for the Raylib game framework published by Tobias Mock (ocaml/opam-repository#29978)
  • OCaml Ecosystem catala 1.2.0 — law-as-code language and LSP server update by vbot (ocaml/opam-repository#29983)
  • OCaml Ecosystem awso 0.9.1 — seven-package AWS OCaml SDK by Michael Bacarella (ocaml/opam-repository#29967)
  • OCaml Ecosystem awa 0.6.1 — SSH library fixing MSG_KEX_n and MSG_USERAUTH_n parsing by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#30001)
  • OCaml Ecosystem Dune 3.24.0 alpha1 and alpha2 released from ocaml/dune; alpha2 submitted to ocaml/opam-repository (ocaml/opam-repository#29996) and release notes indexed on ocaml/ocaml.org (ocaml/ocaml.org#3671)

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    opam-repository merged 10+ package releases and hardened Windows CI; ocaml.org launched the OCaml Workshop 2026 mini-site.

    New Features

  • raylib 2.0.0 — raylib.2.0.0, raygui.2.0.0, and raylib-callbacks.2.0.0 published by Tobias Mock, providing OCaml bindings for the Raylib game framework; includes qcaml compatibility fixes for API changes (ocaml/opam-repository#29978)
  • catala 1.2.0 — catala.1.2.0, catala-format.1.2.0, and catala-lsp.1.2.0 published by vbot, updating the law-as-code language and its LSP server (ocaml/opam-repository#29983)
  • awso 0.9.1 — seven-package AWS OCaml SDK (awso, awso-async, awso-cli, awso-common, awso-eio, awso-lwt, awso-sync) by Michael Bacarella (ocaml/opam-repository#29967)
  • lun 0.0.3 and ppx_lun 0.0.3 — new versions with documentation and website links fixed for prior versions, by Calascibetta Romain (ocaml/opam-repository#29984)
  • awa 0.6.1 — awa.0.6.1 and awa-mirage.0.6.1 fixing parsing of MSG_KEX_n and MSG_USERAUTH_n SSH messages, by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#30001)
  • object 0.1 — new OCaml library package by Tim McGilchrist (ocaml/opam-repository#29973)
  • patricia-tree 0.14.0 — new release by Dorian Lesbre (ocaml/opam-repository#29982)
  • ppxinlinetest_nobase v0.17.0.3 — released by Dmitrii Kosarev with a ppx_expect_nobase constraint (ocaml/opam-repository#29979)
  • ease-caml 0.1.5 — new version by Christopher Sumnicht (ocaml/opam-repository#29981)
  • vsrocq-language-server 2.4.3+1 — patch fixing an incorrect extra-source path, merged by Enrico Tassi (ocaml/opam-repository#29992)
  • bigstringaf 0.10.0 — SHA-256 and SHA-512 hash corrections by Robin (ocaml/opam-repository#29977)
  • caqti-lwt — Lwt upper bound relaxed by @funwithcthulhu (ocaml/opam-repository#29937)
  • OCaml Workshop 2026 mini-site — three new routes (/ocaml-workshop-2026, /ocaml-workshop-2026/cfp, /ocaml-workshop-2026/committee) with a bespoke layout featuring tab navigation and a "Submit a Talk" CTA, authored by Cuihtlauac Alvarado and reviewed by Sudha Parimala (ocaml/ocaml.org#3670)
  • show_header opt-out on Layout.base — new parameter in src/ocamlorg_frontend/layouts/layout.eml allowing workshop pages to suppress the standard header while leaving other pages unaffected (ocaml/ocaml.org#3670)
  • Dune 3.24.0 alpha1 and alpha2 release notes indexed on ocaml/ocaml.org via the automated platform-releases scraper (ocaml/ocaml.org#3671)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/opam-repository merged 10+ package releases including ocaml/opam-repository#29978 (raylib 2.0.0), ocaml/opam-repository#29983 (catala 1.2.0), ocaml/opam-repository#29967 (awso 0.9.1), and ocaml/opam-repository#30001 (awa 0.6.1)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org launched the OCaml Workshop 2026 pre-event mini-site (ocaml/ocaml.org#3670) and indexed dune 3.24.0 alpha release notes (ocaml/ocaml.org#3671)
  • Windows CI infrastructure in opam-repository is being hardened with upgrade-path testing for edited packages and PATH pruning for cleaner depext testing (ocaml/opam-repository#29998)
  • dune 3.24 compatibility work forced dune < 3.24 upper bounds across coq, rocq, and mdx packages (ocaml/opam-repository#29988, ocaml/opam-repository#29989, ocaml/opam-repository#29993)
  • A conf-pkgconf simplification (ocaml/opam-repository#29976) was reverted (ocaml/opam-repository#29987) after breaking downstream lockfiles, prompting policy discussion on in-place conf-package mutations (ocaml/opam-repository#29985)

    • Activity

  • liquid-ml 0.1.4 (5 packages: liquid_interpreter, liquid_ml, liquid_parser, liquid_std, liquid_syntax) — Shopify Liquid template engine in OCaml with whitespace-control and improved time handling, by Ben Faerber; supersedes the 0.1.3 submission (ocaml/opam-repository#30004, ocaml/opam-repository#30003)
  • migra 1.0.0 — first stable OCaml database migration tool supporting PostgreSQL, MariaDB, and SQLite, with checksum validation, out-of-order detection, and a --dry-run flag, by David Sinclair (ocaml/opam-repository#30002)
  • dune 3.24.0~alpha2 (18 packages) — pre-release submission by Shon Feder, superseding the alpha0 submission (ocaml/opam-repository#29996, ocaml/opam-repository#29969)
  • awskit 0.1.0 (10 packages) — new AWS infrastructure library with Eio and Lwt adapters covering signing, credentials, and endpoints, by Abdullah Elsayed (ocaml/opam-repository#29980)
  • melange-edn 0.1.0 — EDN reader and writer for Melange, converting between EDN and JavaScript JSON values, by rcmerci (ocaml/opam-repository#29999)
  • Timedesc 3.1.2 (6 packages) — OCaml date-time library release by Darren Li; supersedes the 3.1.1 submission (ocaml/opam-repository#29995, ocaml/opam-repository#29994)
  • duras 2.0.0 — release by Sergiy Duras (ocaml/opam-repository#29997)
  • Windows CI hardening — David Allsopp opened a PR introducing upgrade-path testing for edited packages (installs existing version, locks switch, then upgrades) and prunes pre-installed tools from GitHub Actions PATH to avoid masking depext failures (ocaml/opam-repository#29998)
  • conf-pkgconf revert — a Windows conf-package simplification (ocaml/opam-repository#29976) was merged then reverted (ocaml/opam-repository#29987) after breaking downstream lockfiles; Raphaël Proust separately attempted a more conservative fix (ocaml/opam-repository#29986)
  • dune 3.24 compatibility — Shon Feder merged fixes adding dune < 3.24 upper bounds to coq/rocq packages using deprecated stanzas (ocaml/opam-repository#29988), disabling then conditionally re-enabling mdx test-running (ocaml/opam-repository#29989, ocaml/opam-repository#29993)
  • Rocq 9.2 Makefile fix — Enrico Tassi fixed the Makefile target needed to build with Rocq 9.2 (ocaml/opam-repository#29991)
  • Backstage OCaml WASI tutorial — @sabine opened a PR covering the OCaml WASI prototype, currently under technical review by Jérôme Vouillon (ocaml/ocaml.org#3667)
  • OCaml Planet — automated scraper merged three batches of community blog posts from robur.coop, anil, cwn, and tunbury (ocaml/ocaml.org#3668, ocaml/ocaml.org#3669, ocaml/ocaml.org#3672)

    • Notable Discussions

  • Lockfile invalidation from conf-* mutations — Yosef reported in ocaml/opam-repository#29985 that in-place changes to conf-* dependency requirements broke existing opam lock lockfiles and CI/Windows builds; David Allsopp reverted the change (ocaml/opam-repository#29987) and noted that locking virtual/conf packages is not fully supported by opam's design
  • Proposal for opam-packages-option-static-linking — Raphaël Proust opened ocaml/opam-repository#29975 proposing convention packages analogous to ocaml-options to signal static linking preference ecosystem-wide; Marcello Seri, Anil Madhavapeddy, and Calascibetta Romain commented, with Calascibetta Romain drawing on MirageOS unikernel toolchain experience; Raphaël published a proof-of-concept branch and a dune-configurator patch as a demo
  • OCaml WASI article technical corrections — Jérôme Vouillon provided detailed corrections on ocaml/ocaml.org#3667 covering Wasm 3.0 standardisation status, --effects=cps availability, exnref-based exception handling now the default for WASI binaries (removing the need for --enable exnref), and updated implementation metrics (5200 lines / 90 files)

    • Emerging Trends

  • dune 3.24 compatibility cascade — removal of the lang coq stanza and changes to mdx test targets in dune 3.24 is requiring upper bounds across coq, rocq-runtime, and mdx packages (ocaml/opam-repository#29988, ocaml/opam-repository#29989, ocaml/opam-repository#29993), with dune 3.24.0~alpha2 already submitted to opam-repository (ocaml/opam-repository#29996) and indexed on ocaml.org (ocaml/ocaml.org#3671)
  • Windows CI testing infrastructure — David Allsopp is systematically improving Windows CI reliability with upgrade-path testing and PATH pruning to catch real-world depext regressions (ocaml/opam-repository#29998)
  • Lockfile semantics and in-place conf-package mutations — the conf-pkgconf revert (ocaml/opam-repository#29987) and issue discussion (ocaml/opam-repository#29985) highlight ongoing tension between updating package metadata in-place versus publishing new versions for virtual/conf packages that users lock
  • Event mini-sites on ocaml.org — the OCaml Workshop 2026 pre-site (ocaml/ocaml.org#3670) establishes a pattern for hosting bespoke event pages directly on ocaml.org when conf.researchr.org is unavailable, using a staged rollout approach (URL-accessible but not yet linked from main navigation)

    • OCaml Tools

    • OxCaml

    oxcaml/oxcaml saw dense typing and flambda2 fixes plus a 5.4 upstream merge push; oxcaml/merlin advanced its minus-37 branch merge.

    New Features

  • The match-in-match heuristic landed in flambda2 via oxcaml/oxcaml#4374 by Basile Clément, enabling continuation specialisation across nested match expressions and exposed via a new -flambda2-match-in-match flag with a cont_spec_threshold parameter.
  • Normal-form mode morphisms merged in oxcaml/oxcaml#5453, refactoring the mode solver's internal representation to enable more precise mode error hints via concrete modality propagation.
  • Frametables are now placed in the .rodata section by default via oxcaml/oxcaml#6094 by Kevin Svetlitski, separating instruction and data pages to improve iTLB efficiency.
  • %%expect_fexpr annotations can now appear in toplevel expect tests via oxcaml/oxcaml#5837 by Keryan Didier, allowing raw, simplified, and reaper-stage flambda2 IR to be snapshot-tested inline.
  • A new OXCAML_RUNTIME C preprocessor symbol was added in oxcaml/oxcaml#6203 by Nick Barnes, giving external stubs a single canonical way to detect an OxCaml runtime.

    • Overview

  • Activity this week was concentrated in oxcaml/oxcaml and oxcaml/merlin; oxcaml/opam-repository, oxcaml/jsofocaml, and janestreet/opam-repository had no recorded activity.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml shipped five notable features including the match-in-match heuristic (oxcaml/oxcaml#4374) and frametable relocation (oxcaml/oxcaml#6094), alongside a wave of any-kind typing correctness fixes and the 5.2.0minus-40 magic number bump (oxcaml/oxcaml#6204).
  • oxcaml/merlin has a large draft PR (oxcaml/merlin#239) merging minus-37 changes into the 5.4 branch (896 files changed), currently blocked on conflict resolution but receiving positive review feedback.

  • Ryan Tjoa merged a cluster of any-kind correctness fixes: topological jkind ordering (oxcaml/oxcaml#6177), its follow-up (oxcaml/oxcaml#6209), sort variables for any-kinded fields (oxcaml/oxcaml#6145), and gating variable-representation types behind -extension layouts_beta (oxcaml/oxcaml#6173), plus atomic field and record representation fixes (oxcaml/oxcaml#6131, oxcaml/oxcaml#6143, oxcaml/oxcaml#6156).
  • Basile Clément merged a static-constants code-size accounting fix (oxcaml/oxcaml#5992) and dropped spuriously created variables during nested env-extension joins (oxcaml/oxcaml#6170).

    • Notable Discussions

  • Basile Clément opened oxcaml/oxcaml#6180 noting that flambda2 eagerly unboxes variant fields even when no local allocation is present; the proposed fix is to only unbox fields that already have at least one use with the field available.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#6146 (closed) discussed the recommended idiom for pairing @ unique destroy with interleaved read operations on C handles; the thread concluded that with-resource combinators or consume-and-return threading are current options and borrowing is not yet available.
  • The box types PR oxcaml/oxcaml#5342 by Ryan Tjoa saw continued review with Jakub Bachurski near-approving, with open questions around GADT exhaustiveness and mcomp aliasability for _ box.
  • Mark Shinwell raised a concern in oxcaml/oxcaml#6177 about topological ordering as a long-term solution to recursive jkind computation; Ryan Tjoa outlined a future unification-based approach using layout variables.
  • Chris Casinghino reviewed the key files in oxcaml/merlin#239 and found the minus-37 merge changes reasonable, providing a positive signal for the large-scale integration.

    • OCaml Core

    Bug fixes for runtime events, flambda, type checker, and build system; RFC #52 implicit source positions design resolved.

    New Features

  • Fixed infinite loop in runtime_events.c's write_to_ring when events exceed the ring buffer size — runtime now terminates with a fatal error rather than hanging (ocaml/ocaml#14834, fixes ocaml/ocaml#13335)
  • Fixed warning 60 (unused-module) source location for non-aliasable module substitutions — now points to the substitution site rather than the original declaration (ocaml/ocaml#14831, fixes ocaml/ocaml#12745)
  • Fixed infinite recursive stub inlining in flambda when optional argument defaults reference the enclosing function (ocaml/ocaml#14839, fixes ocaml/ocaml#14828)
  • Added DragonFly BSD frame pointer support for AMD64, resolving assembler errors with gcc 8.3 and binutils 2.34 (ocaml/ocaml#14840)
  • AR and ARFLAGS are now exported in Makefile.config and support configure-time override; ARCMD deprecated as of OCaml 5.5 (ocaml/ocaml#14552)
  • Fixed type recovery error messages: paths are now deep-copied when freezing type expressions, preventing later unification from changing module names in earlier errors (ocaml/ocaml#14824)
  • Fixed configure.ac incorrect break statements that broke default-argument detection, resolving broken installation on OpenSUSE (ocaml/ocaml#14846)
  • Corrected singular/plural grammar in warning 57 message, upstreamed from OxCaml (ocaml/ocaml#14843)

    • Multicore

    ocaml-uring adds six syscall bindings; eio migrates fixed-buffer management to Eio_linux.Low_level.Fixed; meio CLI migrated to cmdliner.

    New Features

  • ocaml-multicore/eio: New Eio_linux.Low_level.Fixed module introduced by Thomas Leonard, replacing the Uring.Region API with an Eio-managed fixed-buffer abstraction (ocaml-multicore/eio#848); exposes Fixed.alloc, Fixed.alloc_or_wait, Fixed.free, Fixed.use, Fixed.length, Fixed.to_cstruct, Fixed.to_bigstring, and Fixed.to_string
  • ocaml-multicore/eio: ftruncate, fdatasync, and uring-based fsync operations being added to eio_linux by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml-multicore/eio#850), extending the file operations available through the io_uring backend
  • ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring: New fallocate binding with a Fallocate_flags module (keep_size, punch_hole, collapse_range, zero_range, insert_range, unshare_range, write_zeroes) and ftruncate binding for async file size adjustment (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#149)
  • ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring: New shutdown, socket, renameat (with Rename_flags: noreplace, exchange, whiteout), and symlinkat bindings for async networking and filesystem operations (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#147)
  • ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring: Statx.Attr API overhauled — inverted check function replaced by mem_checked ~mask; attributes and attributes_mask now return typed Attr.t instead of Int64.t; Statx.mask returns typed Mask.t; FLAGS.t is now abstract (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#142)
  • ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring: io_uring_submit errors now raised as exceptions instead of returning raw negative integers (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#144)
  • ocaml-multicore/meio: The meio executable now uses cmdliner for argument parsing, adding --help, --version, man pages with examples, proper positional argument handling, and -- flag disambiguation (ocaml-multicore/meio#75)

    • Overview

  • Activity was concentrated in ocaml-multicore/eio, ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring, and ocaml-multicore/meio; the remaining six repositories (domainslib, saturn, eio-trace, picos, kcas, ocaml-iomux) had no activity this week
  • ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring was the most active repo: eight PRs merged and three open, adding six new syscall bindings (fallocate, ftruncate, shutdown, socket, renameat, symlinkat) and overhauling the Statx typed API
  • ocaml-multicore/eio merged three PRs and opened two more, with work focused on decoupling fixed-buffer management from the uring library and adding new file operations
  • ocaml-multicore/meio completed a CLI migration to cmdliner, improving the user-facing interface of the Eio monitoring tool
  • Key contributors: Thomas Leonard, Anil Madhavapeddy, Patrick Ferris, and David Allsopp

  • eio scheduler simplification: Thomas Leonard opened ocaml-multicore/eio#849, moving read/write retry logic out of the scheduler into fiber-level code, removing the special-cased Read/Write job types and the file_offset type
