  • Fix metaprogramming REPL syntax directive issue by Andrej Ivašković (oxcaml/oxcaml#5801); graceful reporting of unsupported language features in runtime metaprogramming merged (oxcaml/oxcaml#5823)
  • Handle staging in Printtyp more carefully by Jakub Bachurski (oxcaml/oxcaml#5785)
  • 5.4 merge: various testsuite promotions merged (oxcaml/oxcaml#5757)
  • Bootstrap compiler update to OCaml 5.4.1 in oxcaml/opam-repository#36 remains open pending resolution of workflow concerns raised by David Allsopp
  • OxCaml opam-repository pointer update away from deprecated branch proposed by Xiaomin Liu in janestreet/opam-repository#75

    • Notable Discussions

  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5831 (skip caml_modify for non_pointer values) includes detailed discussion of interactions with abstract kinds, type substitution edge cases, and how mixed block representations can become stale after substitution
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5809 (move Flambda2 export info to a section) prompted Mark Shinwell to suggest making section storage more generic to also accommodate Slambda code for layout poly
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5820 (use alloc_mode when building unknown types) received detailed review from Vincent Laviron cautioning about the safety of pushing allocation modes from containers to children
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5662 (add env_alloc_mode to Tpat_fun_layout) has ongoing review discussion about the correct error message for the syntactic value restriction in layout-poly let bindings
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5663 (sort variable negative IDs in .cmi files) has a design discussion about whether to reuse or rename a helper function for constructing sort variables with explicit IDs
  • oxcaml/opam-repository#36: David Allsopp raised that replacing the bootstrap compiler entry breaks the existing workflow for the 5.2.0minus-25 tag; Eduardo Souza clarified the intended workflow via opam compiler create oxcaml:main (ocaml-opam/opam-compiler#42)

    • Emerging Trends

  • The representation of unboxed records and variants is being systematically rationalised: all-value/void mixed records will become uniform blocks (oxcaml/oxcaml#5774), float64 records will become mixed blocks (oxcaml/oxcaml#5796), and legacy float-array representation will require an explicit opt-in (oxcaml/oxcaml#5795)
  • Layout polymorphism infrastructure is maturing with multiple PRs fixing sort variable level handling (oxcaml/oxcaml#5791), instantiation errors (oxcaml/oxcaml#5817), and generalisation correctness (oxcaml/oxcaml#5792)
  • The Flambda2 reaper is being incrementally restructured: dep_solver.ml split into points-to analysis, unboxing analysis, and types rewrite modules (oxcaml/oxcaml#5776), with code size computation next (oxcaml/oxcaml#5793)
  • The SSA CFG variant draft (oxcaml/oxcaml#5810) opens a path to loop-level optimisations such as empty loop deletion (oxcaml/oxcaml#5840) directly on the CFG IR
  • Metaprogramming (quotation/splicing) is seeing incremental fixes to REPL usability (oxcaml/oxcaml#5801) and error reporting (oxcaml/oxcaml#5823)
  • Ongoing effort to keep Merlin's compiler flag ignore-lists in sync with OxCaml's extended flambda2 and LLVM backend flags, now reinforced by automated ocamlopt-coverage tests (oxcaml/merlin#232)
  • OxCaml opam packaging coordination is an active area, with both oxcaml/opam-repository#36 and janestreet/opam-repository#75 open this week to align repository pointers and bootstrap compiler versions with the 5.4 compiler branch

    • OCaml Core

    Keep-expansion typechecker fix and primitive aliases (RFC #44) merged; implicit source positions RFC design narrowed to options 2a/2b.

    New Features

  • Primitive aliases (implementing ocaml/RFCs#44) landed via ocaml/ocaml#13377, enabling external foo = Bar.baz syntax to alias C primitives; contributed by Nailen Matschke, reviewed by Jeremy Yallop, Leo White, and Florian Angeletti.
  • Atomic.update was merged via ocaml/ocaml#10798, adding a retry-loop helper ('a -> 'a) -> 'a t -> unit to Atomic, Atomic.Loc, and Atomic.Array; contributed by Gabriel Scherer with extensive review.
  • Format.pp_print_iarray was added via ocaml/ocaml#14724 by Olivier Nicole, addressing the stdlib gap noted in ocaml/ocaml#14320.
  • Format.pp_print_dynarray was added via ocaml/ocaml#14726 by Olivier Nicole, building on the iarray printer.
  • ocamltest cold predicate was introduced via ocaml/ocaml#14713 by Gabriel Scherer, allowing tests to be disabled by default and run only when explicitly requested, closing ocaml/ocaml#12418.

    • Overview

  • Activity was concentrated in ocaml/ocaml, with a high-impact week combining long-awaited typechecker corrections, runtime GC fixes, and stdlib additions.
  • The "keep expansion" typechecker overhaul ocaml/ocaml#11648 merged after years of development, resolving multiple non-termination and principality bugs.
  • Primitive aliases from ocaml/RFCs#44 were implemented and merged via ocaml/ocaml#13377, completing a full RFC-to-implementation cycle.
  • In ocaml/RFCs, design discussion on the implicit source positions RFC (ocaml/RFCs#52) converged toward implementation options 2a/2b.
  • Key contributors active across both repositories include Gabriel Scherer and Olivier Nicole.

    • Activity

  • Keep expansion typechecker overhaul ocaml/ocaml#11648 was merged after years of development by Jacques Garrigue and Stefan Muenzel, fixing non-termination bugs (ocaml/ocaml#9314, ocaml/ocaml#13230, ocaml/ocaml#13881, ocaml/ocaml#14036) and principality regressions.
  • Ephemeron orphaning bug fix for 5.5 was submitted and merged via ocaml/ocaml#14718 by Gabriel Scherer, addressing runtime assertion failures reported in ocaml/ocaml#14349.
  • A series of ephemeron runtime refactoring PRs (ocaml/ocaml#14732, ocaml/ocaml#14733, ocaml/ocaml#14734, ocaml/ocaml#14735) were opened by Gabriel Scherer to clarify phase-change logic and fix the correctness bug on trunk.
  • Domain unique_id assignment was moved earlier during domain creation via ocaml/ocaml#14716 by Gabriel Scherer, improving debuggability of domain lifecycle logging.
  • GADT scope-escape hint was added to typechecker error messages via ocaml/ocaml#14695 by Stefan Muenzel, providing guidance for users encountering ambivalent type errors.
  • Typechecker memory usage fix for counter-example search was proposed via ocaml/ocaml#14727 by Florian Angeletti, addressing excessive memory use in pattern-matching exhaustiveness checks.
  • Compaction corner case test was improved via ocaml/ocaml#14685 by Gabriel Scherer, reducing test runtime from 14s to 1.5s while reproducing the original bug more reliably.
  • translmod.ml refactoring introducing a lambda_subst helper was merged via ocaml/ocaml#14728 by Nicolás Ojeda Bär.
  • Regression test for rectypes keep-expansion was merged via ocaml/ocaml#14730 by Brandon Stride, preventing re-introduction of the typechecker infinite loop.
  • Minor cleanup in Typecore.type_effect_cases was merged via ocaml/ocaml#14723 by Chris Casinghino.
  • Implicit source positions RFC (ocaml/RFCs#52) design discussion progressed, with Gabriel Scherer and Olivier Nicole converging on options 2a/2b as the path forward.

    • Notable Discussions

  • Ephemeron orphaning and adoption semantics were analysed in ocaml/ocaml#14720 by Gabriel Scherer, questioning whether orphaned ephemerons should survive across GC cycles and proposing simplifications; the thread involves Damien Doligez, KC Sivaramakrishnan, Nick Barnes, and Stephen Dolan.
  • Adding extension points to the AST for ppxlib compatibility was discussed in ocaml/ocaml#14668 by Nathan Rebours, exploring how to encode new language features without breaking existing ppx-es, with a concrete proposal forthcoming.
  • Misleading syntactic arity error message was reported in ocaml/ocaml#14719 by Jeremy Yallop for valid functions with module-dependent arrows, prompting a fix PR ocaml/ocaml#14721 from Florian Angeletti.
  • Atomic.fold_update naming continued in ocaml/ocaml#14725, with Simon Cruanes and Daniel Bünzli preferring modify_get or map_update over fold_update.
  • Stdlib gaps around iarray were noted in ocaml/ocaml#14320 by Andreas Rossberg, flagging that Iarray.sub has a divergent signature and Dynarray.to/of_iarray conversions are absent, with ocaml/ocaml#14724 as a partial fix.
  • Implicit source positions implementation strategy in ocaml/RFCs#52: Gabriel Scherer and Olivier Nicole agreed that option 2a is a viable incremental path toward the fuller 2b design for the [%call_pos] feature.

    • Emerging Trends

  • Typechecker correctness and well-foundedness: the landmark keep-expansion merge ocaml/ocaml#11648 resolves deep-seated non-termination and principality bugs; follow-on work is expected around class types and recursive modules.
  • Ephemeron GC hardening for multicore: Gabriel Scherer opened a structured multi-PR series (ocaml/ocaml#14732–ocaml/ocaml#14735) to systematically clarify and fix ephemeron lifecycle management, motivated by multicoretests reproductions from Jan Midtgaard in ocaml/ocaml#14349.
  • Stdlib completeness for immutable and dynamic arrays: addition of pp_print_iarray ocaml/ocaml#14724 and pp_print_dynarray ocaml/ocaml#14726 reflects ongoing work to bring iarray and Dynarray to feature parity with Array, with further gaps tracked in ocaml/ocaml#14320.
  • RFC-to-implementation pipeline: primitive aliases completing the ocaml/RFCs#44 → ocaml/ocaml#13377 cycle, and implicit source positions (ocaml/RFCs#52) advancing toward implementation, illustrate the RFC process maturing as a design gateway for language changes.
  • CI security hygiene: ocaml/ocaml#14676 by Austin Theriault proposed preventing shell injection in GitHub Actions workflows, reflecting broader supply-chain security attention.

    • Multicore
entry.summary: Dune 3.22.2, merlin v5.7.0-504, and ocaml-lsp 1.26.0 released; OCaml keep-expansion typechecker merged; OxCaml sets Runtime 5 as default.

entry.title: Week 14, 2026: Dune 3.22.1 released; OxCaml merged 47 PRs on staging/GADTs, new modes, static modules; ocaml/ocaml landed 5 PRs with Dynarray conversions and Pphyscomp.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Core Dynarray.ofiarray and Dynarray.toiarray added to the standard library, enabling O(n) round-trips between dynamic and immutable arrays.
  • OCaml Core Physical comparison operators (== and !=) now propagate as a distinct Pphyscomp primitive to the lambda IR via ocaml/ocaml#13588, enabling backends such as jsofocaml to emit semantically correct code.
  • OCaml Core Record update syntax relaxed so that { (Gc.get ()) with ... } no longer requires parentheses around function application expressions via ocaml/ocaml#14692.
  • OCaml Core s390x CFI debug metadata improved via ocaml/ocaml#14500, adding a cfi_val_offset emission helper and GDB regression tests.
  • OCaml Core PUSHENVACC4 bytecode opcode now correctly generated after an off-by-one fix in the peephole optimiser via ocaml/ocaml#14534.
  • OxCaml Abstract kinds with kind_ constraints completed the core abstract kinds feature set via oxcaml/oxcaml#5629.
  • OxCaml New write/writing modes added in oxcaml/oxcaml#5608 and corrupted/corruptible modes in oxcaml/oxcaml#5713, enabling cleaner mode implications without needing shared.
  • OxCaml Static modules landed via oxcaml/oxcaml#5724 and the underlying static computation framework via oxcaml/oxcaml#5430.
  • OxCaml Staging and GADTs became mostly sound together through parts 1-3 in oxcaml/oxcaml#5641, with stage tracking in Ctype and exhaustive GADT tests.
  • OxCaml X86 peephole optimizations infrastructure merged in oxcaml/oxcaml#5639, adding rules for dead-register removal and redundant comparison elimination.
  • OxCaml IRC complexity threshold for register allocation added in oxcaml/oxcaml#5705, allowing fallback to a simpler allocator for large functions.
  • OxCaml New Lfor compilation strategy introduced in oxcaml/oxcaml#5728.
  • OxCaml -thunkify-compilation-unit-initialization flag added for wasmofocaml support in oxcaml/oxcaml#5720.
  • OxCaml Metaprogramming type support in Merlin's locate_types.ml with Tquote_eval and Tquote type forms via oxcaml/merlin#228 and oxcaml/merlin#230.
  • Multicore Configurable eventfd creation in the ocaml-multicore/eio Linux and Posix backends, with optional ?eventfd and ?pipe parameters via ocaml-multicore/eio#836.
  • OCaml Ecosystem Rocq 9.2.0 merged to opam-repository by Guillaume Melquiond, adding rocq-runtime, rocq-stdlib, rocq-devtools, and rocqide packages.
  • OCaml Ecosystem opentelemetry 0.90 ocaml/opam-repository#29633 by Simon Cruanes, a major refactor splitting signal providers into separate traces, metrics, and logs packages.
  • OCaml Ecosystem sm 0.1.0 ocaml/opam-repository#29641 — a pure OCaml implementation of Chinese national cryptographic algorithms (SM2, SM3, SM4, ZUC).
  • OCaml Ecosystem aslref 1.0-EAC1 ocaml/opam-repository#29635 — ARM's reference implementation of the Architecture Specification Language (ASL).
  • OCaml Ecosystem lunar 1.0.0 ocaml/opam-repository#29625 by Xavier Van de Woestyne, a date management library with Time, Date, Datetime, Timezone, and Zoned_datetime modules.
  • OCaml Tools Dune DUNE_PROJECT_ROOT environment variable ocaml/dune#13934 allows actions to observe their project root without manual %{project_root} threading.
  • OCaml Tools Relocatable compiler support in dune package management ocaml/dune#13321 enables the compiler to be cached like a regular package.
  • OCaml Tools Hardlink sandboxing on Windows ocaml/dune#13987 lifts the prior restriction and provides clearer errors on symlink failures.
  • OCaml Tools Multiple (dirs ..) stanzas with intersection semantics ocaml/dune#13734 from dune language 3.23.
  • OCaml Tools Class and object hover support coordinated across ocaml/merlin#2053 and ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1599 by Ulysse, addressing ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1587.
  • OCaml Tools jsofocaml Wasm correctness fixes: reference unboxing ocsigen/jsofocaml#2210, empty closure physical identity ocsigen/jsofocaml#2207, and stale global data flow guard ocsigen/jsofocaml#2208 all merged.

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    opam-repository landed Rocq 9.2.0, dune 3.22.1, and 20+ releases; ocaml.org reverted to Plausible analytics and proposed MDX highlighting.

    New Features

  • ocaml/opam-repository#29617 Rocq 9.2.0 merged by Guillaume Melquiond, adding rocq-runtime, rocq-stdlib, rocq-devtools, and rocqide packages
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29632 dune 3.22.1 (18 packages) submitted by Shon Feder, fixing Windows 7 compatibility and correcting dune test behaviour in multi-context workspaces
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29641 sm 0.1.0 — a pure OCaml implementation of Chinese national cryptographic algorithms (SM2, SM3, SM4, ZUC) by sang
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29635 aslref 1.0-EAC1 — ARM's reference implementation of the Architecture Specification Language (ASL), merged by Hadrien Renaud
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29633 opentelemetry 0.90 (9 packages) by Simon Cruanes, a major refactor splitting the library into separate signal providers for traces, metrics, and logs
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29566 gendarme 0.4.1 (9 packages) by Benjamin Somers, a suite for marshalling OCaml data structures to CSV, JSON, TOML, and YAML
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29556 alcobar 0.3 by Thomas Gazagnaire, a fuzzing library forked from Crowbar with an Alcotest-compatible API and per-test timeouts
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29625 lunar 1.0.0 by Xavier Van de Woestyne, a date management library exposing Time, Date, Datetime, Timezone, and Zoned_datetime
  • ocaml/ocaml.org#3593 Hilite ocaml-mdx syntax highlighting proposed by Patrick Ferris, enabling correct syntax highlighting of OCaml MDX code blocks using the # prompt syntax, fixing confusing rendering of line directives (fixes ocaml/ocaml.org#3037)

    • Overview

  • Active week across both repositories: opam-repository recorded 86 files changed with 20+ new or updated packages, while ocaml.org merged 8 PRs covering analytics, content, and tooling
  • Major new package arrivals in ocaml/opam-repository include Rocq 9.2.0 (#29617), dune 3.22.1 (#29632), opentelemetry 0.90 (#29633), and the new SM cryptography library (#29641)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org reverted from Posthog to Plausible analytics (#3594) and received a proposal for improved OCaml MDX syntax highlighting (#3593)
  • Formal methods tooling was particularly active, with binsec 0.11.1 (#29630), bitwuzla 1.0.6 (#29624), smtml 0.24.0 (#29616), and aslref 1.0-EAC1 (#29635) all landing
  • Windows compatibility improvements continued with conf-brotli fix (#29645) and MSYS2 depext work (#29579, #29613) in progress

    • Activity

  • ocaml/opam-repository#29629 rpclib 10.2.0 (6 packages) merged by Török Edwin, improving ppxlib 0.35 compatibility and fixing JSONRPC unmarshalling
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29603 dune-release 2.2.1 merged by Marek Kubica, adding prerelease support
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29586 mdx 2.5.2 merged by Jules Aguillon, adding OCaml 5.5 support
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29642 lwt_eio 0.6 merged by Thomas Leonard
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29598 ocaml-protoc 4.1 (4 packages) merged by Simon Cruanes, with bugfixes for large signed int64 and wrapped options
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29630 binsec 0.11.1 merged by Frédéric Recoules, fixing compilation with OCaml >= 5.4
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29624 bitwuzla 1.0.6 (2 packages) merged by Frédéric Recoules, adding quantifiers and a Cadical 2.1.2 vendor bump
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29583 oniguruma 0.2.0 merged by Alan, raising minimum OCaml to 4.12
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29601 ocaml-solo5 1.2.2 merged by Hannes Mehnert
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29612 libbinaryen 126.0.0 and #29611 binaryen 0.35.0 merged by Grain Bot, upgrading to Binaryen v126
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29634 curses 1.0.12 merged by Michael Bacarella, adding setlocale support for UTF-8; restricted to non-Windows platforms after review
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29579 MSYS2 depext and UCRT64 support by Sora Morimoto, pending merge
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29613 conf-perl Cygwin/MSYS2 support by Sora Morimoto, marked priority for windows support
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29484 colibri2 0.5 (4 packages) opened by François Bobot, a CP/SMT solver with new FP/BV theory propagators and theory of arrays
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29621 pplumbing deprecation documented by Mathieu Barbin
  • ocaml/ocaml.org#3594 Posthog reverted to Plausible by Mark Elvers, removing the Posthog tracking script and restoring the Plausible dashboard link in the privacy policy
  • ocaml/ocaml.org#3592 CNAF job listing added by Denis Merigoux for a compilation engineer role (Catala compiler project, France)
  • ocaml/ocaml.org#3588 markdownlint-cli2-action bumped from v22 to v23 by dependabot, updating to Node.js 24
  • Automated OCaml Planet scraper merged daily blog posts in #3587, #3589, #3590, #3591, and #3595, covering AI disclosure in OCaml code, a CSS engine in OCaml, binary format description, CI for opam overlay repos, and TUI tooling

    • Notable Discussions

  • ocaml/opam-repository#29646 Issue raised by Dmitrii Kosarev reporting that exenum.0.84 and its upstream GitHub repository are missing (404), with comments also noting missing azure-cosmos-db.0.1.3 and omtl — highlighting the risk of source archives disappearing
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29634 curses 1.0.12 required multiple review rounds: Jan Midtgaard identified a Val_none compile error on OCaml < 4.12, a dune lower bound requiring >= 3.17, and a LC_MESSAGES symbol missing on Windows — leading to the package being restricted to non-Windows platforms
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29644 A constraint PR from Vincent Balat to restrict ocsigen-i18n < 5.0.0 for ocsigen-start 8.0.0 was closed after the new ocsigen-i18n 5.0.0 PR (ocaml/opam-repository#29643) was opened instead

    • Emerging Trends

  • Formal methods and SMT solvers had a concentrated week: binsec 0.11.1 (ocaml/opam-repository#29630), bitwuzla 1.0.6 with quantifiers (ocaml/opam-repository#29624), smtml 0.24.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#29616), and ARM's ASL reference implementation aslref 1.0-EAC1 (ocaml/opam-repository#29635) all landed
  • Windows and cross-platform compatibility continued to receive attention: conf-brotli Windows fix (ocaml/opam-repository#29645) merged, MSYS2 depext improvements (ocaml/opam-repository#29579) and Perl conf packages Cygwin/MSYS2 support (ocaml/opam-repository#29613) are in progress
  • Observability maturity: opentelemetry 0.90 (ocaml/opam-repository#29633) split signal providers into separate trace, metrics, and log packages — a sign of the OCaml telemetry stack stabilising around well-defined interfaces
  • Analytics privacy: ocaml.org's revert from Posthog to Plausible (ocaml/ocaml.org#3594) reflects a preference for privacy-respecting, self-hosted analytics in the OCaml community's infrastructure
  • Documentation tooling feedback loop: ocaml.org is being used as the primary test bed for unreleased Hilite ocaml-mdx support (ocaml/ocaml.org#3593), demonstrating how ocaml.org drives upstream library improvements before they reach opam

    • OCaml Tools

    Dune 3.22.1 released; coordinated Merlin/LSP class hover improvements; js_of_ocaml Wasm fixes; opam shell/UI PRs in review.

    New Features

  • ocaml/dune — DUNEPROJECTROOT environment variable (ocaml/dune#13934): Actions can now observe their project root via DUNE_PROJECT_ROOT, avoiding manual %{project_root} threading — merged by Rudi Grinberg
  • ocaml/dune — Relocatable compiler support in package management (ocaml/dune#13321): Dune detects relocatable compilers (via relocatable-compiler meta-package or OCaml 5.5+), enabling the compiler to be cached like a regular package — merged by Ali Caglayan
  • ocaml/dune — Hardlink sandboxing on Windows (ocaml/dune#13987): Restriction on hardlink sandboxing on Windows lifted; symlink attempts now produce a clearer error — merged by Ali Caglayan, partially addressing ocaml/dune#4362
  • ocaml/dune — c_library_flags in foreign_library (ocaml/dune#13484): Flags can now be passed to ocamlmklib via c_library_flags in foreign_library stanzas — merged by @madroach
  • ocaml/dune — Multiple (dirs ..) stanzas (ocaml/dune#13734): Support for multiple (dirs ..) stanzas with intersection semantics from dune language 3.23, fixing ocaml/dune#6249 — merged by Antonio Nuno Monteiro
  • ocaml/dune — Improved diff action inference (ocaml/dune#14008): Source directories are now automatically inferred as dependencies when used as the left-hand side in diff actions — merged by Rudi Grinberg
  • ocaml/merlin — Type enclosing for class types and objects (ocaml/merlin#2053): New Classtype variant in type_enclosing.mli with expanded logic for class types, class type aliases, and object expressions, addressing ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1587 — merged by Ulysse
  • ocaml/ocaml-lsp — Hover support for class and object constructs (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1599): Hovering over class declarations, class fields, object expressions, and record brackets now triggers type-enclosing queries, addressing ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1587 — merged by Ulysse
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml — Reference unboxing substitution fix (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2210): Fixed a substitution bug in js_assign.ml that caused assertion failures when compiling containers-data 3.18 — merged by Jérôme Vouillon
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml — Wasm physical identity of empty closures (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2207): Function equality semantics are now correctly preserved in the Wasm backend — merged by Jérôme Vouillon
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml — Wasm stale global data flow guard (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2208): Guard added to prevent crashes on certain direct function calls in the Wasm backend — merged by Jérôme Vouillon

    • Overview

  • Six of nine repositories had activity this week; ocaml/ocamlfind, ocaml/opam-file-format, and ocaml-dune/spawn had no recorded commits or PRs
  • ocaml/dune was the most active repository with the 3.22.1 patch release (ocaml/dune#13947), six new merged features, and extensive test/CI work
  • ocaml/merlin and ocaml/ocaml-lsp executed a coordinated improvement to class and object hover support, both driven by Ulysse and addressing ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1587
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml merged three targeted bug fixes for the Wasm backend and reference unboxing, with large draft PRs for OCaml 5.5 and ESM support in progress
  • ocaml/opam had three PRs under active review: Nushell shell support (ocaml/opam#6873), action list reordering (ocaml/opam#6864), and a symlink fix (ocaml/opam#6874)
  • ocaml/odoc received two new PRs: OxCaml unboxed type support (ocaml/odoc#1407) and a long-requested @inline tag for module declarations (ocaml/odoc#1408)
  • Release preparation is underway for both Merlin 5.7.0-504 (ocaml/merlin#2055) and ocaml-lsp 1.26.0-504 (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1600)

    • Activity

  • ocaml/dune — Dune 3.22.1 released (ocaml/dune#13947): Patch release by Shon Feder fixing Windows 7 compatibility, dune test crash without default context (ocaml/dune#13930, ocaml/dune#13904), and Chrome trace format timestamps (ocaml/dune#13911)
  • ocaml/dune — Digest caching correctness fixes: Cache now invalidates on device/inode numbers rather than floating-point mtime (ocaml/dune#13991) with a follow-up inode field correction (ocaml/dune#14058) — by Rudi Grinberg
  • ocaml/dune — Sandbox fix for (:include ..) deps (ocaml/dune#13898): Sandbox specifications inside (:include foo.sexp) expressions were previously ignored — fixed by Rudi Grinberg
  • ocaml/dune — macOS SIGCHLD crash fix (ocaml/dune#14047): Ignores unset SIGCHLD signals during SIGINT cleanup on macOS — merged by Antonio Nuno Monteiro
  • ocaml/dune — RPC error message improvement (ocaml/dune#13983): Error now reads "Another Dune instance is currently running. Aborting..." — contributed by Meet Zalavadiya, closing ocaml/dune#13902
  • ocaml/dune — CI line-ending check (ocaml/dune#14013): Detects files with incorrect line endings — merged by Puneeth Chaganti, closing ocaml/dune#14006
  • ocaml/dune — Backporting script (ocaml/dune#13952): Automates cherry-picking fixes to release candidate branches — merged by Shon Feder
  • ocaml/dune — Marshal-to-repr digest migration in progress: Multi-PR effort (ocaml/dune#14015, ocaml/dune#14016, ocaml/dune#14025) replacing marshal-based digests with repr-derived functions; culminating open PR ocaml/dune#14051 by Rudi Grinberg
  • ocaml/dune — Per-module library dependency analysis (ocaml/dune#14021, ocaml/dune#14030): Robin Bate Boerop implementing finer dependency filtering using ocamldep to reduce recompilation, tracking ocaml/dune#4572
  • ocaml/dune — Rocq updated to 9.2 (ocaml/dune#13996): Drops OCaml 4 from Rocq support — merged by Ali Caglayan
  • ocaml/merlin — Pointing indexes for ocaml-index under review (ocaml/merlin#2051): Tim ats's PR adds index files that reference another on-disk index, yielding ~2.7x write performance improvement
  • ocaml/merlin — LRU cache for indexer memory under review (ocaml/merlin#2050): Charlène_Gros replaces an unbounded Hashtable with an LRU cache to bound memory consumption
  • ocaml/merlin — Forward-compatibility fix for keep-expansion (ocaml/merlin#2054): Type annotation added in Destruct.refine_complete_match to avoid a type scope escape that will become a hard error in a future OCaml version — by Stefan Muenzel
  • ocaml/ocaml-lsp — Signature-help readability revert (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1598): Line-break formatting from ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1580 reverted because editors render signature-help labels as one-liners — merged by Charlène_Gros
  • ocaml/ocaml-lsp — Dune 3.22 build fix (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1594): Resolved compilation breakage introduced by the Dune 3.22 release — by Antonio Nuno Monteiro
  • ocaml/opam — Nushell shell support (ocaml/opam#6873): PR by @jneem under review; R. Boujbel requested minimum version check and user-visible warning
  • ocaml/opam — Action list reordering (ocaml/opam#6864): PR by Kate sorting solver actions by priority, fixing ocaml/opam#6863
  • ocaml/opam — Symlink handling in file:// repos (ocaml/opam#6874): PR by Sora Morimoto replacing Unix.lstat with Unix.stat to follow symlinks, fixing errors in opam-repository CI on Windows/Cygwin
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml — Wasm Dynlink/toplevel support in progress (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2187): Large in-progress PR by Jérôme Vouillon (6000+ lines)
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml — OCaml 5.5 runtime support draft (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2195) and ESM tooling draft (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2163) by @hhugo

    • Notable Discussions

  • Concurrent dune invocations and RPC locking (ocaml/dune#13964): Shon Feder, Rudi Grinberg, and Ali Caglayan debated retry-on-lock-contention vs. immediate failure; AI agent workflows cited as a key motivating use case, with Rudi Grinberg arguing immediate failure is preferable for agent loops
  • Deprecating (mode promote) (ocaml/dune#14044): Rudi Grinberg proposed deprecating promote rule mode, arguing both use cases are better served by diff actions and a planned --promote-file flag
  • scope stanza for library visibility when vendoring (ocaml/dune#13337): Thomas Gazagnaire proposing (scope (dir ..) (packages ..)) to control library visibility; Rudi Grinberg raised concerns about long-term maintenance commitment before accepting new dune language features
  • Finer library dependency analysis (ocaml/dune#14021): Robin Bate Boerop implementing per-module dependency filtering with active review from Rudi Grinberg and Marek Kubica on prerequisite PRs (ocaml/dune#14017, ocaml/dune#14030, ocaml/dune#14031)
  • Pointing index race condition (ocaml/merlin#2051): @art-w identified that using with_open to check a file identifier before re-opening provides no safety guarantee if the file is replaced between the two opens; recommendation is to check an already-open file descriptor
  • LRU cache correctness in indexer (ocaml/merlin#2050): @art-w flagged that removing a cache entry when an offset is no longer needed loses sharing, causing duplicate allocations; benchmarks show ~1.1x memory penalty
  • -short-paths configuration in ocaml-lsp (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1579): Ulysse clarified that -real-paths is Merlin-specific and cannot be passed directly; discussion settled on restoring upstream defaults with a Dune workaround for users needing explicit control
  • macOS SIGCHLD signal handling (ocaml/dune#14023): Antonio Nuno Monteiro investigated unreliable signal delivery during high-concurrency builds; mitigation merged (ocaml/dune#14047) while a broader C-stub self-pipe fix remains in draft
  • DockerHub opam versioning (ocaml/opam#6875): Martin Jambon raised confusion over images shipping opam 2.0.10; Anil Madhavapeddy explained that /usr/bin/opam targets the lowest supported release for test coverage breadth, while /usr/bin/opam- provides the latest; DockerHub description updated and issue closed
  • odoc @inline tag design (ocaml/odoc#564): Long-standing 2021 issue on inlining submodule expansions into the parent page revisited by Martin Jambon with concrete implementation ocaml/odoc#1408, reviving discussion on inline-by-default vs. opt-in behaviour

    • Emerging Trends

  • OxCaml ecosystem compatibility: OxCaml-related work appeared in both ocaml/dune (ocaml/dune#13981) and ocaml/odoc (ocaml/odoc#1407), with ocaml/merlin#2054 also ensuring forward compatibility with upcoming OCaml compiler changes, indicating a coordinated push across the toolchain
  • Windows parity in dune: Hardlink sandboxing enabled (ocaml/dune#13987), line-ending CI check added (ocaml/dune#14013), and Windows path-rewriting crash reproduction test added (ocaml/dune#13988); ocaml/dune#11161 continues tracking the full Windows package management story
  • Marshal-to-repr digest migration: Multi-PR effort in ocaml/dune (ocaml/dune#14015, ocaml/dune#14016, ocaml/dune#14025) replacing generic marshal-based digest functions with type-safe repr-derived ones; culminating PR ocaml/dune#14051 claims improved boot speed
  • Merlin indexer scalability: Two concurrent PRs (ocaml/merlin#2050, ocaml/merlin#2051) target ocaml-index from complementary directions — bounded memory via LRU eviction and reduced write volume via pointer-based index sharing — signaling a push to make the indexer viable for larger codebases
  • Wasm backend advancement in jsofocaml: Three correctness fixes merged this week (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2207, ocsigen/jsofocaml#2208, ocsigen/jsofocaml#2210) alongside large in-progress PRs for Dynlink/toplevel (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2187) and OCaml 5.5 support (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2195)
  • Relocatable compiler integration in dune: Following the merge of ocaml/dune#13321, issue ocaml/dune#14012 outlines the next step of preferring the relocatable compiler by default, reducing the need for toolchain rebuilds
  • Release process automation in dune: The backport script (ocaml/dune#13952), reusable revdep workflow (ocaml/dune#14014), and multi-target revdep fix (ocaml/dune#14024) reflect sustained investment in reducing manual release overhead

    • OxCaml

    47 PRs merged in oxcaml/oxcaml on staging/GADTs, new modes, static modules, and backend optimizations; Merlin synced with upstream.

    New Features

  • Abstract kinds with kind_ constraints completed the core abstract kinds feature set via oxcaml/oxcaml#5629, in advance of a formal announcement.
  • New write and writing modes were added in oxcaml/oxcaml#5608, and corrupted and corruptible modes (the contention/portability analogues) followed in oxcaml/oxcaml#5713, enabling cleaner mode implications without needing shared.
  • Static modules landed via oxcaml/oxcaml#5724 and the underlying static computation framework via oxcaml/oxcaml#5430.
  • Staging and GADTs became mostly sound together through the combined parts 1-3 PR oxcaml/oxcaml#5641, with stage tracking in Ctype across quotes/splices and exhaustive GADT tests.
  • Quotes of expansive expressions are now typed at mode once in oxcaml/oxcaml#5698, and top-level Pstr_eval expressions can be at mode once via oxcaml/oxcaml#5715.
  • Sound moding of quotes and splices with tests was merged via oxcaml/oxcaml#5697.
  • Type checking let poly_ landed in oxcaml/oxcaml#5513, with a companion PR adding val poly_ support opened as oxcaml/oxcaml#5755.
  • jkind annotation errors in quotes are now properly raised rather than silently dropped, with assertions added in Translquote via oxcaml/oxcaml#5674.
  • X86 peephole optimizations infrastructure was merged in oxcaml/oxcaml#5639, adding rules for dead-register removal and redundant comparison elimination.
  • New Lfor compilation strategy was introduced in oxcaml/oxcaml#5728.
  • IRC complexity threshold for register allocation was added in oxcaml/oxcaml#5705, allowing fallback to a simpler allocator for large functions.
  • -thunkify-compilation-unit-initialization flag added for wasmofocaml support in oxcaml/oxcaml#5720.
  • Atomic.make_contended was made to work on runtime4 in oxcaml/oxcaml#5640.
  • GC stat samples now record current minor words in oxcaml/oxcaml#5030.
  • Metaprogramming type support in Merlin's locate_types.ml: Tquote_eval is now represented via a Type_ref node pointing to Predef.path_eval, and Tquote recursively builds a type tree for staged expressions (oxcaml/merlin#228, oxcaml/merlin#230).
  • New mode documentation in Merlin for Write visibility and Writing statefulness modes, plus Observing renamed to Reading, contributed by Nailen Matschke (oxcaml/merlin#228).
  • New ignored compiler flags in Merlin's mconfig.ml: -requires-metaprogramming, -uses-metaprogramming, and five x86 peephole flags, preventing rejection of projects using upstream compiler options (oxcaml/merlin#228).
  • Bug fix: allocation size for recursive mixed blocks on bytecode corrected in oxcaml/oxcaml#5754, preventing segfaults with void fields.
  • Bug fix: tricky parallel Memprof bugs fixed in oxcaml/oxcaml#5600.
  • Bug fix: moregeneral now correctly regeneralizes layout vars on error via oxcaml/oxcaml#5691.
  • Performance: caml_modify calls reduced when writing parameterized unboxed records in oxcaml/oxcaml#5736.

    • Overview

  • oxcaml/oxcaml had the most activity with 47 merged PRs spanning language features (staging/GADTs, modes, static modules, abstract kinds), Flambda2/reaper improvements, backend codegen optimizations, and the ongoing OCaml 5.4 merge track.
  • oxcaml/merlin merged a large upstream sync from oxcaml/oxcaml@5.2.0minus-35 (oxcaml/merlin#228, ~27k additions across 131 files), with follow-up fixes for metaprogramming type handling (oxcaml/merlin#230) and an OCaml 5.4 upgrade PR opened (oxcaml/merlin#227).
  • oxcaml/opam-repository received one PR from Eduardo Souza to update the bootstrap compiler to OCaml 5.4.1 (oxcaml/opam-repository#36), keeping opam switch creation tooling current.
  • oxcaml/jsofocaml and janestreet/opam-repository had no recorded activity this week.

    • Activity

  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5774 proposes representing all-value/void mixed records and variants as uniform blocks, bumping mixed block version to v6 and removing the 254-value limit.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5738 proposes improved codegen for int comparisons using XOR before comparison and a better 3-way comparison lowering.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5746 proposes eliminating useless shifts in string/bytes indexed access.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5740 proposes duplicating comparisons in CFG block terminators for select/cmov.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5742 opens work on unwinding support via sframes.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5751 continues the n-way join work adding extra params for CSE-like variables at join points, a reloaded version of oxcaml/oxcaml#5733.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5753 uses constant propagation to rewrite CFG operations.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5743 adds a CFG pass to move instructions common to several blocks.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5761 proposes flipping the default for SPLIT_AROUND_LOOPS regalloc parameter, and oxcaml/oxcaml#5762 proposes enabling prologue shrink-wrap by default.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5734 adds initial aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu support in the dissector; related tracking issue oxcaml/oxcaml#5732 opened for arm64 Linux.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5747 fixes a bug involving effects, callbacks and locals.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5771 fixes a bug in meet for array element kinds in Flambda2.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5770 proposes using callback modules to emulate function specialisation in the patricia tree, targeting a ~1% compiler speedup.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5772 adds most missing primitives to fexpr to support full compiler/stdlib IR dumps.
  • Reaper cleanups merged: oxcaml/oxcaml#5764 (more intuitive -dreaper flag), oxcaml/oxcaml#5744 (remove {co,}field_{usages,sources}), oxcaml/oxcaml#5759 (add profile calls in solver), oxcaml/oxcaml#5731 (dep_solver reorganization).
  • The 5.4 merge track advanced with oxcaml/oxcaml#5765 (dynlink build tidy-up), oxcaml/oxcaml#5717 (make install progress), oxcaml/oxcaml#5711 (testsuite conflict resolution), oxcaml/oxcaml#5729 (5.4 merge miscellany), oxcaml/oxcaml#5694 (disable alerts in testsuite), and oxcaml/oxcaml#5534 (toplevel conflict resolution).
  • oxcaml/merlin#227 (opened by Liam Stevenson) upgrades Merlin to OCaml 5.4, requiring a move to ocamlformat 0.29.0 and touching 62 files.

    • Notable Discussions

  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5627 (Optimized Patricia trees): detailed debate between Basile Clément and @julesjacobs on specialising Set/Map vs. fixing compiler function specialisation, with benchmarks showing a ~5.7% full-repo speedup. Basile Clément opened oxcaml/oxcaml#5770 as an alternative using callback modules.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5733 / oxcaml/oxcaml#5751 (n-way join extra params): discussion between Basile Clément and Vincent Laviron on structuring the boundary between join analysis and join code generation, leading to the reloaded version with improved separation.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5641 (GADTs with staging): detailed review from Leo White covering closure allocations, exception handling in environment traversals, and the fragility of stage tracking in error messages; a ticket was created to track accurate stage information in error traces.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#3181 (Missed CSE opportunity): updated with a new reproducer found during investigation of oxcaml/oxcaml#5691, noting that oxcaml/oxcaml#5733 addresses it via the n-way join.
  • oxcaml/merlin#228 (Upstream sync review): Jakub Bachurski identified that the Tquote_eval handling in ptyp_of_type was incorrect and provided the correct representation, promptly addressed in oxcaml/merlin#230; the PR also called out that Tquote_eval and Tpat_fun_layout changes warrant expert review from metaprogramming and layout polymorphism specialists.

    • Emerging Trends

  • Staging and metaprogramming system maturing rapidly: GADTs, local constraints, sound moding, and jkind assertions all landed in a single week (oxcaml/oxcaml#5641, oxcaml/oxcaml#5697, oxcaml/oxcaml#5698, oxcaml/oxcaml#5674), forming a coherent prototype; Tquote/Tquote_eval type forms are now appearing across multiple analysis modules in Merlin (oxcaml/merlin#228).
  • Modes system expansion: write/writing (oxcaml/oxcaml#5608) and corrupted/corruptible (oxcaml/oxcaml#5713) modes fill gaps in mode implications; a full mode polymorphism system is in draft in oxcaml/oxcaml#5483 and oxcaml/oxcaml#5478; mode documentation is being extended in Merlin in parallel (oxcaml/merlin#228).
  • Backend codegen improvements accumulating: X86 peephole optimizations (oxcaml/oxcaml#5639), improved int comparison lowering (oxcaml/oxcaml#5738), CFG duplicate comparisons (oxcaml/oxcaml#5740), prologue shrink-wrap (oxcaml/oxcaml#5762), and constant propagation in CFG (oxcaml/oxcaml#5753) are all in flight concurrently.
  • Flambda2 reaper systematic cleanup: architectural reorganization removing redundant state, adding profiling, and restructuring rules (oxcaml/oxcaml#5764, oxcaml/oxcaml#5744, oxcaml/oxcaml#5759, oxcaml/oxcaml#5731) in preparation for broader enablement.
  • Merlin upstream sync maintenance burden: each oxcaml/oxcaml release requires Merlin to handle new type constructors (quote/splice, layout patterns) and add new compiler flags to its allowlist (oxcaml/merlin#228); an OCaml 5.4 upgrade is also needed (oxcaml/merlin#227).
  • 5.4 merge track advancing steadily: multiple conflict-resolution and testsuite promotion PRs land each week in oxcaml/oxcaml, with the bootstrap compiler version in oxcaml/opam-repository being updated in parallel (oxcaml/opam-repository#36) to keep opam tooling current.

    • OCaml Core

    Bytecode fixes, stdlib additions, and a Pphyscomp optimisation landed in ocaml/ocaml; ocaml/RFCs revived the implicit source positions design debate.

    New Features

  • Dynarray.ofiarray and Dynarray.toiarray added to the standard library, enabling O(n) round-trips between dynamic and immutable arrays.
  • ocaml/ocaml#13588 merged after a long review: physical comparison operators (== and !=) now propagate as a distinct Pphyscomp primitive to the lambda IR, enabling backends such as jsofocaml to emit semantically correct code for these operators.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14692 relaxed record update syntax so that { (Gc.get ()) with ... } no longer requires surrounding parentheses around function application expressions.
  • s390x CFI (Call Frame Information) debug metadata improved via ocaml/ocaml#14500, adding a cfi_val_offset emission helper and GDB regression tests.
  • The PUSHENVACC4 bytecode opcode, silently never emitted due to an off-by-one in the peephole optimiser, is now correctly generated following ocaml/ocaml#14534.

    • Overview

  • ocaml/ocaml had a productive week: five PRs merged covering stdlib additions (ocaml/ocaml#14693), bytecode correctness (ocaml/ocaml#14534, ocaml/ocaml#14641), lambda optimisation (ocaml/ocaml#13588), and parser relaxation (ocaml/ocaml#14692).
  • ocaml/RFCs saw renewed activity on ocaml/RFCs#52 (implicit source positions) after approximately a year of inactivity, with a proposal to resolve the stalled design debate via a caml-devel meeting.
  • A CVE (CVE-2026-34353) was assigned for the Bigarray.reshape overflow reported in ocaml/ocaml#14655.
  • Several new PRs were opened addressing libunix thread-safety (ocaml/ocaml#14715), typing error hints (ocaml/ocaml#14695), and ocamltest infrastructure (ocaml/ocaml#14713).

    • Activity

  • ocaml/ocaml#14715 opened by Antonin Décimo to fix NULL-dereference bugs in POSIX thread-safe libunix functions (getgrnam_r and related wrappers), with a cherry-pick request for OCaml 5.5.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14713 by Gabriel Scherer proposes a new cold ocamltest action for tests disabled on CI by default but still run on developer machines.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14710 by Florian Angeletti extends package type syntax to accept with type t = int with type x = float as a synonym for with type t = int and type x = float.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14712 by Stefan Muenzel proposes an all-in-one expect test runner executing normal, -principal, and -rectypes checks in a single process with state reset.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14707 by Florian Angeletti enables REPL tracing of module-dependent functions (#trace show;; now works for modular explicit arguments).
  • ocaml/ocaml#14709 by Florian Angeletti proposes changing ocamldoc HTML page titles from Library name : Module_name to Module_name (Library name).
  • ocaml/ocaml#14703 by @hhugo fixes swapped None/Some branches in dll.ml when upgrading a DLL entry from Checking to Execution mode.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14702 by @hhugo merged: fixes a Load_path.add bug where files from a second hidden directory with overlapping basenames could leak into the visible files table.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14695 by Stefan Muenzel adds an actionable hint to the GADT scope-escape error message pointing users toward type annotations and the manual.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14642 by Gabriel Scherer merged: the runtime now silently skips caml_shutdown cleanup when unjoined domains remain rather than segfaulting; superseded PR ocaml/ocaml#14614 was closed.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14641 moved opnames.ml.c and opnames.mli from tools/ into bytecomp/ to resolve a dependency ordering issue.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14690 by cui fixed an ambiguous type path expansion bug in error trace reporting.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14241 by Xavier Van de Woestyne (Merlin typing recovery upstreaming) received an active review round, with Thomas Refis approving the overall structure.
  • ocaml/RFCs#52 (implicit source positions) saw renewed discussion after approximately a year of silence, with Olivier Nicole summarizing outstanding design questions and Nicolás Ojeda Bär proposing a caml-devel meeting to break the deadlock.

    • Notable Discussions

  • ocaml/ocaml#14580 on GC for continuations saw a new proposal: rather than discontinue-ing unreachable continuations from finalisers, a first step could free fiber stack memory only, with an optional explicit Gc.flush() API for users needing finalisation at a known point.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14668 by Nathan Rebours requesting new extension point entries in the OCaml AST to aid ppxlib's frozen-AST strategy received a constructive response from Nicolás Ojeda Bär, who suggested opening a concrete PR ahead of an upcoming developer meeting.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14676 on preventing shell injection in GitHub Actions workflows is stalled: environment variable names conflict with GitHub's own reserved names (e.g., GITHUB_REF_NAME), complicating the security fix.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14594 on parallel test segfaults in cleanup-at-exit mode continued: Gabriel Scherer traced a race condition in ephetest_par where domains can deadlock waiting on ephemerons, reproduced reliably by enabling GC verbose logging.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14655 on overflow in Bigarray.reshape now has CVE-2026-34353 assigned.
  • ocaml/RFCs#52 implicit source positions: the unresolved design question is whether call-site positions should use Lexing.position (option 1) or a richer location type (option 2b); Olivier Nicole argues for 2b with option 1 only if performance concerns are demonstrated.

    • Emerging Trends

  • The runtime team is working through several multicore-specific correctness issues concurrently: continuation memory leaks (ocaml/ocaml#14580), cleanup-at-exit races (ocaml/ocaml#14642), and ephemeron GC liveness (ocaml/ocaml#14594).
  • Multiple bytecode-related fixes landed in the same week (ocaml/ocaml#14534, ocaml/ocaml#14641, ocaml/ocaml#13588), reflecting increased attention to the bytecode backend's correctness and its use as a compilation target by tools such as jsofocaml.
  • The ppxlib ecosystem is pushing for upstream changes to ease long-term AST stability, with ocaml/ocaml#14668 opening a formal discussion track.
  • Long-stalled RFCs with prior design consensus are being revived via structured meetings rather than async PR discussion, as seen with ocaml/RFCs#52 after approximately a year of inactivity.

    • Multicore

    Activity confined to eio: configurable eventfd/pipe backend parameters added; two open issues received discussion.

    New Features

  • Configurable eventfd creation in the ocaml-multicore/eio Linux backend: run_event_loop and run in lib_eio_linux now accept an optional ?eventfd parameter, allowing callers to supply a custom function for creating event file descriptors (ocaml-multicore/eio#836)
  • Configurable pipe creation in the Posix backend: lib_eio_posix domain manager and scheduler now accept an optional ?pipe parameter, enabling callers to control how pipes are created — useful for shells that need to move FDs to higher numbers (e.g. dash savefd pattern) (ocaml-multicore/eio#836)

    • Overview

  • Activity this week was limited to ocaml-multicore/eio; all other repositories (domainslib, ocaml-uring, meio, saturn, eio-trace, picos, kcas, ocaml-iomux) had no recorded commits or discussions
  • One new PR was opened in eio (ocaml-multicore/eio#836) making Linux and Posix backend event FD creation configurable, affecting 8 files (35 additions, 26 deletions)
  • Two pre-existing issues received follow-up discussion: ocaml-multicore/eio#835 (Path.load race condition) and ocaml-multicore/eio#382 (lock-free waiters)
  • Contributors this week: Patrick Ferris, Thomas Leonard, Volker Diels-Grabsch

    • Activity

  • Patrick Ferris opened ocaml-multicore/eio#836 Make Linux and Posix eventfd functions configurable, currently unmerged, to support shells like msh that need to relocate FDs to higher numbers
  • Thomas Leonard commented on ocaml-multicore/eio#382 Make Waiters lock-free, noting that part of the referenced algorithm is already in use via cells.mli
  • Volker Diels-Grabsch filed ocaml-multicore/eio#835 documenting silent truncation in Eio.Path.load on race conditions and empty results for /proc virtual files; Patrick Ferris noted overlap with ocaml-multicore/eio#798 and proposed splitting the concerns into separate issues

    • Notable Discussions

  • Volker Diels-Grabsch reported in ocaml-multicore/eio#835 that Eio.Path.load uses file size as an exact buffer bound rather than a hint, causing silent truncation under race conditions and returning empty strings for /proc virtual files; Patrick Ferris acknowledged overlap with ocaml-multicore/eio#798 and suggested splitting the race condition concern into a dedicated issue
  • Thomas Leonard noted on ocaml-multicore/eio#382 that the cells.mli module already implements part of the lock-free waiter design described in the referenced Kotlin coroutines paper, updating the status of that long-running design discussion

    • Emerging Trends

  • Backend extensibility for system-level tools: ocaml-multicore/eio#836 reflects a pattern where shell authors and low-level tool writers need hooks into how Eio creates internal file descriptors, pointing toward a broader need for configurable backend primitives
  • Eio.Path.load correctness for virtual filesystems: both ocaml-multicore/eio#835 and ocaml-multicore/eio#798 highlight that Path.load's stat-then-read approach is unsuitable for virtual filesystems (e.g. /proc) and concurrent environments, suggesting a fix is becoming a priority
entry.summary: Dune 3.22.1 released; OxCaml merged 47 PRs on staging/GADTs, new modes, static modules; ocaml/ocaml landed 5 PRs with Dynarray conversions and Pphyscomp.

entry.title: Week 13, 2026: OCaml 5.5 alpha3 landed; OxCaml saw 33 merges on metaprogramming and modes; dune gained directory diffing and promote improvements.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

Compiler (ocaml/ocaml)
- OCaml Core DWARF CFI support for the POWER backend merged, bringing backtrace and GDB debugger/profiler support to the last native backend missing it (ocaml/ocaml#14482) by Tim McGilchrist, reviewed by Xavier Leroy
- OCaml Core Application warnings for modular explicit functions — partial application, over-application, and unused argument warnings now enabled for Tfunctor types (ocaml/ocaml#14667) by Florian Angeletti
- OCaml Core Class type system improvements merged (rebase of ocaml/ocaml#12150 by Leo White), fixing long-standing OO type system issues (ocaml/ocaml#14680) by Florian Angeletti
- OCaml Core Dynarray.{of,to}_iarray adds conversions between Dynarray and iarray (immutable arrays) with a single-copy implementation (ocaml/ocaml#14693) by Olivier Nicole
- OCaml Core prefetchw always emitted on x86/x86_64, removing the need for the -mprfchw compiler flag (ocaml/ocaml#14665) by Antonin Décimo
- OCaml Core type_let refactored into type_let_nonrec and type_let_rec, a prerequisite for future improvements to recursive-binding typing (ocaml/ocaml#14394) by Alistair

OxCaml (oxcaml/oxcaml)
- OxCaml Gc.Memprof.participate_globally added to the standard library, enabling memory profiling participation across all domains; participate renamed to enlist (oxcaml/oxcaml#5644)
- OxCaml Sound kinding of quotes and splices — the metaprogramming system now enforces correct kinding rules at quote and splice boundaries, with new Modes module in camlinternalQuote.mli (oxcaml/oxcaml#5636)
- OxCaml Mode annotations under quotes now supported, allowing mode annotations inside quoted expressions (oxcaml/oxcaml#5670)
- OxCaml New compiler flags -requires-metaprogramming and -uses-metaprogramming added, enabling the compiler to track and enforce metaprogramming dependencies (oxcaml/oxcaml#5544)
- OxCaml eval made a regular function — the metaprogramming eval extension point replaced with a standard function call, simplifying implementation across 66 files (oxcaml/oxcaml#5657)
- OxCaml External modalities in with-bounds — the type system now supports external modality constraints in with-bound expressions (oxcaml/oxcaml#5601)
- OxCaml observing mode renamed to reading across the codebase and documentation (oxcaml/oxcaml#5712)
- OxCaml ARM64 instruction sizes derived robustly — replaces fragile hardcoded sizes with derived measurements; relax_poll, relax_allocation, relax_condbranch, relax_branch separated as distinct functions (oxcaml/oxcaml#5499)
- OxCaml x86 LEA instruction used for add/sub with immediates, improving code generation quality (oxcaml/oxcaml#5695)
- OxCaml Register allocation interference edges now added between multiple outputs of the same instruction (oxcaml/oxcaml#5706)
- OxCaml -linscan flag silently ignored by Merlin, preventing errors when projects pass this flag (oxcaml/merlin#226) by Liam Stevenson

Build Tools (dune, opam, jsofocaml)

  • dune: Directory diffing in diff actions (ocaml/dune#13880): the diff stanza now supports diffing entire directories (requires lang dune 3.23), closing a request open since 2018 (ocaml/dune#3567)

  • dune: Sandboxed rule corrections (ocaml/dune#13813): sandboxed actions can produce promotable .corrected files when (corrections produce) is set
  • dune: dune clean path arguments (ocaml/dune#13875): dune clean now accepts path arguments to remove specific targets from _build
  • dune: --debug-backtraces flag added to dune promote, dune cache, and dune trace subcommands (ocaml/dune#13933)
  • dune: Minimum OCaml version raised to 4.14 (ocaml/dune#13533): drops accumulated compatibility shims for Either, Val_none, Array.find_opt, String, and boot stdlib modules

  • jsofocaml: Optional chaining in JS runtime (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2202): caml_wrap_exception and caml_current_dir updated to use ?. for more robust null-safety checks

    • OxCaml

    33 merges in oxcaml/oxcaml covering metaprogramming soundness, mode system expansion, backend fixes; Merlin gained -linscan support.

    New Features

  • Gc.Memprof.participate_globally added to the standard library, enabling memory profiling participation across all domains; the existing participate function was renamed to enlist and the new function surfaces as enlist_all_domains in the public API (oxcaml/oxcaml#5644)
  • Sound kinding of quotes and splices — the metaprogramming system now enforces correct kinding rules at quote and splice boundaries, with camlinternalQuote.mli gaining a new Modes module (legacy, of_string_list) and Type.arrow accepting two extra Modes.t arguments (oxcaml/oxcaml#5636)
  • Mode annotations under quotes are now supported, allowing programmers to annotate modes inside quoted expressions; related changes in Pat.constraint_ and Type_constraint.constraint_ in camlinternalQuote.mli (oxcaml/oxcaml#5670)
  • New compiler flags -requires-metaprogramming and -uses-metaprogramming added to driver/main_args.mli, along with a new ui_requires_metaprogramming field in cmx_format.mli unit info structures, enabling the compiler to track and enforce metaprogramming dependencies (oxcaml/oxcaml#5544)
  • eval made a regular function — the metaprogramming eval extension point was replaced with a standard function call, removing the special-case extension point syntax and simplifying the implementation across 66 files (oxcaml/oxcaml#5657)
  • External modalities in with-bounds — the type system now supports external modality constraints in with-bound expressions, expanding the expressiveness of the modes system (oxcaml/oxcaml#5601)
  • observing mode renamed to reading across the codebase and documentation, aligning the mode name with its intended semantics (oxcaml/oxcaml#5712)
  • ARM64 instruction sizes derived robustly — a comprehensive rework replaces fragile hardcoded sizes with derived measurements; Instruction.max_displacement added; relax_poll, relax_allocation, relax_condbranch, relax_branch separated as distinct functions (oxcaml/oxcaml#5499)
  • x86 LEA instruction used for add/sub with immediates — the x86 backend now emits lea for additions and subtractions with immediate operands, improving code generation quality (oxcaml/oxcaml#5695)
  • Register allocation interference edges now added between multiple outputs of the same instruction, preventing incorrect register assignments for instructions that produce multiple results (oxcaml/oxcaml#5706)
  • ~level parameter removed from the jkind comparison and violation API (Jkind.compare, Jkind.check_sub, etc.), simplifying call sites throughout the type checker (oxcaml/oxcaml#5615)
  • -linscan flag silently ignored by Merlin — added to Merlin's list of ignored OCaml compiler flags in src/kernel/mconfig.ml, preventing Merlin from erroring when projects pass this linear scan register allocator flag (oxcaml/merlin#226)

  • Activity this week was concentrated in oxcaml/oxcaml (33 merges, ~30 new PRs opened) and oxcaml/merlin (1 PR merged); oxcaml/opam-repository, oxcaml/jsofocaml, and janestreet/opam-repository had no recorded activity
  • The dominant theme in oxcaml/oxcaml was metaprogramming soundness — four PRs merged fixing quote/splice kinding (oxcaml/oxcaml#5636), mode annotations (oxcaml/oxcaml#5670), eval semantics (oxcaml/oxcaml#5657), and jkind annotation safety (oxcaml/oxcaml#5685)
  • Mode system expansion continued with the observing→reading rename (oxcaml/oxcaml#5712) merged and three new mode pairs opened: write/writing (oxcaml/oxcaml#5608), corrupted/corruptable (oxcaml/oxcaml#5713), poisoned/poisoning (oxcaml/oxcaml#5666)
  • Flambda2 reaper reliability improved with three bug fixes merged: exception parameter deletion (oxcaml/oxcaml#5563), uses/sources deadlock (oxcaml/oxcaml#5648), and stamp debug printing (oxcaml/oxcaml#5700)
  • 5.4 upstream merge is in sustained progress across stdlib, runtime, ocamltest, and debugger subsystems (oxcaml/oxcaml#5692, oxcaml/oxcaml#5693, oxcaml/oxcaml#5598, oxcaml/oxcaml#5711, oxcaml/oxcaml#5717)
  • Backend code quality: ARM64 instruction size derivation reworked (oxcaml/oxcaml#5499), x86 LEA emission improved (oxcaml/oxcaml#5695), register allocation interference edges fixed (oxcaml/oxcaml#5706), CFG merge block predecessors corrected (oxcaml/oxcaml#5708)
