  • New codegen and compiler infrastructure PRs opened: CFG SSA reconstruction by @ttebbi-janestreet (oxcaml/oxcaml#5722), new Lfor compilation strategy by Mark Shinwell (oxcaml/oxcaml#5728), -thunkify-compilation-unit-initialization flag by James Rayman (oxcaml/oxcaml#5720), static modules by Jack Rickard (oxcaml/oxcaml#5724), codegen examples for materialized bits (oxcaml/oxcaml#5727)
  • 5.4 upstream merge work continues: labeled tuples support (oxcaml/oxcaml#5692), Stdlib iarray (oxcaml/oxcaml#5693), make install for OxCaml 5.4 (oxcaml/oxcaml#5717), testsuite conflicts (oxcaml/oxcaml#5711), and runtime merge (oxcaml/oxcaml#5598); completed merges include stdlib conflicts (oxcaml/oxcaml#5616), ocamltest (oxcaml/oxcaml#5605), debugger (oxcaml/oxcaml#5617), and miscellany (oxcaml/oxcaml#5729)
  • Reaper correctness: three fixes merged by Nathanaëlle Courant — exception parameter deletion bug (oxcaml/oxcaml#5563), deadlock between uses and sources computation with local fields (oxcaml/oxcaml#5648), and value slot stamp printing suppression (oxcaml/oxcaml#5700); reaper testcase for oxcaml/oxcaml#5633 added (oxcaml/oxcaml#5682) and coaccessor/coconstructor renames (oxcaml/oxcaml#5681)
  • Flambda2 continuation lifting improved: fix preventing lifting of continuations that may refer to non-lifted continuations by Guillaume Bury (oxcaml/oxcaml#5689), and a fix for unbound variables in lifted constants by Vincent Laviron (oxcaml/oxcaml#5725), superseding the earlier approach in oxcaml/oxcaml#5719
  • n-way join improvements: missing-cmx variable scoping fix by Basile Clément (oxcaml/oxcaml#5679), follow-on PR using untagged const false for nullability detection (oxcaml/oxcaml#5718) opened; related issue oxcaml/oxcaml#5721 reporting missing CSE with n-way join
  • Sort and jkind type system cleanup: generic sort variable simplification by Zesen Qian (oxcaml/oxcaml#5704), Jkind.Sort.new_var return type corrected (oxcaml/oxcaml#5658), parameter vs return mode fix (oxcaml/oxcaml#5596)
  • Slambda fracturing initial implementation merged — adds the simplest slambda fracturing pass by Jack Rickard (oxcaml/oxcaml#5544)
  • CI and build fixes: dune pinned to 3.20.2 in CI (oxcaml/oxcaml#5684), Dune 3.22 compatibility fix (oxcaml/oxcaml#5686), missing compiler-libs-installation.sexp entries added (oxcaml/oxcaml#5709), macOS compilation fix opened by Amethyst Shen (oxcaml/oxcaml#5714)
  • Ongoing abstract kinds work by Chris Casinghino: with kind_ constraints part 3 (oxcaml/oxcaml#5629) and tests for is_really_poly in typecore (oxcaml/oxcaml#5730)
  • Ongoing mode polymorphism work by @ainageorges: functional mode polymorphism (oxcaml/oxcaml#5483), alloc mode (oxcaml/oxcaml#5482), copy operation (oxcaml/oxcaml#5481), normal form morphisms (oxcaml/oxcaml#5453), and printing of polymorphic mode variables (oxcaml/oxcaml#5488)
  • Multicore module domain lifetime fix merged — joining domains could block indefinitely waiting for the ticker thread; domain.mli alert text updated by Vesa Karvonen (oxcaml/oxcaml#5638)
  • oxcaml/merlin: Liam Stevenson opened, authored, and merged oxcaml/merlin#226, adding -linscan to the ignored compiler flags list in src/kernel/mconfig.ml

    • Notable Discussions

  • Zero-alloc function arguments (oxcaml/oxcaml#5493) received the most review activity this week — Chris Casinghino posted extensive comments covering Tpoly node handling, is_really_poly correctness, filter_arrow interactions, the distinction between Zero_alloc.check option and Zero_alloc.t, and translcore complications; the PR by Andrej Ivašković remains open pending resolution
  • unique implies uncontended (oxcaml/oxcaml#5716) prompted theoretical discussion between @julesjacobs and Leo White on lattice structure for the modes system — specifically whether aliased => contended should be modeled as a general mechanism, how normal forms interact with fixpoints in mode operators, and whether this belongs as a jkind axis
  • Tick thread in runtime (oxcaml/oxcaml#5349) continued review by Max Slater covering threading model correctness, non-blocking syscall safety, locking discipline, and interval timer accuracy for preemptive scheduling
  • Preemption (oxcaml/oxcaml#4881) saw discussion between Aspen Smith and Stephen Dolan on GC-safe stack frame traversal during preemption
  • raise instead of dropping jkind annotations in quotes (oxcaml/oxcaml#5674) discussion on how the compiler should handle jkind annotations inside quoted expressions, leading to the merged fix in oxcaml/oxcaml#5685

    • Emerging Trends

  • Metaprogramming soundness hardening is a clear focus: four PRs merged fixing quote/splice kinding (oxcaml/oxcaml#5636), mode annotations in quotes (oxcaml/oxcaml#5670), eval semantics (oxcaml/oxcaml#5657), and jkind annotation safety (oxcaml/oxcaml#5685), with four more PRs opened extending the same area (oxcaml/oxcaml#5697, oxcaml/oxcaml#5698, oxcaml/oxcaml#5715, oxcaml/oxcaml#5641)
  • Mode system vocabulary expansion: three new mode pairs introduced — write/writing (oxcaml/oxcaml#5608), corrupted/corruptable (oxcaml/oxcaml#5713), poisoned/poisoning (oxcaml/oxcaml#5666) — on top of the observing→reading rename (oxcaml/oxcaml#5712); the mode lattice is actively evolving with theoretical debate on implications such as unique implies uncontended (oxcaml/oxcaml#5716)
  • Backend code quality sustained attention: ARM64 instruction size derivation (oxcaml/oxcaml#5499), x86 LEA usage (oxcaml/oxcaml#5695), register allocation interference (oxcaml/oxcaml#5706), CFG SSA reconstruction (oxcaml/oxcaml#5722), x86 peephole optimizations ongoing (oxcaml/oxcaml#5639), and optimization fuel bisection (oxcaml/oxcaml#5651)
  • Flambda2 reaper reliability: three fixes merged in one week (oxcaml/oxcaml#5563, oxcaml/oxcaml#5648, oxcaml/oxcaml#5700) alongside continuation lifting fixes (oxcaml/oxcaml#5689, oxcaml/oxcaml#5725), suggesting the reaper is in active hardening phase
  • 5.4 upstream merge in sustained progress with dedicated contributors (David Allsopp, Simon Spies, Nick Barnes) working through stdlib, runtime, toplevel, ocamltest, and debugger subsystems in parallel (oxcaml/oxcaml#5692, oxcaml/oxcaml#5693, oxcaml/oxcaml#5598, oxcaml/oxcaml#5711, oxcaml/oxcaml#5717)
  • Merlin compiler flag synchronization: the -linscan fix (oxcaml/merlin#226) highlights a recurring maintenance need to keep Merlin's ignored compiler flags list current with upstream OCaml compiler flags, with intent to add systematic testing to catch similar gaps

    • OCaml Core

    10 PRs merged in ocaml/ocaml: GC ephemeron revert/re-fix, POWER CFI, type system improvements, and testsuite speedups.

    New Features

  • ocaml/ocaml#14482: DWARF CFI support for the POWER backend, bringing backtraces and GDB debugger/profiler support to the last native backend missing them. By Tim McGilchrist, reviewed by Xavier Leroy.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14667: Application warnings for modular explicit (module-dependent) functions — partial application, over-application, and unused argument warnings now enabled for Tfunctor types. By Florian Angeletti, reviewed by Gabriel Scherer.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14680: Class type system improvements (rebase of ocaml/ocaml#12150 by Leo White) — fixes long-standing issues in the OO type system. Rebased and merged by Florian Angeletti.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14394: Refactor type_let into type_let_nonrec and type_let_rec — prerequisite for future improvements to recursive-binding typing. By Alistair, reviewed by Samuel Vivien.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14693: Dynarray.{of,to}_iarray — adds conversions between Dynarray and iarray (immutable arrays) with a single-copy implementation. By Olivier Nicole, approved by Gabriel Scherer.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14665: Always emit prefetchw on x86/x86_64, removing the need for the -mprfchw compiler flag. By Antonin Décimo.

    • Overview

  • Activity this week was concentrated in ocaml/ocaml; ocaml/RFCs had no recorded activity.
  • 10 PRs merged in ocaml/ocaml with 33 files changed (1018 insertions, 393 deletions).
  • Key themes: GC correctness (ephemeron race condition diagnosed, reverted via ocaml/ocaml#14682, and re-attempted via ocaml/ocaml#14688), type-system infrastructure, and architecture backend completeness.
  • 17+ contributors active; Gabriel Scherer authored or co-reviewed 5 merged PRs.
  • Notable open work: GC for continuations (ocaml/ocaml#14580) and a security-relevant Bigarray overflow fix (ocaml/ocaml#14691) pending review.

    • Activity

    Merged PRs:
    - ocaml/ocaml#14680: Class type system improvements (rebase of ocaml/ocaml#12150) — 359 additions, 189 deletions. By Florian Angeletti.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14689: Cosmetic ocamltest refactorings — 38 additions, 32 deletions. By Gabriel Scherer.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14394: Refactor type_let into type_let_nonrec and type_let_rec — 376 additions, 211 deletions. By Alistair.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14684: Clean up ocamlopt man page — 97 additions, 66 deletions. By @shym, reviewed by Florian Angeletti.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14665: Always emit prefetchw on x86/x8664 — 56 additions, 4 deletions. By Antonin Décimo.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14482: CFI support for POWER architecture — 171 additions, 18 deletions. By Tim McGilchrist.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14683: Fix memory-model tests default test size. By Gabriel Scherer.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14681: Speed up lazy/lazy5.ml test from 10s to 0.1s. By Gabriel Scherer.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14682: Revert ephemeron PR ocaml/ocaml#14657 (race condition introduced). By Gabriel Scherer.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14667: Modular explicits: enable application warnings — 222 additions, 15 deletions. By Florian Angeletti.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14669: Allow Config.is_official_release to change without bootstrap. By David Allsopp.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14662: Correct order of compiler flags in ocamltest. By David Allsopp.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14678: Fix test for ocaml/ocaml#14380 (reservedheader_bits config variable). By Damien Doligez.

    Open PRs with notable activity:
    - ocaml/ocaml#14688: Revised ephemeron optimization (without the race condition) — under review.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14580: GC for continuations (draft) — infrastructure for automatically finalising dropped effects continuations. By KC Sivaramakrishnan.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14673: Keep expansion 5.4 (rebase of ocaml/ocaml#11648) — ecosystem testing revealing type-checker bugs in ppxlib and base_quickcheck.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14692: Syntax proposal: unparenthesized applications in record update syntax. By Stephen Dolan.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14691: Bigarray overflow fix in caml_ba_reshape — security relevant, candidate for backport to 4.14. By Stephen Dolan.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14695: Add hint about type annotations for GADT equation scope escapes. By Stefan Muenzel.

    Closed without merge:
    - ocaml/ocaml#14674: Bigarray 4.14 backport superseded by better fix in ocaml/ocaml#14691.
    - ocaml/ocaml#10286: Array.unsafe_blit PR closed after 5 years of inactivity.
    - ocaml/ocaml#14672: Automated shell-injection PR superseded by ocaml/ocaml#14676.

    Notable Discussions

  • Minor heap size defaults (ocaml/ocaml#14634): Gabriel Scherer argues the 256KW (2MiB) default, unchanged since 2011, is too conservative for modern hardware; benchmarks show up to 3x speedup with s=32M on allocation-heavy programs. Stephen Dolan supports increasing the default (Jane Street has used 8MiB since 2017) but cautions against over-interpreting synthetic benchmarks.
  • GC for continuations (ocaml/ocaml#14580): KC Sivaramakrishnan proposes automatically finalising dropped effects continuations for resource cleanup; debate about whether this encourages treating Fun.protect finalizers as GC finalizers (~2% overhead on chameneos benchmark).
  • Extension points in the OCaml AST for ppxlib (ocaml/ocaml#14668): Nathan Rebours proposes adding extension point placeholders to more AST positions (especially type_declaration) so ppxlib can encode new language features without ppx breakage.
  • Ephemeron race condition (ocaml/ocaml#14679): Gabriel Scherer diagnosed a race in ocaml/ocaml#14657 where num_domains_to_mark was decremented before ephe_next_round() was called, causing major GC deadlock in multi-domain programs. The PR was reverted (ocaml/ocaml#14682) and a fixed version (ocaml/ocaml#14688) proposed.
  • keep-expansion type-checker PR (ocaml/ocaml#14673): Ecosystem testing of ocaml/ocaml#11648 (Jacques Garrigue's multi-year type-checker correctness fix) revealed an "Unbound record field" in ppxlib and a Ctype.Unify exception in base_quickcheck.
  • Segfaults in cleanup-at-exit mode (ocaml/ocaml#14594): Ongoing debate on whether caml_shutdown should cancel unjoined domains; Stephen Dolan argues the cleanup-at-exit mode has both false positives and false negatives and should be deleted.

    • Emerging Trends

  • Ephemeron performance and correctness: A full cycle of merge, revert (ocaml/ocaml#14682), and re-attempt (ocaml/ocaml#14688) of ephemeron GC optimization illustrates the difficulty of concurrent GC modifications; the fix targets a quadratic blowup affecting the Rocq proof assistant's evar map use case.
  • Type-checker infrastructure overhaul: Multiple interrelated PRs (ocaml/ocaml#14394, ocaml/ocaml#14538, ocaml/ocaml#14517) by Alistair systematically refactor type_let and type_approx to enable correct handling of polymorphic recursive bindings — groundwork for fixing ocaml/ocaml#14253.
  • keep-expansion type correctness (ocaml/ocaml#11648 / ocaml/ocaml#14673): Jacques Garrigue's multi-year effort to fix principality and non-termination bugs via Texpand type nodes is approaching merger, with ecosystem testing now revealing integration issues in ppxlib and base_quickcheck.
  • CI robustness and testsuite speed: Gabriel Scherer merged multiple PRs reducing testsuite runtime (ocaml/ocaml#14681: lazy5.ml 10s→0.1s; ocaml/ocaml#14683: memory-model tests 7s→2s).
  • Architecture backend completeness: POWER CFI support (ocaml/ocaml#14482) completes native debugger support across all supported architectures; s390x CFI fix (ocaml/ocaml#14500) also pending.
  • ppxlib/compiler interface evolution: Discussion on ocaml/ocaml#14668 reflects ongoing coordination between ppxlib (moving to a frozen AST model) and the compiler team.

    • Multicore

    Quiet week across the multicore group; only eio saw activity, with discussion of a race condition in Eio.Path.load.

    Overview

  • Activity this week was limited to ocaml-multicore/eio; all other repositories (domainslib, ocaml-uring, meio, saturn, eio-trace, picos, kcas, ocaml-iomux) had no recorded activity.
  • The sole active thread was ocaml-multicore/eio#835, a bug report on a race condition in Eio.Path.load that also surfaces as a functional failure when reading /proc virtual files.

    • Activity

  • ocaml-multicore/eio#835 received a follow-up comment during the week adding background reading on /proc file semantics, keeping the discussion active ahead of a potential fix.
  • The bug arises because Eio.Path.load uses the result of stat to size its read buffer: if the file shrinks between stat and read, truncated data is returned silently; if it grows, data beyond the initial allocation is lost.
  • /proc virtual files report size 0 at stat time, causing Eio.Path.load to return an empty string for files such as /proc/sys/fs/file-nr.
  • The proposed fix is to treat the stat size only as an initial buffer-sizing hint and otherwise read to completion, matching the behaviour of Eio.Path.with_open_in path Eio.Flow.read_all.

    • Notable Discussions

  • Volker Diels-Grabsch filed and developed ocaml-multicore/eio#835, providing a reproducer, a root-cause analysis of the stat-before-read race, and a concrete fix strategy; a follow-up comment during the week added further context on /proc file behaviour.
entry.summary: OCaml 5.5 alpha3 landed; OxCaml saw 33 merges on metaprogramming and modes; dune gained directory diffing and promote improvements.

entry.title: Week 12, 2026: Dune 3.22.0 stable released; OCaml 4.14.3 LTS security patch (CVE-2026-28364); compiler gains Atomic.Array and List combinators.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Tools Dune 3.22.0 shipped @revdep, @revdep-check, and @revdep-runtest aliases (ocaml/dune#13800) for building reverse dependencies, plus dune promote path-prefix and --file filtering (ocaml/dune#13876) and custom action trace events with a new dune-action-trace library.
  • OCaml Tools ocaml-lsp 1.26.0-5.5~preview released with a new destruct custom LSP request (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1583), environment-variable build-system configuration ($OCAMLLSP_PROJECT_BUILD_SYSTEM, $OCAMLLSP_PROJECT_ROOT), and improved signature-help readability (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1580).
  • OCaml Tools opam gained PowerShell tab-completions via a cmdliner 2.1.0 update (ocaml/opam#6869 by Brian Ward), replacing the previous bash/zsh-only approach and closing ocaml/opam#6853 and the long-standing ocaml/opam#684.
  • OCaml Tools jsofocaml variable coalescing (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2166) reduces V8 register usage by 28–91%, and a Wasm bigstring DataView optimisation (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2144) improves non-V8 engine performance.
  • OCaml Core A new Atomic.Array module (ocaml/ocaml#14380 by @clef-men and Gabriel Scherer) adds safe and unsafe atomic array operations (make, init, get/set, exchange, compare_and_set, fetch_and_add).
  • OCaml Core List.append_map and List.rev_append_map (ocaml/ocaml#13554 by Sylvain Boilard and Hugo Heuzard) provide tail-recursive-modulo-cons list combinators.
  • OCaml Core Set.S.singleton_to_elt and Map.S.singleton_to_binding (ocaml/ocaml#14121 by Vincent Laviron) add singleton extraction utilities to the Set and Map standard library modules.
  • OCaml Core Hashtbl.is_randomized exposed in Sys.runtime_parameters (ocaml/ocaml#14292 by Hannes Mehnert, David Allsopp, Antonin Décimo) allows runtime introspection of hash-table randomisation state.
  • OCaml Core Bytecode optimization hints (ocaml/ocaml#13438 by Jérôme Vouillon) are now preserved in bytecode output for Jsofocaml and Wasmofocaml consumption.
  • OCaml Core Prefetch read/write distinction (ocaml/ocaml#14570, ocaml/ocaml#14616 by Nick Barnes and Antonin Décimo) differentiates prefetch operations for improved code generation.
  • OCaml Core A type soundness fix for polymorphic parameter checking (ocaml/ocaml#14434, ocaml/ocaml#14652 by Stephen Dolan and Jacques Garrigue) and a bytecode effects heap-corruption fix in reperform (ocaml/ocaml#14644, ocaml/ocaml#14647 by Vincent Laviron) address correctness regressions.
  • OCaml Core Continuation objects reduced from two fields to one (ocaml/ocaml#14469 by KC Sivaramakrishnan) lowers allocation overhead for effect-based code.
  • OCaml Core UTF-8 string processing optimisations (ocaml/ocaml#14618, ocaml/ocaml#14620 by Gabriel Scherer and Stefan Muenzel) and a Float.Array.sub/append/concat bug fix (ocaml/ocaml#14635) round out stdlib improvements.
  • OxCaml eval beta-reduction in type expressions (oxcaml/oxcaml#5323, oxcaml/oxcaml#5402 by Jakub Bachurski) introduces a Tquote_eval type constructor with reduce_head for staged computation in types.
  • OxCaml Mode constraint syntax without a type annotation (oxcaml/oxcaml#5602 by Nailen Matschke) makes (x @ local) valid syntax, improving ergonomics of mode annotations.
  • OxCaml CamlinternalQuote API expansion (oxcaml/oxcaml#5649, oxcaml/oxcaml#5650, oxcaml/oxcaml#5645 by Mark Shinwell) adds Identifier.eval, Vb_attribute module, and let_rec_simple updates.
  • OxCaml The x86 binary emitter gained missing instruction encodings and an ASAN failure fix (oxcaml/oxcaml#5653 by Mark Shinwell), and Camlinternaleval is now compiled at -O3 (oxcaml/oxcaml#5646).
  • OxCaml Two Reaper bug fixes were merged: incorrect argument count (oxcaml/oxcaml#5633 by Nathanaëlle Courant) and a crash when loading mutable variables (oxcaml/oxcaml#5655 by Nathanaëlle Courant).
  • OxCaml Merlin upstream sync incorporating 5.2.0minus-34 changes with layout polymorphism support (oxcaml/merlin#225 by Liam Stevenson).
  • Multicore picos OCaml 5.5 compatibility fix in picos_std.awaitable (ocaml-multicore/picos#387 by Kate) adds an explicit type constraint to the snoc function, tracking upstream ocaml/ocaml#14224.
  • OCaml Ecosystem OCaml 4.14.3 LTS released with a security fix for CVE-2026-28364 (Marshal deserialization buffer over-read, OSEC-2026-01), with announcement at ocaml/ocaml.org#3571.
  • OCaml Ecosystem ocamlformat 0.29.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#29553) adds OCaml 5.5 syntax support, an Odoc 3.0 parser, and a letop-punning formatting option.
  • OCaml Ecosystem atd 4.0.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#29552, 11 packages) adds experimental module support and an atdml code generator.
  • OCaml Ecosystem New libraries published: parseff 0.1.0/0.2.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#29526, ocaml/opam-repository#29573) — direct-style effect-based parser combinators with zero-copy spans; raven 1.0.0~alpha3 (ocaml/opam-repository#29490, 11 packages) — scientific computing suite including nx-oxcaml (pure-OCaml SIMD) and kaun-board TUI; jws 0.0.1 (ocaml/opam-repository#29557) — RFC 7515 JWS implementation; dune-ai-context 0.1.2 (ocaml/opam-repository#29536) — dune external dependency context for AI tools.

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    Dune 3.22.0 release, OCaml 4.14.3 LTS security fix, and Windows/MSYS2 improvements drove ecosystem activity.

    New Features

  • OCaml 4.14.3 LTS release page added to ocaml.org (ocaml/ocaml.org#3571), marking it as the current LTS and documenting the CVE-2026-28364 security fix (Marshal deserialization buffer over-read, OSEC-2026-01), plus backports for ocaml/ocaml#12207, ocaml/ocaml#13430, ocaml/ocaml#13448, and ocaml/ocaml#14007
  • parseff 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 merged — direct-style parser combinator library for OCaml 5 using algebraic effects, with zero-copy span APIs and domain-safe operation; 0.2.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#29573) unified *1 combinators with an ~at_least parameter
  • raven 1.0.0~alpha3 merged — 11-package scientific computing suite including nx-oxcaml (pure-OCaml SIMD tensor backend) and kaun-board (TUI training dashboard), with a unified Nx.t/Rune.t tensor type
  • jws 0.0.1 merged — RFC 7515 JWS implementation using jsont and mirage-crypto; later used as a dependency in letsencrypt 2.0.0
  • dnsrobot 0.1.0 merged — OCaml client for DNS Robot providing DNS lookups, WHOIS, SSL checks, and 50+ network tools via an Lwt-based async API
  • dune-ai-context 0.1.2 merged — extracts dune external dependencies and generates interface context for AI-assisted coding tools
  • tm-grammars 1.1.0 merged — adds TextMate grammar definitions for 200+ languages as OCaml strings, replacing the broken 1.0.0 tarball

    • Overview

  • dune 3.22.0 released to opam-repository with 18 packages, featuring extensive build tracing, expanded sandboxing defaults, and oxcaml .cms file support; a companion announcement PR (ocaml/ocaml.org#3570) is awaiting merge on ocaml.org
  • OCaml 4.14.3 LTS published on ocaml.org (ocaml/ocaml.org#3571) with a CVE-2026-28364 security fix and several backported bug fixes from OCaml 5.x
  • Windows/MSYS2 support received sustained attention with four new issues (ocaml/opam-repository#29575, #29576, #29577, #29578) covering missing MSYS2 depext declarations and UCRT64 migration needs
  • MirageOS ecosystem modernisation progressed: letsencrypt 2.0.0 drops yojson, mirage-runtime relaxes the lwt < 6 constraint, and charrua 3.1.1 fixes DHCP cancellation semantics
  • atd 4.0.0 released with 11 packages, introducing experimental module support and the new atdml code generator as successor to atdgen
  • ocamlformat 0.29.0 released with OCaml 5.5 syntax support, Odoc 3.0 parser integration, and a new letop-punning option
  • Planet content on ocaml.org expanded with automated scrapes merging posts from tunbury, cwn, and anil across PRs ocaml/ocaml.org#3566–#3569 and #3573

    • Activity

  • dune 3.22.0 release required coordinated upper-bound fixes: stdune and dune-rpc updated for breaking API changes; ocamlformat constraints on dune 3.22 pending due to changed (diff) rule behaviour
  • mirage-crypto 2.1.0 merged with 7 packages — exposes Mirage_crypto_ec.Dsa.Primitive for NIST curve primitives useful for protocols like SPAKE2
  • Gospel 0.3.1 merged — OCaml specification language update for ppxlib and cmdliner compatibility
  • elpi 3.6.2 merged — fixes quadratic growth in program signature storage in the embeddable λProlog interpreter
  • xapi-backtrace 0.8 merged — fixes backtrace loss on reraise and adds regression tests
  • camlpdf 2.9 and cpdf 2.9 merged — PDF library and command-line tools update
  • charrua-client 3.0.0 and 3.1.0 marked avoid-version due to MirageOS network stack runtime issues
  • tm-grammars 1.0.0 marked unavailable due to broken release tarball; replaced by 1.1.0
  • Open PRs awaiting review: ppxlib and ppxlib-tools 0.38.0 (OCaml 5.5 support, bivariant type parameters); Ortac 0.8.0 (QCheck-STM+Domains parallel testing); lsp 1.26.0-5.5~preview (destruct custom request, non-dune build system support); gendarme 0.4.1 (9 packages, ppxlib>=0.36); alcobar 0.3 (Alcotest-compatible fuzzing); oniguruma 0.2.0 (new syntaxes and search options)
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29530 — Raphaël Proust continues broad lwt 6 compatibility work across 84 packages
  • Markdown lint fixes for 4.14.x release data files opened on ocaml.org (ocaml/ocaml.org#3572) by Cuihtlauac Alvarado, resolving MD003, MD004, MD012, MD026, and MD040 violations — awaiting merge

    • Notable Discussions

  • MSYS2 depext gaps — Sora Morimoto filed four issues (ocaml/opam-repository#29575, #29576, #29577, #29578) covering missing MSYS2 depext declarations for conf-m4, conf-perl, and conf-findutils, and the need to support UCRT64 as MSYS2 deprecated MINGW64 in March 2026; companion PR ocaml/opam-repository#29579 addresses all four with package-prefix variable interpolation
  • New ocaml-option-clang-cl package — Sora Morimoto proposes a marker package enabling MSVC clang-cl as the OCaml compiler's CC, following the pattern of ocaml-option-musl, affecting 16 compiler packages
  • MirageOS lwt/dune dependency puzzle — Hannes Mehnert asked how to express conditional lwt version constraints depending on dune version; Kate and Marcello Seri explained the disjunctive constraint pattern "dune" {>= "3.22"} | "lwt" {< "6"}, noting that the 0install solver gives slight priority to earlier disjunction terms
  • Refine constraints on lwt 6 — Raphaël Proust continues broad lwt 6 compatibility work spanning 84 files; discussion covers using opam-health-check-ng to detect which packages need lwt < 6

    Active week in oxcaml/oxcaml with metaprogramming and mode system merges; oxcaml/merlin synced upstream compiler with layout polymorphism.

    New Features

  • eval beta-reduction in type expressions now supported via new Tquote_eval type constructor and reduce_head in Ctype; landed via oxcaml/oxcaml#5323 (quote & splice typing, by Jakub Bachurski) and oxcaml/oxcaml#5402 (beta-reducing eval, by Jakub Bachurski).
  • Mode constraint syntax without a type annotation accepted — (x @ local) now valid without spelling out the type; documentation updated and legacy syntax removed from pprintast (oxcaml/oxcaml#5602, by Nailen Matschke).
  • CamlinternalQuote API expanded: Identifier.eval added, new Vb_attribute module exposed with mk, and let_rec_simple updated to accept Vb_attribute.t list for attribute propagation through quotations (oxcaml/oxcaml#5649, oxcaml/oxcaml#5650, oxcaml/oxcaml#5645, by Mark Shinwell).
  • with kind annotations now scanned by ocamldep: dependency analysis correctly records dependencies from with kind_ constraints for sound incremental builds (oxcaml/oxcaml#5628, by Chris Casinghino).
  • x86 binary emitter completeness: missing instruction encodings added and error messages improved, fixing an ASAN failure triggered by Camlinternaleval (oxcaml/oxcaml#5653, by Mark Shinwell).
  • Camlinternaleval compiled at -O3: JIT-based eval library now uses the highest optimisation level (oxcaml/oxcaml#5646, by Mark Shinwell).
  • Tail-call stack-overflow move fixed in the IRC register allocator (oxcaml/oxcaml#5591, by Xavier Clerc).
  • Debuginfo.to_location improved for more accurate zero-alloc (warning 55) error locations (oxcaml/oxcaml#5444, by Guillaume Bury).
  • Reaper bug fixes: wrong argument count for unboxed callees (oxcaml/oxcaml#5633) and crash when loading a mutable variable from an unboxed value with no source (oxcaml/oxcaml#5655), both by Nathanaëlle Courant).
  • flambda2: is_null classified as naked integer operation, fixing a latent type mismatch (oxcaml/oxcaml#5642, by Basile Clément).
  • native_code flag set in the fexpr compiler, fixing a flag mismatch that could affect code generation (oxcaml/oxcaml#5647, by Basile Clément).
  • CamlinternalQuote pretty-printer bug fixes: seven parenthesisation bugs fixed across assert/lazy arguments, PatVariant arguments, match/try case RHS, sequence elements, if-else branches, unboxed field subexpressions, and function constraint position (oxcaml/oxcaml#5660, by Mark Shinwell).
  • Merlin upstream sync incorporating 5.2.0minus-34: new Ptyp_newlayout AST node for layout_ a b c. T syntax, polymorphic sort variables (Genvar), Layout_poly_coercion error type, and updated block access AST (oxcaml/merlin#225, by Liam Stevenson).

    Atomic.Array, List.append_map/rev_append_map merged; GC improvements, type soundness fixes, and bytecode effects bug landed in ocaml/ocaml.

    New Features

  • New Atomic.Array module added to stdlib with make, init, length, get/set, exchange, compare_and_set, and fetch_and_add (safe and unsafe variants); joint work by @clef-men and Gabriel Scherer (ocaml/ocaml#14380)
  • New List.append_map and List.rev_append_map functions added to stdlib, combining map and append in a single tail-recursive-modulo-cons pass with half the allocations of the composed version; by Sylvain Boilard and Hugo Heuzard (ocaml/ocaml#13554)
  • New Set.S.singleton_to_elt and Map.S.singleton_to_binding functions added to the Set and Map modules; by Vincent Laviron (ocaml/ocaml#14121)
  • Hashtbl.is_randomized result is now reflected in the R parameter of Sys.runtime_parameters; by Hannes Mehnert, David Allsopp, and Antonin Décimo (ocaml/ocaml#14292)
  • Gc.stat is now deprecated; users should call Gc.quick_stat directly and explicitly call Gc.full_major () beforehand if up-to-date counters are needed; by Damien Doligez (ocaml/ocaml#12023)
  • Optimization hints from Lambda are now kept in bytecode modules and executables (.cmo/.cma/.cme), making them available to Jsofocaml and Wasmofocaml; by Jérôme Vouillon (ocaml/ocaml#13438)
  • Warning 16 (unerasable-optional-argument) check improved to correctly handle module-dependent functions in the presence of GADTs and first-class modules; by Alistair (ocaml/ocaml#14512, ocaml/ocaml#14626)
  • Prefetch read/write distinction now correctly distinguishes between prefetching for read vs. write access; pass -mprfchw or -march=native for maximum benefit on AMD64; by Nick Barnes and Antonin Décimo (ocaml/ocaml#14570, ocaml/ocaml#14616)
  • Type soundness fix for check_counter_example_pat against polymorphic types that could previously cause segfaults; by Stephen Dolan and Jacques Garrigue (ocaml/ocaml#14434, ocaml/ocaml#14652)
  • Bytecode effects fix for heap corruption in reperform when using try Effect.perform with Effect.Unhandled under deep effect handlers; by Vincent Laviron (ocaml/ocaml#14644, ocaml/ocaml#14647)
  • Float.Array.sub/append/concat bug fixed where these functions could return a value not equal to [||] for empty arrays; by Marc Lasson (ocaml/ocaml#14635)
  • UTF-8 normalization and un/capitalization functions optimized, both within and outside ASCII range; by Gabriel Scherer and Stefan Muenzel (ocaml/ocaml#14618, ocaml/ocaml#14620)
  • Continuation objects now use one field instead of two, reducing allocation overhead for effect handlers; by KC Sivaramakrishnan (ocaml/ocaml#14469)
  • S390x TSan (Thread Sanitizer) support removed, simplifying the s390x backend; by Tim McGilchrist (ocaml/ocaml#14651)

  • Stefan Muenzel has a PR open to run expect tests with -rectypes flag (ocaml/ocaml#14643) to catch behavioral differences, showing ~10% testsuite time increase
  • Florian Angeletti also has a PR for modular explicit optional argument elision in the Lambda IR (ocaml/ocaml#14648)
  • David Allsopp opened a correct compiler flag ordering fix for ocamltest (ocaml/ocaml#14662) and merged a 4.14 maintenance fix for pthread library linking (ocaml/ocaml#14661)
  • Stale issues closed during triage: ocaml/ocaml#12425, ocaml/ocaml#12367, ocaml/ocaml#12218, ocaml/ocaml#11948

    • Notable Discussions

  • Hashtbl default randomization (ocaml/ocaml#14291): Gabriel Scherer proposed tracking insertion order to make iteration deterministic regardless of randomization; Simon Cruanes and others raised concern about breakage comparable to -safe-string; consensus forming around Hashtbl.create_seeded and Hashtbl.create_deterministic
  • Minor heap size defaults (ocaml/ocaml#14634): Gabriel Scherer presents benchmark data showing the current 256Kwords (2MiB) default is too conservative — OCAMLRUNPARAM=s=32M shows up to 3x speedup on allocation-heavy workloads; discussion ongoing on choosing a better default
  • Polymorphic parameters soundness (ocaml/ocaml#14434): minimal fix by Stephen Dolan and Jacques Garrigue chosen over a larger refactoring proposed by Alistair; Florian Angeletti noted the two-timescale consideration between bug-fix speed and long-term maintainability
  • Mutually-recursive function performance regression in Coccinelle reported by Victor Gambier (ocaml/ocaml#14656): chains of 62+ recursive functions cross the 256-word minor-heap allocation boundary, causing closures to be allocated on the major heap; root cause identified by Vincent Laviron
  • Undesirable exponential typechecking time for programs with deeply-nested tuple types reported by Arthur Charguéraud (ocaml/ocaml#14650); Jacques Garrigue and Alistair discussed whether the behavior is inherent to deep copying and ambivalence/principality tracking
  • Bigarray.reshape overflow reported by Andriy Sultanov (ocaml/ocaml#14655): allows reading uninitialized memory on OCaml 4.14.x; confirmed fixed in OCaml 5 as a side effect of ocaml/ocaml#11022; Hannes Mehnert flagged this as deserving a security advisory for the 4.14 branch

    • Emerging Trends

  • Atomic/parallel primitives continue expanding: Atomic.Array merged (ocaml/ocaml#14380), native Iatomic_fetch_add across all backends progressing (ocaml/ocaml#14575), and continuation object size reduction (ocaml/ocaml#14469) indicate sustained investment in multicore performance primitives
  • GC optimization active on multiple fronts simultaneously: ephemeron quadratic blowup fix (ocaml/ocaml#14657), minor GC rewrite (ocaml/ocaml#14571), ephemeron budget fix (ocaml/ocaml#14610), and minor heap size discussion (ocaml/ocaml#14634)
  • Type error message quality improving with Florian Angeletti's semantic highlighting PR (ocaml/ocaml#14659) built on typechecker error trace refactoring (ocaml/ocaml#14536), continuing a multi-release effort
  • Cross-platform and build system work by Antonin Décimo spans multiple PRs: MSVC prefetch docs (ocaml/ocaml#14616), lexer fix (ocaml/ocaml#14654), -Wwrite-strings (ocaml/ocaml#14666), prefetchw emission (ocaml/ocaml#14665), and LN_S/AR standardization (ocaml/ocaml#14552)
  • Typing refactoring towards let rec improvements: Alistair's multi-PR series (ocaml/ocaml#14394, ocaml/ocaml#14537, ocaml/ocaml#14538) separating recursive and non-recursive let typing is groundwork for fixing long-standing polymorphic recursion issues (ocaml/ocaml#14253)

    • Multicore

    Picos merged an OCaml 5.5 compatibility fix; Eio received two new issues around API usability in Path and Flow.

    New Features

  • OCaml 5.5 compatibility fix in picos_std.awaitable by Kate: adds an explicit type constraint (One tail_r : [ \One ] tdt)in thesnoc` function, addressing a type-checking change in OCaml 5.5 (see ocaml/ocaml#14224) (ocaml-multicore/picos#387)

    • Overview

  • Activity this week was limited to two repositories: ocaml-multicore/eio and ocaml-multicore/picos; the remaining seven repositories had no recorded activity.
  • ocaml-multicore/picos merged one PR — a one-line OCaml 5.5 compatibility fix (ocaml-multicore/picos#387) — with discussion around cutting a release for ecosystem beta-testing.
  • ocaml-multicore/eio received two new issues from Volker Diels-Grabsch covering a race condition in Eio.Path.load (ocaml-multicore/eio#835) and a proposal to add Close support to Eio.Flow.buffer_sink (ocaml-multicore/eio#834), plus renewed student engagement on the long-standing lock-free Waiters issue (ocaml-multicore/eio#382).

    • Activity

  • Volker Diels-Grabsch opened ocaml-multicore/eio#835 reporting that Eio.Path.load has a stat-then-read race condition and silently returns empty strings for /proc virtual files (where stat reports size 0); the proposed fix is to treat file size only as a hint for initial buffer allocation.
  • Volker Diels-Grabsch opened ocaml-multicore/eio#834 proposing that Eio.Flow.buffer_sink be made closable, with open design questions about semantics (no-op vs. error on subsequent writes) and backwards-compatibility.
  • Mitesh Sharma commented on the long-standing ocaml-multicore/eio#382 (lock-free Waiters, originally opened by Thomas Leonard in 2022), asking whether a CQS-based implementation from a supervised course project has been completed.
  • Kate followed up with Vesa Karvonen on the possibility of a picos release to support OCaml 5.5 beta-testers and the wider ecosystem (ocaml-multicore/picos#387).

    • Notable Discussions

  • ocaml-multicore/eio#835: Volker Diels-Grabsch includes a concrete reproducer showing "/proc/sys/fs/file-nr" returning "" via Eio.Path.load while cat returns the expected content, highlighting a silent data-loss scenario for /proc virtual files.
  • ocaml-multicore/eio#834: proposal to extend Eio.Flow.buffer_sink with a Close capability raises open API design questions about backwards-compatibility and close semantics for in-memory buffer sinks.
  • ocaml-multicore/eio#382: student engagement from Mitesh Sharma on a coursework CQS implementation (supervised by @kayceesrk) points to ongoing academic use of Eio's synchronization internals as a research and teaching vehicle.
  • ocaml-multicore/picos#387: Kate raised the question of releasing picos with the OCaml 5.5 fix to Vesa Karvonen, surfacing the release-coordination challenge for multicore libraries ahead of a compiler beta.

    • Emerging Trends

  • Two issues filed by the same external contributor (Volker Diels-Grabsch) in a single week — ocaml-multicore/eio#835 and ocaml-multicore/eio#834 — indicate growing external adoption uncovering edge cases in Eio.Path and Eio.Flow, particularly around /proc file handling and composability with close-aware consumers.
  • Academic use of multicore libraries continues: student coursework on CQS-based lock-free synchronization referencing ocaml-multicore/eio#382 suggests Eio's internals are being used as a teaching and research platform.
  • OCaml 5.5 readiness is becoming a coordination point: the picos fix (ocaml-multicore/picos#387) and associated release discussion reflect a pattern of multicore libraries tracking upstream compiler changes to support beta-testing pipelines.
entry.summary: Dune 3.22.0 stable released; OCaml 4.14.3 LTS security patch (CVE-2026-28364); compiler gains Atomic.Array and List combinators.

entry.title: Week 11, 2026: Dune 3.22.0~alpha1 released; OxCaml saw 28 PRs with -O4 level and reaper advances; bytecode hints merged in compiler for Js_of_ocaml.
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

Compiler (ocaml/ocaml)
- OCaml Core ocaml/ocaml#13438 Bytecode optimization hints merged: the bytecode compiler now preserves optimization hints from the Lambda IR (closure kinds, immutable blocks, array lengths, C call details) in a new HINT section in .cmo and .cma files, enabled with -bytecode-hints. This allows Jérôme Vouillon's Jsofocaml and Wasmofocaml to access type-level information previously discarded at the bytecode stage.
- OCaml Core ocaml/ocaml#14618 Faster UTF-8 normalization outside the ASCII range merged, optimizing the Misc.Stdlib unicode normalization path. Contributed by Stefan Muenzel, reviewed by Gabriel Scherer, Daniel Bünzli, and Florian Angeletti.

OxCaml (oxcaml/oxcaml)
- OxCaml oxcaml/oxcaml#5574 A new -O4 optimization level was introduced, bundling the reaper dead-code elimination pass with -O3; the [@flambda_o4] attribute mirrors it at the per-function level.
- OxCaml oxcaml/oxcaml#5610 The [@unpacked] attribute for C stub externals allows unboxed product types as C stub arguments by flattening each product component into separate native C arguments, while bytecode stubs receive a single boxed value.
- OxCaml oxcaml/oxcaml#5597 A CFG block merging pass (-cfg-merge-blocks) was merged, deduplicating equivalent basic blocks after register allocation, achieving up to 4.5% reduction in instruction count with only 0.2% build-time overhead.
- OxCaml Constant propagation in the CFG backend extended to cover integer arithmetic (oxcaml/oxcaml#5545), floating-point arithmetic (oxcaml/oxcaml#5546), and values inferred from predecessor terminators (oxcaml/oxcaml#5562) by Xavier Clerc.
- OxCaml oxcaml/oxcaml#5579 Multicore.spawn_result now accepts value_or_null resources, aligning the multicore API with the null-safety story.
- OxCaml oxcaml/oxcaml#5629 with kind_ constraints added as part of abstract kinds part 3, completing the core feature set for abstract kinds.
- OxCaml oxcaml/oxcaml#5628 ocamldep now scans with kind annotations, ensuring correct dependency tracking for modules using abstract kinds.

Tools
- OCaml Tools ocaml/dune#13805 Sandboxing enabled by default for user rules from dune lang 3.23, catching undeclared dependencies at build time.
- OCaml Tools ocaml/dune#13341 Asynchronous digest computation (part 2) — target files and directories now digested in background threads, reducing main build loop blocking.
- OCaml Tools ocaml/dune#13613 Jsoo config management moved out of dune, reducing the need for dune to track all possible jsofocaml configs upfront.
- OCaml Tools ocsigen/jsofocaml#2177 New --build-config and --apply-build-config CLI flags for both js_of_ocaml and wasm_of_ocaml, enabling coherent multi-unit compilation by printing and overriding build-relevant compiler settings.
- OCaml Tools ocsigen/jsofocaml#2197 OCaml 5.5.0~alpha1 support added to jsofocaml, including new JS and Wasm runtime primitives for gc, sys, and domain modules.
- OCaml Tools ocsigen/jsofocaml#2198 Shape computation performance overhauled with coinductive caching in Flow.the_shape_of, fixing potential exponential blowups — a pathological case dropped from >7 hours to ~200ms compilation time.
- OCaml Tools ocsigen/jsofocaml#2191 Binaryen version check added to the wasm_of_ocaml runtime build, providing a clear error on missing wasm-merge when Binaryen < 119.

Ecosystem (opam-repository)
- OCaml Ecosystem ocaml/opam-repository#29543 olint.0.1.0 — new OCaml linter inspired by Rust's Clippy, checking 10 antipattern rules using compiler-libs on the untyped AST, by Zane Hambly.
- OCaml Ecosystem ocaml/opam-repository#29523 oui.0.1.0 — a tool that builds standalone installers for OCaml applications, by Nathan Rebours.
- OCaml Ecosystem ocaml/opam-repository#29531 libinput.0.1 — initial release of OCaml bindings for the libinput input device library, by Thomas Leonard.
- OCaml Ecosystem ocaml/opam-repository#29526 parseff.0.1.0 — direct-style parser combinator library for OCaml 5 powered by algebraic effects, by David Sancho.
- OCaml Ecosystem ocaml/ocaml.org#3558 The Installing OCaml and Configuring Your Editor tutorials updated to mention the OCaml devcontainer as a zero-install path, with a new Dev Containers section added to the Docker Images tutorial, by Cuihtlauac Alvarado.
- OCaml Ecosystem ocaml/ocaml.org#3556 A new release-scrapers.yml GitHub Actions workflow introduced by Cuihtlauac Alvarado to build and publish the scraper binary as a scraper-latest release, eliminating source recompilation on every scrape run.

Group Activity Summaries

OCaml Ecosystem

~30 opam packages merged including new linter and SIMD tensor backend; ocaml.org improved devcontainer tutorials and scraper CI.

New Features

ocaml/opam-repository
- ocaml/opam-repository#29543 olint.0.1.0 — new OCaml linter inspired by Rust's Clippy, checking 10 antipattern rules using compiler-libs on the untyped AST, by Zane Hambly
- ocaml/opam-repository#29523 oui.0.1.0 — a tool that builds standalone installers for OCaml applications, by Nathan Rebours
- ocaml/opam-repository#29531 libinput.0.1 — initial release of OCaml bindings for the libinput input device library, by Thomas Leonard
- ocaml/opam-repository#29526 parseff.0.1.0 — direct-style parser combinator library for OCaml 5 powered by algebraic effects, by David Sancho (open, CI issue)
- ocaml/opam-repository#29541 dnsrobot.0.1.0 — OCaml client for DNS Robot with 11 API methods using cohttp-lwt-unix (open, needs reporter action)
- ocaml/opam-repository#29536 dune-ai-context.0.1.2 — tool to extract dune external dependencies and generate interface context for AI coding tools

ocaml/ocaml.org
- The Installing OCaml and Configuring Your Editor tutorials were updated by Cuihtlauac Alvarado (ocaml/ocaml.org#3558) to mention the OCaml devcontainer as a zero-install path, with notes that it ships with OCaml LSP, OCamlFormat, and editor support pre-configured.
- A new Dev Containers section was added to the Docker Images tutorial (ocaml/ocaml.org#3558) to distinguish development-oriented devcontainer setup from CI-focused Docker images.
- A new GitHub Actions workflow release-scrapers.yml was introduced by Cuihtlauac Alvarado (ocaml/ocaml.org#3556) to build and publish the scraper binary as a scraper-latest release, eliminating the need to recompile from source on every scrape run.
- The scrape workflows were updated (ocaml/ocaml.org#3557) to download the pre-built scrape.exe binary instead of rebuilding it, installing only runtime libraries (libev4, libonig5) rather than the full OCaml toolchain.

Overview

  • ocaml/opam-repository saw approximately 30 merged PRs, covering new packages, security library updates, infrastructure tooling, and a notable policy change on package immutability enforcement
  • ocaml/ocaml.org landed tutorial improvements referencing the OCaml devcontainer, scraper CI optimisation using a pre-built binary release, an exercise sort bug fix, and a wave of new OCaml Planet posts
  • Key security-related updates included ocaml/opam-repository#29532 tls 2.0.4 (exception fix) and ocaml/opam-repository#29545 mirage-crypto 2.1.0 (NIST curve primitive exposure)
  • Infrastructure changes in both repos reflect a shared push toward reproducibility: immutability enforcement in opam-repository and pre-built CI binaries in ocaml.org
  • Over 20 contributors were active across both repositories this week

    • Activity

    ocaml/opam-repository — package updates
    - ocaml/opam-repository#29532 tls 2.0.4 (6 packages) — fixes an exception in parse_change_cipher_spec on empty input present since 0.1.0, by Hannes Mehnert
    - ocaml/opam-repository#29545 mirage-crypto 2.1.0 (7 packages) — adds Mirage_crypto_ec.Dsa.Primitive exposing NIST curve operations for protocols like SPAKE2, by Hannes Mehnert (open)
    - ocaml/opam-repository#29520 mpi 1.07 — updated for OCaml >= 5.4.1 compatibility and dynamic linking of stubs, by Xavier Leroy
    - ocaml/opam-repository#29538 charrua 3.1.1 (4 packages) — DHCP wire frame library with cancellation semantics fix, by Reynir Björnsson
    - ocaml/opam-repository#29495 posix bindings 4.0.2 (14 packages) — new release of the savonet/ocaml-posix suite covering sockets, stat, signals, time, uname, and more, by Romain Beauxis
    - ocaml/opam-repository#29534 smtml.0.23.0 — SMT solver frontend with improved SMTZilla decision tree cleanup and new CLI options, by @filipeom
    - ocaml/opam-repository#29529 malfunction.0.7.1 — new release of the malfunction intermediate language, by Matthieu Sozeau
    - ocaml/opam-repository#29533 jasmin.2026.03.0 — date-versioned release of the Jasmin cryptographic compiler, by Jean-Christophe Léchenet
    - ocaml/opam-repository#29539 slipshow.0.10.0 — presentation tool with improved compile-time warnings and keyboard shortcut fixes, by Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac
    - ocaml/opam-repository#29540 melange-fest.0.2.0 — minimal Melange test framework updated for melange 6 API changes, by David Sancho
    - ocaml/opam-repository#29483 ortools.9.15.0-1 (2 packages) — updated Google OR-Tools bindings removing eigen3 depext, by Timothy Bourke
    - ocaml/opam-repository#29527 tm-grammars.1.0.1 — TextMate grammars as OCaml strings (replacing broken 1.0.0 release), by David Sancho
    - ocaml/opam-repository#29524 iri.1.2.0 — Internationalized Resource Identifiers implementation, by Zoggy
    - ocaml/opam-repository#29490 raven.1.0.0~alpha3 (11 packages) — scientific computing suite including new nx-oxcaml pure-OCaml SIMD tensor backend and kaun-board TUI training dashboard, by Thibaut Mattio (open)
    - ocaml/opam-repository#29507 ppxlib.0.38.0~5.5preview — preview release of ppxlib for upcoming OCaml 5.5, by Nathan Rebours

    ocaml/ocaml.org — site updates
    - Exercise slug sorting was fixed by Lucas Rodrigues (ocaml/ocaml.org#3553), resolving ocaml/ocaml.org#3552 where exercises were ordered alphabetically (1, 10, 100, 11…) rather than numerically
    - Thomas Gazagnaire added his personal blog to the OCaml Planet sources (ocaml/ocaml.org#3561), enabling backfill of posts about MirageOS, unikernels, and satellite software
    - The ppxlib developer meeting entry was removed from governance data by @sabine (ocaml/ocaml.org#3560) as routine data maintenance
    - The automated OCaml Planet scraper ran daily throughout the week (ocaml/ocaml.org#3555, ocaml/ocaml.org#3559, ocaml/ocaml.org#3562, ocaml/ocaml.org#3563, ocaml/ocaml.org#3564, ocaml/ocaml.org#3565), ingesting posts on OCluster, ciao-lwt, OxCaml SIMD, Pi Day performance comparisons, and the OCaml Roundup for February 2026

    Notable Discussions

  • ocaml/opam-repository#29072 Stricter immutability policy merged after months of discussion — strengthens the rule that published package tarballs must not change, now a hard enforcement in opam-repo-ci lint; this directly triggered the tm-grammars 1.0.0 checksum situation and the decision to release 1.0.1 instead of patching, by Hannes Mehnert
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29451 relocatable.packages virtual package merged — introduces a virtual package that non-relocatable packages (compilers < 5.5, ocamlfind, ocamlbuild) can conflict with, enabling Dune package management to require relocatable installs; included discussion of naming conventions for virtual/property packages, by David Allsopp
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29530 lwt 6 constraint refinements — open PR adjusting upper bounds across ~84 files after lwt 6 removed long-deprecated APIs (Lwt_main.exit_hooks, Lwt_unix.run, abstract Lwt_engine); Jan Midtgaard noted 440 downstream failures with lwt.6.1.1, by Raphaël Proust
  • ocaml/opam-repository#29535 dune 3.22.0~alpha1 draft — extensive alpha release with 30+ bug fixes; a breaking API change in dune-rpc was identified and addressed in a separate constraint PR ocaml/opam-repository#29544, with a regression in mccs builds also filed upstream, by Shon Feder

    • Emerging Trends

  • OCaml 5 effects adoption: ocaml/opam-repository#29526 parseff uses algebraic effects for parser backtracking, and ocaml/opam-repository#29490 raven's nx-oxcaml uses OxCaml unboxed types and SIMD intrinsics for a pure-OCaml tensor backend
  • Tooling ecosystem growth: new packages for code review management (crs), dune file linting (dunolint), OCaml source linting (ocaml/opam-repository#29543 olint), and AI coding assistance (ocaml/opam-repository#29536 dune-ai-context) all appeared this week
  • Reproducibility infrastructure tightening: the merged immutability policy (ocaml/opam-repository#29072) and the switch to a pre-built scraper binary (ocaml/ocaml.org#3556, ocaml/ocaml.org#3557) both reflect a push toward deterministic, reproducible workflows across the ecosystem
  • Relocatability groundwork: the relocatable.packages virtual package (ocaml/opam-repository#29451) sets up infrastructure for Dune's package management mode to enforce switch portability on OCaml 5.5+
  • MirageOS and unikernels in aerospace: Thomas Gazagnaire's Planet posts (ocaml/ocaml.org#3561) connect MirageOS and unikernel concepts to satellite software, NASA's F Prime framework, and multi-tenant payload isolation, suggesting an emerging thread at the intersection of OCaml systems research and space computing

    • OCaml Tools

    Dune 3.23 lands sandboxing by default and async digests; js_of_ocaml gains OCaml 5.5 alpha support and shape computation speedup.

    New Features

  • ocaml/dune: Sandboxing enabled by default for user rules from dune lang 3.23, catching undeclared dependencies (ocaml/dune#13805)
  • ocaml/dune: Asynchronous digest computation (part 2) — target files and directories now digested in background threads, reducing main build loop blocking (ocaml/dune#13341)
  • ocaml/dune: Jsoo config management moved out of dune, reducing the need for dune to track all possible jsofocaml configs upfront (ocaml/dune#13613)
  • ocaml/dune: Slang simplifications for package management — deduplicate And/Or blangs, simplify when with Nil body, and substitute installed variable at solve time for absent packages (ocaml/dune#13772, ocaml/dune#13773, ocaml/dune#13776)
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml: New --build-config and --apply-build-config CLI flags for both js_of_ocaml and wasm_of_ocaml, enabling coherent multi-unit compilation by printing and overriding build-relevant compiler settings (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2177)
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml: OCaml 5.5.0~alpha1 support added, including new JS and Wasm runtime primitives for gc, sys, and domain modules (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2197)
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml: Shape computation performance overhauled with coinductive caching in Flow.the_shape_of, fixing potential exponential blowups — a pathological case went from >7 hours to ~200ms compilation time (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2198)
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml: Binaryen version check added to the wasm_of_ocaml runtime build to verify Binaryen >= 119 is available, providing a clear error on missing wasm-merge (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2191)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/dune was the most active repository this week with 46 commits, bumping to version 3.23 with sandboxing on by default and async digests merged
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml saw substantial activity with 8+ PRs merged, covering OCaml 5.5 alpha support, new CLI build-config flags, and a major shape computation performance fix
  • ocaml/odoc had 4 PRs merged addressing bugs in the markdown backend, URL remapping, type substitution, and incremental builds (ocaml/odoc#1403, ocaml/odoc#1400, ocaml/odoc#1395, ocaml/odoc#1402)
  • ocaml/opam had three PRs under active review covering Windows portability (ocaml/opam#6862), Darcs VCS cleanup (ocaml/opam#6866), and shell PATH ordering (ocaml/opam#6859)
  • ocaml/merlin had minimal activity: two Dependabot CI PRs closed without merging and one OxCaml compatibility issue triaged (ocaml/merlin#2045)
  • ocaml/opam-file-format had one README update PR opened (ocaml/opam-file-format#65); ocaml/ocaml-lsp had one Dune 3.22 compatibility fix opened (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1594)
  • ocaml/ocamlfind and ocaml-dune/spawn had no activity this week

    • Activity

  • ocaml/dune: Fixed regression in dune lang 1.0 (select ..) semantics for non-OCaml files (affecting packages like mccs) (ocaml/dune#13804)
  • ocaml/dune: Fixed silent hang when dune connects to a non-existent RPC server while the build directory is locked (ocaml/dune#13767)
  • ocaml/dune: Fixed default trace file placement to use build directory at workspace root (ocaml/dune#13735)
  • ocaml/dune: Fixed Rocq module duplication internal error with a user-facing hint (ocaml/dune#13733)
  • ocaml/dune: Opened PRs for symlink resolution in fetched package targets (ocaml/dune#13792), @revdep alias for reverse dependency builds (ocaml/dune#13800), and a how-to guide for multiple dune contexts (ocaml/dune#13749)
  • ocaml/odoc: Fixed URL remapping for page references — prefix check now includes filename (ocaml/odoc#1395), resolving long-standing issue ocaml/odoc#930
  • ocaml/odoc: Fixed type substitution crash when substituting the same name at different arities (ocaml/odoc#1400)
  • ocaml/odoc: Markdown backend now emits ocaml as the language identifier for OCaml API declarations; documentedSrc refactored to consolidate code items into a unified block (ocaml/odoc#1403)
  • ocaml/opam: Windows _WIN32_WINNT fix for MSYS2 environments updated to place the flag in the dune build file rather than C source (ocaml/opam#6862)
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml: Dynlink and toplevel support for Wasm under review (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2187); WASI runtime PR (ocsigen/jsofocaml#1831) unblocked by the merged jsoo config management changes
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml: Large draft PR for full OCaml 5.5 support (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2195) under investigation for a Wasm int test failure
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml: Build failure with wasm-merge: not found on Debian bookworm (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2190) resolved by the Binaryen version check (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2191)
  • ocaml/ocaml-lsp: Dune 3.22 compilation compatibility fix opened (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1594); Nix flake lock updated to 2026-03-14 snapshot (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1437)
  • ocaml/merlin: Two Dependabot bumps for cachix/install-nix-action (ocaml/merlin#2035, ocaml/merlin#2046) closed without merging due to a regression in Nix 2.34.0

    • Notable Discussions

  • Dune RPC API compatibility (ocaml/dune#13674): the 3.22.0 release tracker saw discussion about an intentional dune-rpc API change that breaks ocaml-lsp-server; Rudi Grinberg confirmed the break was deliberate and plans to fix LSP compatibility separately
  • Dune RPC/watch mode blocking (ocaml/dune#13788): a new issue reports that dune build @@fmt blocks until the watch process completes its current targets, making editor on-save hooks impractical
  • Dune context usability (ocaml/dune#13768): reported that dune exec --context does not pick up the right binary and that there is no per-context flag for dune build, complicating multi-compiler setups
  • Merlin OxCaml Emacs debugger issue (ocaml/merlin#2045): Ben Lieberman reported the Lisp debugger firing repeatedly in the OxCaml variant of Merlin (5.2.1-502+ox); Ulysse triaged it as OxCaml-specific, and Liam Stevenson identified debug-on-error as the immediate trigger though the underlying parser recovery exception remains open
  • jsofocaml shape computation performance (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2198): discussion around a 15% increase in ocamlc compilation time from the fix, with Jérôme Vouillon adding an extra optimization round; Ricky Vetter confirmed a real-world pathological case dropped from >7 hours to ~200ms
  • jsofocaml force-push incident (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2177): a git push --force-with-lease unexpectedly dropped commits pushed by @hhugo to a shared branch, highlighting risks of force-pushing to collaborative branches
  • opam Darcs VCS model (ocaml/opam#6866): @toastal provided detailed commentary on how the current module VCS abstraction is Git-centric and does not fit Darcs's context-file approach and weak hashes; R. Boujbel welcomed follow-up PRs
  • opam shell hook PATH ordering (ocaml/opam#6859): Kate flagged that in-place PATH updates could be a breaking change for users who add paths after sourcing opam-init.sh and recommended a prominent release note

    • Emerging Trends

  • Sandboxing and build correctness: dune 3.23's sandboxing-by-default (ocaml/dune#13805) continues the trend toward stricter build guarantees, complemented by the async digest pipeline (ocaml/dune#13341) moving blocking I/O off the main build loop
  • Wasm backend maturation in jsofocaml: multiple concurrent PRs advancing dynlink/toplevel support (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2187), WASI runtime (ocsigen/jsofocaml#1831), and full OCaml 5.5 compatibility (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2195) indicate sustained investment in the Wasm target
  • Compiler build configuration formalization: jsofocaml's new --build-config/--apply-build-config flags (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2177) and dune's jsoo config management extraction (ocaml/dune#13613) together point toward reproducible, coherent multi-unit compilation across the dune/jsoo toolchain
  • Dune version compatibility as a recurring concern: ocaml-lsp required a compatibility fix (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1594) for dune 3.22, and jsofocaml's WASI PR was blocked on a dune feature; dune API changes have downstream effects across the tools group
  • Windows and shell portability: opam continues to see improvements for Windows MSYS2 environments (ocaml/opam#6862) and shell hook correctness (ocaml/opam#6859), with cross-references to ocaml/ocaml#14484 suggesting coordinated Windows effort
  • OxCaml compatibility tracking: the Merlin OxCaml parser recovery issue (ocaml/merlin#2045) and jsofocaml's OxCaml support PR (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2105) both active, reflecting ongoing effort to keep the tools group compatible with the OxCaml variant
  • Automated dependency update friction: Dependabot/bot PRs for Nix CI actions closed without merging in both merlin (ocaml/merlin#2046) and a long-lived flake.lock PR in ocaml-lsp (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1437) reflects a pattern of automated dependency PRs stalling due to upstream regressions

    • OxCaml

    Active week in oxcaml/oxcaml: type system advances, reaper stabilization, backend optimizations, and OCaml 5.4 merge progress.

    New Features

  • A new -O4 optimization level was introduced (oxcaml/oxcaml#5574), bundling the reaper dead-code elimination pass with -O3; the [@flambda_o4] attribute mirrors it at the per-function level.
  • The [@unpacked] attribute for C stub externals (oxcaml/oxcaml#5610) allows unboxed product types as C stub arguments by flattening each product component into separate native C arguments, while bytecode stubs receive a single boxed value.
  • A CFG block merging pass (-cfg-merge-blocks) was merged (oxcaml/oxcaml#5597), deduplicating equivalent basic blocks after register allocation, achieving up to 4.5% reduction in instruction count with only 0.2% build-time overhead.
  • Constant propagation in the CFG backend was extended to cover integer arithmetic (oxcaml/oxcaml#5545), floating-point arithmetic (oxcaml/oxcaml#5546), and values inferred from predecessor terminators (oxcaml/oxcaml#5562).
  • Multicore.spawn_result now accepts value_or_null resources (oxcaml/oxcaml#5579), aligning the multicore API with the null-safety story.
  • with kind_ constraints were added as part of abstract kinds part 3 (oxcaml/oxcaml#5629), completing the core feature set for abstract kinds ahead of a broader announcement.
  • A new Ptyp_newlayout AST node and layout_ syntax for locally abstract layouts was introduced, supporting layout-polymorphic type checking work.
  • ocamldep now scans with kind annotations (oxcaml/oxcaml#5628), ensuring correct dependency tracking for modules using abstract kinds.

    • Overview

  • Activity this week was concentrated in oxcaml/oxcaml; the other repositories in the group (oxcaml/opam-repository, oxcaml/merlin, oxcaml/jsofocaml, janestreet/opam-repository) had no recorded activity.
  • Twenty-eight PRs were merged in oxcaml/oxcaml, with over twenty contributors active across typing, backend, reaper, and 5.4 merge work.
  • Three parallel workstreams dominated: mode system expressiveness (oxcaml/oxcaml#5608, oxcaml/oxcaml#5602), reaper dead-code elimination stabilization (oxcaml/oxcaml#5593, oxcaml/oxcaml#5611, oxcaml/oxcaml#5612), and the OCaml 5.4 upstream merge (oxcaml/oxcaml#5618, oxcaml/oxcaml#5599, oxcaml/oxcaml#5582).
  • Backend infrastructure investment continued with CFG block merging (oxcaml/oxcaml#5597) and extended constant propagation (oxcaml/oxcaml#5545, oxcaml/oxcaml#5546, oxcaml/oxcaml#5562).

    • Activity

  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5608 proposes write and observable modes, introducing a partial-order diamond where read and write are incomparable; a bit-vector solver encoding makes this as efficient as simpler alternatives.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5627 proposes optimized Patricia trees bitpacking two ints together, delivering 3–11% compile-time speedups and up to 19% reduced allocations on key compiler files.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5630 hoists primitive repr tables out of prim_has_valid_reprs, avoiding repeated reconstruction of large String.Map values and achieving up to 1.79× faster compilation of modules with many external declarations.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5623 adds a CI workflow for continuation specialization, expanding test coverage for the match-in-match optimization.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5615 removes the ~level parameter from jkind comparison/violation APIs via a level_fresh sentinel, simplifying call sites across 14 files.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5601 extends with-bounds to support external modalities, allowing types like type 'a t : value mod portable external_ with 'a @@ external_.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5602 adds syntax for mode constraints without a type — (expr : @ modes) — and updates pprintast accordingly.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5569 works to remove legacy mode syntax from the AST, making pprintast emit new-style mode annotations.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5517 merged abstract kinds part 2.5, adding kind declarations in recursive modules with cycle detection.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5498 merged the canonical layout poly value description, implementing parsing, printing, and inclusion checks for layout-polymorphic value signatures.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5575 fixed buggy abstract kinds error messages, including a fatal_error triggered during error printing.
  • Multiple reaper fixes merged: oxcaml/oxcaml#5593 (zero_alloc hack for local fields), oxcaml/oxcaml#5611 (improved error messages), oxcaml/oxcaml#5612 (unboxed arguments with no sources), oxcaml/oxcaml#5619 (local fields under -O4), oxcaml/oxcaml#5595 (Not_found fatal error wrapper), oxcaml/oxcaml#5590 (stop exporting toplevel functions in cmx).
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5588 added a reaper + local value slots CI job to expand coverage.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5609 and oxcaml/oxcaml#5589 fixed SIMD gather register allocation by marking the index operand as overwritten and refreshing the index register during instruction selection.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5625 reverted then oxcaml/oxcaml#5580 re-merged an unboxed GADT jkind projection fix after verifying the internal codebase.
  • Several 5.4 merge PRs landed: oxcaml/oxcaml#5618 (boot-compiler build fixes), oxcaml/oxcaml#5599 (printer conflicts), oxcaml/oxcaml#5582 (env operation renames), oxcaml/oxcaml#5504 (lambda conflicts), oxcaml/oxcaml#5585 (root file fixes).
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5577 passes magic number versions via ./configure, simplifying minting new tags.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5576 refactored the reaper by extracting generic datalog helpers into a separate module.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5002 added equality functions for CFG basic and terminator instructions as infrastructure for the block merging pass.

    • Notable Discussions

  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5608: Richard Eisenberg and Nailen Matschke debated whether the write/observable diamond should use separate non-diamond axes internally for performance; Nailen Matschke demonstrated that a bit-vector encoding makes the diamond approach equally efficient.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5600: Nick Barnes identified an edge case in parallel Memprof where a near-zero-lambda profile started after stopping could trigger assertion failures, and proposed precise fixes for the config invalidation race.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5544: Luke Maurer conducted extensive review of the slambda fracturing pass, with Jack Rickard iterating on the design.
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#5597: Vesa Karvonen raised questions about hash function correctness and whether mutable fields (like terminator) cause problems for block equality hashing in the CFG block merging pass.

    • Emerging Trends

  • The reaper pass is stabilizing rapidly, with fixes for local fields, zero_alloc interactions, and error messages (oxcaml/oxcaml#5593, oxcaml/oxcaml#5611, oxcaml/oxcaml#5619) suggesting it is approaching production readiness at -O4.
  • Abstract kinds are nearing feature completeness with recursive module support (oxcaml/oxcaml#5517) and with kind_ constraints (oxcaml/oxcaml#5629) now implemented, setting up for a broader public announcement.
  • The mode system continues to expand, with write/observable modes (oxcaml/oxcaml#5608), external modality in with-bounds (oxcaml/oxcaml#5601), and improved syntax (oxcaml/oxcaml#5602) all progressing in parallel.
  • CFG backend infrastructure around block equality and constant propagation (oxcaml/oxcaml#5002, oxcaml/oxcaml#5545, oxcaml/oxcaml#5546, oxcaml/oxcaml#5562) is being built out systematically by Xavier Clerc, enabling increasingly sophisticated optimizations.
  • The OCaml 5.4 merge effort spans multiple parallel PRs across runtime, stdlib, lambda, parsing, and typing subsystems (oxcaml/oxcaml#5618, oxcaml/oxcaml#5599, oxcaml/oxcaml#5582, oxcaml/oxcaml#5504).

    • OCaml Core

    Bytecode optimization hints land for Js_of_ocaml/Wasm_of_ocaml, faster UTF-8 normalization, typing fixes, and runtime bug fixes.

    New Features

  • ocaml/ocaml#13438 Bytecode optimization hints: the bytecode compiler now preserves optimization hints from the Lambda IR (closure kinds, immutable blocks, array lengths, C call details) in a new HINT section in .cmo and .cma files, enabled with -bytecode-hints. This allows Jérôme Vouillon's Jsofocaml and Wasmofocaml to access type-level information previously discarded at the bytecode stage.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14618 Faster UTF-8 normalization outside the ASCII range was merged, optimizing the Misc.Stdlib unicode normalization path. Contributed by Stefan Muenzel, reviewed by Gabriel Scherer, Daniel Bünzli, and Florian Angeletti.

    • Overview

  • Activity this week was concentrated in ocaml/ocaml; ocaml/RFCs had no recorded activity.
  • Nine PRs were merged in ocaml/ocaml, covering a major bytecode feature (ocaml/ocaml#13438), a performance improvement (ocaml/ocaml#14618), typing fixes (ocaml/ocaml#14626, ocaml/ocaml#14638), a runtime bug fix (ocaml/ocaml#14635), and documentation/test improvements.
  • Sixteen new PRs were opened across the compiler, runtime, and typing areas.
  • Notable open issues include bytecode heap corruption with effects (ocaml/ocaml#14644), a missing GC root in reperform (ocaml/ocaml#14647), and an ARM Thumb mode instruction selection bug (ocaml/ocaml#14646).

    • Activity

  • ocaml/ocaml#14626 Warning 16 false positive with module-dependent functions fixed by Alistair: the typechecker now correctly handles function types with module-dependent parameters when determining whether an optional argument is unerasable.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14638 is_inferred now traverses local opens correctly, fixing the issue reported in ocaml/ocaml#14629 where a let open expression prevented proper detection of optional argument elimination. Merged by Florian Angeletti.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14635 caml_floatarray_gather control flow bug fixed by Marc Lasson: Float.Array.sub, Float.Array.append, and Float.Array.concat could return a non-empty array when the result should have been [||].
  • ocaml/ocaml#14645 Ephemeron GC corner case documented by Damien Doligez to prevent future confusion around ephemeron marking during the major GC.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14617 The ocaml_deprecated_cli alert is now made fatal in compiler development flags by Florian Angeletti, enforcing migration away from deprecated CLI patterns.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14640 A surplus argument in the Fun.protect test was fixed by Jérôme Vouillon.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14648 Modular explicits: optional arguments are elided for functional arguments to higher-order functions in the Lambda IR, opened by Florian Angeletti as part of ongoing modular explicit work.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14646 ARM Thumb mode: Xavier Leroy opened a fix to avoid using the TBH (Table Branch Halfword) instruction in Thumb mode, which can cause issues on some ARM targets.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14647 Missing GC root for continuation in reperform opened by Vincent Laviron as a fix for the interpreter's handling of effects.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14636 Ban unsafe primitive aliases inside recursive modules proposed by Nailen Matschke to prevent potential unsoundness.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14642 Runtime cleanup-at-exit improvement proposed by Gabriel Scherer: caml_shutdown would be ignored rather than cause errors when other domains remain running.

    • Notable Discussions

  • ocaml/ocaml#14634 Gabriel Scherer opened a discussion on what should be the default minor heap size, noting that the current 256Kword (2MiB) default has not changed since 2011 and that allocation-heavy benchmarks with OCAMLRUNPARAM=s=2M often show 2x speedups. The discussion explores sizing relative to L3 cache or total RAM.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14644 Thibaut Mattio reported bytecode heap corruption when using try Effect.perform with Effect.Unhandled under a deep effect handler, a likely regression related to continuation representation changes in ocaml/ocaml#14469.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14639 Raphaël Proust reported a bug where a labelled argument of a labelled tuple gets its labels confused in the typechecker.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14630 Kate reported a regression in 5.5 where "The signature for this packaged module couldn't be inferred" is incorrectly raised in the presence of recursive functions and first-class modules.
  • ocaml/ocaml#14594 Ongoing discussion around segfaults and timeouts on parallel tests in cleanup-at-exit mode, tracked by Olivier Nicole with a proposed fix via ocaml/ocaml#14642 from Gabriel Scherer.

    • Emerging Trends

  • Bytecode backend as a vehicle for JavaScript/WebAssembly optimization: ocaml/ocaml#13438 adds a new HINT section to bytecode files so tools like Jsofocaml can access Lambda-level information (closure kinds, C call details, mutability) that was previously unavailable at the bytecode level, controlled by a new -bytecode-hints flag.
  • Modular explicits continue active development with Florian Angeletti's work on eliding optional arguments in the Lambda IR (ocaml/ocaml#14648) and Gabriel Scherer's refactoring of Typeopt.is_function_type (ocaml/ocaml#14631, ocaml/ocaml#14632) to handle Tfunctor.
  • Effects and continuations stability: both the heap corruption bug (ocaml/ocaml#14644) and the missing GC root in reperform (ocaml/ocaml#14647) point to ongoing hardening of the effects runtime.
  • Typing precision improvements from Alistair (University of Cambridge) continue with multiple open PRs addressing let-rec approximation, polymorphic patterns, and warning 16 correctness.

    • Multicore

    Eio saw filesystem API proposals from a contributor; all other multicore repos were quiet this week.

    Overview

  • Activity this week was confined to ocaml-multicore/eio; the remaining eight repositories (domainslib, ocaml-uring, meio, saturn, eio-trace, picos, kcas, ocaml-iomux) recorded no new PRs, issues, or commits
  • Two open items in eio are awaiting merge/resolution: ocaml-multicore/eio#833 (approved PR adding missing_ok to Eio.Path.unlink) and ocaml-multicore/eio#831 (proposal for tempdir utilities)
  • Both items were authored by Volker Diels-Grabsch and reviewed by Patrick Ferris

    • Activity

  • Volker Diels-Grabsch opened ocaml-multicore/eio#833 adding an optional missing_ok parameter to Eio.Path.unlink, allowing callers to silently ignore missing-file errors; the PR addresses ocaml-multicore/eio#828, is small (8 additions, 3 deletions across 2 files), and has been approved by Patrick Ferris
  • Volker Diels-Grabsch also opened ocaml-multicore/eio#831 proposing Eio.Stdenv.tmp, Eio.Path.open_temp_dir, and Eio.Path.with_temp_dir convenience APIs; design feedback from Patrick Ferris is shaping the direction of the proposal

    • Notable Discussions

  • Patrick Ferris responded to the tempdir proposal ocaml-multicore/eio#831 noting that Eio must not depend on eio.unix, so run_in_systhread is not directly usable; he suggested routing the temp-directory path through Stdenv for backend portability (covering /tmp, $TMPDIR, and the Windows GetTempPath equivalent), and raised whether cleanup should be opt-out rather than always automatic
  • Patrick Ferris approved ocaml-multicore/eio#833, commenting "this looks good to me"

    • Emerging Trends

  • Volker Diels-Grabsch is contributing a set of filesystem convenience utilities to eio — missing_ok for unlink (ocaml-multicore/eio#833) and tempdir lifecycle management (ocaml-multicore/eio#831) — filling gaps users currently handle manually via Eio.Stdenv.fs and Filename from the standard library
  • Backend portability is a recurring design constraint in eio API additions, as seen in the tempdir discussion (ocaml-multicore/eio#831) where Unix-specific implementation paths must be avoided to keep the API usable across all eio backends
entry.summary: Dune 3.22.0~alpha1 released; OxCaml saw 28 PRs with -O4 level and reaper advances; bytecode hints merged in compiler for Js_of_ocaml.

entry.title: Week 10, 2026: 63 PRs merged with type system fixes, backend optimizations, and new developer tooling features
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Core Added Fun.todo function to signal unimplemented functionality with code location support and optional todo alert in ocaml/ocaml#14525 by Olivier Nicole
  • OCaml Core Improved warning 16 (unerasable-optional-argument) detection to properly handle module-dependent function types (Tfunctor) in ocaml/ocaml#14512 by Alistair
  • OCaml Core Optimized UTF-8 lexeme processing in the compiler in ocaml/ocaml#14620 by Gabriel Scherer
  • OCaml Core Made continuation objects more efficient by reducing from two fields to one in ocaml/ocaml#14469
  • OCaml Core Fixed uncaught Cannot_apply exception when mixing polymorphic types and unboxed constructors in ocaml/ocaml#14604 by Gabriel Scherer
  • OxCaml Improved register allocation by only reloading loop invariant registers in oxcaml/oxcaml#5514
  • OxCaml Optimized shift operations by eliminating unnecessary sign extensions in oxcaml/oxcaml#5535
  • OxCaml Avoided redundant sign extensions in Cmm builtins returning int32 in oxcaml/oxcaml#5550
  • OxCaml Replaced array block index syntax with explicit %unsafearrayidx primitives in oxcaml/oxcaml#5556 by Ryan Tjoa
  • OxCaml Fixed missing mode-crossing in functional record update in oxcaml/oxcaml#5564 by Stephen Dolan
  • OxCaml Added static computation framework with new tlambda→slambda→rawlambda pipeline in oxcaml/oxcaml#5430 by Jack Rickard
  • OxCaml Exposed Domain.maxdomaincount for reliable multicore detection in oxcaml/oxcaml#5522 by Stephen Dolan
  • OxCaml Improved type recovery in function applications with argument type mismatches in oxcaml/merlin#222 by Liam Stevenson
  • OxCaml Synchronized merlin with upstream OCaml compiler version 5.2.0minus-32 in oxcaml/merlin#224 by Liam Stevenson
  • OCaml Tools Fixed Dune tar extraction compatibility on OpenBSD by passing explicit decompression flags in ocaml/dune#13688 by Ali Caglayan
