  • OCaml Core Manual updates including new native debugger chapter covering GDB and LLDB support by Tim McGilchrist in ocaml/ocaml#13747
  • OCaml Core Runtime_events.Timestamp documentation improvements clarifying timestamp precision and behavior by Raphaël Proust in ocaml/ocaml#14293
  • OCaml Ecosystem OCaml 5.4 reference manual update with improved native debugger documentation by Florian Angeletti in ocaml/opam-repository#28722

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    Package ecosystem activity with Rocq releases, Sail 0.20, ppxlib 0.37.0, and mobile UI improvements for ocaml.org

    New Features

  • OCaml 5.4 reference manual update with improved native debugger documentation by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/opam-repository#28722)
  • Sail 0.20 released with Rocq semantics implementation - core stepwise semantics now in Rocq, improved C++ backend support across 13 packages by Alasdair Armstrong (ocaml/opam-repository#28713)
  • Rocq 9.1.0 and 9.0.1 releases by Guillaume Melquiond bringing latest Coq fork updates (ocaml/opam-repository#28706, ocaml/opam-repository#28707)
  • ppxlib 0.37.0 released with ppxlib-tools by Nathan Rebours (ocaml/opam-repository#28686), including compatibility fix for ppx_yojson (ocaml/opam-repository#28717)
  • lambdapi 3.0.0 released with new tactics (simplify, orelse, repeat, eval), string literal builtins, and websearch options by Frédéric Blanqui (ocaml/opam-repository#28178)
  • miou 0.5.0 performance improvement - now uses poll(2)/ppoll(2) instead of select(3P) for better concurrency by Calascibetta Romain (ocaml/opam-repository#28714)
  • domain-name 0.5.0 bug fix disallowing trailing hyphen (-) in host labels per RFC requirements by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#28709)
  • ca-certs-nss 3.117 security update with latest Mozilla NSS X.509 trust anchors from 2025-10-03 by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#28712)
  • coq-lsp 0.2.4+9.1 released by Emilio Jesús Gallego Arias (ocaml/opam-repository#28534)
  • Mobile package page layout improved by moving table of contents from right sidebar to mobile-friendly location, fixing space consumption issue on small screens by Seth Rider (ocaml/ocaml.org#3369)
  • ocaml.nvim Neovim plugin announced providing advanced LSP features like typed holes navigation and semantic code movement (ocaml/ocaml.org#3372)

    • Overview

  • Package ecosystem growth with 20 merged package updates in ocaml/opam-repository including releases for Rocq 9.x, Sail 0.20, ppxlib 0.37.0, and lambdapi 3.0.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#28706, ocaml/opam-repository#28713, ocaml/opam-repository#28686, ocaml/opam-repository#28178)
  • Website improvements for ocaml/ocaml.org with mobile UI fixes for package documentation pages and editor tooling announcements (ocaml/ocaml.org#3369, ocaml/ocaml.org#3372)
  • OCaml 5.4 preparation beginning with preview packages, reference manual documentation improvements, and ocamlformat support work (ocaml/opam-repository#28722, ocaml/opam-repository#28716)
  • Security updates with ca-certs-nss 3.117 and base package checksum verification improvements (ocaml/opam-repository#28712, ocaml/opam-repository#28718)
  • Community content additions including Gospel ecosystem status update and ocaml.nvim plugin announcement on backstage blog (ocaml/ocaml.org#3352, ocaml/ocaml.org#3372)
  • 26 contributors actively participated across both repositories with package releases, UI improvements, and content additions

    • Activity

  • Catala 1.0.0~beta proposed by Denis Merigoux - domain-specific language for tax code specification with literate programming for legislative texts (ocaml/opam-repository#28723)
  • otp 0.2 package proposed by A.G. - RFC6238 time-based One Time Password implementation with HMAC-SHA1, QR code generation, and authenticator integration (ocaml/opam-repository#28704)
  • Fmlib 0.6.0 update opened by @hbr with breaking changes including more generic HTTP requests in fmlib_browser and simple tasks in Command module (ocaml/opam-repository#28732)
  • ocaml-dockerfile 8.3.3 update by Mark Elvers covering 3 packages (dockerfile, dockerfile-cmd, dockerfile-opam) from OCurrent project (ocaml/opam-repository#28736)
  • OCaml 5.4 preview preparation work by Kate including ocamlformat support and marking preview packages unavailable (ocaml/opam-repository#28716, ocaml/opam-repository#28719, ocaml/opam-repository#28733)
  • Additional package updates opened including Nicolás Ojeda Bär proposing genjsapi 1.1.6 (ocaml/opam-repository#28721), Enrico Tassi proposing elpi 3.4.2 (ocaml/opam-repository#28729), Kaustubh Maske Patil proposing handlebars-ml 0.2.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#28730), Marcello Seri proposing doi2bib 0.7.9 (ocaml/opam-repository#28703), and Tobias Mock proposing raylib/raygui 1.5.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#28680)
  • Package maintenance updates merged including David Sancho releasing htmlofjsx 0.0.6 (ocaml/opam-repository#28711), Oliver Friedmann releasing mlsolver 1.5 and fadecider 0.7 (ocaml/opam-repository#28701, ocaml/opam-repository#28702), Stephen Sherratt releasing climate 0.8.5 (ocaml/opam-repository#28708), Anton Yabchinskiy releasing pcrc 0.25.2 (ocaml/opam-repository#28699), Jason D. Nielsen releasing p5scm 0.5.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#28700), and Calascibetta Romain releasing spoke 0.0.4 (ocaml/opam-repository#28640)
  • Dune Package Management migration for OCaml.org build system remains under active development by @sabine, with related announcement PR (ocaml/ocaml.org#3152) closed in favor of merged content in (ocaml/ocaml.org#3281)
  • Gospel ecosystem blog post published by @sabine describing ready-to-use testing tools and evolving proof capabilities (ocaml/ocaml.org#3352)
  • Automated content scraping merged two updates adding OCaml community blog posts and videos (ocaml/ocaml.org#3374, ocaml/ocaml.org#3373)
  • Graph exercise adjacency list corrected to include missing h vertex entry for proper bidirectional representation by @feefs (ocaml/ocaml.org#3371)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Rocq ecosystem expansion with releases of 9.0.1 and 9.1.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#28706, ocaml/opam-repository#28707), related packages like coq-lsp (ocaml/opam-repository#28534), and Sail integrating Rocq semantics (ocaml/opam-repository#28713) showing growing adoption of the Coq fork
  • OCaml 5.4 preparation beginning with preview packages, documentation updates including reference manual improvements (ocaml/opam-repository#28722), and compatibility work (ocaml/opam-repository#28716, ocaml/opam-repository#28719, ocaml/opam-repository#28733)
  • Large coordinated releases such as Sail's 13-package update (ocaml/opam-repository#28713) demonstrating ecosystem maturation and better coordination of multi-package projects
  • Security infrastructure maintenance with regular updates to ca-certs-nss following Mozilla certificate releases (ocaml/opam-repository#28712) and checksum verification improvements (ocaml/opam-repository#28718)
  • Domain-specific languages reaching production readiness with Catala 1.0.0~beta for tax code (ocaml/opam-repository#28723) and Sail for processor instruction semantics (ocaml/opam-repository#28713)
  • Mobile-first design refinements addressing usability issues on package documentation pages with responsive layout adjustments (ocaml/ocaml.org#3369)
  • Editor tooling expansion through new plugin releases targeting different editor ecosystems with Neovim support (ocaml/ocaml.org#3372) following earlier Emacs support
  • Formal verification accessibility highlighted through Gospel ecosystem maturation (ocaml/ocaml.org#3352), emphasizing practical testing tools available today while proof capabilities develop

    • OCaml Tools

    OxCaml parametric libraries gaining tooling support, opam 2.5.0~alpha1 released, and package management features maturing

    New Features

  • Package search command in ocaml/dune via dune pkg search for finding packages by name using substring or glob patterns (ocaml/dune#12547)
  • Concurrent test execution with watch mode in ocaml/dune allowing dune runtest while watch server is active (ocaml/dune#12473, ocaml/dune#8114)
  • Completion for inlined record labels in ocaml/merlin fixing pattern matching against constructors with inline record syntax (ocaml/merlin#1978)
  • Multi-file support in ocaml/odoc for markdown-generate and html-generate commands accepting multiple .odocl files (ocaml/odoc#1388)
  • Shell initialization improvements in ocaml/opam including writing to .bashrc instead of .profile for Bash users (ocaml/opam#6603)
  • AppArmor support in ocaml/opam install script resolving issues on Ubuntu 24.04 (ocaml/opam#6647, fixes ocaml/opam#5968)
  • Consistent NaN handling in ocsigen/jsofocaml across JavaScript engines by converting signaling NaNs to quiet NaNs (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2110)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/dune led activity with package management features, OxCaml parametric library support, extensive stanza refactoring, and concurrent test execution (ocaml/dune#12547, ocaml/dune#12473, ocaml/dune#12550)
  • ocaml/opam released version 2.5.0~alpha1 with shell initialization improvements, platform-specific fixes, and testing infrastructure enhancements (ocaml/opam#6744)
  • ocaml/merlin fixed completion for inlined record labels and updated CI for OCaml 5.4 support (ocaml/merlin#1978)
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml delivered runtime bug fixes, WebAssembly backend cleanup, and ongoing OCaml 5.4 compatibility work (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2110, ocsigen/jsofocaml#2107)
  • ocaml/odoc enhanced markdown generator with multi-file support and improved CLI organization (ocaml/odoc#1388)
  • ocaml/ocaml-lsp saw new PRs for labelled argument autocompletion and metrics precision improvements (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1564, ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1565)
  • ocaml/ocamlfind received Windows build fixes for OCaml 5.0+ on Cygwin and MSYS2 (ocaml/ocamlfind#112)

    • Activity

  • Dune internal refactoring by Rudi Grinberg with extensive stanza definition cleanup removing boilerplate and duplicate code (ocaml/dune#12593, ocaml/dune#12592, ocaml/dune#12594, ocaml/dune#12595)
  • Package management autolocking ongoing work by Marek Kubica making lock files build targets in ocaml/dune (ocaml/dune#11775)
  • Melange improvements by Antonio Nuno Monteiro fixing .cmj dependency tracking with include_qualified in ocaml/dune (ocaml/dune#12531)
  • LSP completion intelligence work by Tom Ekander adding labelled argument autocompletion with : trigger character in ocaml/ocaml-lsp (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1564)
  • Metrics precision improvement by Tim ats switching to Unix.gettimeofday for sub-second timestamps in ocaml/ocaml-lsp (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1565)
  • MLX file formatting support by David Sancho integrating ocamlformat-mlx for .mlx files in ocaml/ocaml-lsp (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1528)
  • WebAssembly eval function PR opened by Jérôme Vouillon for JavaScript eval access in ocsigen/jsofocaml (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2108)
  • OCaml 5.4 CI testing ongoing by @hhugo in ocsigen/jsofocaml, blocked on wasmofocaml compatibility (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2103)
  • Opam post-release work including version bumps and installer updates following 2.5.0~alpha1 release in ocaml/opam (ocaml/opam#6747, ocaml/opam#6749)

    • Notable Discussions

  • Labelled argument autocompletion design extensive discussion in ocaml/ocaml-lsp with Ulysse raising concerns about : trigger character scope, Tom Ekander demonstrating usefulness in large codebases, and proposals for configurable construct query behavior (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1564)
  • Package lock directory placement ongoing debate in ocaml/dune about whether lock directories should default to _build versus worktree, balancing portability against repository noise (ocaml/dune#12097)
  • WebAssembly eval function behavior discussion in ocsigen/jsofocaml between @hhugo and Jérôme Vouillon about ensuring runtime consistency between Wasm and JS backends (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2108)
  • Admin script cleanup discussion in ocaml/opam between Kate and David Allsopp regarding removal of unused scripts and fate of opam-admin.top (ocaml/opam#6750)
  • Stdout vs stderr output discussion in ocaml/dune about improving shell pipeline compatibility for informational commands (ocaml/dune#12586)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Parametric libraries ecosystem maturation with coordinated tooling support across build system (ocaml/dune#12550), IDE (ocaml/merlin#1978), LSP (ocaml/dune#12536), and compilation targets (ocsigen/jsofocaml), representing investment in OxCaml feature completeness
  • Package management feature convergence between Dune and opam with search capabilities (ocaml/dune#12547), lock file improvements (ocaml/dune#12549), and autolocking work (ocaml/dune#11775) moving toward production-ready package management in Dune
  • Editor experience refinement focus across tools with completion improvements in ocaml/merlin (ocaml/merlin#1978) and ocaml/ocaml-lsp (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1564), metrics precision (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1565), and MLX formatting support (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1528)
  • Platform-specific hardening emphasis with Windows fixes in ocaml/ocamlfind (ocaml/ocamlfind#112) and ocaml/opam (ocaml/opam#6592), AppArmor support (ocaml/opam#6647), and Alpine Linux hardening (ocaml/opam#6742)
  • WebAssembly backend investment continuing in ocsigen/jsofocaml with runtime cleanup (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2109), eval function support (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2108), and WASI runtime development (ocsigen/jsofocaml#1831)
  • OCaml compiler evolution tracking shown through 5.4 adoption in ocaml/merlin and ocsigen/jsofocaml, compiler-libs integration (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2111), and consuming compiler hints (ocsigen/jsofocaml#1721)

    • OxCaml

    Metaprogramming advances, Merlin integration of quotation infrastructure, and js_of_ocaml patch maintenance

    New Features

  • New quotation API functions Code.Closed.to_exp and Code.Closed.print added to CamlinternalQuote module for converting closed code to expressions and formatted printing in oxcaml/oxcaml#4896
  • Quotation and metaprogramming support integrated into Merlin via new CamlinternalQuote module (2,805 lines) providing infrastructure for compile-time code generation with variable binding, staging, and AST manipulation facilities in oxcaml/merlin#191
  • Layout polymorphism language extension (Layout_poly) with maturity levels (alpha, beta, stable) allowing types to be polymorphic over memory representations in oxcaml/merlin#191
  • New jkind primitives including immediate64_or_null for nullable immediate64 values and kind_of_idx for block indices with mode crossing support in oxcaml/merlin#191
  • Stage tracking in environment with new stage type and operations enter_quotation, enter_splice, and check_no_open_quotations for managing multi-stage compilation contexts in oxcaml/merlin#191
  • bits8 and bits16 kinds now allowed without requiring the small_numbers extension in oxcaml/oxcaml#4898, improving library integration while maintaining upstream compatibility
  • Improved location information in pattern matching for better debugger stepping behavior and source code position reporting in oxcaml/oxcaml#4884
  • Enhanced debugger register handling in Name_for_debugger operations with proper register substitution and unknown location handling in oxcaml/oxcaml#4880
  • Shrink-wrapping testing now enabled in CI through new option to regalloc.exe tool for inserting prologues in oxcaml/oxcaml#4892
  • Fixed over-expunged toplevel by removing unboxed types (Float_u, Iarray, Int32_u, Int64_u, Nativeint_u) not in compatible Stdlib in oxcaml/oxcaml#4877
  • Fixed loading paths from paths file bug in load_path.ml where variable shadowing caused incorrect path resolution for -I-paths flag in oxcaml/oxcaml#4878
  • New compiler warning 215 (Implied_attribute) detecting when attributes are redundant because they're implied by other attributes in oxcaml/merlin#191

    • Activity

  • Metaprogramming infrastructure advanced in oxcaml/oxcaml with quotation evaluation fixes by Jack Rickard addressing exception handling and primitive addresses in oxcaml/oxcaml#4896, double-linking prevention for eval support files by Mark Shinwell in oxcaml/oxcaml#4895, and ongoing work on Camlinternaleval dependencies in oxcaml/oxcaml#4899 and oxcaml/oxcaml#4900
  • Flambda2 optimization work delivered n-way join analysis exposure by Basile Clément in oxcaml/oxcaml#4821, datalog Virtual_machine.iterator cleanup in oxcaml/oxcaml#4897, and reverted static constant sharing in oxcaml/oxcaml#4893 due to backtrace issues
  • Backend and type system improvements included CFG terminator simplification revert due to loop information issues by Xavier Clerc in oxcaml/oxcaml#4885, private Reg.t refactoring in progress by Greta Yorsh in oxcaml/oxcaml#4888, and path loading fix by Andrei Odintsov in oxcaml/oxcaml#4878
  • Modes system refinement with 10 new PRs opened including continuation handling improvements by Aspen Smith in oxcaml/oxcaml#4901, global/aliased implications by @dkalinichenko-js in oxcaml/oxcaml#4889, mode variable conversion in oxcaml/oxcaml#4792, exception crossing improvements in oxcaml/oxcaml#4891, and external array renaming in oxcaml/oxcaml#4890
  • Effects system development progressing with continuation handling refactoring in oxcaml/oxcaml#4901, preemption support work by Aspen Smith in oxcaml/oxcaml#4881, and domain lock unification by Stephen Dolan in oxcaml/oxcaml#4769
  • Infrastructure and tooling updates included GDB memsearch utility improvements by Nick Barnes in oxcaml/oxcaml#4886, const qualifiers for camlstartup functions in oxcaml/oxcaml#4882, cfgtool.exe development in oxcaml/oxcaml#4596, and toplevel expunging fix by David Allsopp in oxcaml/oxcaml#4877
  • Additional work includes Unix local/read annotations by Vesa Karvonen in oxcaml/oxcaml#4830, CFG value propagation for floats by Xavier Clerc in oxcaml/oxcaml#4879, extended CFG terminator simplification in oxcaml/oxcaml#4807, and documentation typo fixes by @tkoukpari in oxcaml/oxcaml#4883

    • Emerging Trends

  • Metaprogramming as core feature with investment in quotation infrastructure across oxcaml/oxcaml#4896, oxcaml/oxcaml#4895, oxcaml/oxcaml#4899, oxcaml/oxcaml#4900, and integration into Merlin via oxcaml/merlin#191
  • Mode-aware type system evolution with multiple PRs refining uniqueness, locality, and sharing constraints in oxcaml/oxcaml#4889, oxcaml/oxcaml#4792, oxcaml/oxcaml#4891, and global/aliased relationship work
  • Backend optimization caution demonstrated by reverts in oxcaml/oxcaml#4893 and oxcaml/oxcaml#4885 when optimizations cause backtrace or loop analysis issues, prioritizing correctness
  • Effects system maturation with continuation handling in oxcaml/oxcaml#4901, preemption support in oxcaml/oxcaml#4881, and domain lock unification in oxcaml/oxcaml#4769
  • Language extensibility through maturity-tracked extensions (alpha/beta/stable levels) enabling gradual rollout of experimental features like layout polymorphism in oxcaml/merlin#191
  • Upstream compatibility focus with work allowing erasable features like bits8/bits16 kinds without extensions in oxcaml/oxcaml#4898 and toplevel fixes in oxcaml/oxcaml#4877
  • Patch stability challenges in jsofocaml integration with recurring issues where resolved patches reappear in oxcaml/opam-repository#20 and oxcaml/opam-repository#19
  • AI-assisted development workflow with explicit acknowledgment of Claude for automated conflict resolution and compilation fixes in oxcaml/merlin#191

    • OCaml Core

    BLAKE128 hash migration merged, thread safety improvements, and ongoing tuple projections RFC discussion

    New Features

  • BLAKE128 hash migration for compiler CRCs replacing MD5 across all file formats (cmi, cmo, cmx, cmxs) and consistency checking by Vincent Laviron in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#13913)
  • New C API function caml_c_thread_register_in_domain for registering C threads in specific OCaml domains by Jack Joergensen in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#14275)
  • TSan fixes for C calls with many stack arguments affecting ARM64, POWER, RISC-V, s390x, and x86_64 architectures by Olivier Nicole in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#14255)
  • FlexDLL build improvements with new configuration options for MANIFEST_TOOL, RC (resource compiler), and FLEXLINKFLAGS, requiring FlexDLL >= 0.44 by Antonin Décimo in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#14034)
  • Type checker determinism improvements avoiding hash table iteration for types and terms by Vincent Laviron in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#14297, ocaml/ocaml#14299)
  • Manual updates including new native debugger chapter covering GDB and LLDB support by Tim McGilchrist in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#13747)
  • Runtime_events.Timestamp documentation improvements clarifying timestamp precision and behavior by Raphaël Proust in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#14293)
  • Symbol naming changes using $ instead of . to separate module from identifiers in symbols by Tim McGilchrist in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#13050)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/ocaml merged twelve PRs including the BLAKE128 hash migration (ocaml/ocaml#13913), thread safety improvements (ocaml/ocaml#14255, ocaml/ocaml#14275), and FlexDLL build enhancements (ocaml/ocaml#14034)
  • ocaml/RFCs continued discussion on tuple projections RFC (ocaml/RFCs#57) with focus on row-polymorphic tuples approach
  • New PRs include Hannes Mehnert proposing to make Hashtbl seeded by default (ocaml/ocaml#14291) and Gabriel Scherer addressing runtime memory safety in multiple areas (ocaml/ocaml#14303, ocaml/ocaml#14304, ocaml/ocaml#14305, ocaml/ocaml#14306)
  • Runtime improvements focused on thread safety with TSan fixes and new C API for domain-specific thread registration (ocaml/ocaml#14275)

    • Activity

  • Twelve new PRs opened in ocaml/ocaml including Hannes Mehnert proposing to make Hashtbl seeded by default (ocaml/ocaml#14291), deprecate Digest top-level bindings (ocaml/ocaml#14294), and preserve option R in runtime parameters (ocaml/ocaml#14292)
  • Runtime memory safety improvements by Gabriel Scherer addressing race conditions in minor GC (ocaml/ocaml#14306), memprof configuration (ocaml/ocaml#14304, ocaml/ocaml#14305), and backup thread synchronization (ocaml/ocaml#14303)
  • Thread sanitizer improvements by Olivier Nicole fixing POWER shadow stack accounting (ocaml/ocaml#14302), disabling flaky TSan test (ocaml/ocaml#14301), and improving pipe operator typechecking (ocaml/ocaml#14286)
  • Build and tooling improvements including Antonin Décimo improving mingw format specifiers (ocaml/ocaml#14308) and Tim McGilchrist fixing frame pointer tests (ocaml/ocaml#14295)
  • Documentation updates with Guillaume Munch-Maccagnoni clarifying thread registration constraints (ocaml/ocaml#14296) and Hannes Mehnert fixing CI typo (ocaml/ocaml#14309)
  • Tuple projections RFC discussion continued in ocaml/RFCs with Alistair and Florian Angeletti debating the scope of row-polymorphic tuples (ocaml/RFCs#57)

    • Notable Discussions

  • One-liner comment syntax proposal by David Wong exploring the addition of single-line comment syntax to OCaml in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#12066)
  • Row-polymorphic tuples debate in ocaml/RFCs with Florian Angeletti suggesting separation into a separate RFC and Alistair clarifying that the current tuple projections RFC only discusses them as a future compatibility consideration (ocaml/RFCs#57)
  • Hashtbl seeded by default proposal by Hannes Mehnert to improve security and prevent DoS attacks in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#14291)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Runtime memory safety focus with multiple PRs from Gabriel Scherer addressing race conditions and memory management in runtime components including minor GC (ocaml/ocaml#14306), memprof (ocaml/ocaml#14304, ocaml/ocaml#14305), and domain termination (ocaml/ocaml#14303)
  • Thread sanitizer testing becoming more comprehensive with Olivier Nicole fixing bugs across multiple architectures (ocaml/ocaml#14255, ocaml/ocaml#14302) and improving test coverage (ocaml/ocaml#14301)
  • Cryptographic hash migration from MD5 to BLAKE128 reflecting modern security practices and performance considerations (ocaml/ocaml#13913)
  • Build toolchain flexibility improvements for Windows/FlexDLL enabling better compiler selection and cross-platform support (ocaml/ocaml#14034, ocaml/ocaml#14308)
  • Compiler determinism as a continued focus with hash table iteration being eliminated from type and term generation (ocaml/ocaml#14297, ocaml/ocaml#14299)

    • Multicore
entry.summary: BLAKE128 hash migration and runtime safety focus in core, metaprogramming advances in OxCaml, and package management maturation in tools

entry.title: Week 41, 2025: OCaml 5.4.0 released with runtime quotations in OxCaml, package ecosystem expansion, and filesystem performance improvements
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Ecosystem OCaml 5.4.0 compiler officially released by Florian Angeletti with labelled tuples, immutable arrays, atomic record fields, four new standard library modules (Pair, Pqueue, Repr, Iarray), and profiling documentation (ocaml/opam-repository#28683, ocaml/ocaml.org#3353, release notes)
  • OxCaml Runtime quotations and metaprogramming system with new <[ ]> quotation syntax and $ splicing operator for runtime code generation, including stage tracking in the type system and AST representation in CamlInternalQuote module by Andrej Ivašković, Jack Rickard, and Mark Shinwell (oxcaml/oxcaml#4395, oxcaml/oxcaml#4852, oxcaml/oxcaml#4864, oxcaml/oxcaml#4874)
  • OxCaml Full jsofocaml compiler integration imported into oxcaml with JSIR mode for JavaScript compilation and complete backend support by Jacob Van Buren and Leo Lee (oxcaml/oxcaml#4730, oxcaml/oxcaml#4737, oxcaml/oxcaml#4739, oxcaml/oxcaml#4743)
  • OxCaml Block indices moved to stable production-ready status with new %unsafe_get_ptr and %unsafe_set_ptr primitives, improved flattened float field handling with unboxed types, and safety constraint disallowing block indices to [@atomic] fields by Ryan Tjoa and Chris Casinghino (oxcaml/oxcaml#4827, oxcaml/oxcaml#4824, oxcaml/oxcaml#4826, oxcaml/oxcaml#4828)
  • OCaml Tools OxCaml parameterized libraries implemented by @art-w in ocaml/dune adding new (parameters ...) field to library stanza requiring -parameter compiler flag (ocaml/dune#12336)
  • OCaml Tools Cram test conflict marker detection added to ocaml/dune via (conflict error|ignore) stanza option by Rudi Grinberg (ocaml/dune#12538)
  • OCaml Tools dune tools env command implemented for adding dev tools to PATH by Stephen Sherratt (ocaml/dune#12521)
  • OCaml Tools Opam exit code behavior fix for opam install --depext-only returning proper error code 20 by R. Boujbel (ocaml/opam#6516)
  • OCaml Tools Pin-depends handling fix for simulated pins during --deps-only operations by Kate (ocaml/opam#6611)
  • OCaml Core New C API function caml_c_thread_register_in_domain enables registering C threads in specific domains with caml_find_index_of_running_domain helper by Guillaume Munch-Maccagnoni (ocaml/ocaml#14275, commit 1f39a26)
  • OCaml Core GC root mishandling bug fixed in memprof.c preventing memory corruption by Sadiq Jaffer (ocaml/ocaml#14287)
  • OCaml Core Error handling during domain spawn improved fixing potential memory leaks and deadlocks by Guillaume Munch-Maccagnoni (ocaml/ocaml#12410)

  • For loop optimization approaches debated in oxcaml/oxcaml#4752 with Akshat proposing lambda simplification approach while Guillaume Bury noted simplif happens before inlining, related to implementation PRs by Xavier Clerc (oxcaml/oxcaml#4772, oxcaml/oxcaml#4807)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Metaprogramming infrastructure build-out with runtime quotations introducing <[ ]> syntax and $ splicing in oxcaml/oxcaml, ocaml-jit integration for JIT compilation, stage tracking in type system, and foundation for staged computation (oxcaml/oxcaml#4395, oxcaml/oxcaml#4852, oxcaml/oxcaml#4864, oxcaml/oxcaml#4874, oxcaml/oxcaml#4855, oxcaml/oxcaml#4856)
  • JavaScript backend maturation with full jsofocaml integration importing 300K+ lines of code in oxcaml/oxcaml, JSIR mode development, making ocamlj a fully-featured compiler, and coordinated opam package updates in oxcaml/opam-repository (oxcaml/oxcaml#4730, oxcaml/oxcaml#4737, oxcaml/oxcaml#4739, oxcaml/oxcaml#4743, oxcaml/oxcaml#4791, oxcaml/oxcaml#4753)
  • DWARF debugging improvements across oxcaml/oxcaml through continuous refinement including register availability analysis, better debuginfo for inlined code, experimental flags for testing new features, with consistent collaboration between Mark Shinwell and Greta Yorsh (oxcaml/oxcaml#4835, oxcaml/oxcaml#4870, oxcaml/oxcaml#4871, oxcaml/oxcaml#4872, oxcaml/oxcaml#4837, oxcaml/oxcaml#4863, oxcaml/oxcaml#4842, oxcaml/oxcaml#4834, oxcaml/oxcaml#4829)
  • Type system evolution in oxcaml/oxcaml with unboxed types moving to production through block indices stabilization, mode system refactoring for extensibility, jkind normalization fixes, and modality tracking improvements (oxcaml/oxcaml#4827, oxcaml/oxcaml#4824, oxcaml/oxcaml#4826, oxcaml/oxcaml#4828, oxcaml/oxcaml#4790, oxcaml/oxcaml#4777)
  • Package ecosystem expansion in oxcaml/opam-repository with Jane Street v0.18~preview.130.55+197 bringing latest experimental features, addition of widely-used OCaml libraries (ctypes, lwt, re, dune 3.20.2) ensuring broader compatibility with existing OCaml codebases (oxcaml/opam-repository#18, oxcaml/opam-repository@26cb9899)
  • CI and build infrastructure modernization across oxcaml/oxcaml through setup-ocaml adoption, speed optimizations saving 15+ seconds per job, Nix flake integration, and automated diff promotion workflows (oxcaml/oxcaml#4857, oxcaml/oxcaml#4858, oxcaml/oxcaml#4859, oxcaml/oxcaml#4711, oxcaml/oxcaml#4810)
  • Backend modularity refactoring in oxcaml/oxcaml for parameterized backends, splitting monolithic files like asmlink into three files, and preparing for multiple target architectures (oxcaml/oxcaml#4825, oxcaml/oxcaml#4838)
  • IDE tooling synchronization with oxcaml/merlin upstream merge incorporating compiler changes including runtime quotations support, demonstrating commitment to keeping editor integration current with language developments (oxcaml/merlin#191)

    • OCaml Core

    OCaml 5.4.0 release preparation merged with C API enhancements for domain-specific thread registration

    New Features

  • New C API function caml_c_thread_register_in_domain enables registering C threads in specific domains rather than just domain 0, with accompanying caml_find_index_of_running_domain helper function for looking up domain indices by unique ID in ocaml/ocaml (1f39a26, f8de0cb, ocaml/ocaml#14275)
  • Fixed GC root mishandling bug in memprof.c that could cause memory corruption in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#14287)
  • Improved error handling during domain spawn fixing potential memory leaks and deadlocks when rare errors occur during domain creation in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#12410)
  • Enhanced module signature pretty-printing to preserve (mod) and other escaped infix keyword operators in -dsource output in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#14279)
  • Updated C interface manual with documentation for the new thread registration API and domain lookup functions in ocaml/ocaml

    • Overview

  • OCaml 5.4.0 release preparation completed in ocaml/ocaml with highlights document and changelog updates merged (ocaml/ocaml#14284)
  • Runtime system improvements focused on multicore safety with C API enhancements for domain-specific thread registration (ocaml/ocaml#14275), GC root bug fixes (ocaml/ocaml#14287), and domain spawn error handling (ocaml/ocaml#12410)
  • Language design discussions active in ocaml/RFCs with one RFC withdrawn after community feedback (ocaml/RFCs#56) and ongoing tuple projections proposal under review (ocaml/RFCs#57)
  • Hash algorithm migration discussions initiated around deprecating MD5 in favor of Blake128 (ocaml/ocaml#14290) and switching Hashtbl to seeded by default (ocaml/ocaml#14291)
  • Cross-platform work progressing with Haiku native backend activation (ocaml/ocaml#14138), relocatable OCaml implementation (ocaml/ocaml#14245), and LoongArch architecture support (ocaml/ocaml#11974)

    • Activity

  • Florian Angeletti merged OCaml 5.4.0 release preparation including highlights document, changelog synchronization, and calendar updates in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#14284)
  • Olivier Nicole proposed pipe operator type-checking change to typecheck x |> f y as (f y x) instead of ((f y) x) for better compatibility with OxCaml variant in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#14286)
  • David Allsopp continuing work on relocatable OCaml implementation with PRs for search/suffix handling and relative libdir configuration in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#14245, ocaml/ocaml#14244)
  • Xavier Van de Woestyne progressing on Merlin typing recovery integration for better IDE error handling in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#14241)
  • Jan Midtgaard updated multicoretests compatibility to version 0.11 to match Domain.spawn error message changes in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#14285)
  • Anarchos working on Haiku native backend activation to bring OCaml native compilation support to Haiku OS in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#14138)
  • Kate proposing string splitting functions cut_on_char and rcut_on_char for String/Bytes/StringLabels modules in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#14068)
  • Emile Trotignon working on making -init flag work with -e option in toplevel in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#14190)
  • Yawar Amin proposing application let-operator ( let@ ) syntax addition in ocaml/ocaml (ocaml/ocaml#13698)
  • Sacha Ayoun withdrew the for...in syntax RFC following community feedback about syntactic sugar design tradeoffs in ocaml/RFCs (ocaml/RFCs#56)
  • Alistair continues developing tuple projections RFC proposing labeled and unlabeled tuple field access syntax in ocaml/RFCs (ocaml/RFCs#57)

    • Notable Discussions

  • Discussion about migrating from MD5 to Blake128 for user-facing Digest module APIs in ocaml/ocaml after internal compiler migration completed, with consideration of deprecation strategy and ecosystem impact (ocaml/ocaml#14290)
  • Proposal by Hannes Mehnert to change default Hashtbl behavior to seeded (non-deterministic) unless explicitly disabled in ocaml/ocaml, requiring investigation of compiler dependency on deterministic hashing and potential opam package breakage (ocaml/ocaml#14291)
  • Discussion in ocaml/RFCs centered on syntactic sugar justification thresholds, with @Makefile-dot-in arguing that OCaml's equivalence between (fun x -> e) y and let y = x in e eliminates the need for special for-each syntax unlike other languages (ocaml/RFCs#56)
  • Olivier Nicole raised pipe operator typing behavior in ocaml/ocaml for compatibility between upstream OCaml and OxCaml variant, with implications for code portability (ocaml/ocaml#14286)
  • Sacha Ayoun opened discussion about snapshot test fragility in ocaml/ocaml when standard library line numbers change, seeking solutions for more robust testing (ocaml/ocaml#14289)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Runtime system safety improvements with multiple merged fixes for domain creation error handling (ocaml/ocaml#12410), thread registration (ocaml/ocaml#14275), and GC root management (ocaml/ocaml#14287) showing continued focus on multicore stability in ocaml/ocaml
  • Migration away from MD5 continuing with Blake128 now used internally in compiler (ocaml/ocaml#13913) and discussion of deprecating user-facing MD5 APIs in Digest module (ocaml/ocaml#14290) in ocaml/ocaml
  • Security-conscious defaults discussion with proposals for seeded hash tables by default (ocaml/ocaml#14291) and consideration of attack resistance versus determinism trade-offs in ocaml/ocaml
  • Cross-platform expansion efforts including Haiku native backend work (ocaml/ocaml#14138) and LoongArch architecture support (ocaml/ocaml#11974) demonstrating broader hardware support goals in ocaml/ocaml
  • OCaml variant compatibility work with OxCaml-inspired changes like pipe operator typing being proposed for upstream integration (ocaml/ocaml#14286) in ocaml/ocaml
  • Syntactic sugar design philosophy emerging across ocaml/RFCs with community establishing thresholds for when new syntax is justified versus relying on functional programming idioms (ocaml/RFCs#56)

    • Multicore

    Focus on filesystem performance improvements in Eio and type safety enhancements in ocaml-uring

    Overview

  • Most activity centered on ocaml-multicore/eio with new incremental directory reading API (ocaml-multicore/eio#821) and ongoing socket options work (ocaml-multicore/eio#575)
  • ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring saw design discussions on file descriptor type safety with two PRs (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#128, ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#130) exploring abstraction boundaries
  • No activity recorded in ocaml-multicore/domainslib, ocaml-multicore/meio, ocaml-multicore/saturn, ocaml-multicore/eio-trace, ocaml-multicore/picos, ocaml-multicore/kcas, or ocaml-multicore/ocaml-iomux

    • Activity

  • Patrick Ferris opened draft PR for incremental directory reading in ocaml-multicore/eio with with_dir_entries API, showing performance improvements from 1.46s to 110ms on io_uring backend and 2.02s to 1.58s on POSIX, with feedback from Anil Madhavapeddy suggesting error handling and traversal strategies (ocaml-multicore/eio#821)
  • David Allsopp opened two PRs in ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring addressing type-safe file descriptor handling: ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#128 eliminates Obj.magic by handling AT_FDCWD in C stubs, while draft ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#130 proposes type-safe wait functions
  • Thomas Leonard provided detailed code review feedback on ocaml-multicore/eio#575 for socket options API implementation, focusing on mock improvements and pretty-printer consistency
  • Anil Madhavapeddy indicated readiness to merge ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#128 pending end-to-end testing with Eio integration

    • Notable Discussions

  • File descriptor abstraction design sparked debate on ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#128: Thomas Leonard argued kernel interfaces require integer access and avoiding it pushes dangerous code into C, while David Allsopp maintained that exposing OCaml integer representations is risky due to C/OCaml differences, with Anil Madhavapeddy supporting abstract types with safe conversions
  • Windows vs Linux portability discussed on ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#128 and ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#130, noting file descriptors are definitively integers on Linux but require different handling on Windows, potentially warranting a separate library for Windows ioring
  • Compiler optimization of optional arguments explored on ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#128, with David Allsopp noting flambda 1 and 2 optimize optional arguments better than current assumptions suggest

    • Emerging Trends

  • Eliminating unsafe operations emerged as a priority, with ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#128 and ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#130 both targeting removal of Obj.magic usage, motivated by upstream work in ocaml/ocaml#14258
  • Type safety vs allocation trade-offs became central to design discussions on ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#130, exploring ways to differentiate return types without increasing allocations on fast paths
  • Linux-specific optimizations gaining attention, with Anil Madhavapeddy suggesting on ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#128 that private int types for file descriptors and deeper Eiolinux integration could reduce Unix.filedescr usage
  • Performance measurement highlighted in ocaml-multicore/eio#821 with comprehensive benchmarks demonstrating concrete gains from incremental APIs, particularly on io_uring backend
entry.summary: OCaml 5.4.0 released with runtime quotations in OxCaml, package ecosystem expansion, and filesystem performance improvements

entry.title: Week 40, 2025: OCaml 5.4.0 RC1 released, merlin/LSP updates, cmdliner 2.0 ecosystem migration, oxcaml compiler advances, and multicore type safety work
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Ecosystem OCaml 5.4.0~rc1 first release candidate for OCaml 5.4.0 by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/opam-repository#28622)
  • OCaml Tools merlin 5.6-504 and 5.6-503 releases by Ulysse with OCaml 5.4 support and locate-types command for navigating complex type structures like a -> (b * c) (ocaml/opam-repository#28650, ocaml/merlin#1951)
  • OCaml Tools ocaml-lsp-server 1.24.0 and 1.23.1 releases by Ulysse enabling OCaml 5.4 support and fixing hover on method calls (ocaml/opam-repository#28649, ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1553)
  • OCaml Tools Dune promoted files read-only by Antonin Décimo prevents accidental edits to generated files (ocaml/dune#12519)
  • OCaml Tools Dune package management performance improvements reducing null build times from 8s to 1s through optimized lockdir parsing by @v-gb and Stephen Sherratt (ocaml/dune#12487, ocaml/dune#12517, ocaml/dune#12518)
  • OCaml Tools Opam incremental file loading reduces opam update time from ~10s to ~0.01s on Windows and ~3.5s to ~1ms on Unix by @arozovyk (ocaml/opam#6614)
  • OCaml Tools Merlin typer cache control via -use-typer-cache flag for debugging and testing by Tim ats (ocaml/merlin#1972)
  • OCaml Tools Merlin Vim plugin crash fix when :MerlinOccurrencesProjectWide encounters inaccurate text preview by Jules Aguillon (ocaml/merlin#1970)
  • OCaml Tools OCaml-LSP .mll file support fixed error when opening ocamllex files by Török Edwin (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1557)
  • OCaml Ecosystem cmdliner 2.0.0 command-line parsing library update by Daniel Bünzli (ocaml/opam-repository#28599)
  • OCaml Ecosystem raven 1.0.0~alpha1 machine learning library with 11 packages (nx, nx-datasets, fehu, hugin, kaun) by Thibaut Mattio (ocaml/opam-repository#28626)
  • OCaml Ecosystem alcotest 1.9.1 testing framework update across 5 packages by Calascibetta Romain (ocaml/opam-repository#28629)
  • OCaml Ecosystem Neovim LSP setup guide covering both vim.lsp (v0.11.0+) and nvim-lspconfig approaches by Jacob Kim (ocaml/ocaml.org#3322)
  • OCaml Ecosystem Command-line argument parsing cookbook with examples using Sys.argv, Arg module, and Cmdliner by Richard Huxton (ocaml/ocaml.org#2573)
  • OCaml Ecosystem Web server cookbook recipes demonstrating HTML template rendering with Dream and Cohttp by Odinaka Joy (ocaml/ocaml.org#3185)
  • OCaml Ecosystem First-class modules tutorial added to Language/Module System documentation by Frédéric Loyer (ocaml/ocaml.org#2090)
  • OCaml Ecosystem RSS feed button on OCaml Planet page to improve feed discoverability by sabine (ocaml/ocaml.org#3338)
  • OCaml Ecosystem Nushell shell support added to Windows opam environment setup by Tim Hutt (ocaml/ocaml.org#3307)
  • OxCaml Reaper direct call preservation flag -reaper-preserve-direct-calls with options never, always, zero-alloc, and auto for Flambda2 by Nathanaëlle Courant (oxcaml/oxcaml#4787)
  • OxCaml Debugging support now enabled by default with -g added to default compilation flags by Jack Rickard (oxcaml/oxcaml#4804)
  • OxCaml Jkind immediate64ornull for 64-bit immediate values that can be null by @dkalinichenko-js (oxcaml/oxcaml#4788)
  • OxCaml Datalog debugging infrastructure with provenance information for troubleshooting by Basile Clément (oxcaml/oxcaml#4818)
  • OxCaml Mode error messages improved by printing both sides separately by Zesen Qian (oxcaml/oxcaml#4719)
  • OxCaml Block indices now cross all modal axes by Ryan Tjoa (oxcaml/oxcaml#4806)
  • OxCaml ppx_template completion support via merlin.ppx_template_generated attribute in oxcaml/merlin by Liam Stevenson (oxcaml/merlin#190)

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    OCaml 5.4.0 RC1 released, cmdliner 2.0.0 migration completed, documentation expansion, and security infrastructure improvements

    New Features

  • OCaml 5.4.0~rc1 first release candidate for OCaml 5.4.0 by Florian Angeletti (ocaml/opam-repository#28622)
  • cmdliner 2.0.0 command-line parsing library update by Daniel Bünzli (ocaml/opam-repository#28599)
  • raven 1.0.0~alpha1 machine learning library with 11 packages (nx, nx-datasets, fehu, hugin, kaun) by Thibaut Mattio (ocaml/opam-repository#28626)
  • alcotest 1.9.1 testing framework update across 5 packages by Calascibetta Romain (ocaml/opam-repository#28629)
  • merlin 5.6-504 and ocaml-lsp-server 1.24.0 editor support improvements by Ulysse (ocaml/opam-repository#28650, ocaml/opam-repository#28649)
  • Neovim LSP setup guide covering both vim.lsp (v0.11.0+) and nvim-lspconfig approaches by Jacob Kim (ocaml/ocaml.org#3322)
  • Command-line argument parsing cookbook with examples using Sys.argv, Arg module, and Cmdliner by Richard Huxton (ocaml/ocaml.org#2573)
  • Web server cookbook recipes demonstrating HTML template rendering with Dream and Cohttp by Odinaka Joy (ocaml/ocaml.org#3185)
  • First-class modules tutorial added to Language/Module System documentation by Frédéric Loyer (ocaml/ocaml.org#2090)
  • RSS feed button on OCaml Planet page to improve feed discoverability by sabine (ocaml/ocaml.org#3338)
  • charrua 2.1.1 DHCP implementation across 4 packages by Reynir Björnsson (ocaml/opam-repository#28634)
  • moonpool 0.9 parallel programming library across 3 packages (ocaml/opam-repository#28597)
  • ppxlib 0.36.2 PPX framework update by Nathan Rebours (ocaml/opam-repository#28610)
  • uring 2.7.0 io_uring bindings by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml/opam-repository#28604)
  • b0 0.0.6 and odig 0.1.0 build system and documentation tools by Daniel Bünzli (ocaml/opam-repository#28611)
  • ocp-indent 1.9.0 code indentation tool by Nathan Rebours (ocaml/opam-repository#28630)
  • mirage-kv-mem 4.0.1 and mirage-monitoring 0.0.8 MirageOS libraries by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#28627, ocaml/opam-repository#28625)
  • Nushell shell support added to Windows opam environment setup by Tim Hutt (ocaml/ocaml.org#3307)
  • Updated Ahrefs success story with expanded petabyte-scale crawler details by sabine (ocaml/ocaml.org#2863)

    • Overview

  • 43 packages merged in ocaml/opam-repository including OCaml 5.4.0~rc1 (ocaml/opam-repository#28622), cmdliner 2.0.0 migration (ocaml/opam-repository#28599), raven ML packages (ocaml/opam-repository#28626), and MirageOS ecosystem updates (ocaml/opam-repository#27551, ocaml/opam-repository#28464, ocaml/opam-repository#28481)
  • Documentation expansion in ocaml/ocaml.org with Neovim setup guide (ocaml/ocaml.org#3322), CLI parsing cookbook (ocaml/ocaml.org#2573), web server recipes (ocaml/ocaml.org#3185), and first-class modules tutorial (ocaml/ocaml.org#2090)
  • Security infrastructure established with Security Response Team announcement (ocaml/ocaml.org#3337) and improved GitHub vulnerability reporting (ocaml/ocaml.org#3335)
  • Development tooling advanced with merlin 5.6-504 (ocaml/opam-repository#28650), ocaml-lsp-server 1.24.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#28649), ppxlib 0.36.2 (ocaml/opam-repository#28610), and ocp-indent 1.9.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#28630)
  • Active contributors included Hannes Mehnert leading MirageOS work, Daniel Bünzli managing cmdliner migration, sabine improving documentation infrastructure, and Yawar Amin optimizing content delivery

    • Activity

  • cmdliner 2.0.0 migration completed across ocaml/opam-repository with multiple compatibility fixes including upper bounds on ocamlformat by @mserpi (ocaml/opam-repository#28651), constraint revisions by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#28635), and constraint additions by Daniel Bünzli (ocaml/opam-repository#28607, ocaml/opam-repository#28606, ocaml/opam-repository#28603)
  • MirageOS core releases across multiple versions: 4.9.0, 4.10.0, and 4.10.1 by Hannes Mehnert showing active unikernel platform development (ocaml/opam-repository#27551, ocaml/opam-repository#28464, ocaml/opam-repository#28481)
  • Dune Package Management migration in ocaml/ocaml.org (ocaml/ocaml.org#3281) by sabine remains in progress with active discussion about Docker build issues on Ubuntu 25.04 and performance impacts
  • Lwt 6 compatibility work by Raphaël Proust adding incompatibility constraints for packages using deprecated APIs (ocaml/opam-repository#28641)
  • Governance infrastructure cleanup by Sacha Ayoun removing deprecated mailing lists (ocaml/ocaml.org#3306) and updating Zulip links (ocaml/ocaml.org#3328)
  • OCaml Planet optimization by Yawar Amin removing full blog post bodies from stored data, reducing repository size (ocaml/ocaml.org#3125)
  • Security Response Team announcement added to OCaml Changelog by sabine establishing formal vulnerability reporting process (ocaml/ocaml.org#3337)
  • MSys2 infrastructure improvements with symlink handling by Jan Midtgaard (ocaml/opam-repository#28614)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Rapid ecosystem coordination on breaking changes demonstrated through cmdliner 2.0.0 migration with 6 PRs within days across ocaml/opam-repository (ocaml/opam-repository#28599, ocaml/opam-repository#28603, ocaml/opam-repository#28606, ocaml/opam-repository#28607, ocaml/opam-repository#28635, ocaml/opam-repository#28651)
  • Documentation-first approach emerging with cookbook recipes (ocaml/ocaml.org#2573, ocaml/ocaml.org#3185, ocaml/ocaml.org#3201) and editor setup guides (ocaml/ocaml.org#3322) growing alongside package releases
  • MirageOS platform maturation with three successive releases (4.9.0, 4.10.0, 4.10.1) showing rapid iteration by Hannes Mehnert (ocaml/opam-repository#27551, ocaml/opam-repository#28464, ocaml/opam-repository#28481)
  • Development tooling investment with coordinated releases of merlin (ocaml/opam-repository#28649, ocaml/opam-repository#28650), ocaml-lsp-server (ocaml/opam-repository#28649), ppxlib (ocaml/opam-repository#28610), and ocp-indent (ocaml/opam-repository#28630)
  • OCaml 5.x progression with first release candidate for 5.4.0 (ocaml/opam-repository#28622) and Lwt 6 migration planning (ocaml/opam-repository#28641)
  • Security infrastructure development established as priority with Security Response Team (ocaml/ocaml.org#3337) and improved reporting workflows (ocaml/ocaml.org#3335)
  • Build system modernization efforts with Dune Package Management migration in ocaml/ocaml.org (ocaml/ocaml.org#3281)
  • Machine learning ecosystem expansion with raven framework alpha introducing 11 new packages (ocaml/opam-repository#28626)

    • OCaml Tools

    OCaml 5.4 support across toolchain, performance improvements in dune/opam, multiple releases shipped

    New Features

  • Dune promoted files now read-only to prevent accidental edits to generated files (ocaml/dune#12519 by Antonin Décimo)
  • Dune package management performance improvements for null builds, reducing build times from 8s to 1s through optimized lockdir parsing and hash computation (ocaml/dune#12248 via ocaml/dune#12487, ocaml/dune#12517, ocaml/dune#12518 by @v-gb, Stephen Sherratt)
  • Dune package release dev tools dune-release and opam-publish enrolled as installable dev tools (ocaml/dune#12522 by Sudha Parimala)
  • Merlin locate-types command enables navigation to all type identifiers within complex types like a -> (b * c), returning a tree structure with locations for each type component (ocaml/merlin#1951 by Liam Stevenson)
  • Merlin OCaml 5.4 support through vendored typer upgrade (ocaml/merlin#1971, ocaml/merlin#1974 by Xavier Van de Woestyne)
  • Merlin typer cache control via -use-typer-cache flag for debugging and testing (ocaml/merlin#1972 by Tim ats)
  • Merlin Vim plugin crash fix when :MerlinOccurrencesProjectWide encounters inaccurate text preview (ocaml/merlin#1970 by Jules Aguillon)
  • Opam incremental file loading reduces opam update time from ~10s to ~0.01s on Windows and ~3.5s to ~1ms on Unix by processing only changed files (ocaml/opam#6614 by @arozovyk, closes ocaml/opam#5824)
  • Opam Windows extra-files fix for false-positive mismatch warnings during opam update when processing nested extra-files (ocaml/opam#6715 by Kate)
  • Opam reftest engine improvements including new unset builtin (ocaml/opam#6708) and hardened regexp for variable checksum substitution (ocaml/opam#6710 by Kate)
  • OCaml-LSP OCaml 5.4 support enabling compilation with latest compiler version (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1559 by Ulysse)
  • OCaml-LSP .mll file support fixed error when opening ocamllex files (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1557 by Török Edwin)
  • OCaml-LSP method call hover fix now displays type information correctly (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1553 by Ulysse, resolves ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1552)

    • Overview

  • OCaml 5.4 migration coordinated across toolchain with ocaml/merlin shipping two releases (5.6-503 and 5.6-504) and ocaml/ocaml-lsp shipping releases 1.23.1 and 1.24.0 (ocaml/merlin#1973, ocaml/merlin#1974, ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1558, ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1559)
  • Performance optimization focus with ocaml/dune achieving 8x build time reduction for null builds (ocaml/dune#12248) and ocaml/opam delivering 100-1000x faster opam update operations (ocaml/opam#6614)
  • Developer tooling improvements across ocaml/dune with release tools enrollment (ocaml/dune#12522), dev tools environment access (ocaml/dune#12521), and ocaml/merlin with enhanced navigation via locate-types command (ocaml/merlin#1951)
  • Windows platform compatibility addressed in ocaml/opam with extra-files fix (ocaml/opam#6715), reftest engine fixes (ocaml/opam#6716, ocaml/opam#6714), and macOS GHA compatibility work (ocaml/opam#6719)
  • Active repositories this week: ocaml/dune (20+ PRs), ocaml/merlin (8 PRs, 2 releases), ocaml/opam (15+ PRs), ocaml/ocaml-lsp (2 releases), ocsigen/jsofocaml (Oxcaml support PR opened)
  • Quiet repositories with no activity: ocaml/ocamlfind, ocaml/odoc, ocaml/opam-file-format, ocaml-dune/spawn

    • Activity

  • Dune melange refactoring PRs opened for ocamldep rules (ocaml/dune#12532), ocamlobjinfo targets (ocaml/dune#12533), and include_qualified cmj dependencies fix (ocaml/dune#12531 by Antonio Nuno Monteiro)
  • Dune dev tools environment access under development with dune tools env command for editor integration (ocaml/dune#12521 by Stephen Sherratt, addresses ocaml/dune#10964)
  • Dune OxCaml library parameters feature adds (parameters ...) field to library stanza for parameterized libraries requiring -parameter compiler flag (ocaml/dune#12336 by @art-w, fixes ocaml/dune#12086)
  • Dune test concurrency work continues allowing tests to run concurrently with watch server (ocaml/dune#12473 by Ambre Austen Suhamy, supersedes ocaml/dune#11900)
  • Dune changelog restructuring progressing with new directory-based structure (ocaml/dune#12472, ocaml/dune#12516 by Etienne)
  • Merlin refactoring commands under development with expression extraction to let bindings (ocaml/merlin#1948 by Tim ats) and inlay hints improvements via [@merlin.hide] attribute (ocaml/merlin#1894 by Marc Lasson)
  • Opam repository inspection command opam repo show opened to display URL and rank of specific repositories (ocaml/opam#6720 by Francisco Santos)
  • Opam OPAMAUTOANSWER support for internal use ready to merge, required for pinned dependencies fix (ocaml/opam#6709 by Kate, follow-up ocaml/opam#6718)
  • Opam reproducible releases PR using git archive to eliminate timestamp/metadata variations (ocaml/opam#6706 by Kate, fixes ocaml/opam#6619)
  • Opam depexts status checking under review to check system package availability during opam update for performance (ocaml/opam#6489 by @arozovyk, fixes ocaml/opam#6461)
  • Opam AppArmor profile support in installation script tested and awaiting final review (ocaml/opam#6647 by Kate, fixes ocaml/opam#5968)
  • OCaml-LSP .mlx file formatting support under development with ocamlformat-mlx, manual testing revealing integration issues (ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1528 by David Sancho)
  • Jsofocaml Oxcaml support PR opened affecting 127 files with 5,515 additions (ocsigen/jsofocaml#2105 by Jérôme Vouillon)
  • Jsofocaml Stack Switching proposal implementation for effects-based Wasm code generation continues (ocsigen/jsofocaml#1832 by Jérôme Vouillon)

    • Notable Discussions

  • Opam repository redirect handling investigation into why repositories containing redirects are marked as changed (ocaml/opam#6717 by R. Boujbel, tracing back to ocaml/opam#5146)
  • Opam pin workflow regression where opam pin remove no longer upgrades to latest version after unpinning, causing switch recompilation with old version (ocaml/opam#6622 by Daniel Bünzli)
  • Opam OPAMFETCH tokenization issue where quoted arguments in environment variable are split by whitespace, breaking authorization headers for private GitHub repositories (ocaml/opam#5490 by SeungCheol Jung, PR ocaml/opam#5492)
  • Opam build-env field behavior discussion clarifying interaction between setenv and build-env, with agreement that build-env should apply after setenv (ocaml/opam#6574 by Daniel Bünzli and Kate, fix in ocaml/opam#6713)
  • Opam MSys2 symlink behavior under MinGW with Cygwin-incompatible default winsymlinks:deepcopy mode, potential for opam to control via MSYS=winsymlinks:native (ocaml/opam#6712 by Jan Midtgaard)
  • Jsofocaml performance costs of const/let bindings due to TDZ checks, referencing TypeScript, esbuild, and Scala.js decisions to continue using var (ocsigen/jsofocaml#1570 by Henry Till)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Compiler version support prioritized across toolchain with coordinated OCaml 5.4 adoption in ocaml/merlin (#1971, #1974) and ocaml/ocaml-lsp (#1559), ensuring rapid adoption of new compiler features
  • Build and update performance optimization emerged as cross-repository priority with ocaml/dune achieving 8x null build speedup (#12248 via #12487, #12517, #12518) and ocaml/opam delivering 100-1000x faster updates (#6614)
  • Developer experience improvements focusing on IDE integration with ocaml/dune dev tools environment access (#12521), ocaml/merlin enhanced navigation (#1951) and refactoring commands (#1948)
  • Windows and cross-platform compatibility receiving attention in ocaml/opam with multiple fixes (#6715, #6716, #6714, #6719) and platform-specific behavior investigation (#6712)
  • Test infrastructure hardening in ocaml/opam with reftest engine improvements (#6708, #6710) and macOS GHA compatibility work (#6719)
  • File format and dialect support expansion with ocaml/ocaml-lsp adding .mll support (#1557) and .mlx formatting work (#1528)
  • Package management ecosystem maturation with ocaml/dune release tools enrollment (#12522) and ongoing work on lock directories as targets (#11775)

    • OxCaml

    Main oxcaml repository advances js_of_ocaml integration, mode system, and Flambda2 optimizations with tooling improvements

    New Features

  • oxcaml/oxcaml#4787: New -reaper-preserve-direct-calls flag with options never, always, zero-alloc, and auto to control direct call preservation strategy in the reaper pass for Flambda2
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#4804: Debugging support now enabled by default with -g added to default compilation flags by Jack Rickard
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#4788: New jkind immediate64_or_null for 64-bit immediate values that can be null by @dkalinichenko-js
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#4818: Datalog debugging infrastructure added with provenance information for easier troubleshooting by Basile Clément
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#4719: Mode error messages improved by printing both sides separately for easier integration by Zesen Qian
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#4634: Mode hints now displayed in inclusion errors for better diagnostics by Zesen Qian
  • oxcaml/oxcaml#4806: Block indices now cross all modal axes, expanding their applicability by Ryan Tjoa
  • oxcaml/merlin#190: Added merlin.ppx_template_generated attribute support for marking identifiers generated by ppx_template in completion results by Liam Stevenson
  • oxcaml/merlin#190: Completion results now include ppx_template_generated boolean field in JSON responses when identifiers are marked with the attribute
  • oxcaml/opam-repository#16: Fixed uutf.1.0.3+ox package conflict declaration to mark Cmdliner 2.0 as incompatible by Marek Kubica

    • Overview

  • Main development concentrated in oxcaml/oxcaml repository with 26 active contributors and approximately 40 merged PRs across Flambda2 optimizations, mode system evolution, datalog infrastructure, and jsofocaml integration
  • Basile Clément delivered five datalog infrastructure PRs (oxcaml/oxcaml#4814, oxcaml/oxcaml#4815, oxcaml/oxcaml#4816, oxcaml/oxcaml#4817, oxcaml/oxcaml#4818) improving debugging and query representation
  • Zesen Qian advanced mode system extensibility with six PRs including new staticity axis (oxcaml/oxcaml#4799) and improved error reporting (oxcaml/oxcaml#4719, oxcaml/oxcaml#4634)
  • Jacob Van Buren led jsofocaml integration with compiler changes (oxcaml/oxcaml#4791), sourcemap fixes (oxcaml/oxcaml#4792), and linking optimizations (oxcaml/oxcaml#4793)
  • Ryan Tjoa pushed block indices toward stable status with five PRs including modal axis expansion (oxcaml/oxcaml#4806), stabilization (oxcaml/oxcaml#4827), and new primitives (oxcaml/oxcaml#4828)
  • Minimal activity in supporting repositories: oxcaml/opam-repository merged two PRs for package compatibility, oxcaml/merlin merged one PR for ppxtemplate support, and no activity in oxcaml/jsof_ocaml or janestreet/opam-repository

    • Activity

  • Jsofocaml integration progressing across multiple fronts with Jacob Van Buren implementing compiler and driver changes generating 46 comments (oxcaml/oxcaml#4791), sourcemap fixes (oxcaml/oxcaml#4792), linking optimizations (oxcaml/oxcaml#4793), and backend parameterization for optcomp (oxcaml/oxcaml#4823)
  • Mode system refactoring by Zesen Qian simplifying new axis additions (oxcaml/oxcaml#4789), converting modes to constants in .cmi files (oxcaml/oxcaml#4790), introducing new staticity mode axis with 8 comments (oxcaml/oxcaml#4799), and handling monadic closure axes (oxcaml/oxcaml#4798)
  • Block indices stabilization with Ryan Tjoa implementing unboxed versions for flattened float fields (oxcaml/oxcaml#4826), moving to stable status (oxcaml/oxcaml#4827), adding unsafe get/set primitives (oxcaml/oxcaml#4828), and restricting atomic field usage (oxcaml/oxcaml#4824)
  • Datalog infrastructure improvements with five merged PRs by Basile Clément: break instruction printer fix (oxcaml/oxcaml#4814), API cleanup (oxcaml/oxcaml#4815), explicit query representation (oxcaml/oxcaml#4816), high-level variable storage (oxcaml/oxcaml#4817), and provenance debugging (oxcaml/oxcaml#4818), plus ongoing join analysis work (oxcaml/oxcaml#4819)
  • Flambda2 optimizations including Guillaume Bury fixing continuation specialization bug resolving three match-in-match issues (oxcaml/oxcaml#4751, oxcaml/oxcaml#4731, oxcaml/oxcaml#4732, oxcaml/oxcaml#4733), Nathanaëlle Courant improving reaper to preserve direct calls in zero-alloc functions with 33 comments (oxcaml/oxcaml#4787), and Greta Yorsh fixing zero-alloc warning scope (oxcaml/oxcaml#4811)
  • CI and testing infrastructure enhancements by Xavier Clerc: PR number tracking in metrics (oxcaml/oxcaml#4822), workflow automation for test promotion (oxcaml/oxcaml#4808, oxcaml/oxcaml#4809), CFG terminator simplification (oxcaml/oxcaml#4807), and Vincent Laviron fixing ocamlformat CI (oxcaml/oxcaml#4820)
  • Merlin tooling with Liam Stevenson adding ppxtemplategenerated attribute support marking generated identifiers in completion results (oxcaml/merlin#190)
  • Package management with Marek Kubica fixing Cmdliner 2.0 compatibility in uutf package (oxcaml/opam-repository#16) and @dkalinichenko-js adding dev branch to CI workflow (oxcaml/opam-repository#17)
  • Other work includes Mark Shinwell improving register availability computation (oxcaml/oxcaml#4801), Chris Casinghino fixing documentation links (oxcaml/oxcaml#4774), automatic primitive list generation (oxcaml/oxcaml#4812), static constant sharing restoration (oxcaml/oxcaml#4800), and testsuite cleanup (oxcaml/oxcaml#4794)

    • Notable Discussions

  • Jsofocaml integration architecture generated 46 comments on oxcaml/oxcaml#4791 discussing compiler and driver changes, integration approach, and compatibility considerations
  • Reaper direct call preservation sparked 33-comment discussion on oxcaml/oxcaml#4787 debating zero-alloc function handling strategy and trade-offs between optimization levels
  • Mode hints in errors had 10 comments on oxcaml/oxcaml#4634 debating presentation and integration approaches for better error diagnostics
  • Staticity mode axis generated 8 comments on oxcaml/oxcaml#4799 exploring design decisions and implications for the mode system
  • Metrics CSV tracking discussed through 7 comments on oxcaml/oxcaml#4822 improving CI infrastructure and data collection

    • Emerging Trends

  • Flambda2 maturity progressing through systematic datalog infrastructure improvements (oxcaml/oxcaml#4814, oxcaml/oxcaml#4815, oxcaml/oxcaml#4816, oxcaml/oxcaml#4817, oxcaml/oxcaml#4818), match-in-match bug fixes (oxcaml/oxcaml#4751), reaper refinements (oxcaml/oxcaml#4787), and zero-allocation optimization work (oxcaml/oxcaml#4811)
  • Mode system evolution showing architectural improvements for extensibility with new axis addition support (oxcaml/oxcaml#4789), staticity axis introduction (oxcaml/oxcaml#4799), and better error reporting (oxcaml/oxcaml#4719, oxcaml/oxcaml#4634)
  • Unboxed types stabilization accelerating with block indices moving from experimental to stable (oxcaml/oxcaml#4827), expanded modal coverage (oxcaml/oxcaml#4806), and new primitive operations (oxcaml/oxcaml#4828)
  • Backend flexibility increasing through jsofocaml integration work (oxcaml/oxcaml#4791, oxcaml/oxcaml#4792, oxcaml/oxcaml#4793) and optcomp parameterization (oxcaml/oxcaml#4823)
  • Developer experience improvements through default debug flag enablement (oxcaml/oxcaml#4804), CI workflow automation (oxcaml/oxcaml#4808, oxcaml/oxcaml#4809), metrics tracking (oxcaml/oxcaml#4822), documentation fixes (oxcaml/oxcaml#4774), and improved tooling support (oxcaml/merlin#190)

    • OCaml Core

    Ongoing technical discussion of tuple projection RFC addressing row-polymorphic tuples and projection semantics

    Overview

  • Active discussion on ocaml/RFCs#57 proposing tuple projections with labeled and unlabeled syntax
  • No commits or merged changes in ocaml/ocaml during this period
  • Focus on technical review and clarification of RFC semantics and implementation considerations

    • Activity

  • Alistair clarified semantics for the tuple projections RFC in ocaml/RFCs#57, addressing questions about mixed labeled/unlabeled tuples and confirming that let x = ~a:1, ~b:2 in x.1 is rejected
  • Samuel Vivien provided detailed technical review on ocaml/RFCs#57, analyzing row-polymorphic tuples expressiveness and backend implementation requirements
  • Discussion of type inference limitations for row-polymorphic patterns in ocaml/RFCs#57, noting that let get_y t = let ~y, .. = t in y is rejected when expected type is unknown

    • Notable Discussions

  • Row-polymorphic tuples feature discussed in ocaml/RFCs#57 as increasing OCaml's polymorphism expressiveness, with Samuel Vivien noting backend implementation considerations
  • Labeled vs unlabeled projection semantics clarified by Alistair in ocaml/RFCs#57, maintaining consistency with current pattern matching behavior where mixed labeled/unlabeled tuples restrict projection syntax
  • Type inference limitations highlighted in ocaml/RFCs#57 for row-polymorphic patterns, drawing parallels with module polymorphism challenges

    • Multicore

    Type safety improvements in ocaml-uring and ongoing API refinements in eio

    Overview

  • Activity concentrated in 3 of 9 repositories this week: ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring with type safety improvements, ocaml-multicore/eio with API refinements, and ocaml-multicore/meio with CI updates
  • Type safety emerged as the primary focus with three PRs in ocaml-uring addressing file descriptor handling and Obj.magic elimination (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#128, ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#129, ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#130)
  • API improvements continued in eio with updates to long-standing PRs for socket options (ocaml-multicore/eio#575) and Pool API (ocaml-multicore/eio#747)
  • Six repositories showed no activity: domainslib, saturn, eio-trace, picos, kcas, and ocaml-iomux

    • Activity

  • David Allsopp opened three PRs in ocaml-uring focused on type safety improvements: type-safe wait functions (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#130), safer file descriptor handling (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#129), and eliminating Obj.magic for AT_FDCWD (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#128)
  • Anil Madhavapeddy updated socket options implementation in eio (ocaml-multicore/eio#575) adding Eio_unix.Sockopt module, addressing review feedback on string handling and test compatibility
  • Thomas Leonard advanced Pool API improvements in eio (ocaml-multicore/eio#747) to move the never_block optional argument for better compiler inference
  • Tim McGilchrist updated meio CI workflow to OCaml 5.1.1 compiler (ocaml-multicore/meio#70)

    • Notable Discussions

  • File descriptor type safety debate in ocaml-uring explored whether OCaml file descriptors should be abstract types, with David Allsopp noting platform differences between Unix (integers) and Windows (not integers) and questioning when direct integer access is necessary (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#130)
  • Platform-specific considerations examined with discussion of how OCaml file descriptors differ from C file descriptors on Windows, and how OS-level Windows descriptors are pointers rather than integers (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#130)
  • Potential for Windows support in ocaml-uring raised by David Allsopp, noting similarities between liburing and ioringapi.h (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#130)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Type safety improvements gaining focus with elimination of Obj.magic usage and ensuring proper type representation for system-level abstractions in ocaml-uring (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#128, ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#129, ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#130)
  • Cross-platform considerations emerging despite current Linux focus in ocaml-uring, with exploration of design decisions that might affect potential Windows support (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#130)
  • API refinement continuing in eio with long-standing PRs receiving updates and review feedback, indicating focus on API stability and ergonomics (ocaml-multicore/eio#575, ocaml-multicore/eio#747)
entry.summary: OCaml 5.4.0 RC1 released, merlin/LSP updates, cmdliner 2.0 ecosystem migration, oxcaml compiler advances, and multicore type safety work

entry.title: Week 39, 2025: Major oxcaml advances with TLS, JavaScript compilation, and security fixes alongside ocaml-uring v2.7.0 release and ecosystem maintenance
entry.content:
Weekly Summary

New Features

  • OCaml Core String sharing optimization in Lambda code by Stephen Dolan enables better constant folding for string literals in pattern matching (ocaml/ocaml#14259)
  • OCaml Core TSan shadow stack fixes by Olivier Nicole resolved crashes in Thread Sanitizer debugging builds (ocaml/ocaml#14213)
  • OCaml Core Lambda string constant normalization by Vincent Laviron unified string representations throughout the compiler backend (ocaml/ocaml#14260)
  • OxCaml Thread-local storage (TLS) implementation in oxcaml/oxcaml#4747 with comprehensive API in Domain.TLS and Thread.TLS modules, providing per-thread data storage alongside existing Domain-local storage
  • OxCaml Forkable mode axis added in oxcaml/oxcaml#4748 to track whether functions can access shared values in parent stack, with documentation and default behaviors based on locality
  • OxCaml Layout polymorphism extension infrastructure in oxcaml/oxcaml#4756 with layout_poly extension available in alpha/beta/stable maturity levels
  • OxCaml SIMD constants and casts updated in oxcaml/oxcaml#4778 to use int8#/int16# types with sign-extension, improving type safety for SIMD operations
  • OxCaml LLVM backend float data emission improvements in oxcaml/oxcaml#4784 now using bitwise representations instead of textual format to avoid NaN issues
  • Multicore Socket bind and listen operations added to ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring with comprehensive OCaml bindings for asynchronous socket binding and listening (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#118)
  • Multicore Use-after-free data race fixed in ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring completion queue entry handlers preventing potential memory corruption (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#124)
  • Multicore Liburing upgrade to version 2.7 in ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring bringing new io_uring operations and setup flags with extensive vendor updates (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#118)
  • Multicore Enhanced API documentation in ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring with detailed parameter descriptions, return value explanations, and usage examples across all interface functions (ocaml-multicore/ocaml-uring#126)
  • OCaml Ecosystem Cmdliner 2.0.0 released with breaking changes requiring ecosystem-wide coordination by Daniel Bünzli (ocaml/opam-repository#28599, ocaml/opam-repository#28602, ocaml/opam-repository#28603)
  • OCaml Ecosystem Windows MinGW support improvements by Jan Midtgaard including new conf-gtksourceview3 MinGW packages and CI workflow (ocaml/opam-repository#28585, ocaml/opam-repository#28598)
  • OCaml Tools Melange JavaScript compilation optimization by Antonio Nuno Monteiro avoids emitting empty files for module aliases (ocaml/dune#12464)
  • OCaml Tools Benchmarking infrastructure by Xavier Van de Woestyne in ocaml/merlin with timing tests for server operations on large files (ocaml/merlin#1967, ocaml/merlin#1968)
  • OCaml Tools Static linking support for OpenBSD by bin in ocaml/opam enables fully static release binaries (ocaml/opam#6705)
  • OCaml Tools WebAssembly effects implementation development by Jérôme Vouillon in ocsigen/jsofocaml with Stack Switching proposal integration (ocsigen/jsofocaml#1832)

    • Group Activity Summaries

    OCaml Ecosystem

    Major cmdliner 2.0.0 ecosystem coordination alongside community website improvements and infrastructure modernization

    New Features

  • Cmdliner 2.0.0 released with breaking changes requiring ecosystem-wide coordination by Daniel Bünzli (ocaml/opam-repository#28599, ocaml/opam-repository#28602, ocaml/opam-repository#28603)
  • Windows MinGW support improvements by Jan Midtgaard including new conf-gtksourceview3 MinGW packages and CI workflow (ocaml/opam-repository#28585, ocaml/opam-repository#28598)
  • New OCaml blog content added through automated scraping including database testing guides and opam performance research (ocaml/ocaml.org#3331, ocaml/ocaml.org#3329, ocaml/ocaml.org#3326)

    • Overview

  • Package repository dominated by Daniel Bünzli's cmdliner 2.0.0 release coordination requiring ecosystem-wide compatibility updates (ocaml/opam-repository#28599)
  • Community website focused on content expansion through automated blog imports and documentation improvements by Jacob Kim (ocaml/ocaml.org#3322)
  • Cross-platform support advances with Windows MinGW tooling by Jan Midtgaard (ocaml/opam-repository#28585, ocaml/opam-repository#28598)
  • Infrastructure modernization spanning both repositories with governance updates and automated content management

    • Activity

  • Major package releases delivered across multiple domains including postgresql 5.3.2 by Markus Mottl (ocaml/opam-repository#28605), uring 2.7.0 by Anil Madhavapeddy (ocaml/opam-repository#28604), and moonpool 0.9 by Simon Cruanes (ocaml/opam-repository#28597)
  • Network security stack updates by Hannes Mehnert with coordinated TLS 2.0.3 (ocaml/opam-repository#28590) and DNS 10.2.1 (ocaml/opam-repository#28582) releases
  • Editor setup documentation being expanded by Jacob Kim to include comprehensive Neovim LSP configuration alongside existing editor guides (ocaml/ocaml.org#3322)
  • Governance modernization led by Sacha Ayoun to remove inactive mailing lists and migrate community infrastructure (ocaml/ocaml.org#3306, ocaml/ocaml.org#3328)
  • Static site generation advancement with YoCaML 2.6.0 release including 13 packages by Xavier Van de Woestyne (ocaml/opam-repository#28571)

    • Notable Discussions

  • LSP configuration enhancement discussed by Török Edwin who proposed simplifications to upstream nvim-lspconfig while reviewing Jacob Kim's comprehensive Neovim setup documentation (ocaml/ocaml.org#3322)
  • Community infrastructure modernization discussed between Anil Madhavapeddy and Sacha Ayoun regarding mailing list removal due to spam issues and migration to discuss.ocaml.org forum (ocaml/ocaml.org#3306)
  • Package compatibility coordination with extensive discussion around cmdliner 2.0.0 ecosystem impact and automated constraint management by Kate (ocaml/opam-repository#28601)

    • Emerging Trends

  • Ecosystem-wide breaking change management demonstrates mature coordination processes with Daniel Bünzli leading cmdliner 2.0.0 release while community systematically handles compatibility (ocaml/opam-repository#28599, ocaml/opam-repository#28601)
  • Cross-platform support expansion with Jan Midtgaard systematically improving Windows compatibility through MinGW tooling and CI infrastructure (ocaml/opam-repository#28585, ocaml/opam-repository#28598)
  • Community infrastructure modernization trend with migration from traditional mailing lists to forum-based discussions and improved automation for content management (ocaml/ocaml.org#3306)
  • Developer experience improvements through comprehensive editor documentation expansion and better tooling integration across the ecosystem

    • OCaml Tools

    Active development across build tools and language services with 19 merged PRs in dune, new benchmarking in merlin, and OpenBSD support in opam

    New Features

  • ocaml/dune: Melange JavaScript compilation optimization by Antonio Nuno Monteiro avoids emitting empty files for module aliases (#12464), dependency set marshalling fix by Rudi Grinberg resolves ocaml-re compatibility (#12509), and CLI module reorganization using qualified subdirs (#12478)
  • ocaml/merlin: Benchmarking infrastructure by Xavier Van de Woestyne with timing tests for server operations on large files (#1967, #1968)
  • ocaml/opam: Static linking support for OpenBSD by bin enables fully static release binaries (#6705) and updated build dependencies including dune.3.20.2 by Kate (#6700)
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml: WebAssembly effects implementation development by Jérôme Vouillon with Stack Switching proposal integration (#1832)

    • Overview

  • ocaml/dune led activity with 19 merged PRs focusing on CLI refactoring, package management optimization, and Melange compilation improvements
  • ocaml/opam delivered platform reliability enhancements with OpenBSD static linking support and dependency updates
  • ocaml/merlin introduced benchmarking infrastructure for performance testing and ongoing expression extraction refactoring
  • ocsigen/jsofocaml continued WebAssembly and effects development with three active draft PRs
  • ocaml/ocaml-lsp resolved Nix build issues and maintained automated dependency updates
  • ocaml/odoc received navigation improvement request comparing to Rustdoc functionality (#1386)
  • ocaml/ocamlfind, ocaml/opam-file-format, and ocaml-dune/spawn had no activity this week

    • Activity

  • ocaml/dune advanced package management infrastructure with lock directory handling by Marek Kubica (#12394), test environment improvements (#12488, #12489), and comprehensive CONTRIBUTING.md updates by Shon Feder (#12440)
